bl_add_collection_instance:
Instance a Blender collection (an Empty drawing it) at transforms or points without copying geometry; LIST them with each one's world box, or REALIZE them into real objects. A target inside the collection itself is refused. See mif_help. mode is ADD (default: one Empty per transform or point), LIST (every collection-instance Empty with its world box) or REALIZE (objects' Empties made into real objects, the Empty removed); instance_offset [x, y, z] sets the collection's own instance offset, shared by every instance of it.

mode ADD (default): collection, then transforms [{location, rotation (radians, as transform_object), scale (a number or [x, y, z])}] or points [[x, y, z], ...] - one Empty per entry, named name (default <collection>_inst), linked into target (default the scene's root collection). instance_offset sets the collection's own instance offset, which every instance of it shares. Each Empty answers its world location, rotation, scale, the objects it draws and their world box (read off the evaluated instances). A target inside the instanced collection's tree is refused: Blender drops that cycle silently and draws nothing.

mode LIST: every collection-instance Empty (of collection, or only objects), each with its box. mode REALIZE: objects are instance Empties; each is made real (Blender's duplicates_make_real - meshes keep sharing the collection's mesh data) and the Empty removed; made lists the new objects.

The reverse read is bl_mesh_stats instances=true, which lists what any instancer draws. Versions 3.6-5.2.
bl_bake_grease_pencil:
Bake Blender Grease Pencil objects' modifiers and animation - Line Art included - into a new object of plain strokes, a keyframe per baked frame. See mif_help. frame_start and frame_end bound the bake (default the scene's range) and step is the frame interval (default 1, at least 1); frame_target is the first frame written (default frame_start); project is KEEP (default), FRONT, SIDE, TOP, VIEW or CURSOR on 3.6 and 4.2, and only KEEP from 4.3, where the op writes the bake itself.

objects: the Grease Pencil objects baked. frame_start / frame_end (default the scene's range), step (default 1), frame_target (the first frame written, default frame_start), name (the new object's). On 3.6 and 4.2 this runs Blender's gpencil.bake_grease_pencil_animation inside a 3D View the op borrows (it polls for one), with project KEEP (default), FRONT, SIDE, TOP, VIEW or CURSOR. From 4.3 Blender's grease_pencil.bake_grease_pencil_animation made an object with no layers headless (measured on 5.2.1), so the bake is written by the op: at each frame each object's EVALUATED drawings - modifiers such as Line Art applied - are copied in world space into a layer <object>_<layer> of the new object, materials carried; only project KEEP there. Reply: object, keyframes, strokes, points, layers, and operator or route.
bl_create_mask:
Make a Blender mask - layers of splines (point lists, or CIRCLE / SQUARE primitives) with feather, keyed at frames and parented to a motion-tracking track - and wire it into a compositor Mask node and / or a sequencer strip's MASK modifier. See mif_help. scene names the scene whose compositing tree gets the Mask node (default the current scene; with strip, the strip's own sequencer scene is used), and an unknown name is refused.

layers [{name?, splines: [...], invert?, blend?, alpha?, falloff?}]; each spline is points [[x, y], ...] (at least 2) or primitive CIRCLE | SQUARE with center [x, y] and size, plus feather (0-1, each point's feather weight) and cyclic (default true). Coordinates are the mask's own space: 0 to 1 across the frame's width, (0, 0) at the bottom left. A CIRCLE gets AUTO handles (a smooth round), a SQUARE and a point list VECTOR handles. keys [{frame, points (every point of the spline) | center + size (a primitive spline), feather?}] keys the points at those frames as F-curves on the mask; the reply reads each key back from the curves (keys: channels, readBack). parent {track, clip? (default the scene's active clip), object? (the tracking object, default the camera's), type? POINT_TRACK, frame? (the scene frame the points are given at, default the current)} makes every point of the spline follow that track. Blender's Parent operator also stores the track's position at parenting, a field Python cannot set, so the points (and keys) are stored minus the track's position at the reference frame instead - they sit as given there and move with the track (parent.offset in the reply). A PLANE_TRACK parent is refused: it evaluates through corners stored at parenting that Python cannot set either. compositor=True adds a Mask node holding it to the scene's compositing tree (refused when the scene has none - bl_set_compositing makes one); strip adds a MASK modifier using it to that sequencer strip. Everything is checked before the mask is made, so a refusal leaves no mask (a build that cannot key a mask point removes it and says so). The reply reads every layer's splines and points back, and what it was wired into.
bl_edit_grease_pencil_strokes:
Clean up Blender Grease Pencil strokes on a keyframe - simplify, smooth, subdivide, merge by distance, thickness, opacity, caps, cyclic, direction, join, reproject onto a surface, separate (4.3+), outline (5.0+); point counts before and after. See mif_help. layer (required) and frame (a keyframe on that layer; default the one shown at the scene's frame) pick the drawing; action is SIMPLIFY, SMOOTH, SUBDIVIDE, MERGE_BY_DISTANCE, SET_THICKNESS, SET_OPACITY, SET_CAPS, CYCLICAL, SWITCH_DIRECTION, JOIN, REPROJECT, SEPARATE or OUTLINE, and settings is that action's own keys (any other key is refused).

layer (required) and frame (a keyframe; default the one shown at the scene's frame) pick the drawing; strokes [indices] (default all). action and settings: SIMPLIFY {distance, local units, default 0.01: Ramer-Douglas-Peucker, ends kept}; SMOOTH {iterations 1-100 default 2, factor 0-1 default 0.5: each inner point toward its neighbours' mean, all points on a cyclic stroke}; SUBDIVIDE {cuts 1-10, default 1}; MERGE_BY_DISTANCE {threshold, default 0.001}; SET_THICKNESS {value: a point radius in metres on 4.3+, the stroke's line_width in pixels on 3.6 / 4.2 - thickness.unit says which}; SET_OPACITY {value 0-1}; SET_CAPS {start, end: ROUND | FLAT}; CYCLICAL {value true | false | 'TOGGLE'}; SWITCH_DIRECTION; JOIN (two or more strokes into the first, in order); REPROJECT {surface: a mesh, offset along its normal, default 0}: every point to the nearest surface point; SEPARATE (grease_pencil.separate, 4.3+: the strokes to a new object, made in the reply); OUTLINE {radius, offsetFactor} (grease_pencil.outline, 5.0+). The geometry verbs are written on the stroke data because Blender's edit-mode stroke operators change nothing in a 3.6 background session (measured); SEPARATE and OUTLINE are refused by name on builds without them. Reply: points per stroke before and after, frameBefore and frameAfter.
bl_groom_attach:
Attach a Blender hair groom (Curves) to its surface - set the surface and UV map, snap the roots onto it (NEAREST, or DEFORM by the existing binding), or report the roots that float off it. See mif_help. mode is REPORT (default, writes nothing), SET_SURFACE or SNAP; attach_mode is SNAP's only, NEAREST (default) or DEFORM (refused when the groom has no surface_uv_coordinate); tolerance is the world distance above which a root counts as floating (default 0.001, 0 or more).

object: a CURVES (hair) object. mode REPORT (default) reads only: each curve's root (its first point, world space) against the surface's evaluated mesh - curves, floating (farther than tolerance, default 0.001 world units), maxDistance, meanDistance and the worst roots (limit, default 20) - plus the current surface, uvMap and hasSurfaceUV. SET_SURFACE sets Curves.surface to surface (a mesh) and surface_uv_map to uv_map (default the surface's active UV map). SNAP sets them when given, then runs Blender's curves.snap_curves_to_surface in sculpt-curves mode (measured headless on 4.2 and 5.2): attach_mode NEAREST (default) moves each curve so its root sits on the nearest surface point and writes surface_uv_coordinate; DEFORM re-attaches by that existing binding after the surface changed - refused when the groom has none (SNAP NEAREST first). The object's mode is put back and the distances after are in the reply.
bl_groom_stroke: Comb, lengthen or shorten, smooth, cut, puff, pinch or slide a Blender hair Curves object's strands, or add and remove strands - natively on its points, in a region or everywhere; lengths, moves and counts read back. See mif_help. A native per-point implementation (sculpt_curves.brush_stroke is keymap-only and region-bound), so repeatable and the same on every build that has what a mode needs. center [x, y, z] and radius (world meters) select the strands whose ROOTS lie within radius - give both or neither (every strand); falloff SMOOTH (default) | LINEAR | CONSTANT over the radius times strength (0-1) is each strand's weight. Roots stay put except in SLIDE. COMB vector [x, y, z]: the tip moves by vector x weight, each point by the square of its share of the strand's length, so the strand bends from a stiff root. LENGTH factor (> 0): every segment scaled by 1 + (factor - 1) x weight. SMOOTH iterations (1-100): Laplacian passes on the inner points, blended by weight, roots and tips held. CUT length (world meters): a strand longer than that is trimmed toward it by weight - the points past the cut are removed and the last one placed on it (Curves.resize_curves: 4.4 and later; refused by name on 3.6 and 4.2). PUFF: strands raised toward the surface normal at the root by weight, segment lengths kept (needs the hair's surface, Curves.surface). PINCH (needs center and radius): strands pulled toward the line through center along each strand's root-to-tip direction, the tip most and the root not, lengths kept. SLIDE vector [x, y, z]: the root moves by vector x weight and is put back on the surface, the strand keeps its shape, and surface_uv_coordinate follows (needs the surface). DENSITY count, seed: count > 0 adds that many strands at area-weighted random roots on the surface within the region, each a copy of the nearest strand's shape moved to its root, with radius and surface_uv_coordinate written when the hair has them (Curves.add_curves: 4.2 and later); count < 0 removes that many of the stroked strands, picked by seed (Curves.remove_curves: 4.4 and later). The reply carries the strands stroked, the mean length before and after, the largest root and tip moves in world meters (null when strands were removed, since indices shift), and for CUT and DENSITY the points and strands before and after (trimmed, added, removed).
bl_heightmap_from_mesh:
Ray-cast a Blender terrain mesh straight down on a grid and write a 16-bit .r16 heightmap at the same mapping as bl_mesh_from_heightmap; misses and clamped heights are counted. See mif_help. Sample (i, j) is cast at origin ([x, y, z] Blender world meters, default [0, 0, 0]) + (i x cell_size, -j x cell_size_y) in meters (cell_size_y defaults to cell_size; both above 0), and its value is mid_value (default 32768) + (hit z - origin z) / height_scale (meters per height unit, above 0), with values outside 0-65535 clamped and counted; miss_value (0-65535, default mid_value) fills grid points the mesh does not cover; samples is a list of [i, j] grid points to report value and hit height for (default the four corners and the center, at most 200).

Each grid point (i, j) at origin + (i x cell_size, -j x cell_size_y) is ray-cast straight down onto the object's evaluated mesh (modifiers count) and written as mid_value + (z - origin.z) / height_scale, rounded. A point the terrain does not cover gets miss_value (default mid_value) and is counted as a miss; a height beyond 0-65535 is clamped and counted. A ray that lands exactly on an edge is retried with a nudge of a ten-thousandth of a cell, so a grid laid on the mesh's own vertices hits every one. file must be .r16 / .raw - the landscape's own raw format, written byte-exact; a PNG is refused. samples [[i, j], ...] lists grid points to report with their value and hit height (default the corners and the centre). Measured: a mesh made by bl_mesh_from_heightmap writes back byte-identical to its source. mif_send_terrain_to_unreal calls this at the landscape's own mapping.
bl_image_stats:
Describe a Blender image's pixels - per channel min, max, mean, stddev, NaN and Inf counts, share at 0 and 1, alpha coverage; a normal-map check, a tiling check and samples at pixels or UVs. Catches a black bake, an inverted normal or a NaN EXR. See mif_help. tile picks a UDIM tile by number (such as 1001) to read; it is refused on an image that is not tiled or has no such tile.

image: an image in the file, or file: a path on disk (loaded, read and removed again). Values are read with Image.pixels as stored: an 8-bit sRGB texture reads its encoded 0-1 values, a float image (an EXR bake) its linear ones. stats per channel (R, G, B, A): nan, inf, and over the finite values min, max, mean, stddev, atZero and atOne (shares of all pixels), constant. nanTotal, infTotal, alphaCoverage (share with alpha above 0.5), and a warning for NaN / Inf or an all-black image.

normal=true decodes n = 2 x rgb - 1: blueUnderHalf (pointing into the surface), meanLength, meanRed and meanGreen (0.5 on a flat map), looksLikeNormalMap, and a colorspaceWarning when the image is tagged sRGB. The green direction (OpenGL or DirectX) is not readable off pixels alone. tiling=true compares the step across the wrap (last column to first, last row to first) with the mean step between neighbours: ratioX / ratioY near 1 tile, well above 2 is a seam (tilesX / tilesY). pixels [[x, y]] (0,0 bottom left) and uvs [[u, v]] (nearest pixel, wrapping) sample values. tile picks a UDIM tile. Images over 8192 x 8192 are refused. Versions 3.6-5.2.
bl_inspect_node_output:
Evaluate a Blender object's Geometry Nodes tree AT ONE NODE - its geometry output routed to the Group Output, read (counts per component, attributes, world box), then every link put back and the restore checked. Finds which node empties the geometry. See mif_help. modifier names which Geometry Nodes modifier on the object to use (default its first NODES modifier); socket picks the node's geometry output by name, identifier or index (default its first enabled geometry output), and a socket that is not a geometry output is refused.

object: an object with a Geometry Nodes modifier (modifier names one when there are several). node: a node at the top level of that modifier's tree (by name). socket: its geometry output by name, identifier or index (default its first). attributes: attribute names whose min / max / mean are read on the mesh at that node.

The op removes the links into the Group Output's geometry input, links the node's output there, evaluates the object and reads it - components (mesh, point cloud, curves and instance counts with their attributes; on 3.6-4.4 the mesh and the drawn instance count), mesh counts, the world box, and empty when nothing came out - then removes the temporary link, puts the original links back and compares the tree's whole link list: restored is true only when it matches, else restoreError lists what differs. A node inside a simulation, repeat or for-each zone is refused (a link from inside a zone to the output is invalid), as is a node with no geometry output. Versions 3.6-5.2.
bl_knife_project: Cut a cutter object's outline (a mesh, curve or text) into a Blender mesh along a direction, through the whole mesh or only the faces seen first, without a 3D View - the crossed faces divided, nothing removed, the seam welded clean. See mif_help. mesh.knife_project projects through the 3D View's region, and in a background session that region has no size - measured on 3.6, 4.2 and 5.2 it answers FINISHED and cuts nothing. So this op sweeps the cutter's outline (its faces, or its closed loops filled) along direction (world, default straight down [0, 0, -1]) into a closed prism, splits the target with EXACT booleans into the part outside and the part inside, welds them back, and drops any prism wall left inside a solid: the crossed faces are divided along the outline and nothing is removed. cut_through (default true) cuts every face the outline crosses, front and back; false cuts only the faces seen first along the direction (Blender's cut_through off) - a face counts when it is not edge-on and a ray from its center back toward the cutter meets nothing else of the mesh, so a half-hidden face is cut whole or not at all (frontFaces and facesLookedAt in the reply). clean_weld (default true) closes the seam a curved or solid cut leaves: on OPEN edges only, outline vertices closer than weld_distance (default 1e-4 of the object's bounding diagonal, in its space; at most a tenth of it) are merged, and an open edge with another half's vertex lying on it is split there and welded (weld: verticesMerged, tJunctionsClosed, openEdgesBefore). nonManifoldEdges counts what is still open after; bl_clean_mesh merge by distance or a fill closes the rest. An outline that misses the mesh changes nothing and says cut false. Refused: the cutter being the object, a cutter that is not a mesh, curve or text, a zero direction, an outline with no face and no closed loop, an object in edit mode, weld_distance without clean_weld.
bl_mask_extract:
Extract a Blender mesh's masked region into a new object (thickness, smoothed border) or slice it out - Blender's own mask extract and slice under either name (mesh.* to 4.4, sculpt.* from 5.0). See mif_help. mode is EXTRACT (default) or SLICE and threshold (0-1, default 0.5) is the mask value that counts; EXTRACT takes add_boundary_loop (default true), smooth_iterations (default 4), solidify (default true) and shrinkwrap (default true), SLICE takes fill_holes (default true), and a key of the other mode is refused.

mode EXTRACT (default) or SLICE; threshold 0-1 (default 0.5) is the mask value that counts. The object needs a mask (bl_sculpt_mask makes one) and is entered into sculpt mode for Blender's own operator - mesh.paint_mask_extract / paint_mask_slice up to 4.4, sculpt.paint_mask_extract / paint_mask_slice from 5.0 (renamed, not removed; operator in the reply) - then its mode is put back.

EXTRACT: add_boundary_loop (default true), smooth_iterations (default 4), solidify (default true: a Solidify modifier on the new object, whose thickness is thickness when given), shrinkwrap (default true: the result is shrink-wrapped back onto the source), name (the new object's). SLICE: fill_holes (default true), new_object (default true: the sliced faces also become an object). EXTRACT keys on SLICE and SLICE keys on EXTRACT are refused. Reply: made [{name, type, vertices, faces, modifiers, thickness}], source counts before and after, maskStorage.
bl_material_from_maps:
Wire a Blender material's Principled inputs from texture files, each map given a role and the channel it is read from - a packed ORM split back to three maps, a DirectX normal's green flipped. See mif_help.

maps is [{file, role, channel?, directX?}]: role baseColor | normal | roughness | metallic | ao | alpha | emissive; channel RGB (the colour roles' default and only value) or R | G | B | A (a scalar role's, default R); directX (normal only) says the file is DirectX-convention (green down) and its green is inverted to Blender's OpenGL. Each map is written as its own PNG under <folder>/<material>/ - a scalar read from one channel split out to grayscale, a flipped normal re-written, anything else copied - and the folder is wired with bl_import_pbr_texture_set: sRGB for base colour and emission only, Non-Color for the rest, the normal through a Normal Map node, AO multiplied into the base colour. A role given twice, a file that is missing or a channel the image does not have is refused before anything is written. The reply lists every written file with how it was made and its channel means, and the wiring. mif_send_to_blender materials=True calls it with an Unreal material's textures.
bl_mesh_filter:
A whole-mesh sculpt filter on a Blender mesh in mesh space - smooth, surface smooth, inflate, scale, sphere, random, relax, relax face sets, sharpen, enhance details - the sculpt mask protecting what it covers. See mif_help. strength is 0-1 (default 0.5) and iterations 1-200 (default 1); use_mask (default true) weights each move by 1 minus the sculpt mask; vertex_group further weights it by that group's weight; center is the [x, y, z] local point SCALE and SPHERE work from (default the bounding box center); shape_preservation and current_vertex are SURFACE_SMOOTH's alpha and beta, 0-1, default 0.5 each.

filter: SMOOTH (toward the neighbours' mean), SURFACE_SMOOTH (the HC Laplacian: shape_preservation alpha and current_vertex beta, 0-1, default 0.5 each, Blender's names), INFLATE (along the vertex normal, strength x the mean edge length), SCALE (out from center, default the bounding box's), SPHERE (toward the sphere of the mean radius), RANDOM (along the normal by a random amount, seed), RELAX (the smoothing move with its normal part removed: spacing evens out, the surface stays), RELAX_FACE_SETS (RELAX on the vertices where face sets meet), SHARPEN (away from the neighbours' mean), ENHANCE_DETAILS (away from a smoothed copy). ERASE_DISPLACEMENT is refused: it erases toward a Multires level this filter does not have.

strength 0-1 (default 0.5), iterations 1-200 (default 1). Each vertex's move is weighted by 1 - the sculpt mask (use_mask, default true) and by vertex_group's weight when given. center is [x, y, z] local. Native in mesh space because Blender's sculpt.mesh_filter segfaults headless; shape keys and edit mode are refused. Reply: verticesMoved, maxDisplacement (world), boxBefore and boxAfter, masked.
bl_mesh_from_heightmap:
Build a Blender grid mesh from a 16-bit heightmap (.r16 or 16-bit PNG) at a stated cell size and height scale - an Unreal landscape as a surface. See mif_help. cell_size_y is the spacing in meters along -Y (default cell_size); mid_value (default 32768) is the sample value that sits at origin's height; origin [x, y, z] is the Blender world position in meters of sample (0, 0); collection names an existing collection to link the new object into (default the scene's root collection; an unknown name is refused before anything is made).

file is a .r16 / .raw (little-endian uint16, row-major, no header - width and height are required) or a 16-bit greyscale PNG (an 8-bit one is refused: 256 steps are not a heightmap). cell_size is the spacing in metres along X (Unreal's landscape scale.x / 100), cell_size_y along -Y (default cell_size); height_scale is metres per height unit (Unreal's scale.z / 128 / 100); mid_value (default 32768) is the sample value that sits at origin's height; origin [x, y, z] is Blender world metres of sample (0, 0). Vertex (i, j) sits at origin + (i x cell_size, -j x cell_size_y, (v - mid_value) x height_scale) - Unreal's +Y is Blender's -Y. The reply carries the object, the vertex and face counts, the height range, the raw value range, the world box and the mapping in words. Over 16.7 million samples is refused. mif_send_landscape_to_blender reads a landscape's own numbers and calls this.
bl_sculpt_mask:
Make, change or read a Blender mesh's sculpt mask by rule - from cavity, the boundary, a vertex group (or into one), an expand from a vertex, a filter (smooth, grow, shrink, contrast), invert, set, clear; masked count and stats before and after. See mif_help. mode is FROM_CAVITY, FROM_BOUNDARY, FROM_VERTEX_GROUP, TO_VERTEX_GROUP, EXPAND, FILTER, INVERT, CLEAR, SET or READ (nothing written); combine (REPLACE default, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, MAX, MIN) merges a FROM_* or EXPAND result into the existing mask; value (0-1) is what SET writes everywhere; steps (edge rings, 1-1000, default 1) is FROM_BOUNDARY's width; EXPAND starts at vertex or the vertex nearest near ([x, y, z] world) and reaches radius (edge steps for by TOPOLOGY, meters for GEODESIC; required, above 0); falloff (LINEAR default, CONSTANT, SMOOTH) shapes FROM_BOUNDARY and EXPAND; iterations (1-100, default 1) repeats a FILTER; min_weight (default 0) keeps TO_VERTEX_GROUP from adding vertices whose mask is not above it.

Computed in mesh space, so it runs headless and the same on every build; the mask is written where the build keeps it (Mesh.vertex_paint_masks on 3.6, the .sculpt_mask point attribute from 4.2 - storage in the reply), and sculpt mode is left and re-entered around the write. Edit mode is refused.

mode: FROM_CAVITY (cavity {blurIterations 0-40 default 2, contrast 0.1-10 default 1}: 1 in crevices, from the Dirty Vertex Colors angle measure, normalized); FROM_BOUNDARY (boundary MESH, the open edges, or FACE_SETS, where face sets meet; steps edge rings, default 1; falloff LINEAR default, CONSTANT or SMOOTH); FROM_VERTEX_GROUP (group's weights); TO_VERTEX_GROUP (the mask written into group, made when missing; min_weight leaves lower vertices out; the mask itself is unchanged); EXPAND (from vertex, an index, or near, [x, y, z] world - the nearest vertex; by TOPOLOGY edge steps, default, or GEODESIC world distance along edges; radius in steps or meters; falloff); FILTER (filter SMOOTH, SHARPEN, GROW, SHRINK, CONTRAST_INCREASE or CONTRAST_DECREASE, iterations 1-100); INVERT; CLEAR; SET (value 0-1 everywhere); READ (nothing written).

combine says how a FROM_* or EXPAND result meets the mask there: REPLACE (default), ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, MAX, MIN; invert inverts the computed result first. Reply: before and after - vertices, masked (0.5 or more), partly (above 0, under 0.5), min, max, mean - storage and readBackMatches.
bl_set_camera_display:
What a Blender camera's VIEW shows - passepartout, composition guides, safe areas and background images (a reference plate behind a matchmove camera). None of it changes a render. guides {thirds: true, ...} by this Blender's names; safe_area_margins {title, action, titleCenter, actionCenter: [x, y]} is a scene setting; background_images [{image | imageName | movie | movieName, alpha, depth, frameMethod, offset, rotation, scale, flipX, flipY, show}] are appended (clear_background_images empties the list first). Every value is read back in display; only object is the read.

What each setting is: passepartout darkens the view outside the camera frame (passepartout_alpha 0..1, how much). guides turns the camera's composition guides on or off by the names this Blender gives them - the show_composition_<name> settings, read off the camera type, so a refusal lists exactly the ones this version has (thirds, center, center_diagonal, golden, golden_tria_a, golden_tria_b, harmony_tri_a, harmony_tri_b on current builds); guides not named keep their state. safe_areas and safe_center draw the title/action safe areas and the center-cut ones; their margins (fractions of the frame, 0..1) live on the SCENE, so every camera shares them. show_limits, show_mist, show_name, show_sensor and display_size are the camera's other viewport overlays.

Background images: each entry names one source - image (a file path, loaded once; an image already loaded from that file is reused) or imageName (an image already in the file), movie (a video file) or movieName (a movie clip already in the file) - and optionally alpha (0..1), depth (BACK or FRONT), frameMethod (STRETCH, FIT or CROP), offset [x, y], rotation (radians), scale (> 0), flipX, flipY and show. Entries are APPENDED; adding any turns show_background_images on unless that is passed too. loaded names the image or clip datablocks this call created.

Every check runs before anything is written, and a file Blender cannot load is unloaded again, so a refusal leaves the file as it was. The response carries display (the whole read-back), changedFields and changedAnything.
bl_set_stereo:
Stereoscopic and multiview rendering in Blender: on or off, stereo or multiview, how the views are written, and the camera's convergence, interocular distance and pivot - read back. See mif_help. enabled sets RenderSettings.use_multiview; views_format is STEREO_3D or MULTIVIEW; output is INDIVIDUAL or STEREO_3D; display_mode (ANAGLYPH, INTERLACE, SIDEBYSIDE, TOPBOTTOM) is the single-file stereo layout; convergence_mode (OFFAXIS, PARALLEL, TOE) and convergence_distance (metres, 0 or more) set the camera's stereo, refused when the scene has no camera and none is named; every enum is checked against this build's list, case-insensitively, before anything is written.

enabled: RenderSettings.use_multiview. views_format: STEREO_3D (the left and right views) or MULTIVIEW (the views list; views {name: true | false} turns render views on or off). output: INDIVIDUAL (a file per view) or STEREO_3D (one file in display_mode: ANAGLYPH, INTERLACE, SIDEBYSIDE or TOPBOTTOM). camera (default the scene camera): convergence_mode OFFAXIS, PARALLEL or TOE, interocular_distance and convergence_distance in metres, pivot LEFT, RIGHT or CENTER. Every enum is checked against this build's own list before anything is written; with nothing to set the call reads. before and after hold the state, with a warning when STEREO_3D is on and the left or right view is off.
bl_smooth_vertices:
Smooth a region of a Blender mesh - vertices, a vertex group or all - by iterations and factor along chosen axes, boundary kept, optionally Laplacian; displacement read back. See mif_help. min_weight is the vertex_group weight a vertex must exceed to be smoothed (default 0); keep_boundary (default true) leaves open-boundary vertices in place; preserve_volume (default true) is only accepted with laplacian=true.

vertices [indices], or vertex_group (vertices with weight above min_weight, default 0), or every vertex. iterations 1-500 (default 1) of bmesh's smooth_vert at factor 0-1 (default 0.5), moving only along axes ('XYZ' default, any of its letters). keep_boundary (default true) leaves open-boundary vertices where they are (boundaryKept counts them). laplacian=true uses smooth_laplacian_vert instead, with preserve_volume (default true). Shape keys and edit mode are refused. Reply: verticesChosen, verticesMoved, maxDisplacement (world units), boundaryKept, and a warning when nothing moved.
bl_symmetrize_mesh:
Report where a Blender mesh is not symmetric (vertices with no mirror partner), snap near pairs to exact symmetry, or symmetrize one side onto the other. See mif_help. mode is REPORT (default, writes nothing), SNAP or SYMMETRIZE about the object's local axis plane (axis X default, Y or Z); threshold (default 0.0001 local units) is the partner distance; factor (0-1, default 1) is how far SNAP moves each pair; direction (NEGATIVE_X default for X, or POSITIVE_X, and the Y / Z forms) picks which half SYMMETRIZE keeps and mirrors.

mode REPORT (default, writes nothing), SNAP or SYMMETRIZE, about the object's own axis plane through its origin (axis X default, Y or Z), in local space. threshold (default 0.0001 local units) is the largest distance at which a vertex and the mirror of another are partners, and a vertex that close to the plane is a center vertex. REPORT answers pairs, centers, unmatched and unmatchedVertices (limit, default 100) and symmetric. SNAP moves each pair to exact mirror positions by factor (0-1, default 1) and center vertices onto the plane - a wider threshold catches near pairs. SYMMETRIZE copies one half onto the other with bmesh's symmetrize: direction NEGATIVE_X (default for X: the -X half is kept and mirrored onto +X) or POSITIVE_X (and Y / Z); it cuts new vertices where edges cross the plane, and counts before and after are in the reply. Shape keys are refused for SNAP and SYMMETRIZE.
bl_trace_image_to_strokes:
Trace a black-and-white image - a logo, a sketch, a scan - into a new Blender Grease Pencil object's strokes with Blender's own trace, optionally converted to a mesh. See mif_help. threshold (0-1, default 0.5) is the black/white cut; turn_policy (default MINORITY) is FOREGROUND, BACKGROUND, LEFT, RIGHT, MINORITY, MAJORITY or RANDOM, with the pre-4.3 names BLACK and WHITE accepted; frame is the keyframe written (default the scene's current frame); thickness (pixels) and resolution pass to the pre-4.3 trace only and are refused on Blender 4.3+; convert_to accepts only MESH, converts a copy after the trace (the Grease Pencil object is kept) and is refused before 4.3.

image (a name in this file) or file (a path, loaded for the trace). Blender's trace runs on a temporary image Empty, removed after: gpencil.trace_image on 3.6 and 4.2 (4.2 has it although its UI does not list it), grease_pencil.trace_image from 4.3 - measured headless on 3.6, 4.2, 4.4 and 5.2. threshold 0-1 (default 0.5); turn_policy FOREGROUND, BACKGROUND, LEFT, RIGHT, MINORITY (default), MAJORITY or RANDOM (BLACK and WHITE, the pre-4.3 names, map across); frame the keyframe written (default the scene's); thickness (pixels) and resolution exist only on 3.6 / 4.2 and are refused from 4.3. name renames the new object. convert_to MESH converts the result with bl_convert_object, from 4.3 only (object.convert makes nothing from a Grease Pencil on 3.6, and no CURVE on any build measured) - refused before the trace otherwise. A blank image traces to nothing and is refused. Reply: object, generation, strokes, points, operator, layers, converted.
bl_uv_stitch:
Stitch two Blender UV islands along their shared edges (the second fitted onto the first), weld UVs, or merge them by distance; split edges and islands before and after. See mif_help. mode is STITCH (default), WELD or MERGE_BY_DISTANCE; faces [face indices] picks the islands those faces belong to, in place of islands (not both; WELD and MERGE_BY_DISTANCE default to every island); threshold is MERGE_BY_DISTANCE's UV distance (default 0.0001, 0 or more) and refused in the other modes; uv_layer names the UV map (default the active one).

mode STITCH (default): islands [kept, moved] (uv_info islands:true lists them; faces picks islands too). The moved island gets the best-fit similarity - a turn, a uniform scale and a shift, least squares through the mesh vertices the two islands share - that puts its shared UVs on the kept island's, and the shared UVs are then made one; the islands must share at least one mesh edge. The reply gives kept, moved, sharedVertices, scale and turnDegrees. WELD: at each mesh vertex of the chosen faces (default all) the UVs are set to their mean - every split at those vertices is closed. MERGE_BY_DISTANCE: at each vertex, UVs closer than threshold (default 0.0001, in UV units) become one. Every mode answers splitEdges and splitLength (world) - the mesh edges whose two faces' UVs differ - and islandCount, before and after. The data route, headless on every build; Blender's uv.stitch, uv.weld and uv.remove_doubles need the UV editor.
bl_add_accessory_physics:
Simulate a Blender chain, necklace or lace through a low-poly cage: built round it, pinned near points or where it rests on the body, run as cloth with the body colliding; the accessory follows by a bound Surface Deform.

WHY (2026-10-06): a cage along the chain, run as cloth with pins where it rests on the body, drives the detailed accessory through a Surface Deform; each piece existed (bl_add_cloth, bl_set_vertex_weights, bl_add_collision, bl_bind_modifier) and nothing built the cage. The cage is the accessory's base mesh pushed margin (default half of cage_density) out along its normals and voxel-remeshed at cage_density (world units, default 0.02): one closed shell that fuses the links. Pins (vertex group group, default Pin): cage vertices within pin_radius (default 1.5 x cage_density) of a pin_near point and/or within pin_within of the body's surface. The accessory gets a Surface Deform (CageDeform) bound at rest, then the cage gets cloth (cloth takes bl_add_cloth's settings, preset among them) pinned by the group; the body and each collision_with object (another chain's cage) get a Collision modifier where they have none. Drive it with bl_step_simulation on the cage. Reply: cage {name, vertices, faces, voxelSize, margin}, pins {count, perPoint, byBody}, cloth, deform {bound}, collisions. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a 768-vertex necklace's cage is one closed shell; stepped 12 frames its front falls more than 5 cm while the vertices by the pin move under 5 mm. Refused with nothing left behind (a cage built before a refusal is removed): no pin, a pin point out of reach, a cage holding no pin or empty, a taken name, an accessory already on a Surface Deform, a cloth setting bl_add_cloth refuses.
bl_add_cloth:
Add a cloth simulation to a Blender mesh (refused under 16 vertices). preset COTTON/DENIM/LEATHER/RUBBER/SILK from the build's own files, or FLEECE/CANVAS; bending springs; pin_group pins; pressure_group scales pressure by region.

WHY (2026-10-06): bending - the setting that decides whether a hood stands - was not a key, and Blender's cloth presets are scripts that run only inside the Properties panel. Cloth deforms the geometry it is given and a quad has nothing to bend, so subdivide first. preset reads the running build's presets/cloth file and sets it field by field; FLEECE and CANVAS are MifBridge's own starting points, not measured fabrics. Explicit keys win over the preset; the reply's preset {name, source, values, overridden, storedDifferently} lists what is in effect. On 5.0 and later the build's presets turn pressure off and leave uniform_pressure_force at 76.0, and presetPressureNote says so. bending, bending_damping, bending_model ANGULAR or LINEAR, bending_group and bending_max set the bending springs. pin_group names a vertex group (make it with bl_set_vertex_weights) whose vertices hold the cloth in place, with pin_stiffness. An explicit use_pressure beats pressure. pressure_group scales pressure 0-1 by vertex and pressure_factor scales it overall; pressure is one value per object, so a two-layer garment pushed apart by pressure is a lining joined at the rims into one closed shell (bl_add_inner_layer join RIM) - pressureLayersNote says so. bl_physics_info reads every one of these back. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: DENIM with bending 12 reads back bending 12 and the rest of Denim. Refused, with nothing added: an unknown preset (the reply lists this build's), a bad bending_model, a negative or non-finite value, an unknown vertex group, a second cloth modifier.
bl_add_constraint:
Add an object or bone constraint in Blender, and MEASURE that it moves the thing. Constraints are how camera and light rigs are actually built - a Track To on an empty stays correct as the target moves, which a one-shot bl_aim_object cannot - and nothing here could create one. THE MEASUREMENT IS THE DESIGN: a constraint does NOT touch obj.matrix_world, it is applied by the depsgraph at evaluation, so reading the object's own transform reports no change for every constraint that works perfectly. This samples the EVALUATED world matrix before and after and reports movedDistance and turnedRadians. hadEffect false is not automatically wrong - a Copy Location onto something already in place moves nothing - so read it beside isValid: valid and inert means nothing to do, INVALID and inert means a target that does not resolve. Call mif_help("bl_add_constraint") first.

THE CONSTRAINT'S OWN NAME IS constraint_name. name is an alias for object on every op here, so object and name given with different values are refused as two names for one parameter, and name alone is read as the object.

A constraint type that takes no target is refused rather than given one, and the constraint is removed again before the refusal so a rejected call leaves no stack entry behind.

SUBTARGET CHECKED (2026-10-05): subtarget is a bone on an ARMATURE target or a vertex group on a MESH or LATTICE target, and a name the target lacks is refused listing what it has - a misspelled group used to be stored, the constraint read valid and the object sat at the target's origin. Any other target type, or a subtarget with no target, is refused. The reply's constraint carries subtargetKind (bone or vertexGroup).

WALKING ALONG A PATH, TWO WAYS (2026-10-11): FOLLOW_PATH with a keyed evaluation time (the character cycles in place) against copying the planted foot's travel to the root with a Cycles modifier repeating with offset. The second locks the feet; the first says nothing about slide - measure the planted foot's world position over its contact frames with bl_evaluate_at_frame. A path's default duration is 100 frames (3.6 and 4.4.0), so the evaluation-time key must run to the duration the path really has, not to the scene's end.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): COPY_LOCATION with target a mesh and subtarget one of its vertex groups puts the owner on the group's centre on the EVALUATED mesh (a Shrinkwrap under it included) at every frame; CHILD_OF with a vertex group carries the owner with the group's motion, rotation included, from where it was when added (movedDistance 0 then: Blender sets the parent inverse). A misspelled group is refused naming the groups there are (Blender would store it and follow the target's origin, still reading valid). GEOMETRY_ATTRIBUTE (5.0+, refused before by name): set attribute_name, data_type, domain and sample_index with bl_set_constraint; read back with bl_list_constraints rna, and the owner moves to that sample.
bl_add_driver:
Drive a Blender property (data_path, index for one element) with an expression over variables [{name, object, dataPath}], and prove the driver actually EVALUATES. Drivers are the one animation feature that fails completely silently: a broken expression, or a variable pointing at an object that no longer exists, stays in place and evaluates to ZERO - nothing errors, nothing warns, and every field a caller can read looks perfectly correct. Blender shows it as a coloured field in the UI and reports it nowhere else. So this refuses a data_path that does not resolve (Blender would create the driver permanently invalid), refuses a variable whose target object does not exist, refuses a second driver on a path that already has one, and reports isValid plus the driven property read back through the depsgraph. Read them back with bl_list_animation_data. Call mif_help("bl_add_driver") first.

Each variable becomes a SINGLE_PROP driver variable, and the default expression is simply the first variable.

valueAfterEvaluated is the driven property read back through the depsgraph and isValid is Blender's own verdict. A driver that exists and evaluates to nothing is the normal failure, identical to a working one in every other field. bl_list_animation_data reports each driver's validity and variable targets.

VARIABLE TYPES: a variable {type TRANSFORMS, object, bone, transformType LOC_X ... ROT_X ... SCALE_AVG, rotationMode, space WORLD_SPACE | TRANSFORM_SPACE | LOCAL_SPACE} reads the EVALUATED channel - a helper bone turned 30 degrees by a Copy Rotation reads 0 through a SINGLE_PROP rotation_euler and 0.523599 through TRANSFORMS, which is why a corrective reads TRANSFORMS. LOC_DIFF and ROTATION_DIFF take object, bone, object2, bone2. driver_type SCRIPTED (default) | SUM | AVERAGE | MIN | MAX; only SCRIPTED takes an expression. RESPONSE CURVE: curve {points [{x, y, handle}], extrapolation CONSTANT | LINEAR} replaces the driver curve's Generator and its default keys with these keys; map_range {inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax, clamp (true)} is the straight-line case - radians in, 0 to exactly 1 out. The reply evaluates the curve at its first, middle and last input.
bl_add_dynamic_paint:
Make a Blender mesh a dynamic paint CANVAS or BRUSH - wetmaps, footprints in snow, weathering, anything where one object marks another. The last of the modifier types this addon could add and not configure: like FLUID it sits in _SIM_MODIFIERS so bake_physics and physics_info always handled one, and its modifier carries exactly ONE writable property, ui_type, with everything real on canvas_settings or brush_settings. ui_type ALONE DOES NOTHING - setting it leaves those settings None on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.0 alike, so a modifier that looks configured in the outliner can have no settings at all; the settings are created by an operator, which this runs for you. A CANVAS ARRIVES WITH ONE SURFACE and this configures that one - several surfaces on a canvas is a real setup and is not built here, so the count does not depend on how often you called this. surface_type IS A DYNAMIC ENUM whose members depend on the surface FORMAT, so it is validated against Blender at the moment of writing and a refusal names what is available NOW - which is the only correct answer to 'why can I not set WAVE'. Format is applied before type for the same reason. A setting sent to the wrong role is refused naming the role that owns it: a canvas receives paint and a brush applies it. Nothing is baked.

PARAMETERS. name (string, default "Dynamic Paint"): the new modifier's name. CANVAS-only settings, written to the canvas's one surface: surface_format (string, read from the build's enum, for example VERTEX or IMAGE) is applied before surface_type; frame_start, frame_end (whole numbers) set the surface's frame range; use_dissolve (bool) and dissolve_speed (whole number, frames) fade the paint away over time. BRUSH-only settings: paint_color ([r, g, b], at least three finite numbers; only the first three are written), paint_alpha (float), paint_wetness (float), paint_source (string, read from the build's enum; checked by assigning it), paint_distance (float), use_absolute_alpha (bool). All default to unset, which leaves Blender's own value.

OUT: object, modifier, paintType (CANVAS or BRUSH, read from which settings exist), bakeNote. A canvas adds surface, surfaceType, surfaceFormat, frameStart, frameEnd, useDissolve, dissolveSpeed, surfaceCount, surfaceNote. A brush adds paintSource, paintColor, paintAlpha, paintWetness, paintDistance, useAbsoluteAlpha. All values are read back off the settings.

REFUSED, with nothing changed: a type other than CANVAS or BRUSH; a setting that belongs to the other role (named with its owner); an object that already has a dynamic paint modifier; a paint_color with fewer than three numbers; a non-numeric or fractional frame or speed. Refused after the modifier was made, which is then removed: the toggle operator failing, the toggle leaving no settings, a canvas with no active surface, and an enum value Blender refuses or reads back differently ("NOTHING was created").
bl_add_fcurve_modifier:
Put a modifier on a Blender curve - most usefully CYCLES, which is how an animation LOOPS. There was no way to loop anything: every turntable, idle, cycling fan and blinking light had to be keyed out to full length by hand, and a two-key rotation could not be made to repeat at all. A CYCLES modifier on a curve with fewer than two keyframes is REFUSED, because there is no cycle to repeat and Blender adds the modifier anyway and does nothing with it, which looks like success. Every other type is configured through settings - any writable property of that type by Blender's own name (LIMITS use_max_y + max_y, STEPPED frame_step, GENERATOR poly_order + coefficients, FNGENERATOR function_type + amplitude, SMOOTH sigma + filter_width on 5.2), checked against this Blender before anything is added; an out-of-range value is refused rather than clamped - and an ENVELOPE takes control_points [{frame, min, max}]. The response counts modifiers off the curves before and after, reads each setting back off the modifier, and samples the curve before and after: noEffect is true, with a note saying why, when the modifier changed nothing - a LIMITS with no bound enabled and an ENVELOPE with no points both do exactly that. To prove a loop is live, sample past the last key with bl_evaluate_at_frame. Call mif_help("bl_add_fcurve_modifier") first.

MEASURED 2026-10-05: all true with type CYCLES on a 30-bone rig keyed 0 to 0.2 over frames 1-24 (one location channel per bone) added 30 modifiers - one per curve - and changed 600 of 750 sampled frames, on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1 alike.

Put a modifier on a Blender curve - most usefully CYCLES, which is how an animation LOOPS. There was no way to loop anything: every turntable, idle, cycling fan and blinking light had to be keyed out to full length by hand, and a two-key rotation could not be made to repeat at all. A CYCLES modifier on a curve with fewer than two keyframes is REFUSED, because there is no cycle to repeat and Blender adds the modifier anyway and does nothing with it, which looks like success. Every other type is configured through settings - any writable property of that type by Blender's own name (LIMITS use_max_y + max_y, STEPPED frame_step, GENERATOR poly_order + coefficients, FNGENERATOR function_type + amplitude, SMOOTH sigma + filter_width on 5.2), checked against this Blender before anything is added; an out-of-range value is refused rather than clamped - and an ENVELOPE takes control_points [{frame, min, max}]. The response counts modifiers off the curves before and after, reads each setting back off the modifier, and samples the curve before and after: noEffect is true, with a note saying why, when the modifier changed nothing - a LIMITS with no bound enabled and an ENVELOPE with no points both do exactly that. To prove a loop is live, sample past the last key with bl_evaluate_at_frame.

There was no way to loop anything through this addon. Every turntable, idle, cycling fan and blinking light had to be keyed out to its full length by hand, and a two-key rotation could not be made to repeat at all. Blender has had this forever; the bridge simply never exposed it.

A CYCLES modifier on a curve with FEWER THAN TWO keyframes is refused. There is no cycle to repeat, and Blender will add the modifier anyway and do nothing with it - which looks exactly like success and is the failure this op exists to prevent.

modeBefore and modeAfter (NONE / REPEAT / REPEAT_OFFSET / MIRROR) are CYCLES-only and are refused on any other type rather than ignored. REPEAT_OFFSET is the one you want for a walk cycle or anything that should accumulate rather than snap back.

EVERY OTHER TYPE IS CONFIGURED THROUGH settings: any writable property of that type, by Blender's own name - LIMITS use_min_y / use_max_y / min_y / max_y, STEPPED frame_step / frame_offset, GENERATOR poly_order / coefficients (poly_order is written first, since it decides how many coefficients there are), FNGENERATOR function_type / amplitude, NOISE depth / phase, SMOOTH sigma / filter_width (5.2), and on every type mute, influence and the restricted range. Each key is checked against THIS Blender before anything is added: an unknown name is refused with the writable list, and an out-of-range value is refused rather than clamped - Blender clamps cycles_before 1000000 to 32767 without a word. An ENVELOPE takes controlPoints [{frame, min, max}]; one point per frame. strength / scale are NOISE-only and refused on any other type. If Blender itself rejects a combination after the modifier exists (coefficients the wrong length), what this call added is removed again.

EACH SETTING IS READ BACK OFF THE MODIFIER (modifiersAdded[].settings / controlPoints).

Modifiers are COUNTED off the curves before and after, because fcurve.modifiers.new returns an object whether or not it stuck. countsAgree is that arithmetic checked rather than asserted.

WHAT IT DID TO THE CURVE IS SAMPLED: effect {sampledFrames, framesChanged, maxChange} compares the curve across its keyed range and one range either side, before and after. noEffect is true, with noEffectNote saying why, when nothing changed - a LIMITS with no bound enabled and an ENVELOPE with no control points both do exactly that, and both used to report countsAgree true.

A MODIFIER EXISTING IS NOT THE SAME AS IT HAVING AN EFFECT. To prove a loop is live, sample past the last keyframe with bl_evaluate_at_frame - that reads through the depsgraph, so it sees the modifier where every raw property read does not.

MANY CURVES IN ONE CALL (2026-10-04): data_path is optional - bones [names] or all=true instead adds the same modifier (type, modes, settings) to every matching curve of the object's action, or of the action named by `action`: a CYCLES on every curve of a 30-bone walk is one call where it was dozens. In that form a curve with fewer than two keys is skipped for CYCLES (skipped.fewerThanTwoKeys) and a curve that already carries a modifier of that type is skipped (skipped.alreadyHasOne), and the call is refused only when no curve is left; curvesChanged lists the curves written. Measured: 58 curves of a 6-bone rig keyed at 1 and 25 all took a CYCLES, and frame 37 evaluated as frame 13. data_path with bones or all, bones with all, a bone no curve animates and an action that does not exist are refused.

driver true puts the modifier on the driver of the driven property data_path (not with bones or all) - a LIMITS max_y caps a driven value. remove ALL | FIRST | a type (2026-10-06) removes instead, over the same curves, and takes no type; stack_index puts the new modifier at that place in the stack (the stack rebuilt with every setting kept; before 5.2 a CYCLES must stay first and such a stack is refused with every curve put back).

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): NOISE takes lacunarity, roughness and use_legacy_noise on 4.4+ (refused by name on 3.6 and 4.2) and changes every sampled frame; SMOOTH is a 5.2 type (refused before) and goes on top of the stack (stackIndex after the existing ones); on a straight two-key line it changes nothing, as it should.
bl_convert_object:
Convert a Blender object to another type - a curve or text to a MESH, a mesh to a CURVE - with its WHOLE modifier stack baked in. Target HAIR_PARTICLES or HAIR_CURVES converts hair between Curves and a particle system. Call mif_help("bl_convert_object") first.

This is how a modifier on a curve or text gets applied at all: Blender refuses a constructive modifier on a curve until it is converted. In place (the default) the same object keeps its name, parent, children and material slots, the stack is emptied, and every other object sharing its data converts too (named in alsoConverted); keep_original leaves it untouched and returns the new object's name in `created`. A mesh converted to MESH applies its entire stack. target is read off Blender's own list (MESH, CURVE, CURVES, and GPENCIL on 3.6-4.2 / GREASEPENCIL from 4.4, POINTCLOUD from 5.0). bakedMatchesEvaluated compares the real mesh with what the stack evaluated to before. No undo through the bridge. Converting in place REFUSES, before changing anything, when the object's Geometry Nodes tree draws instances or it has particle systems: the conversion keeps only the evaluated mesh and destroys them (measured on 3.6-5.2). Pass keep_original to convert a copy (copyLacks says what it lacks) or drop_instances to convert anyway (droppedInstances / droppedParticleSystems). An Armature modifier is baked in the pose its rig holds now, so a mesh whose rig is not at rest is refused unless pose says which: 'rest' converts in the rest position and puts the rig back, 'current' bakes the pose as it stands (posedRigs names each rig and how many bones moved).

HAIR, BETWEEN ITS TWO SYSTEMS (2026-10-06), through Blender's curves.convert_to_particle_system and curves.convert_from_particle_system; the source is always kept, so keep_original, drop_instances and pose are refused with these targets. HAIR_PARTICLES takes a CURVES object whose Curves.surface is a mesh (refused without one) and makes a hair particle system on that surface named after the Curves object, one strand per STORED curve: a fur object's guides, not the curves its modifiers evaluate to (evaluatedNote says so). A system of that name already on the surface is REWRITTEN in place (updatedExisting true). The reply gives strands, keysPerStrand, guideCurves, evaluatedCurves and strandsBelowSurface - strands with a point under the surface, against its normal (inside a closed mesh). HAIR_CURVES takes a mesh and its hair system (particle_system, default the active one; an emitter system is refused) and makes a new Curves object named after the system, at the emitter's world matrix and not parented; the bridge sets its Curves.surface to the mesh (Blender leaves it unset) so it can go back. Points follow the system's display path (2^display_step + 1 per strand), not its hair keys, and a system with interpolated children converts to one curve per CHILD, parents dropped (childrenNote). Measured the same on 3.6, 4.2, 4.4, 5.0 and 5.2.
bl_copy_keyframes:
Copy Blender keys with their handles to another frame, channel or object - repeated, value-scaled about a pivot, or flipped onto the other side; reports the evaluated difference.

Copy Blender keys with their handles: from_range {frameStart, frameEnd} to {frame | offset}, onto to_data_path or to_object, repeated, value-scaled about a pivot, or flipped onto the other side's bones; reports the evaluated difference.

WHY: bl_move_keyframes shifts or scales the TIME of keys, bl_edit_fcurve changes how a curve moves between them and bl_set_keyframe writes one value: nothing copied keys, scaled or offset their values, or pasted them flipped. Blender's graph.copy / graph.paste need a Graph Editor, so this is native and works on the curves of 5.x slotted actions too; settled 2026-10-18 on 3.6.23-5.2.1 against graph.copy and graph.paste(flipped) run under a Graph Editor override, the flipped keys are the same. SOURCE: data_paths ['location', 'location[1]', 'pose.bones["arm.L"].rotation_quaternion'] | bones [names] | all, narrowed by index, keys inside from_range (default every key). DESTINATION: to {frame: n} puts the first copied key at n, {offset: n} shifts by n; to_object (default the same object) and to_data_path ('location[1]' - one destination, so the selection must be one path) send the keys elsewhere; flip with name_rule (FLIP_NAME, a suffix pair or a table, as bl_copy_pose) writes each bone's curves onto its partner's with Blender's paste-flipped signs (location x, euler Y and Z, quaternion y and z negated); a curve that is not a bone's is copied without a swap and listed in notFlipped. repeat (1-100) pastes that many copies `period` frames apart (default the copied keys' span, so a loop's closing key lands on the next copy's first). merge is Blender's own paste merge enum read from the operator: MIX (default: keys added, one at the same frame replaced), OVER_ALL (the destination curve cleared first), OVER_RANGE (its keys inside its pasted range removed), OVER_RANGE_ALL (inside the whole paste's range). VALUES: v' = pivot + (v - pivot) * value_scale + value_offset, pivot FIRST_KEY (each curve's first copied key, the default) or {value: v}; a key's handles go through the same transform, so a negative scale mirrors them. Every key keeps its interpolation, easing, handle types and the ELASTIC/BACK parameters. Destination curves (and an action) are made when missing - createdCurves. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: a planted foot's y (0 -> -1.8 over 0-18) onto a root's location[1] at value_scale -1 reads 0.9 at frame 9; a 3-key clip repeated 3 times at period 20 reads at 26 and 46 as at 6; check.maxDifference 0 - each destination curve is sampled at the pasted frames and between them against the source sampled BEFORE the write. Refused before anything is written: an euler path into a quaternion one (or any two properties of different kinds, both named), no to or both frame and offset, repeat outside 1-100, an unknown merge, flip without name_rule, to_data_path with several source paths, a range with no keys, an index past the destination's length, a curve or object that does not exist, two curves onto one.
bl_clean_keyframes:
Remove Blender keys whose removal moves the curve less than threshold, and/or make euler curves continuous (euler_filter true or 'ONLY'); reports keys before and after and the largest deviation.

WHY: nothing removed redundant keys or fixed rotation flips, and Blender's graph.clean and graph.euler_filter poll for a Graph Editor area, so both are native. The curve's first key always stays, as graph.clean keeps it (settled 2026-10-18 on 3.6.23-5.2.1 under a Graph Editor override: the same keys left on a curve with holds, a 0.0004 bump and a trailing hold). CLEAN: each key in range is tried without it, and stays out when the evaluated curve moves by less than threshold at every integer frame - measured against the curve as it was, so the error never adds up past threshold. threshold defaults to Blender's own (graph.clean's 0.001, read from the operator on each build). Measured: 21 LINEAR keys on a straight line keep the two ends with 0 deviation; a 0.0005 bump goes at 0.001 and stays at 0.0001. channels=true then removes a curve left with one key at its property's default (Blender's Clean Channels). EULER FILTER: on rotation_euler and delta_rotation_euler curves each key is shifted by whole turns so it lies within 180 degrees of the key before it, handles with it - measured 0, 170, -170, -100 degrees -> 0, 170, 190, 260, keysShifted 2, the largest key-to-key step 340 -> 170. It makes a curve continuous; it does not wrap it into 0-360, and a gimbal flip across all three axes is not what it fixes. euler_filter 'ONLY' runs the filter without the clean; true runs the filter then the clean. Selection as bl_copy_keyframes (data_paths | bones | all, index), frame_start / frame_end bound both. Reply per curve: keysBefore, keysAfter, maxDeviation, and keysShifted, maxStepBeforeDegrees, maxStepAfterDegrees for the filter. Refused, NOTHING changed: a negative threshold, an unknown euler_filter, 'ONLY' with threshold or channels, an end before the start, no selection, a path with no curve.
bl_add_modifier:
Add a modifier to a Blender object's stack - the write half of bl_list_modifiers. The response's facesFold is true when this modifier made faces fold over themselves (triangleOverlapAfter above 1.02: a render-only defect every count misses, typically a bevel wider than half a thin wall after a boolean - put a TRIANGULATE modifier before it). A mesh takes every type; a curve or text takes 28 (ARRAY, BEVEL, SOLIDIFY, SCREW, SUBSURF, WELD, SIMPLE_DEFORM, CAST and more, not the ones that need mesh data); a lattice only deforming ones; a Grease Pencil object the GREASE_PENCIL_* types and LINEART (GP_* on Blender 3.6 and 4.2). A type the object cannot take is refused naming its type. `settings` takes the curated camelCase names or any writable RNA property of the modifier by its identifier (foam_layer_name, limit_method, use_axis) - the path bl_set_modifier uses - and a setting that refuses removes the new modifier again. A SOLIDIFY that would make a second inward shell inside a closed mesh is refused, naming bl_transform_selection's SHRINK_FATTEN to grow it; hollow true keeps the cavity, for a wall to cut through or a shell to print.

The general form of edits this addon otherwise hardcodes one at a time: bl_decimate_mesh already builds, configures and applies a DECIMATE modifier internally, and this exposes the same mechanism for mirror, solidify, subsurf, weighted-normal and the rest. IT DOES NOT APPLY, on purpose - a modifier left in the stack still changes what bl_export_mesh writes (use_mesh_modifiers is on), so the caller may well want it live and unapplied; bl_apply_modifier is the separate destructive step. SETTINGS TAKE BOTH SPELLINGS (since 2026-09-21; they were curated-only before): the curated camelCase names - a handful per type, the ones that decide what an export produces, mirroring what bl_list_modifiers decodes on the read side - and any writable RNA property of the modifier by its identifier (foam_layer_name, limit_method, use_axis), validated exactly as bl_set_modifier validates them. A name the type does not have is REFUSED rather than silently ignored, and a modifier that fails partway through configuration is REMOVED again, because a half-configured modifier left in the stack silently changes every later export after the caller was told nothing changed. The response reads the modifier back through bl_list_modifiers' own describer, so a setting that did not take is visible rather than assumed from ok:true. Curves, point cloud and volume objects have modifier stacks too (2026-10-04): a Curves or point cloud object takes NODES (and MESH_SEQUENCE_CACHE from 4.2), a volume NODES, MESH_TO_VOLUME and VOLUME_DISPLACE. A grease-pencil modifier type on anything but grease pencil is refused: from 4.4 Blender accepts every GREASE_PENCIL_* type and LINEART on a volume, where it does nothing.

COPY A MODIFIER OR A WHOLE STACK (copy_from, to; 2026-10-05): copy_from {object, modifier: name | all: true} and to [objects] copies each modifier onto every target with every writable property, in the source's stack order (index puts the first copy there and the rest after it) - Copy to Selected without a context. No object_name, type, modifier or settings in this mode. Each target's row in targets names what was made, what was skipped and why - a vertex group or UV layer the target lacks, a pointer at the target itself, a custom bevel profile or falloff curve in use (their points are not copied) - and needsBind for SURFACE_DEFORM, MESH_DEFORM and LAPLACIANDEFORM copies (bl_bind_modifier binds each; a bind is data of its own object). A geometry-nodes modifier keeps its input values (id-properties up to 5.0, mod.properties.inputs on 5.2). Simulation types (cloth, soft body, collision, fluid, dynamic paint, particle system, particle instance, explode) are refused - each has its own op. Refused before any write: no to, the source among the targets, a target with no modifier stack, an unknown modifier, modifier with all. Any failure removes every copy made in the call. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a Bevel, Shrinkwrap and Array stack copied onto a twin cube evaluates to the source's vertex count and bounds.

RULE - MODIFIER ORDER FOR THICKNESS AND BEVELS (2026-10-06). Bevel then Solidify bevels the outline and thickens it, so the rim stays square; Solidify then Bevel bevels both skins and the rim (a 2 m plane, bevel 0.1 and thickness 0.2: 8 evaluated vertices at two heights against 24 at three - test_blender_workflow_rules R102, 4.2-5.2). A hard-surface panel is Mirror, Bevel, Solidify, Subdivision Surface; cloth is Mirror, Cloth, Subdivision Surface, then Solidify, so the thickness is added after the simulation and the subdivision. THE THICKNESS SIGN is decided by the normals, not by a recipe: thickness 0.2 at the default offset -1 grows the shell against the normal, thickness -0.2, or 0.2 with offset +1, grows it along the normal (R103). Probe after the apply with bl_ray_cast (evaluated true) down the normal: the first hit says which side the shell grew.
bl_quilt_surface:
Divide a Blender garment into quilted cells: seam loops cut every cell_height (BANDS) or as a GRID, pinched in, cells puffed out; seams and puff become vertex groups, and the cloth's pin and pressure groups when pressure is given.

WHY (2026-10-06): a puffer jacket's quilted cells - horizontal bands or a grid - are made by pinning or pinching seam lines and inflating each cell; vertex groups and cloth pressure existed, nothing divided the surface. Seams are cut as exact edge loops on world planes across axis (default Z) every cell_height from start (default one cell above the mesh's lowest point) and, for GRID, across across (default X) every cell_width (default cell_height) from start_across. Seam vertices go in group (default QuiltSeams, weight 1) and move pinch (world units) against their normal; every other vertex goes in puff_group (default QuiltPuff) at a dome weight (smoothstep of its distance to the nearest seam plane over half a cell: 0 at a seam, 1 mid-cell) and moves inflation x that weight along its normal. pressure, on an object with a cloth modifier (bl_add_cloth first), turns pressure on at that force scaled by puff_group, with the seams as the pin group (pin_seams, default true). Reply: seamPlanes, seamVertices, cellCount, cells [{faces, area}], cellsWithoutInterior (cells too coarse to puff, with coarseNote), puffWeightMax, groups, cloth. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a 0.2 m tube banded every 0.12 m with pinch 0.01 reads r 0.19 at a seam and above 0.2 mid-cell, six cells, still manifold. Refused, nothing changed: a bad mode, axis or size, no plane crossing the mesh, a group already on the object, pressure without a cloth modifier, cell_width on BANDS, shape keys.
bl_set_nla_track:
Mute, solo, lock, rename or remove an NLA track ("*": all). Solo silences every other track while each still reads mute:false - silencedBySolo names them.

Mute, SOLO, lock or rename an NLA track. bl_list_animation_data reported a track's mute and nothing could write it, so a track could be built and never silenced - that is the small half. THE LARGE HALF IS SOLO, AND THE READ SIDE WAS MISLEADING ABOUT IT: setting solo on one track silences every OTHER track's contribution while each of them still reports mute:false. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1 - two tracks moving a cube to z=-5 and z=+5, evaluated at frame 10, give -5 with both live and +5 with the first soloed, and nothing on the second track says why it stopped contributing. So a caller reading every track, seeing every one unmuted, and asking why only one plays had no field that could answer. isSolo is now reported per track, and this op names the soloed track and lists silencedBySolo. Solo is EXCLUSIVE and Blender clears it on the others itself, so the response reports which track ended up soloed rather than assuming it is this one. REMOVAL (2026-10-06): a rig's leftover tracks were removed before an export in raw Python. remove true deletes the track named in track with its strips; with track "*" every track on the object. The active action is kept, and the reply lists each removed track with its strips, tracksLeft and activeAction, with a note when nothing animates the object any more. Refused: remove with mute, solo, lock or rename; remove with no track, or with "*" on an object with no tracks; an unknown track name (the tracks present are named).
bl_add_nla_strip:
Put an action on an NLA track as a strip - how several clips live on one Blender object. An object holds ONE active action at a time; the NLA is how a walk, an idle and a wave coexist on the same rig, how they blend, and what glTF reads to export multiple clips. THE TRAP IS THAT THE ACTIVE ACTION SHADOWS THE WHOLE STACK: Blender evaluates animation_data.action ON TOP of the NLA, so an object with an active action set plays that and every strip below contributes nothing while the stack reads as perfectly correct. activeActionShadowsNla reports it, and push_down_active moves the active action onto its own track first - what the UI's Push Down button does. Overlapping strips on one track are refused by Blender and the message says so. Read the result back with bl_list_animation_data. INFLUENCE IS ANIMATED OR IGNORED: Blender plays a strip at full strength unless its animated influence is on, so passing influence turns it on and keys the value (measured on every supported build: 0.5 plays at half; without the flag every value played the full action). The response and bl_list_animation_data report animatedInfluence and effectiveInfluence - what the strip plays at. With nothing beneath the strip, a partial influence blends every channel toward 0, not toward the object's own value - influenceNote says so when the strip lands on the bottom track.

An object holds ONE active action at a time. The NLA is how a walk, an idle and a wave coexist on the same rig, how they blend, and what glTF reads to export multiple clips. None of it was reachable.

THE TRAP IS THAT THE ACTIVE ACTION SHADOWS THE WHOLE STACK. Blender evaluates animation_data.action ON TOP of the entire NLA, so an object that still has an active action plays THAT and every strip below it contributes nothing - while the stack reads as perfectly correct from every field. activeActionShadowsNla reports whether you are in that state, and push_down_active moves the active action onto its own track first, which is exactly what the UIs Push Down button does.

Two strips cannot overlap on one track. Blender refuses it and the message says so rather than leaving a caller to wonder why a placement failed.

blend_type (REPLACE / ADD / SUBTRACT / MULTIPLY) is validated against this Blenders own enum. Read the result back with bl_list_animation_data, which reports every track and strip with its frame range. With nothing beneath the strip a partial influence blends every channel toward 0, not toward the object's own value: a z keyed 0.6 -> 2.6 plays 0.15 -> 0.65 at 0.25 (measured on every build, REPLACE and ADD alike). influenceNote says so when the new strip sits on the bottom track with an effective influence below 1.
bl_aim_object: Point a Blender object's local -Z axis - the way a light or camera faces - at an object (target) or a point (look_at [x,y,z]). Nothing could aim anything after creation - bl_create_camera took look_at at birth and that was the only user of the aiming maths, so a spot light could not be aimed at all. Pass exactly one of target (an object, aimed at its world origin) or look_at (a point). THE POSTCONDITION IS MEASURED, not assumed: it reports the ANGLE between the object's world-space local -Z and the direction to the target after the write, and refuses above ~1e-3 rad. That matters because the aiming derivation was once wrong by exactly pi - aiming 166 degrees off while returning a perfectly plausible euler - and reading back the euler you just wrote is a proxy that cannot catch it. Both, or neither, is refused. Blender aims down LOCAL -Z for lights and cameras alike.
bl_append_from_file:
Bring datablocks IN from another .blend - the half of the Blender file ops that did not exist. bl_save_file wrote and bl_open_file REPLACES the session, so a scene this addon built could be saved and then never reused; every asset-library workflow is this call. APPEND COPIES, LINK REFERENCES, and the difference decides whether you can edit what you just brought in: link=false (the default) copies the datablocks into this file - editable, and they survive the source being moved; link=true leaves them in the source file and points at it, which means NOT editable (a transform on a linked object is refused by Blender, and reads as this addon being broken if you did not know you linked) and the source must exist forever. The response says which happened and what it costs. list_only=true READS THE FILE AND IMPORTS NOTHING, so you can see what is in it before choosing names. A name the file does not contain is REFUSED naming what it does have - Blender's own append silently imports nothing for a missing name and reports no error, which is a call that succeeds and does nothing. Objects and collections are linked into the scene's active collection so they are actually VISIBLE: bpy.data.libraries.load puts them in bpy.data and nothing else, and an object in no collection is invisible, unrendered, and saved anyway. Colliding names get Blender's .001 suffix and the response reports every one under `renamed`, so you know what you actually have. FONTS ARE IN THE LIST because a typeface is the one thing you cannot re-derive from a file you did not build: bl_create_text's `font` takes a PATH, so text set in somebody else's face has no name you can reach - list_only:true now shows you. instance_empty=true (2026-10-06, with link) places each collection as an EMPTY instancing it - Blender's own File > Link default - instead of a child collection; instancers names each; bl_library_override MAKE replaces that empty with the override.

CHANGE CAP: it has no preview, so a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct data-blocks (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) is refused, writing nothing, and says to split it or have the user raise the cap (docs/15 section 6). link "PACKED" (5.0+, 2026-10-06) links and stores the linked data inside this file: not editable, and alive when the source file is moved; packed lists them. Refused by name before 5.0.
bl_apply_modifier:
Bake a modifier into a Blender mesh's data. Destructive, and it reports what that cost. THE COUNTS ARE THE POINT: Blender's modifier_apply returns FINISHED whether or not it changed the mesh, so a Mirror that doubled the geometry and a disabled modifier that did nothing are indistinguishable from the operator's return alone - this reads vertex and face counts before and after and reports both, plus changedGeometry, and says so in words when they are identical. REFUSES ON MULTI-USER MESH DATA for the same reason bl_apply_transform does: applying rewrites data other objects share, and refusing first with the sharing count is a better error than the one Blender's operator produces. dry_run reports what is on the stack and what applying would touch, and changes nothing. Pair with bl_list_modifiers to see the stack first - a Mirror or Subsurf still in it changes the exported geometry whether or not you meant it to. as_shape_key captures a deforming modifier's result as a new shape key instead of baking it (key_name names it, keep_modifier keeps the modifier on the stack) - refused with Blender's reason for a constructive one. On a mesh with shape keys Blender applies a deform-only modifier to every key and refuses a constructive one; that refusal is passed on naming as_shape_key.

A SIMULATION AT A CHOSEN FRAME (2026-10-05): applying a CLOTH, SOFT_BODY, FLUID, DYNAMIC_PAINT, OCEAN or similar modifier bakes the shape it evaluates to at the frame the scene is on, and the reply names it (simulationFrame, simulationNote). To keep a settled drape, bl_step_simulation to that frame first - a simulation needs every frame stepped, and step_simulation leaves the scene there - then apply. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a cloth grid stepped to frame 10 and applied keeps exactly the frame-10 shape it evaluated to (fallen from z 2 to about 1.63). With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. On a mesh with shape keys keep_shape_keys=True bakes a deforming modifier into the basis and each key, keeping them.

KEEP SHAPE KEYS (2026-10-11): Blender's own apply refuses every modifier on a keyed mesh (measured on 3.6.23-5.2.1), so keep_shape_keys captures each key's shape with only this modifier evaluated (the shape-key lock on that key, its vertex group and mute cleared for the capture), writes the basis and every key, and removes the modifier; the reply gives each key's largest vertex move, read back. A modifier that changes the vertex count is refused by name before anything is written, and so are simulation and particle modifiers, as_shape_key beside it, dry_run, and a mesh with no keys. Keyed shapes come out as the modifier made them on the stack (a Displace: the same box at each key value within 1e-4, test_blender_garment_ops GO167).
