CURVES (2026-10-15, the settle pass): a hair Curves object's modifier - a Geometry Nodes one, the only kind a Curves object takes - is applied through Blender's own modifier_apply, which Blender supports on Curves from 3.5; the reply has countsBefore / countsAfter (curves, points), changedTopology, pointsMoved and stackAfter. The mesh modes (as_shape_key, keep_modifier, key_name, keep_shape_keys, preview_id) are refused by name there. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1: a pass-through node group applied on 50 curves keeps 50 and leaves no modifier (test_blender_settle_routes BS508); before, it was refused 'not a MESH'.
bl_apply_transform:
Bake an object's loc/rot/scale into its MESH DATA in Blender. Name a channel and only named ones apply; name none and all three do. An ARMATURE is applied with its skinned meshes (with_meshes, default true).

Bake an object's loc/rot/scale into its MESH DATA in Blender, restoring the identity transform. THE OP THE FIDELITY GATE NEEDS: bl_object_info reports isIdentityTransform and mif_mesh_roundtrip asserts it before and after every edit, because a non-identity object transform means the pivot moved - an FBX written from an object scaled at the OBJECT level imports into Unreal at a size nobody asked for, and the mesh's own vertices disagree with what the viewport showed. Until this existed the addon could DETECT that state and not escape it. Name any of location, rotation and scale and only the named ones apply; name none and all three do. The three channels are independent on purpose: baking rotation into a mesh destined for a rig is usually wrong (the armature expects the object rotation), while baking SCALE is almost always right, because non-uniform object scale is what silently breaks normals on import. NEGATIVE SCALE IS REPORTED, NOT SILENTLY FIXED - a mirrored object carries a negative component, applying it inverts the winding order so the mesh renders inside-out, and Blender does not warn; this does, and recalculates normals when fix_normals is left on, naming that in the response. REFUSES on multi-user mesh data, because applying would move every object sharing it, one of which you did not ask about. Reports before/after object_info and the resulting isIdentityTransform. WHEN NOT TO USE THIS, and it is a real case rather than a caveat: where the object transform IS the placement - spline instances, scattered props, anything positioned by its transform rather than by its vertices - applying bakes that placement into the geometry and every instance shears. bl_export_mesh's guidance used to read as a blanket NEVER apply a transform, for exactly that reason. The distinction is what the transform MEANS: baking is right for a single asset heading to Unreal whose pivot should be identity, and wrong for geometry whose transform is carrying position information nothing else records. ARMATURES (2026-10-06): applying a rig's scale or rotation together with its skinned meshes was raw Python. The armature and every mesh parented to it or deformed by its Armature modifier are applied in one transform_apply (with_meshes false: the armature alone); the evaluated skin and the bone heads are measured in world space before and after, and maxSkinMove (per mesh and overall) and maxBoneHeadMove say what moved - under 1e-5 m measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2 for a rig scaled 2 and moved. animationNote names bones whose location keys are now in the old scale's units. fix_normals is refused on an armature, with_meshes on a mesh, shared data on any of them.
bl_artifact_inventory: Which files MifBlender's ops wrote and what a folder holds, each classed referenced, protected, unknown, candidate or gone, with why. Reads only: it moves and deletes nothing, and never calls a project clean. Recording is opt-in (the Record artifacts preference); with it off the report says so. roots names folders to walk too, links not crossed, and a file there with no record reads unknown. status lists one class, limit and offset page, largest first; the summary counts all. hash adds duplicates (identical bytes alone make neither removable). archive_root adds a plan to review, which no op applies. coverage.notChecked says what was not read, such as unopened .blend files and Unreal. docs/35_ARTIFACTS.md. max_files stops walking roots after that many files (default 20000), and coverage.truncated says it stopped.
bl_assign_action:
Put an existing action on a Blender object, or clear it. An object held ONE action forever - bl_set_keyframe creates one on first use and nothing could swap it, so a second clip on the same rig was impossible. Pass clear:true to unlink instead, which is the dangerous direction and says so: an unlinked action with no fake user drops to zero users and is deleted on the next save, so the response reports whether the action you just unlinked will survive. On Blender 4.4+ an object plays an action only through a SLOT, so the op binds the slot named for the object or the action's only object slot and reports slot and slotUsers; slot picks one by identifier or name when there are several. The assignment is re-read afterwards and refuses to claim success if it did not take. rest_pose=True first resets every pose bone of an armature to rest (location 0, rotation identity, scale 1) so channels the new action does not key do not keep the previous action's values; the reply counts them in poseBonesReset, and it is refused on a non-armature and with clear.

An object held ONE action forever. bl_set_keyframe creates one on first use and nothing could swap it, so a second clip on the same rig was impossible without deleting the first.

CLEARING IS THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. An unlinked action with no fake user drops to zero users and is deleted on the next save, so this reports previousSurvivesSave - read AFTER the unlink, because the user count is exactly what the unlink changed. Give it a fake user first if you want to keep it.

The assignment is re-read off the object afterwards and the op refuses to claim success if it did not take, rather than trusting that setting the property worked.

SLOTS, BLENDER 4.4 AND LATER. An action keeps its curves per slot and an object plays only the slot it is bound to, so an action keyed on one object and handed to another used to bind NO slot there: the second object sat still while bl_list_actions counted it as a user. The op now binds the slot named for the object, or the action's only object slot, and refuses before assigning anything when there are several and none is named for it - pass slot (identifier like 'OBBall' or display name 'Ball') to choose. The response reports slot and slotUsers; both are null on 3.6 and 4.2, which have no slots.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): a shape-key key on an object that already has an action goes into that action as a SECOND slot (KE<key>) on 4.4+, and into its own action on 3.6/4.2; clear on the object removes only the object's binding - the Key keeps its action and slot on every build.

rest_pose=True first puts every pose bone of an armature back to rest (location 0, rotation identity, scale 1): a channel the new action does not key otherwise keeps whatever the previous action left there - measured on 5.2.1, a clip that left the root at its reference pose played with the previous clip's root turn, 165 cm off at the head. The reply's poseBonesReset counts them. Refused on a non-armature and with clear.
bl_assign_material_to_faces: Point a range of polygons at one of a Blender object's material SLOTS. bl_set_material_slots decides which materials a mesh has and in what order; this decides which faces use which, and only the first existed. ADDRESSED BY SLOT INDEX, not material name, because the index is what a polygon actually stores and what Unreal's material array lines up against on import. Omit faces to assign every polygon. An out-of-range slot or face index is REFUSED rather than ignored - a face storing an index past the end renders as another slot with no error at all. `changed` is the MEASURED number of polygons that actually moved, so re-assigning faces to the slot they already had reports 0 rather than echoing the request.
bl_bake_texture:
Bake AO / NORMAL / DIFFUSE / COMBINED / ROUGHNESS / EMIT / GLOSSY / SHADOW / CURVATURE / METALLIC / ALPHA / MATERIAL_ID / HEIGHT / POSITION / THICKNESS into an image (or target COLOR_ATTRIBUTE) on a Blender mesh - how a high-poly detail becomes a texture an Unreal material can use. Judged by the IMAGE, not the operator: bpy.ops.object.bake returns FINISHED and writes NOTHING when there is no active image-texture node, so the result is checked with is_dirty plus a before/after pixel signature and a blank bake is reported as the failure it is. Needs a UV layer. Render engine, device, samples and selection are all restored afterwards. Pass filepath to write it to disk - without one the image is in memory only. See mif_help.

THE FAILURE THIS IS BUILT AROUND IS A SILENT SUCCESS, and it was measured rather than feared. With no ACTIVE image-texture node in the material, bpy.ops.object.bake returns {'FINISHED'} and writes nothing at all - no error, no warning, an untouched image, and a call that looks exactly like one that worked. A caller then saves a blank PNG and wires it into a material. So the result is judged from the image: is_dirty plus a before/after pixel signature, and a bake that reports FINISHED over an unchanged buffer is reported as a failure with the image discarded rather than handed back blank.

A MISSING UV LAYER IS LOUD, and worth saying because the request that asked for this endpoint predicted otherwise: the operator raises "No active UV layer found in the object" itself. It is still checked up front, so the refusal can name uv_unwrap as the fix.

SELECTION IS PART OF THE CONTRACT. bake reads the SELECTED objects and writes into the ACTIVE one, so a stray selection left over from earlier work is one of the ways it produces nothing while reporting success. This selects only the target and restores whatever was selected before.

THE SCENE IS PUT BACK. Render engine, Cycles device and sample count belong to whoever is using that Blender; a bake that leaves the scene on CYCLES at 4096 samples is a side effect nobody asked for. Device defaults to CPU because a headless machine may have no configured GPU and a silent fallback is a bake nobody can reason about.

A material is REQUIRED as somewhere for the bake target to live, and one is created and reported rather than refused - an AO bake on an unmaterialed mesh is a reasonable request. The target node is removed afterwards unless keep_node.

Without filepath the image exists in memory only and is lost on file reload, which the response says. If Blender uniquifies the image name because one already existed, that is reported too - looking the image up by the name you asked for would otherwise find the OLD one. colorspace overrides the image's colour space: DATA writes Non-Color - a roughness, normal or displacement map baked through an emission shader is an EMIT bake and was written sRGB - and any name from this config is taken as given.

FLOAT AND THE FILE FORMAT (2026-10-05): float=true bakes into a 32-bit float image with no alpha, so a value past 0-1 survives (an emission of 3.0 baked 3.0; the 8-bit image clipped it to 1.0) - signed or large data such as a bump height needs it. format (PNG, JPEG, TARGA or OPEN_EXR; EXR is accepted) names the saved file's format and needs filepath; a filepath extension that disagrees is refused. An EXR makes the image float, and float=false with one is refused. An EXR bake is written into a Non-Color (data) image unless colorspace says otherwise: a float buffer holds the same numbers either way, and a Linear Rec.709 image saved as EXR came back 3.0 -> 1.612 on 4.2.23 and 4.4.0 (exact on 5.0.1 and 5.2.2) - measured 2026-10-05. The reply's isFloat, savedFormat and savedSignature ([min, max, mean] of the file read back from disk) say what landed. HIGH TO LOW (2026-10-06): source names the high-poly object(s) baked onto this mesh's UVs (Blender's selected-to-active) - the garment work found a low-poly asset's look was its baked normal map, not its triangle count. extrusion (default 0.01) pushes the low poly out along its normals before rays are cast back; max_ray_distance limits them; cage names an object with the low poly's topology to cast from instead (not with extrusion). green_channel DIRECTX writes a normal map's green flipped (Unreal's convention; OPENGL, the default, is Blender's) - measured: the DirectX map's green is the OpenGL one mirrored, red unchanged. CURVATURE bakes the high poly's Cycles pointiness (0.5 flat, above convex, below concave) as data, through a temporary emission material on the sources that is removed after, their own materials put back. blob_fix true or {maxTiltDeg, minBlobPx} runs bl_fix_normal_map's repair on a NORMAL bake before it is saved, and the reply's blobFix block counts what it filled. Refused: extrusion, max_ray_distance or cage without source; the object as its own source; a cage of other topology; CURVATURE without source; green_channel or blob_fix on another bake type.

PER PIECE (2026-10-06): pieces [{object, source, cage}] bakes each low part from its own high part into the one image, one selected-to-active pass per piece, so a ray from one part cannot land on a neighbour's high (measured: one pass from two highs tilted over a tenth of a flat part's texels; per piece it stays flat). Only the first pass clears the image; each piece's UVs must have their own island. explode (scene units) also moves each piece (low, sources, cage) along +X by its index times explode for the bake and puts every object back after, so an AO bake is not darkened by its neighbours. The reply's pieces row per piece says whether it changed the image; a piece that wrote nothing fails the call. With pieces, object may be left out (the first piece's low); a top-level source or cage, an object in two pieces, explode without pieces or at 0 are refused. green_channel or blob_fix on another bake type. multires {type NORMAL | DISPLACEMENT | VECTOR_DISPLACEMENT (5.0+), space OBJECT | TANGENT (5.0+), lowResMesh, lowLevel} (2026-10-06) is Blender's multires bake of the Multires top level against lowLevel (default 0) into a float data image; it takes width, height, image_name, filepath, margin and keep_node only.

WHAT THE RAYS CAN HIT (2026-10-14). A one-object bake (no source, no pieces) bakes the object alone: every other geometry object is hidden from render for the bake and put back after (lights, cameras and empties stay, so a SHADOW or COMBINED bake keeps its lighting). Collision meshes - names starting UCX_, UBX_, USP_ or UCP_ - are hidden in every bake. include [names] keeps those objects in the rays' way (a neighbour's occlusion wanted). The reply's excluded and excludedNames say what was hidden, included what was kept. Measured: a 1 m cube inside a 3 m UCX_ hull baked AO mean 0.25 before, 0.70 now (tools/test_blender_bake_isolate.py).

1.3 (2026-10-19): METALLIC, ALPHA, MATERIAL_ID, POSITION and THICKNESS bake through a temporary emission (as CURVATURE does) on the sources of a high-to-low bake, or on the object itself - a SELF-BAKE, which CURVATURE now allows too (a mesh's own curvature for an edge-wear mask). METALLIC and ALPHA copy each material and route the Principled input's own link or value into the emission. MATERIAL_ID gives each material (id_by MATERIAL, default) or object (id_by OBJECT) a flat color from its name; idColors lists them. POSITION maps world position into the baked objects' bounds (positionBounds). THICKNESS is Cycles' Ambient Occlusion looking inside the mesh (thin is dark) over thickness_distance (default a quarter of the largest bound). HEIGHT (with source) is three internal bakes - the high's position seen from the low, the low's position, the low's normal - combined into the distance along the low's normal, mapped -height_range..+height_range to 0..1 (0.5 on the surface; default range the largest distance found), returned as a float image with distanceMin/Max. target COLOR_ATTRIBUTE bakes into the low's color attribute (color_attribute, default Bake_<TYPE>, made CORNER byte color when missing) instead of an image; width, height, filepath and the image options are refused with it. Emission-route types are refused with pieces.

BASE_COLOR (1.4): the Base Color input itself through a temporary emission - the albedo, metallic or not. DIFFUSE is the diffuse color pass, base color x (1 - metallic), black wherever the surface is metal.
bl_bake_hidden_face_map:
Bake a body hidden-face map from garments in the Blender body's UV layout (black covered, gray edge band, white open) - a MetaHuman outfit's body mask - and count what Unreal's geometry removal would cut with it.

WHY (2026-10-04): an outfit hides the body under it through a texture in the body's UV space, and nothing made one - a suit's mask was the engine's body mask painted black by hand. Each texel of the body's UV layout (uv_map, default the active one; resolution square, default 512) that a triangle covers is a point on the evaluated body with its interpolated normal; a ray along the normal that meets a garment within max_distance (default 0.1 m) marks it covered. Covered texels farther than gray_band (default 4) texels from an open one are 0, the rest of the covered ones 0.5, open ones 1; keep [{min, max}] world boxes are forced to 1 (wrists and ankles left showing); margin (default 4) bleeds the values past the UV islands' edges. output_path writes an 8-bit PNG; the image (<body>_HiddenFaceMap) stays in the file. engineCheck applies the 5.7 / 5.8 rule to the map: a triangle is removed when every texel it covers is at or under max_cull_value (0.1), a vertex shrinks on a texel between that and min_keep_value (0.9) - by MaxShrinkDistance, 0 by default. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a garment over half a grid body gives a black half, a 3-texel gray band at gray_band 3, a white half, coveredShare 0.5. Refused: the body as a garment, no UV map, resolution outside 16-4096, max_cull_value not under min_keep_value, a keep box with min over max, an output_path that is not .png. The Unreal side - writing the texture asset and setting it on the wardrobe item - is not built yet.
bl_fix_normal_map:
Repair blobs in a Blender normal map - patches tilted past max_tilt_deg (70) where bake rays hit a facing surface - by filling them from the texels round them; thin real lines are kept. texelsFilled, blobs.

WHY (2026-10-04): where cloth pinches (a crotch, an armpit) a selected-to-active bake's rays land on the facing surface and the tangent normal map gets connected patches of extreme tilt; every garment bake was repaired offline with a Pillow and numpy script. The same rule here, also run by bl_bake_texture blob_fix on a NORMAL bake: texels tilted past max_tilt_deg are eroded one texel (a thin real stitch line drops out of the mask), components smaller than min_blob_px (default 40) are dropped, the rest grown 6 texels, and that mask is filled from the texels round it by repeated neighbour averaging and renormalised. image names an image in this file (changed in memory), or filepath loads a file, fixed into output_path or back into filepath with overwrite true. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a 64 x 64 flat map with a 10 x 10 patch tilted 80 degrees and a 1-px line tilted 80 degrees - every patch texel back to flat within 1/255, the line unchanged, texelsFilled 400; min_blob_px 100 leaves it and says so. Refused: neither or both of image and filepath, filepath with no output_path or overwrite, max_tilt_deg outside 0-180, a missing file or image.
bl_bake_to_keyframes:
Bake an object's evaluated motion (constraints, drivers, a simulation) into REAL keyframes an exporter will carry; frame_start/frame_end default to the scene range, step to 1. This matters more than it sounds: bl_bake_physics bakes POINT CACHES and no exporter reads them, so a rigid-body simulation authored through this bridge could be rendered here and handed to NOTHING. Constraints and drivers have the same problem one step removed - they evaluate correctly in Blender and export as a static object, because an exporter writes keyframes and a constraint is not one. THE POSTCONDITION IS THE MOTION, NOT THE KEY COUNT: the evaluated world matrix is sampled across the range before the bake and again after, and maxPositionError / maxRotationErrorRadians / motionPreserved report whether the movement survived. Producing the right NUMBER of keys while losing the motion is the normal failure when visual keying is off, and a key count cannot see it. Sources left in place keep evaluating ON TOP of the new keys - clear_constraints and remove_rigid_body exist for that, and hadConstraints/hadRigidBody say what was there. Call mif_help("bl_bake_to_keyframes") first.

visual_keying defaults TRUE. With it off the bake records the object's OWN transform and discards everything a constraint or a simulation was contributing, which is precisely how this goes wrong.

The probe frames are spread across the range rather than taken from one end, because a bake that loses the motion still matches at the first frame, where the object has not moved yet.

An object whose rigid body is still active is still driven by the simulation, with its new keyframes ignored - remove_rigid_body handles that. No exporter reads a point cache, not FBX and not glTF.

A FRAME CHANGE STEPS EVERY LIVE SIMULATION (2026-10-05): moving the scene's frame evaluates each unbaked cloth, soft body, emitter or dynamic-hair particle system, dynamic-paint canvas and rigid body world in the view layer, and a fluid domain whose cache type is REPLAY - on an object hidden with the eye or from the render too (only hide_viewport or the modifier's show_viewport off takes it out). A leftover cloth on a render-hidden object stepped against a body's collision during a pose check and asked for 58.7 GB. So a call that would move the frame past such a cache's first frame is REFUSED before anything changes, naming each simulation and the colliders it would step against; bake them, take them out of the depsgraph, or pass allow_simulation=true, and the reply's simulationsStepped and colliders say what stepped. A Geometry Nodes simulation zone is listed (geometryNodesSimulations) and not refused: Blender exposes no baked flag for it.
bl_batch:
Run several Blender ops as ONE job ({op, ...params} each, in its bl_ tool's names), with an honest partial-failure contract; results='errors' returns only the ops that failed. The addon is single-threaded by design - one worker draining one queue - so this is not concurrency; it is one round trip instead of N, which matters because every op here is a socket call. IT IS NOT ATOMIC AND THE RESPONSE SAYS SO. A batch failing at op 7 of 10 leaves six applied - but the whole batch is ONE undo step, so a single bl_undo takes all six back, and atomicNote says whether this batch's step was recorded. The response carries `atomic: false`, `applied`, `failed` and `skipped` by name, plus a per-op `results` list in order with each op's own result and timing - so what happened is readable rather than a single verdict. THE WHOLE BATCH IS VALIDATED BEFORE ANY OF IT RUNS: an unknown op name in the last entry refuses the batch without applying the first, and an empty ops[] is a hard failure rather than ok:true with zero rows, because the response IS the audit trail. Each op's own parameters are checked by the handler it dispatches to, which already refuses unknown keys by name. IT STOPS AT THE FIRST FAILURE by default, because a batch is usually a build sequence where a later op depends on an earlier one and running on turns one diagnosable error into several; continue_on_error=True runs the rest when the ops are independent. budget_seconds is a TIME budget, not an op cap, and that is deliberate: measured op costs span four orders of magnitude (bl_list_objects 0.05ms, bl_add_modifier SUBSURF 205ms, a first bl_render_still 610ms), so 1000 ordinary ops is about a second while 250 renders is 150 seconds. The budget is checked BETWEEN ops - nothing can interrupt a running handler - so the guarantee is that it will not START an op it cannot afford, and it names the one it skipped. Hitting the budget is not a failure: the ops that ran succeeded. With dry_run=True it previews every op's changes with their values before and returns a preview_id, refused when an op takes no preview or two ops change one target; preview_id alone commits them all, rolled back together on a mismatch.

CHANGE CAP: a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct objects, materials or collections (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) writes nothing and answers ok:false, capped, the targets and a previewId; preview_id alone commits it once within 10 minutes, refused if a target has gone or moved since (docs/15 section 6).
bl_bevel_edges:
Round or chamfer the selected edges with bmesh.ops.bevel (NOT bpy.ops.mesh.bevel, which needs an EDIT_MESH context and a real VIEW_3D area and therefore cannot run under blender -b). THE ADDON'S DEFAULTS, NOT A ROAD TILE'S: `selector` is required (the same keys as bl_select_edges - preview with it first), and exactly one of `offset` (Blender units) or `offset_uu` (Unreal units); segments defaults to 1, a flat chamfer (>1 rounds), profile to 0.5, and no axis is guarded unless preserve_x=true. Until 2026-09-21 this tool defaulted to a sidewalk tile's settings - 15 uu, 3 segments, the Y boundary edges, preserve_x on - and preserve_x snaps every vertex within the offset of the X extremes back onto them: measured on 5.0.1, bevelling all edges of a plain cube with it left all 96 vertices on the two X planes, the bevel beside those faces flattened, under ok:true. Pass preserve_x=true for a tile that must butt against the next one (mif_mesh_roundtrip keeps the tile defaults). clamp_overlap, loop_slide, harden_normals, miter_outer, miter_inner and spread are bmesh.ops.bevel's own options - left unset they keep the addon's defaults. THE RESULT CAN PASS THROUGH ITSELF while every guard holds: selfIntersectingFacePairs counts faces that cross and share no vertex (with the count before the bevel when there are any), and selfIntersectionNote says when the bevel made them - measured, a 0.7 BU bevel on a radius-0.5 tube's rim crossed 424 pairs unclamped on every build and 386 with clampOverlap on from Blender 4.4. shapeBefore/shapeAfter fingerprint every vertex position, because profile and offset move vertices without changing a count - compare shapeAfter to tell two bevels apart. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. finish (true or {minAngleDeg, triangleBudget}) is the hard-surface finish: the sharp edges when no selector is given, hardened and weighted normals, flat faces shading flat, triangles held to the budget.

offset_uu is in UNREAL units and is sent as offsetUU - the addon does the one conversion against its own UU_PER_BU, so nothing here divides by 100. segments=1 gives a flat chamfer, >1 a rounded profile. Two bmesh defaults are overridden for you because the defaults are silently wrong here: affect is forced to EDGES (the default is VERTICES) and material to -1 (the default 0 dumps every new face into slot 0). preserve_x=true is the tiling defence (it defaulted TRUE until 2026-09-21 and is off unless asked for now - on a general mesh it flattens every bevel beside the X extremities) - a bevel also drags the vertices at the X extremities inward, which moves the end-cap seam off exactly +/-500 and shears anything extruded along a spline; it is sent as preserveAxes:['X'] AND assertAxes:['X'] together, never one without the other, so verts near the original min/max X are clamped back and X is then asserted, and a surviving drift REFUSES and leaves the mesh unmodified. The assert is TWO checks: the X SIZE, and seam PLANARITY. The second is not a refinement of the first - MEASURED on 4.4.0, a guards-off bevel of the Y edge loops on a 1000x300x50 uu tile left 24 of 32 verts 15 uu inside the X seam and still reported sizeDeltaUU [0,0,0], because the surviving corner verts pin the bounding box. A size check cannot ever see that. selector takes the same keys as bl_select_edges. Returns before/after sizes, offSeamVerts and a per-axis seamPlanarity block (reported for X, Y and Z whatever is guarded - guards decide what FAILS, never what is looked at), plus objectAfter. Prefer bl_extrude_skirt when a skirt is what you actually want: it moves nothing in X or Y by construction rather than by clamping.

FINISH (1.4, 2026-10-30): finish true or {minAngleDeg (30), triangleBudget}. selector is then optional - without one the finish takes every edge whose faces meet minAngleDeg or more off flat. The bevel hardens its normals and marks the faces it touched with a lower face strength; every face is set smooth and a Weighted Normal modifier with face influence goes on (bl_set_shading's MifWeightedNormal; on Blender before 4.1 auto smooth at 180 degrees so custom normals take effect). The answer's finish block measures the evaluated mesh: normals.flatFacesMaxLeanDeg (how far the flat faces' shading normals lean off their face - 0.000 on a beveled cube, where the Weighted Normal modifier alone left 1.64 degrees and hardened normals alone 70), bevelFacesMeanLeanDeg, and triangles {before, after, added, budget, budgetFrom, addedShareOfBudget, withinBudget} against triangleBudget or the size class's budget (bl_mesh_quality game_ready's). hardenNormals false beside finish is refused.
bl_bind_modifier: Bind a Blender deform modifier that does nothing until bound - Surface Deform, Mesh Deform, Corrective Smooth (rest source Bind), Laplacian Deform - or unbind it. Blender's bind is a toggle, so the state is read first and read back after. WHY: these four deform nothing until bound, and nothing typed bound them, so a garment morph that follows a body morph (Surface Deform onto the body, then apply as a shape key) stopped at the first step. A Surface Deform needs its target and a Mesh Deform its cage object set first (bl_set_modifier); a Corrective Smooth binds only with rest source BIND. Blender's own refusal (a target with non-manifold or concave faces) is passed on. The reply carries bound, boundBefore and alreadyInState.
bl_bisect_plane:
Cut a Blender mesh with a plane - the fundamental 'cut at a plane' that bevel, boolean, separate, decimate and clean are not. A boolean needs a second object authored, positioned and cleaned up for what is one plane. Works through bmesh rather than bpy.ops.mesh.bisect, which needs EDIT mode and a selection - a mode switch from a socket call can strand every op after it. THE PLANE IS WORLD SPACE and converted in, because 'cut at z=2.4' is a world statement every time and handing a local plane to a moved object cuts somewhere else silently. The postcondition is that the mesh actually MOVED: bisect raises nothing when the plane misses the geometry, so it would report success having changed not one vertex - if that happens the refusal quotes the object's world bounding box so you can see where the plane should have been. With clear_inner or clear_outer it also CLOSES the opening with a cap face unless fill=False - pass fill=False to keep it open; a cut that clears nothing leaves no opening to fill. faces [indices] or near_bone {bone, radius, armature} limits the cut and any clear to a region (faces whose centre is within radius of the bone's rest segment), so a cuff cut no longer slices the torso. The reply says what the fill did - capped, cappedFaces, cappedFaceCount and capNote, with fillFrom saying whether fill was sent or took its default - and a garment cut (a hem, a cuff, a neckline) passes fill=False, since the default caps the opening and a later fold finds no open boundary.

plane_co [x, y, z] (list, required) is a point ON the cutting plane, in world space. Give the plane's direction with exactly one of axis (str, default None: X | Y | Z, case-insensitive, the world axis used as the normal) or plane_no [x, y, z] (list, default None: any world-space normal, normalized before use). threshold (float, default None, which the op reads as 0.0001) is the distance under which a vertex counts as on the plane; with faces or near_bone it is also the margin a region face's centre must clear to be deleted by clear_inner/clear_outer. The point goes through the inverse world matrix and the normal through its inverse transpose, so non-uniform scale does not tilt the plane. clear_inner deletes the side opposite the normal, clear_outer the side it points to.

OUT: ok, object, planeCo, planeNo (normalized, world), space 'WORLD', clearInner, clearOuter, filled (fill as resolved: true by default when clearing), regionFaces (faces in the region before the cut; null without faces or near_bone), before / after / delta {vertices, edges, faces}.

Refused: an unknown key; an object that is not a MESH, or not in OBJECT mode; plane_co missing; both axis and plane_no, or neither; an axis other than X, Y or Z; a zero-length normal; clear_inner and clear_outer together (use clear_mesh); a negative threshold; faces and near_bone together; near_bone not {bone, radius, armature?} or radius not above 0, or a bone the lookup cannot resolve; faces not a non-empty list of valid face indices; a near_bone region holding no face; a clear that would remove every vertex; and a cut that leaves the mesh unchanged (the plane missed). The last two quote the object's world bounding box. All of these are raised before the bmesh is written back, so the mesh is untouched; the source says NOTHING was changed for each except the miss, which says Nothing was cut.
bl_boolean_op:
Cut, merge or intersect mesh `target` with mesh `cutter` - operation 'difference' (default), 'union' or 'intersect'. APPLIES the modifier rather than leaving it stacked, and reports before/after vertex and face counts as the evidence. Says changed:false with the likely cause when the boolean legally did nothing. bl_add_modifier can name a cutter too (settings object) but leaves the modifier unapplied. The cutter is KEPT unless delete_cutter. material_mode 'transfer' gives the faces the cutter adds the cutter's own material (a slot is added to the target if it lacks one), 'index' (Blender's default) the target's slot with the same number - EXACT solver only. cutter may be a list: cutters, and a cutter's shells, are cut one at a time (touching shells cut at once came back empty). cleanup (on unless false; true or {angle, minFaceArea, ngons} to set it) cleans only the faces the cut made or touched - slivers welded, a Limited Dissolve, then n-gons split into quads (default), triangles or kept, needles dissolved and collapsed UVs opened - and counts faces, triangles, quads and n-gons before and after in the answer's cleanup. See mif_help.

SEVERAL CUTTERS ARE CUT ONE AT A TIME. cutter takes a list of names, each cut in turn; and one cutter whose mesh holds several shells (separate boxes joined into one object) is cut shell by shell when the operation is difference or union and the solver EXACT (Blender's default). Measured on Blender 5.0.1: a door box and a window box in ONE cutter object, sharing a face, cut a 4 x 3 m wall down to a 9-vertex sliver; overlapping by 5 cm, they emptied it. The same boxes cut one at a time leave the wall with its door and window. The answer then carries cutters, cutterShells (per cutter), cutsApplied and steps (each cut's cutter, shell, changed and counts), with appliedOneAtATime true. A cut that refuses partway puts the target's mesh back as it was before the first cut, and says which cut refused; the temporary shell objects are always removed. deleteCutter with a list deletes every cutter (cuttersDeleted).

AN INTERSECT takes one cutter: met with each of several in turn it keeps only what is inside every cutter, which is rarely the ask - union the cutters first. One intersect cutter of several shells is cut whole with the modifier's self-intersection on, which measured right where the plain cut came back empty; the answer says selfIntersection true with cutterShells.

Boolean is a MODIFIER, not an operator, which makes it the awkward one of the three mesh-combining verbs (the others being bl_join_objects and bl_separate_mesh). Three steps fail independently: add the BOOLEAN modifier naming the cutter, APPLY it, and dispose of the cutter.

THE FAILURE THIS GUARDS is a modifier added and never applied. That is the worst shape available here, because the viewport shows the cut and the exported FBX does not - the 3D view agrees with what you asked for while the deliverable disagrees, and nothing on screen betrays it. So success is judged from the mesh afterwards: the response carries before/after vertex and face counts, and the op refuses rather than leaving a modifier behind if apply fails.

AN UNCHANGED MESH IS REPORTED, NOT SWALLOWED. A DIFFERENCE whose cutter misses, or an INTERSECT with no overlap, applies cleanly and changes nothing. That is geometry rather than failure, and it is almost always a modeling mistake - so the response says changed:false and names the likely cause (usually that the two objects do not overlap) instead of reporting a plain success. A result of zero faces is called out the same way.

TOPOLOGY IS COMPARED, NOT ASSUMED. topologyBefore/topologyAfter report boundary, loose and non-manifold edge counts plus local bounds. topologyDegraded becomes true only when the boolean ADDS structural defects relative to the input, so an intentionally open target is not rejected merely for already being open. topologyWarning recommends inspection or solver:'exact'; the operation remains ok:true because Blender did apply it and the measurements, rather than caller intent, are the evidence.

bl_add_modifier CAN NAME A CUTTER TOO since 2026-09-21 - settings {object: 'Cutter', operation: 'DIFFERENCE'} - but it leaves the modifier on the stack unapplied, which is the viewport-cut, export-uncut state described above. This op applies it and judges the result.

THE CUTTER IS KEPT by default. bpy's own workflow deletes it, but a cutter is usually reusable and deleting someone's object as a side effect is not a default worth having. Pass delete_cutter to opt in; the response says which happened.

solver is read off this Blender's own enum, in any case, and is Blender's choice when omitted: FAST and EXACT on 3.6 to 4.4, FLOAT, EXACT and MANIFOLD on 5.0, where FAST was renamed FLOAT (measured on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1).

CLEANUP AFTER THE CUT (opt-in, default off - a call without it cuts exactly as before). cleanup true, or {angle (degrees, default 5), minFaceArea (the mesh's units squared, default 1e-6), ngons ('quads' default, 'triangulate' or 'keep')}, works on the faces the cut made or touched and on no other face: a face whose corners all match a face the target had before the cut is never an argument to any step, and is checked unchanged before the mesh is written. In order: slivers under minFaceArea are collapsed by welding their short edges (an end on an untouched face stays put; the weld is undone if it would add an open or non-manifold edge, and sliverNote says so); a Limited Dissolve at angle over edges with cut faces on both sides (material, seam, sharp and normal borders kept); then the cut's n-gons are triangulated (BEAUTY) and, for 'quads', the triangles joined back into quads where two meet within 40 degrees. The answer's cleanup carries cutFaces and mesh {before, after} as {faces, tris, quads, ngons}, untouchedFaces, sliversMerged / sliversLeft, facesDissolved, ngonsSplit and trianglePairsJoined. With several cutters it runs once, after the last cut. Measured 2026-10-30 on 3.6 to 5.2: an EXACT cut of twelve slits from a 48-sided cylinder, a door and window from a wall, and a box intersected with a sphere left 48, 4 and 54 n-gons and nothing a 5-degree dissolve could merge - the EXACT solver already leaves the fewest faces its outline allows - so the n-gon split is what changes a box-cutter cut; the dissolve takes a cutter's own split faces (a 3 x 3 gridded notch: 18 faces to 8). The triangle count is the same with or without cleanup: an engine splits an n-gon on import anyway, and this decides how, where it can be seen.
bl_clean_mesh:
The cleanup pass an imported or edited mesh needs before it goes back to Unreal. FIVE INDEPENDENT STEPS, run in the only correct order: merge first (so loose/degenerate detection sees merged topology), then remove loose, then dissolve degenerates, then triangulate, then recalc normals LAST because every earlier step changes what a face's normal should be. merge_distance welds vertices closer than that - the most useful one on an imported mesh, since duplicate verts along a seam are invisible in the viewport and split the smoothing in Unreal. remove_loose deletes verts and edges belonging to no face: they export, cost nothing visible, and make Unreal's bounds wrong. dissolve_degenerate collapses zero-area faces. triangulate means the triangulation you SEE is the one you ship rather than one the importer picked. IT REPORTS WHAT EACH STEP DID, NOT THAT IT RAN - per-step counts before and after, so 'cleaned' is a number; a mesh already clean returns zeroes and says so in words instead of a cheerful ok that reads as work performed. recalc_normals is REFUSED with a named reason when the mesh has custom split normals (usually authored deliberately for hard-surface shading or foliage cards) unless force is set. The merge distance is in the MESH's own units by default (space LOCAL): under a scaled parent - an FBX rig at 0.01 or 100 - the same number welds a different world distance, so every merge reports localDistance, worldDistance and the object's worldScale, and a scaled object's reply carries spaceNote. Pass space="WORLD" to give the distance in world units; it is refused on a non-uniform world scale, and space without merge_distance is refused. min_face_area deletes faces smaller than that area (mesh units squared) with the edges and vertices only they used - the slivers a boolean or remesh leaves; remove_unused_slots drops every material slot no face uses, each face's material compared by name before and after (removedUnusedSlots), and a slot drop counts as a change. open_collapsed_uvs gives a face with no UV area a tiny ring of corners, so Unreal computes tangents there. keep_custom_normals, with recalc_normals or split_non_manifold alone, puts each corner's normal back after the step, so an imported mesh can be turned without losing them. split_non_manifold gives each face on an edge of three or more faces its own copy of it; nothing moves.

HOLES, FINS AND RAGGED LOOPS (2026-10-04), from a short film's garment pass, run after min_face_area and before triangulate: despike_distance (WORLD units; refused on a non-uniform scale) pulls a vertex within near_boundary_rings (default 4) edge rings of a boundary back to its neighbours' average when it stands farther than that from it - a rim vertex is averaged with its two neighbours ALONG the rim (by boundary edge) - up to 6 passes, reported per pass (steps.despiked). A rim corner stands off its neighbours' average too (a square grid's corner by 0.71 of its edge), so the distance must be above that. smooth_loop_near [x,y,z] straightens the boundary loop nearest that world point along itself smooth_loop_iterations times (default 10): halfway to the two loop neighbours' midpoint, then scaled about the loop's centroid back to its mean distance from it, so a round cuff stays where it is (plain halving shrinks an 8-sided loop 15% a pass) and only the raggedness goes - measured, a bump 15.0 mm past the mean radius came to 2.5 mm in 10 passes (steps.smoothedLoop). fill_holes_up_to N fills every hole of at most N vertices, each on its own, with a face that copies its neighbours' UVs (bmesh.ops.holes_fill, then a face through the hole's vertices where that adds none - a hole with a wire edge at it); two holes touching at a vertex are split and filled apart. An open sheet's own rim is a loop too, so N is what keeps a cuff open. steps.filledHoles lists what it filled and, under skipped, each hole it did not with its vertices and why (larger than N, three or more holes at one vertex, flipped faces round it, a face over those vertices already there); an answer that skipped a hole at or under N never says the mesh was clean (2026-10-05). Refused: despike_distance not above 0, near_boundary_rings without it, smooth_loop_iterations without smooth_loop_near, smooth_loop_near on a closed mesh, fill_holes_up_to under 3. QUADRIFY: quadrify {maxAngleDeg (40), shapeAngleDeg (40), respectSeams, respectSharp, respectMaterial, respectUV} joins triangle pairs back into quads (Blender's Tris to Quads); a respected edge is never removed, so a marked sewing line stays. Refused with triangulate. trianglesBefore, quadsBefore, trianglesAfter, quadsAfter and trianglesLeft come back. FLIP (2026-10-05): flip_normals true reverses every face, or a list of face indices those faces - last, after recalc_normals, so recalc_normals plus flip_normals true points a closed mesh inward. Cloth pressure acts along the normal (a blazer whose shoulders sagged instead of lifting was fixed by flipping them all), and a shell traced inside-out needs it; recalc_normals never reverses on purpose. steps.flippedNormals counts the faces. A face list is refused with a step that renumbers faces (merge, loose, degenerate, min_face_area, fill_holes_up_to, quadrify, triangulate).

CRUMPLES (2026-10-05): relax_crumples - true, or {creaseDeg (55), growRings (3), iterations (25), factor (0.6)} - finds every edge whose two faces turn more than creaseDeg apart, grows its vertices growRings edge rings and Laplacian-relaxes that region only (each pass a vertex goes factor of the way to its neighbours' mean; a boundary vertex only along its loop), so a drape's sub-centimetre crumples at a hood border or a neck junction go and the folds elsewhere keep their shape - a whole-mesh smooth flattens every fold. It runs after smooth_loop_near and before the hole fill; steps.relaxedCrumples reports seedVertices, relaxedVertices and creaseEdgesBefore / After. Measured on a 0.1 m grid with one vertex pushed 0.2 m out: the crease edges go to 0 and a 1 cm fold eight rows away does not move. TOPOLOGY INFLUENCE (2026-10-06): quadrify.topologyInfluence 0-2 (Blender 4.4+, bmesh join_triangles' topology_influence; refused by name on 4.2) prefers the pairings that leave a quad grid - a seeded jittered triangulated 6 x 6 grid at shapeAngleDeg 60 gave 29 quads at 0 and 31 at 1.0 on 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): mergeDistance keeps the FIRST vertex of a merged run at its own position on every build (x 0, 0.001, 0.002 with 0.0015: 0 and 0.002 survive), not the centre. dissolve_degenerate takes a number too (1.4): the distance in mesh units, up to 0.01 - a face no wider and an edge no longer than it is dissolved (true works at 1e-6). bl_mesh_quality game_ready names the distance for its sliverFaces. open_collapsed_uvs (a UV layer's name, or true for the active one) gives each face with no UV area a ring of corners 1e-4 across, so Unreal computes tangents there and no other UV moves: a palette keeps its look, where a fresh unwrap replaces the layer. bl_mesh_quality game_ready names it for nearZeroTangents.
bl_remove_mesh_attributes:
Take attributes off a Blender mesh: names (bl_mesh_stats lists them; a UV map too) or kinds CUSTOM_NORMALS, SHARP_EDGE, SHARP_FACE (every face then shades smooth), COLOR. Replies what was removed, what was not there, and what remains.

WHY (2026-10-05): after a round trip through an exchange format a custom-normals attribute and a sharp-edge attribute had to come off before the mesh behaved - an extrude misbehaved until the custom normals were cleared - and bl_set_vertex_color and the kit builders only ever add attributes. CUSTOM_NORMALS runs Blender's Clear Custom Split Normals: custom normals are an attribute named custom_normal from 4.4 and a layer that is not an attribute at all on 4.2, and that operator cleared them headless on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2 (customNormalsBefore / customNormalsAfter say what it did). SHARP_EDGE removes sharp_edge (no edge marked sharp after); SHARP_FACE removes sharp_face, so EVERY FACE SHADES SMOOTH after - bl_set_shading flat brings flat shading back; COLOR removes every colour attribute. A kind the mesh does not have is listed in notPresent. Every name is checked before anything is removed: a required attribute (position), an internal one (a name starting with '.', Blender's own bookkeeping) or a name the mesh lacks is refused, and a call that would remove nothing at all is refused - NOTHING is changed by a refusal. Reply: removed [{name, domain, dataType, kind}], notPresent, remaining (internal attributes not listed).
bl_clear_scene:
Delete objects in the Blender scene. object_type limits it to ONE Blender type ('MESH', 'ARMATURE', 'EMPTY', ...) so a rig or the lights and cameras can be kept while the meshes go; omit it to clear everything. purge_orphans (default TRUE in the addon) sweeps the WHOLE FILE for datablocks with zero users, not only the ones this call orphaned - so a material or node group made and not yet assigned is destroyed by it, and object_type='LIGHT' in a scene with no lights answers removedCount 0 while still purging. Measured; orphansPurgedNames and orphanPurgeNote now say what went. Pass purge_orphans=false to keep work in progress. bl_import_mesh already clears by default, so the usual reason to call this directly is to inspect a failed run's leftovers first and then reset. A baked rigid body world whose bodies go is freed and reported (freedRigidBodyBake): it would otherwise replay the old frames onto the next scene's bodies, which made shape, friction and bounciness look inert. Rigid body joints and bodies are taken out of the physics world before they are removed - removing them in either order crashed Blender on some build - and a joint whose body is cleared goes with it (jointsRemovedWithBodies), even when object_type would have kept it. bl_undo takes the whole clear back as one step. It deletes objects, not collections: emptyCollectionsLeft names the collections left empty, since bl_create_collection refuses a name that is still taken. Colour management is scene settings and survives it too: colorManagementKept reports it, with a note naming anything not at Blender's factory values.

CHANGE CAP: it has no preview, so a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct data-blocks (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) is refused, writing nothing, and says to split it or have the user raise the cap (docs/15 section 6).
bl_closest_point_on_mesh:
The nearest point ON a Blender mesh to a point in space - the other half of bl_ray_cast, for when there is no obvious direction to cast in: snapping to a surface, measuring clearance, finding which face something sits over. World in, world out, with the same local-space conversion and the same inverse-transpose normal. Also returns signedOffset - positive means the query point is outside that face, negative behind it - which answers 'is this inside the mesh' without a second cast. Answers on the MODIFIER RESULT by default (what renders); evaluated:false answers on the object's own base mesh instead, and `against` says which was used, beside `modifiers`. An object that draws instances - Geometry Nodes instances, particles, instancing - answers with instancesNote: instances are not part of any evaluated mesh, so this does not see them (measured on 3.6-5.2).

Parameters: distance (float, default None = unlimited) is the maximum search range in WORLD units, like point and the answer's distance. It is converted for the object's scale: a uniform scale divides the limit by that one number; any other scale searches a world-space tree instead, so the limit is a true world sphere. It must be greater than 0. object must be a MESH; point is [x, y, z] in world space.

OUT: ok, found, space "WORLD", against ("<object> (evaluated geometry)" or "(base geometry)"), object, point, modifiers [names]; with evaluated, instancesNote; on the base mesh with modifiers present, modifierNote. When found: location (world), normal (world, inverse-transpose), localLocation, faceIndex, distance, signedOffset (positive = query point outside that face, negative = behind it). When not found: note. In edit mode the read is not refused: editModeStale true, objectMode and staleNote say the mesh is as it was when OBJECT mode was last left.

Refusals (a read; nothing is changed): no object by that name (the message lists up to 25 present); the object is not a MESH; distance 0 or less; the mesh asked (modifier result, or base mesh with evaluated false) has no faces; point missing or malformed; any unknown key.
bl_collect_vdb_frames:
Copy the frames of a baked OpenVDB sequence into a clean folder, renumbered from 0 - COPIED, never moved, so the cache is untouched. The source is a Blender Mantaflow DOMAIN (object=, its cache folder's data/ is found for you) or any folder of .vdb files (folder=, prefix= when it holds more than one sequence). The kept frames default to the frames the scene plays (scene start to the domain's cache end) for a domain and to every non-negative frame for a folder - Mantaflow writes pre-roll frames with a minus sign (fluid_data_-0001.vdb), which Unreal's importer reads as frame 1 and aliases onto the real frame 1. start/end choose the source frames to keep; a gap inside them is refused (Unreal's importer stops at the first gap, and renumbering would hide it). destination must hold no .vdb that would join the new sequence. base_name names the files (and so the Unreal asset: fire -> fire_0000.vdb -> asset fire). Reports every grid (name, type, channels, voxel size) read by Blender's own OpenVDB reader and, with sample_ranges (default true), each grid's value range on the first, middle and last frame through Blender's bundled openvdb module when it has one - the numbers a material's multipliers depend on (Mantaflow temperature runs to about 3, not kelvin). ueImport carries the next call.

WHY IT EXISTS. Unreal's OpenVDB importer reads a frame number as the digits after the last non-digit, takes every
.vdb starting with the base name and stops at the first gap. A Mantaflow cache breaks all three: pre-roll frames are
written with a minus sign (fluid_data_-0001.vdb) that the importer drops. Copying the kept frames to their own folder,
named <baseName>_0000.vdb upward, gives every importer the same reading. import_vdb_as_volume_texture audits a folder
with Unreal's rule and refuses one it would misread; this is the op that writes a clean one.

BY OBJECT the domain's cache folder, cache_data_format and range are read off the domain; the kept frames default to
the scene's start frame (or the cache start, whichever is later) through the cache end. BY FOLDER a minus sign right
before the digits is a negative frame only where the same prefix also has unsigned files; where every file carries it,
it is a separator (smoke-0001.vdb is frame 1).

VALUE RANGES come from Blender's bundled openvdb module (5.x ships one): per scalar grid min, max, active voxels and
whether it is constant; per vector grid only the largest magnitude, because its evalMinMax compares by length (a
velocity grid came back with min z above max z). A Mantaflow fire measured: temperature 0..3, flame 0..1, density to
~0.07 for FIRE and ~1 for FIRE+SMOKE; shadow is -1 everywhere in a scene with no light.

NOTHING IS DELETED OR OVERWRITTEN: a destination holding a .vdb that starts with the base name (case-insensitive, as
Unreal matches) is refused; a failed copy reports how many frames were copied and leaves the source untouched.
bl_compare_to_reference:
TURN 'match this reference' INTO A NUMBER. Returns silhouetteIoU (intersection over union of the two subject masks - ignores colour and lighting entirely and asks only whether the subject occupies the same space in frame, which is the number for matching a blockout) and meanAbsDiff (per-pixel luminance difference - sensitive to lighting and materials, so useful for 'is this the same shot' and useless for 'is this the same shape'). Reported separately rather than blended, because one score would hide which of the two moved. RENDER WITH A TRANSPARENT FILM FIRST (bl_set_render_settings film_transparent) - with an opaque background every pixel counts as subject, the mask becomes the whole frame, and IoU is 1.0 by definition; the op detects that and returns null with degenerateMask explaining, rather than a meaningless number. This is PIXEL similarity, not semantic similarity: a render matching a blockout's silhouette exactly with entirely wrong materials scores well and should.

image (str, required) and reference are FILE PATHS on disk (made absolute with bpy.path.abspath, so // paths resolve against the .blend), not Blender image datablock names. compare_px (int, default None, which the op reads as 128) is the longest edge both images are scaled to before comparing; 16 to 512 is accepted. threshold (float, default None, read as 0.1) is the luminance above which a pixel counts as subject. It is used only when one or both images are fully opaque: when BOTH have transparency, alpha above 0.5 is the mask instead and threshold is ignored. A mask covering over 95% or under 1% of the frame is degenerate and silhouetteIoU comes back null.

OUT: image, reference (absolute paths), comparedAt [w, h], silhouetteIoU (4 places, or null), meanAbsDiff (mean per-pixel luminance difference, 4 places), maskSource (alpha or the luminance threshold used), subjectPixels {image, reference}, maskCoverage {image, reference} (fractions), degenerateMask (null or why the IoU was withheld), emptyMaskNote (set when neither image has a subject pixel), iouNote, limitNote.

Refused: an unknown key; image or reference missing, or not an existing file (NOTHING was compared); compare_px outside 16-512 (NOTHING was compared); a non-finite compare_px or threshold; an image that loads with a zero dimension; and two images whose aspect ratios differ after scaling, refused after both were loaded, with 'No comparison was performed' - render at the reference's aspect ratio first.
bl_create_action:
Create a named action, optionally assigning it to an object.

NAMING IS THE ENTIRE POINT. An object gets whatever Blender auto-named its action, and that string is what glTF and FBX write into the engine as the clip name - so every clip exported through this bridge arrived downstream named after nothing. Nothing here could set it.

fake_user DEFAULTS TRUE. A freshly created, unassigned action has zero users by definition, so without a fake user it would be deleted by the next save. Where a default can either lose work or keep it, this one keeps it.

nameWasTaken is reported because Blender uniquifies silently: ask for 'Walk' when one exists and you get 'Walk.001', and a caller who then looks up 'Walk' finds a DIFFERENT action, or none.
bl_create_camera:
Create a Blender camera, optionally aimed at a point.

look_at derives the rotation for you. This matters more than it sounds: a Blender camera faces its local -Z, not +X and not +Z, which is the single thing hand-written camera aiming gets wrong first - the first version of this op was off by pi and pointed 166 degrees away from its target while returning a perfectly plausible euler. Passing look_at AND rotation is refused, because they are two answers to the same question.

lens/focal length is PERSP only and ortho_scale is ORTHO only; each is refused on the other. Depth of field is only enabled when f_stop or dof_distance is given, so a plain camera is never silently defocused.

make_active (default true) also sets scene.camera, and the response reports both isSceneCamera and previousSceneCamera so a caller can put it back.
bl_create_collection:
Create a Blender collection and LINK it into the scene, because bpy.data.collections.new() alone makes one that belongs to no scene - its objects are outside the view layer, outside the depsgraph and outside the render, while every field on it reads perfectly. Before this the only collection creation anywhere in the addon was a private helper inside bl_set_light_linking that made an EMPTY one, so light linking could reach only its broken state (litsNothing) and nothing could fix it without bl_run_python. Pass objects to fill it at birth. The postcondition is REACHABILITY from the scene collection, not existence.

Parameters: name (str, required; the op also accepts the key collection for it), parent (str, default None: the scene's root collection) is an existing collection to nest the new one under; link (bool, default None, which the op reads as true) links the new collection into the scene tree - false makes a deliberately unlinked collection, in no scene, and the reply says inScene false with a note; color_tag (str, default None) is the outliner color, NONE or COLOR_01..COLOR_08 (upper-cased before it is written; an empty string is ignored). Every object in objects is resolved before anything is created.

The postcondition is that the collection is reachable from the scene collection, checked under the name Blender actually gave it (Blender may shorten or suffix a name).

OUT: ok, collection (the name Blender gave it), requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, parent (null when unlinked), inScene, objectCount, objects (sorted names), colorTag, note (null unless link was false).

Refused with nothing changed: a missing name; a name a collection already has (link objects into it with bl_link_objects instead); an object in objects that does not exist; objects that is neither a list nor a single name; a parent that does not exist (the refusal lists the collections); parent together with link=false; a color_tag Blender rejects (the new collection is removed again); a linked collection that is not reachable from the scene afterwards (removed again).
bl_create_light:
Create a Blender light: type POINT, SUN, SPOT or AREA; energy in watts (a SUN's is irradiance), color [r,g,b], rotation in RADIANS. Type-specific settings are REFUSED on the wrong type rather than ignored - spot_angle on a POINT light is an error, not a no-op. rotation and spot_angle/angle are RADIANS. The response reports what the light IS, read back off the datablock. COLOUR TEMPERATURE IN KELVIN: temperature is how lighting is actually specified - 3200 tungsten, 6500 daylight - rather than as linear RGB, and it MULTIPLIES the colour rather than replacing it, so colour becomes a tint. Refused by name on a Blender without bpy.types.Light.use_temperature rather than silently ignored.

type is validated against THIS Blender's own enum rather than a remembered list. spot_angle/spot_blend are SPOT only, size/size_y/shape are AREA only, angle is SUN only, and radius (soft-shadow size) is POINT/SPOT only; passing one on the wrong type is an error naming the mismatch - Blender itself would simply not have the attribute, and the write would vanish. The reported `name` may differ from what you asked for: Blender appends .001 on a name collision rather than failing or overwriting.
bl_create_light_probe:
Create an EEVEE LIGHT PROBE - the objects that give a scene reflections and bounced light. The addon could make every other lighting object and not this one: bl_create_light makes lamps and the bl_set_light_* ops tune them, while a probe is what makes that light appear in a reflection or fill a room indirectly. A PROBE EMITS NOTHING - it captures its surroundings, so one placed where nothing reflective sits is the usual reason it looks like it does nothing. BLENDER RENAMED ALL THREE TYPES AT 4.2 and they are aliased here so one script works on 3.6 and 5.0 without branching: SPHERE/CUBE/CUBEMAP are one probe, PLANE/PLANAR another, VOLUME/GRID the third. On 3.6 the name you pass and the name Blender reports DIFFER - you pass CUBE and it calls the result CUBEMAP - so the response carries requestedType, passedType and type separately. FROM 4.2 EACH TYPE IS ITS OWN CLASS with different fields: only the SPHERE one has falloff, clipEnd and influence_type, while PLANE and VOLUME carry influence_distance and clip_start and nothing else. A setting the chosen type does not have is REFUSED naming that, rather than dropped, and `settingsOnThisType` in the response lists what this probe actually took. On 3.6 there is one class and all five apply to every type. Parameters: location (default None = origin) and rotation (default None = [0, 0, 0], Euler XYZ in RADIANS, written to rotation_euler) each take [x, y, z] or a partial {x, y, z} dict (missing axes are 0; a dict naming none of them is refused). clip_end (float, default None = Blender's own) is the far distance the probe captures to; from 4.2 only the SPHERE (CUBE) probe has it, so on a PLANE or VOLUME probe it is refused. No range check is applied beyond the value being a number. collection links the probe into that collection instead of the scene's root collection, as bl_create_empty does; an unknown name is refused before anything is made.

OUT: name, dataName, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, objectType, requestedType (as passed, upper-cased), passedType (the spelling this build's new() took), type (what Blender reports), location, note, then whichever of influenceType, influenceDistance, falloff, clipStart, clipEnd this probe type has, read back, and settingsOnThisType (the list of those names). Rotation is not read back.

Refusals ("NOTHING was created." in each): a type this build does not accept under any of its aliases (the message lists both); a setting the chosen type does not carry on this build (the half-made probe is removed first); influence_type outside this build's enum (read from bpy; ELIPSOID or BOX on current builds, the probe is removed); a malformed or non-finite location or rotation; intensity, gridResolution, resolution, dataDisplaySize, energy and color are refused with the reason (version-specific, or a probe emits nothing); any other unknown key.
bl_create_material: Create a Blender material with a Principled BSDF - base_color [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a], metallic and roughness can be set inline. Before this the addon could assign material slot NAMES and could not create a material or set a single shading value. `reuse` makes it get-or-create and STILL APPLIES the inline values, which is right when you mean to set them and fatal when you are only fetching the material: a Principled input that some node DRIVES ignores its default value completely, so writing one is refused rather than silently doing nothing. `skip_linked_inputs` is for the get-or-create case - a driven input is left alone and NAMED in skippedLinkedInputs alongside the node driving it, while every unlinked value is still written normally. It is off by default so the refusal still catches a caller who meant it. The case this exists for: a pipeline calls create_material with the same literal values in several stages purely to fetch the material, then a later stage wires a procedural pattern into Base Color, and every one of those earlier calls starts failing - which is exactly what made the bunker showcase unrunnable in its own documented stage order until 2026-09-07. The reported name is echoed from the material, not the request: bpy.data.materials.new appends .001 on a collision and never says so; reuse=True returns the EXISTING material instead of a numbered copy when the name is taken. copy_from copies a material's node tree under the new name (one per row of a hair atlas, each with its own Mapping offset); the name Blender gave and both node counts come back. Refused with reuse, or when the source does not exist.
bl_create_primitive:
Create a primitive mesh in Blender - kind: cube, sphere (alias uvsphere), icosphere, cylinder, cone, torus, plane, grid, circle or monkey; a cube takes size (its full edge), a sphere radius. A CONE takes radius1/radius2 and a TORUS takes major_radius/minor_radius - neither accepts size or radius, and passing the wrong one is refused rather than reinterpreted. align is WORLD/VIEW/CURSOR; fill_type (NGON/TRIFAN/NOTHING) applies to a circle, a cylinder and a cone, whose ends are fans by default, and is refused by name elsewhere. THE FOUNDATIONAL CREATION OP - before this every mesh had to enter through bl_import_mesh, so the bridge could edit assets authored elsewhere and could not originate a single vertex. An unknown kind is REFUSED with the full list rather than defaulting to a cube, because a silently substituted shape survives all the way to an Unreal import. Per-kind parameters (segments/ring_count on a sphere, vertices/depth on a cylinder, subdivisions on an icosphere, x/y_subdivisions on a grid) are refused when passed to a kind that has no such parameter, rather than raising a TypeError from deep inside Blender. The reported `name` is the one the object ACTUALLY has: Blender never fails and never overwrites on a collision, it appends .001, so a request for 'Crate' can yield 'Crate.003' and every later op addressing 'Crate' would hit the wrong object. Geometry facts are nested under `object`, matching bl_object_info.

TORUS SEGMENTS (2026-10-05): major_segments and minor_segments are the torus operator's own counts (48 x 12 by default; a donut used 48 x 18) - a torus of 48 x 18 has 864 vertices and 864 faces. Like the other extras they are refused by name on any other kind.
bl_decimate_mesh: Reduce a mesh's triangle count in Blender - the LOD edit a game pipeline wants most, and where analyze_skeletal_split's triangle counts finally have somewhere to go. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. A DISSOLVE's merged n-gons are split into triangles unless keep_ngons. THREE MODES, because Blender's decimate modifier is three different algorithms under one name: COLLAPSE (default) is ratio-driven quadric edge collapse and the general-purpose one - pass ratio (0-1, the fraction of faces to KEEP) or target_tris (an absolute count, from which the ratio is solved); UNSUBDIV reverses subdivision and is only sensible on quad grids that WERE subdivided, driven by iterations; DISSOLVE is a planar merge driven by angle_limit degrees, so it removes only geometry that was already flat and may legitimately remove NOTHING on a tight mesh. THE RESPONSE REPORTS WHAT HAPPENED, NOT WHAT YOU ASKED: a collapse decimate solves for a face budget and cannot split a triangle to hit a target exactly, so you get trisBefore, trisAfter and ratioAchieved beside ratioRequested, and a note when they diverge by more than 0.05. If nothing was removed at all it says so in words rather than returning ok with two identical counts. A result with NO faces left - a DISSOLVE near 180 degrees does that to any closed shape - answers emptied:true with a note. angle_limit must be 0-180 degrees and iterations 0-32767, because Blender clamps anything else without a word, and a parameter the mode does not read (angle_limit outside DISSOLVE, iterations outside UNSUBDIV) is refused rather than ignored. WARNS rather than silently damaging: custom split normals do not survive a COLLAPSE (use DISSOLVE, or re-author them) and UV layers are stretched across the survivors rather than re-unwrapped. dry_run reports the counts and warnings and modifies nothing. Applied through Blender's own modifier, never a hand-rolled collapse, and the modifier is removed if applying it throws so no stranded modifier can change a later export invisibly.
bl_delete_collection:
Delete a Blender collection and say what became of its objects. bpy.data.collections.remove() deletes the collection and leaves the objects alone, which sounds safe and is exactly how objects end up in no collection at all - still in bpy.data, in no scene, invisible, surviving the save. So this decides it explicitly: objects that would be stranded move to the scene root (or reparent_to), or are deleted outright with delete_objects. Objects that are ALSO in another collection are left where they are rather than silently reorganised. Child collections are relinked rather than orphaned. Only objects the deletion would strand are rehomed: an object also linked in another collection or the scene root stays there, and objectsKeptElsewhere maps each such object to the homes it keeps (with a keptNote when reparent_to was given). bl_link_objects with move:true moves them. With delete_objects, rigid bodies leave the physics world first, as bl_delete_object's do: a joint holding one of the collection's bodies is deleted with it even when it sits elsewhere (jointsRemovedWithBodies), and a rigid body bake the delete leaves stale is freed (freedRigidBodyBake, rigidBodyBakeNote).

CHANGE CAP: it has no preview, so a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct data-blocks (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) is refused, writing nothing, and says to split it or have the user raise the cap (docs/15 section 6).
bl_delete_keyframe:
Remove keyframes from a Blender channel - the correction path bl_set_keyframe never had, which forced delete-and-recreate for any mistake. Omit frame to clear every key on the path; omit index to clear every array element. Counted before and after off the fcurves, because keyframe removal reports a bool that is False both for 'there was nothing there' and for 'it refused', and those are different answers. The response carries keyframesBefore, keyframesAfter, removed and countsAgree - the last is the op checking its own arithmetic against the curve rather than asking you to trust it.

Omit frame to clear EVERY key on the path; omit index to clear every array element. A path with no fcurve is refused with a pointer to bl_list_keyframes rather than reported as a successful deletion of nothing.

COUNTED OFF THE CURVES, before and after. Blenders keyframe removal reports a bool that is False both for there-was-nothing-there and for it-refused, and those are different answers. The response carries keyframesBefore, keyframesAfter, removed and countsAgree - the last is this op checking its own arithmetic against the curve instead of asking you to trust it.

Keys are removed in REVERSE order, because removing during an ascending walk shifts the collection underneath and silently skips every second key. A NODE TREE: target world, material or node_group with datablock (its name) works on that tree's own curves instead of an object's - data_path is the path on the tree, e.g. 'nodes["Mapping"].inputs[2].default_value'.
bl_delete_mesh_elements:
Delete part of a Blender mesh: elements VERTS, EDGES, FACES or ONLY_FACES, chosen by ONE of indices (from bl_select_faces or bl_vertex_info), vertex_group with min_weight (default 0.5), or loose_islands_under N (every face-connected island with fewer faces), occluded_by {meshes, reach, margin} or disagree_with {reference, maxDistance, minDot}. Counts before and after; a selector that matches nothing is refused. WHY: no op deleted part of a mesh, and the garment work did it in raw Python again and again - the inner shell a solidify left, body faces hidden under clothing, the one-face islands a voxel remesh leaves. FACES (the default for indices and islands) takes a face's now-unused edges and vertices with it; ONLY_FACES keeps them (Blender's Delete > Only Faces); VERTS (the default for vertex_group) takes every face on them. Islands are face-connected; the reply lists islandFaceCounts, largest first, and islandsRemoved. Indices are of the kind elements names. One selector per call.

OCCLUDED (2026-10-05): occluded_by {meshes: [names], reach (default 0.1 m), margin (default 1)} deletes the faces hidden under other meshes - a body under its outfit, the robust fix for skin poking through. A face is covered when a ray along its normal from its centre and from each of its vertices meets one of the meshes within reach (the object as its base mesh under its transform, the meshes as they evaluate - compare them in the same pose); margin rings of covered faces that share an edge with an uncovered face are kept, so the cut sits under the cloth. A mesh's own open border is no cut and keeps no margin. Reply occludedBy {facesCovered, facesKeptByMargin}. Measured: a 10x10 grid under a 0.6 x 0.5 m cover 5 cm above loses its 20 wholly covered faces, or 8 with margin 1.

DISAGREEING (2026-10-05): disagree_with {reference, maxDistance (default 0.01 m), minDot (default 0.3)} deletes every face whose centre is farther than maxDistance from the reference surface or whose normal's dot with the reference's normal at the nearest point is under minDot - the outer sheet of a thickened, voxel-remeshed garment kept by agreement with the garment it came from. Reply disagreeWith {facesTooFar, facesTurnedAway, facesKept}. Measured: an open 2 m box solidified 5 cm inward (14 faces) keeps exactly its 5 outer faces.
bl_fold_boundary_under: Fold a single-sheet Blender mesh's open rim under itself - edge-only thickness for a hem, cuff or opening: a wall thickness down (default 5 mm) and a lip depth back under (15 mm), world units. loop_near [x,y,z] folds one loop; straighten smooths the rim first. WHY: a draped garment is one sheet, so its hem, cuffs and openings read as paper in a render; Solidify thickens the whole sheet and doubles the triangles. A short film folded rims under in raw Python ten times. Two rings are added per boundary loop: ring 1 is the rim pushed in along minus the surface normal by thickness (the visible edge wall), ring 2 is ring 1 carried back under the fabric by depth, toward the centres of the faces the rim belongs to (a corner goes along its diagonal). The lip winds with the sheet: measured on a 2x2 sheet, 4 faces up, 8 under-lip faces down and the walls facing out, 8 new rim edges and none non-manifold. loop_near folds only the loop with the boundary vertex nearest that world point (a cuff, not the hem), and the reply carries loopNearDistance; without it every loop is folded. straighten N moves each rim vertex halfway to its two rim neighbours' midpoint N times first (a drape leaves rims ragged). A BOW-TIE vertex - more than two rim edges - is left out with its edges (skippedBowtieEdges): extruding there made non-manifold edges. group names a vertex group that receives the old rim, the folded edge, at 1.0 - for hem stitching in a high poly, or a pin. The reply has the counts before and after and boundaryEdgesAfter. Refused before any write: a mesh with no open boundary, a thickness or depth that is not above 0, straighten over 100, a loop_near that is not [x,y,z], a mirrored or uninvertible transform, and shape keys.
bl_push_out_of: Push a Blender mesh out of another to a clearance (offset, world units, default 5 mm): a garment off the body or the layer under it. side 'garment' (default) moves each vertex; 'collider' pushes the garment faces a body bump pokes through between vertices. Penetration is measured before and after. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.
