WHY: after a drape or a fit a short film's garments were pushed out of the body and the balaclava in raw Python six times, then again from the body's side, because a cloth collider keeps VERTICES out and a bump between them still pokes through - the acromion came up between hoodie vertices 1.25 cm apart. SIDE 'garment': each garment vertex within reach (default 3 cm) of the collider whose height above it, along the collider's normal, is under the offset moves out along that normal to the offset; the moves are then spread smooth rings (default 3) so no dent shows. SIDE 'collider': each COVERED collider point - a ray from 3 cm inside it along its normal meets the garment within cover_distance (default 8 cm), so a hand past a cuff or a face in a hood opening is left alone (the first recorded run chased the hands 174 mm) - against the nearest garment face within reach (default 4 cm): when the point stands less than the offset under that face, the face's vertices move out along their normals by the shortfall; repeated up to iterations (default 3) until nothing is short, then spread. skip_facing_collider (default true) leaves a garment face that looks at the body alone - a lining, a folded-under lip; skip_slots leaves faces on those material slots alone (cords riding on top); inside_box [[min],[max]] limits the test to a world box. MEASURED BOTH WAYS, before and after: garmentSide (vertices inside the collider, the worst depth, vertices under the offset) and colliderSide (collider points through the garment - the bump between vertices - the worst depth, points under the offset, points that met only a face facing them). remainingPenetration is after.colliderSide.maxPenetration. The collider is read as evaluated now (modifiers and pose applied) and the object's base mesh is written, in world units with the object's own origin as the working origin (float32 coordinates carried 240 m out and back moved by micrometres). A garment deformed by its own Armature at a posed frame is computed on its base mesh, so put the rig at rest first. dry_run plans the first pass and writes nothing. Refused before any write: one object twice, an unknown side, iterations with side 'garment', a negative offset, a reach or cover distance of 0, a malformed box, a mirrored or uninvertible transform, shape keys, and a call that tests nothing (no garment vertex within reach; no covered collider point near a garment face it may push) - which would otherwise answer clean having looked at nothing.
bl_delete_object:
Delete one object from the Blender scene by name. purge_orphans removes object data with no user - meshes, curves, lights, cameras, armatures, particle settings, in the whole file - which frees those names for a rebuild, named in orphansPurgedNames. Materials, images, node groups and actions the delete leaves with no user are KEPT and named in orphansKeptNames (since 2026-10-05: a purged car took its paint materials and the rebuild's bl_create_mesh refused them); bl_purge_orphans takes them by name, bl_clear_scene sweeps every orphan in the file. It defaults to FALSE here (unlike bl_clear_scene, which defaults it TRUE), so a mesh deleted this way leaves its mesh data behind until something purges it. Use it to clean up a specific import; bl_clear_scene is the whole-scene form. Deleting a RIGID BODY out of a baked rigid body world frees that bake (freedRigidBodyBake, rigidBodyBakeNote): the cache is stored by position in the world, so the bodies left behind would replay the deleted ones' frames. Deleting a rigid body also deletes every RIGID BODY JOINT that holds it (jointsRemovedWithBodies, and in `removed`): removing a body and its joint in the wrong order crashed Blender - 5.2.1 one way round, 4.2.17 the other - so both are taken out of the physics world first and the joint goes with its body. bl_undo takes a delete back, the object's modifiers and materials with it.

CHANGE CAP: it has no preview, so a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct data-blocks (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) is refused, writing nothing, and says to split it or have the user raise the cap (docs/15 section 6).
bl_delete_view_layer:
Remove a Blender view layer, refusing to remove the last one - a scene with no view layer cannot be rendered at all, and the API will happily let you get there.

Parameters: name (str, required) is the exact name of the view layer to remove from the CURRENT scene (bpy.context.scene); there is no scene parameter. The op also accepts the key viewLayer as an alias, which the MCP tool does not send.

OUT: ok, scene, deleted (the name), remaining (sorted names of the layers left), activeViewLayer (the window's active view layer after the removal).

Refusals: no view layer by that name in the current scene (lists the ones present; "NOTHING was changed."); it is the scene's only view layer ("NOTHING was changed."); the layer is still present after removal (an internal check, raised after the remove call); any unknown key.
bl_derive_image_map:
Derive a HEIGHT, NORMAL or SPECULAR map from one Blender colour image (luminance as height, blur and contrast, strength and green-up/down for normals, a 0-0.5 range for specular) as a new image; filepath also saves it.

kind (str, required, case-insensitive): HEIGHT | NORMAL | SPECULAR. name (str, default None: '<image>_<kind>', the source name with any extension dropped and kind in lower case). invert (bool, default None: false) makes dark high instead of light. flip_green (bool, default None: false) is NORMAL only and writes green down (DirectX) instead of Blender's green up; passing it at all with another kind is refused. value_range [lo, hi] (list, default None: [0, 0.5]; sent as range) is SPECULAR only and maps height 0-1 onto lo..hi. colorspace (str, default None: 'Non-Color') is set on the new image; any name this Blender's colour management offers. Height is the luminance of the stored pixels, blurred (blur 0-256 px, fraction dropped), then contrast about 0.5, clamped to 0-1, then inverted. The new image is a float image with a fake user; filepath saves it as PNG through bl_save_image.

OUT: image, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, source, kind, size [w, h], valueRange [min, max] over RGB, mean [r, g, b], settings {strength, blur, contrast, invert, flipGreen, range} (null where the kind ignores it), colorSpace, saved (bl_save_image's reply or null), note (the green convention, NORMAL only).

Refused before anything is created: an unknown key; no such image, or a viewer image; a kind outside the three; strength with a kind other than NORMAL; blur outside 0-256; flip_green or value_range with the wrong kind; value_range not two finite numbers; an output path the path check refuses; a source under 2x2 pixels; a colour space this Blender lacks (the image just made is removed). Any failure after the image exists, including the save, removes it before re-raising.
bl_describe_material: Read one Blender material in full: its Principled BSDF values, the node tree shape, every image texture with its FILE PATH, and with links=true every node link as from/to 'Node.Socket'. The texture paths are the point for a pipeline - they are what an Unreal-side import has to resolve, and nothing in the addon reported them before. `resolvedInputs` names the socket spelling this Blender version uses. links=True also returns every node connection. nodes=True adds every node's SETTINGS and socket values - a Noise texture's scale, a colour ramp's stops, a Mapping node's rotation - which is what makes this a read-back for a PROCEDURAL material rather than a summary of one. Without it a graph of noise, a ramp and a bump node reports as three names and a link list: correct, and no help to somebody asking whether the scale they just wrote landed. A LINKED input reports its SOURCE and not its default value, because Blender evaluates the link and never reads default_value on a connected socket - printing the stale default beside a live connection is how a caller comes to believe a number nothing renders. `settings` reports every setting bl_set_material_settings writes that this build has (blendMethod, backfaceCulling, alphaThreshold, surfaceRenderMethod and the rest), read off the same map, so the read side cannot fall behind the write side.
bl_duplicate_collection: Duplicate a Blender collection with its objects and child collections under new_name: each object copied once (linked shares its mesh), parents remapped to the copies. WHY: a whole collection copied into a low-poly and a high-poly pair for a bake went through raw Python. Every object anywhere under the collection is copied once (bl_duplicate_object's copy), every child collection is copied with the copies linked in the same places, and a copy whose parent was copied too is parented to that copy. Child collections keep their names, suffixed by Blender; every name is echoed (collections, objects). parent puts the copy under that collection; by default it is linked wherever the source is (the scene root for a collection linked nowhere). inScene says the copy is reachable from the scene.
bl_duplicate_object: Duplicate Blender objects under new names (names, or suffix): a full copy with its own mesh, or linked (the same mesh, as Alt+D); offset, rotation (radians) and scale; include_children; hide original or copy. WHY: the most basic object operation had no typed call - a shell made from a copy of a donut, a light made from the sun, six variants from one, a simulated shirt kept as a hidden backup, a high-poly copy for a bake all went through raw Python. objects is a list or one name. names gives one name per object; suffix adds to each source name; with neither each copy asks for its source's name and Blender appends .001 - every copy's actual name, requestedName and nameWasSuffixed come back. linked shares the data, so an edit to one mesh shows on both; materials and any action are shared either way, as Blender's own duplicate does. collection puts every copy there; by default each copy joins its source's collections. offset [x,y,z] is in world units, rotation [x,y,z] turns each copy about its own origin, scale multiplies its scale. include_children copies each object's children too, parented to the copies (listed under children). hide 'original' or 'copy' hides that one in the view layer and the render. Every name and target is checked before anything is made: an unknown object or collection, names of the wrong count, names with suffix, a 0 in scale, and a child listed beside its parent with include_children are refused, nothing created.
bl_edit_fcurve:
Change how a Blender curve moves BETWEEN its keys. bl_set_keyframe can set an interpolation at INSERT time and reaches three of Blender's thirteen; nothing could change one afterwards, and nothing could touch EASING at all - which is most of the craft in motion graphics, where BACK with ease-out versus LINEAR is the entire look. Retiming or re-feeling an existing animation meant deleting and re-keying it. Omit frame to apply to every key on the curve, omit index for every array element. All four enums are validated against this Blender's own RNA rather than a remembered list. amplitude and period shape an ELASTIC key (period is in FRAMES; the default spring is 0.3 of the segment and on a long one is over almost at once) and back sets a BACK key's overshoot - each is read back into keyParamsAfter, and a key whose interpolation ignores it is named in warnings.

Change how a curve moves BETWEEN its keys - interpolation, easing, handle type, extrapolation.

bl_set_keyframe can set an interpolation at INSERT time and reaches three of Blenders thirteen. Nothing could change one afterwards, and nothing could touch EASING at all - which is most of the craft in motion graphics, where BACK with ease-out against LINEAR is the entire look.

easing is the DIRECTION an easing interpolation runs (AUTO / EASE_IN / EASE_OUT / EASE_IN_OUT) and is meaningless without one of the easing interpolations set.

extrapolation is a property of the CURVE, not of its keys, and controls what happens outside the keyed range - which is a different question from looping, and a much blunter answer than a CYCLES modifier.

Omit frame to apply to every key on the curve; omit index for every array element. Every enum is validated against this Blenders own RNA rather than a remembered list, and everything is checked before anything is written.

amplitude and period shape an ELASTIC key, and back a BACK key, per key. period is in FRAMES between swings: its default is 0.3 of the segment, so on a long segment the spring is over almost at once, and a longer period is what makes it read. amplitude 0 swings as far as the move itself; larger boosts every swing. Each is read back from the keys into keyParamsAfter, and a key whose interpolation does not use one is named in warnings rather than silently accepted.

CURVE FLAGS AND HANDLE COORDINATES (2026-10-04): mute, lock and hide write the curve's own flags (FCurve.mute, .lock, .hide - the same three on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2); a muted curve stops animating its channel, which keeps its last value - only NLA tracks had a mute before (bl_set_nla_track). curveFlags gives each curve's flags before and after. handle_left and handle_right [frame, value] place one key's handle (frame is required, and index when the path has several curves): a handle pulled in X only holds a curve up longer before it drops. AUTO and AUTO_CLAMPED recompute a handle on the next update, so the key's handle type is set first - FREE when both sides are given, ALIGNED when one is (Blender keeps the other side in line, at its own length) - and handleTypeNote names the type it had. Measured on keys 3: 0 and 17: 10 (BEZIER): handle_right [10, 0] on the key at 3 turned AUTO_CLAMPED into ALIGNED, the left handle stayed on the line through the key, and frame 7 read 1.228 against 1.983 before. handlesAfter reads both handles and types back. Refused, NOTHING changed: handles without frame, with handle_type AUTO, AUTO_CLAMPED or VECTOR, a left handle after its key or a right one before it (the curve would loop back), not [frame, value], a non-boolean flag. A NODE TREE: target world, material or node_group with datablock (its name) works on that tree's own curves instead of an object's - data_path is the path on the tree, e.g. 'nodes["Mapping"].inputs[2].default_value'.

A DRIVER'S RESPONSE CURVE: driver true edits the driver of the driven property data_path (on the object, its data or its shape keys - data.shape_keys.key_blocks["X"].value is found on the Key) instead of an action's curve; frame then names a key by its INPUT value. value (with frame, one curve) moves that key's output, its handles with it - pulling a driver's end key from 2 to 1.2 - and keyAfter reads it back.
bl_evaluate_at_frame:
What a Blender object ACTUALLY is at a LIST of frames, read through the evaluated depsgraph: each sample's world location/rotationEuler/scale, plus any data_paths you name. Every other read in this addon reads the RAW property off the datablock, which is not what the scene evaluates to whenever a constraint, driver, NLA stack, parent or simulation cache is involved - a constraint does not touch obj.matrix_world at all, so reading the base object reports every constraint as having done nothing. This is the substrate for verifying anything procedural: reading back the value you wrote is a proxy that cannot fail. The scene frame is restored and the restoration is ASSERTED, because leaving somebody's scene on frame 47 as a side effect of a READ is exactly the quiet damage this bridge refuses. movedAcrossFrames answers the question behind most uses - a list of identical matrices is what a dead driver, a muted NLA track and a bake that lost its motion all look like. WHERE THE OBJECT IS is each sample's top-level location/rotationEuler/scale, the world matrix: a data_paths entry like 'location' is the object's OWN channel, which keys and drivers move and a parent, a constraint or a rigid body never does - a baked body's values.location stays at its start while it falls. Asking for a transform channel reports transformChannelsDiffer, and channelsNote names what moves the object. Call mif_help("bl_evaluate_at_frame") first.

PASS A LIST OF FRAMES. A single number is accepted and wrapped. data_paths adds extra properties sampled at each frame, resolved on the EVALUATED object; one that does not resolve reports its error in place rather than failing the whole call.

frameRestored and startedOnFrame report the restoration. The depsgraph is re-fetched every frame on purpose: the evaluated object is a temporary the depsgraph owns, and holding one across a frame change reads stale data that looks plausible.

A FRAME CHANGE STEPS EVERY LIVE SIMULATION (2026-10-05): moving the scene's frame evaluates each unbaked cloth, soft body, emitter or dynamic-hair particle system, dynamic-paint canvas and rigid body world in the view layer, and a fluid domain whose cache type is REPLAY - on an object hidden with the eye or from the render too (only hide_viewport or the modifier's show_viewport off takes it out). A leftover cloth on a render-hidden object stepped against a body's collision during a pose check and asked for 58.7 GB. So a call that would move the frame past such a cache's first frame is REFUSED before anything changes, naming each simulation and the colliders it would step against; bake them, take them out of the depsgraph, or pass allow_simulation=true, and the reply's simulationsStepped and colliders say what stepped. A Geometry Nodes simulation zone is listed (geometryNodesSimulations) and not refused: Blender exposes no baked flag for it.

BONES IN WORLD SPACE: bones [names] on an armature with point HEAD (default) | TAIL adds each sample's bones {name: [x, y, z]} - the evaluated armature's world matrix times the evaluated pose bone's head or tail, the point a motion path draws (bl_motion_paths) - and boneSpacing {name: [null, gap, ...]}, the world distance each point moved since the previous sample, with bonePoint and boneMethod "depsgraph" (every frame is evaluated; nothing is inferred from curves alone).
bl_motion_paths:
Calculate, update or clear a Blender motion path of an object or pose bones and return its points (frame, world position, gap to the previous), length and spacing. Call mif_help("bl_motion_paths") first.

object; bones [names] for bone paths (an armature), else the object's own path. action CALCULATE (default) | UPDATE (recompute the existing paths after an edit) | CLEAR. type RANGE (default) | CURRENT_FRAME (frame_before / frame_after around the current frame). range SCENE (default) | KEYS_ALL | KEYS_SELECTED | MANUAL (frame_start and frame_end, both inclusive). frame_step is the display step. bake_location HEADS | TAILS for bones - a hand's path is usually its TAILS. display {lineThickness 1-6, lines, color [r,g,b], colorPost [r,g,b] (the colour after the current frame, Blender 4.2+, refused by name before), useCustomColor}. max_points (default 1000) caps the points listed; pointCount is always the whole.

Reply: paths [{bone, frameStart, frameEnd, pointCount, points [{frame, co, gap}], length, maxGap, minGap, bakeLocation, lineThickness, lines, useCustomColor, color, colorPost}], settings read back, frameRestored and modeRestored, cleared (for CLEAR). Points are WORLD positions, one per frame - the same numbers bl_evaluate_at_frame gives (its bones / point HEAD | TAIL for a bone). gap is the distance from the previous frame's point: evenly spaced dots are an even speed, bunched dots an ease.

MEASURED on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: pose.paths_calculate needs POSE mode and reads the bone SELECTION, so the call selects the bones, enters pose mode and puts both back; a bone path keeps the bake location it was made with (recalculating HEADS as TAILS leaves it on the heads), so a calculate clears the chosen paths first. Calculating steps the scene's frames, so a live simulation is refused unless allow_simulation is true. A calculate that makes no path is refused rather than answered with nothing.
bl_spread_pose:
Spread the change made to Blender pose bones at a frame over the frames before and after it with a falloff, or run Blender's pose propagate (mode). With slider BREAKDOWN, PUSH or RELAX and a factor it keys the pose sliders' in-between at the frame instead. Call mif_help("bl_spread_pose") first.

object is an armature; bones [names] | name_prefix | all pick the bones; frame is the frame the pose was changed at, which must be the scene's current frame (the default) - a bone's channels hold the pose of the current frame, so move there (bl_set_frame_range current) before posing. THE CHANGE is each chosen channel's CURRENT value minus its curve at that frame - pose the bones with bl_set_bone_pose (unkeyed) first; channels location | rotation | scale (default all three; rotation in the bone's own mode).

Falloff route: before and after (frames each side), falloff SMOOTH (default) | LINEAR | EASE_IN | EASE_OUT | NONE, influence (0-1, default 1), keys ALL_FRAMES (default: a key on every frame of the range) | EXISTING (only the keys already in the range, plus the frame itself). Each frame t gets its old value plus change x w(|t - frame| / span) x influence, span being before or after: LINEAR 1 - u, SMOOTH 1 - (3u^2 - 2u^3), EASE_IN (1 - u)^2, EASE_OUT 1 - u^2, NONE 1. Only the chosen bones' curves change, so the feet keep their own animation. Measured: a flat curve changed by 1 at frame 20 and spread 10 back and 10 forward LINEAR reads 0, 0.5, 1, 0.5, 0 at 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30.

Mode route: mode NEXT_KEY | LAST_KEY | BEFORE_FRAME (with end_frame) | BEFORE_END runs Blender's own pose.propagate, which copies the KEY at the frame to the keys its mode reaches - an unkeyed change propagates nothing there (measured on 4.2 and 5.2), so the op keys the pose at the frame first. SELECTED_KEYS and SELECTED_MARKERS are not offered: they read a key or marker selection this bridge does not make.

Reply: curves [{dataPath, index, change, keysWritten, frames, largestChange}] (mode route: keysBefore and keysAfter), unkeyed (changed channels with no curve to spread over - key them first). A call that would spread nothing - every chosen channel already equal to its curve - is refused, as are an influence over 1, before and after both 0, and falloff parameters with mode.

SLIDER ROUTE. slider BREAKDOWN, PUSH or RELAX with factor (0-1, default 0.5) keys one value per chosen channel at frame (the scene's frame), between the channel's nearest key before and nearest key after: BREAKDOWN keys prev + (next - prev) x factor; PUSH moves the current pose value away from the straight line between those keys by factor (current + (current - line) x factor); RELAX moves it toward the line (current + (line - current) x factor). A quaternion is normalized after its channels are set. A channel without a key on both sides is skipped and named (skipped); none at all is refused. Not with before, after, falloff, influence, keys, mode or end_frame. These are Blender's pose sliders (pose.breakdown / push / relax), which are modal and need a region, written as their math.
bl_filter_keys:
Smooth, Gaussian-smooth, Butterworth-filter, decimate or blend a Blender object's F-curve keys over a frame range, replying each curve's keys before and after and its largest change. The Graph Editor sliders too - ease, blend offset, blend to ease or default, match slope, scale average or from neighbor, push-pull, shear, time offset. Call mif_help("bl_filter_keys") first.

Pick the curves with ONE of data_paths ['location', 'location[0]', 'pose.bones["Hand"].rotation_euler'], bones [names] or all: true - on the object, its data and its shape keys. frame_start / frame_end limit it to the keys inside (default every key). filter and settings:
- SMOOTH: each key but the first and last in the range becomes (the key before + 2 x itself + the key after) / 4.
- GAUSSIAN {sigma (frames, default 2), width (frames, default 3 x sigma)}: a Gaussian-weighted mean of the keys within width frames.
- BUTTERWORTH {cutoff (Hz, under half the scene's fps; default 3), order 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 (default 4)}: the curve sampled every frame, low-passed forward and backward (zero phase, ends padded by odd reflection), and each key set to the filtered curve. Native on every build (Blender's own Butterworth smoothing is 4.2+).
- DECIMATE {ratio (the share of the range's keys to keep) | error (the largest change allowed, in the curve's units)}: the first and last keys kept, then keys kept where the curve would be missed most; with error, keys are put back until no whole frame of the range moves by more than error on the rebuilt curve.
- BLEND_TO_NEIGHBOR {factor -1 to 1}: each key moves |factor| of the way to the key just before the range (negative) or just after it (positive).
A moved key's handles move with it. Blender's own Graph Editor operators for these poll for a Graph Editor, which a bridge call has no window for, so the work is done on the curves directly.

Reply: filter, settings, fps, curves [{dataPath, index, keysBefore, keysAfter, keysInRange, frames, largestChange (the largest change of the evaluated curve at any whole frame of the range)}]. Refused, with nothing changed: an unknown filter or setting, two curve picks, a curve with too few keys in the range (3 for the smoothers and DECIMATE), DECIMATE with both or neither of ratio and error, a cutoff at or above half the fps, a factor of 0, and BLEND_TO_NEIGHBOR with no key on the side it blends toward.

THE GRAPH EDITOR SLIDERS, on the keys of the range with L the key just before it and R the key just after, u a key's place between them (0-1), native so every build has them: EASE {factor -1..1, default 0.5}: the keys laid on an ease from L to R, u^(1 + 4|factor|) easing in for a positive factor, its mirror easing out for a negative one. BLEND_TO_EASE {factor -1..1}: each key moves |factor| of the way to that ease. BLEND_OFFSET {factor -1..1}: the run shifted so its first key meets L (negative) or its last meets R (positive), by |factor|. BLEND_TO_DEFAULT {factor 0..1}: toward the channel's rest value (1 for scale and a quaternion's w, else 0). MATCH_SLOPE {factor -1..1}: toward the line continuing the slope of the two keys before the range (negative) or after it (positive). SCALE_AVERAGE {factor 0..2, default 1}: scaled about the run's mean. SCALE_FROM_NEIGHBOR {factor -1..1}: scaled by 1 + |factor| about L (negative) or R (positive). PUSH_PULL {factor 0..2, default 1}: the distance from the straight line L-R multiplied (over 1 pushes, under 1 pulls). SHEAR {factor -1..1, direction FROM_LEFT | FROM_RIGHT}: a ramp of factor x (R - L) added across the run. TIME_OFFSET {frames}: each key takes the curve's value from frames earlier. A slider that needs a neighbour the range lacks is refused, naming the curve.
bl_match_world_transform:
Match a Blender object's or pose bone's world transform to another's at frames, keyed, or carry it along with a moving object, replying the position and rotation error after. Call mif_help("bl_match_world_transform") first.

object (+ bone) moves; target (+ target_bone) is matched - the parent, the parent inverse and a bone's rest are applied through Blender's own setters, so a parented object or a bone on a posed chain lands exactly. frames [..] or frame_start + frame_end (default the current frame); key (default true; false matches the current frame only); channels [LOC, ROT, SCALE] (default all) - rotation is written in the holder's own mode, eulers kept continuous. relative_to (+ relative_to_bone): each frame takes relative_to(frame) x relative_to(first)^-1 x target(first) - with no target, the moved thing rides relative_to from where it stands on the first frame (a passenger in a moving vehicle). Reply frames [{frame, positionError, rotationErrorDeg, scaleError}] read through the depsgraph after the writes, and the largest of each.
bl_edit_action_slots:
Make, list, rename, assign, merge, separate or move a Blender action's slots (4.4+), or replace an action on everything that plays it. Call mif_help("bl_edit_action_slots") first.

From 4.4 an action keeps its curves per SLOT and each user plays one slot; two objects on one slot play and key the same curves. op:
- LIST: slots [{identifier, name, idType, users, curves}]. users counts NLA strips that play the slot.
- NEW: name, id_type (default OBJECT).
- RENAME: slot (identifier or name), name - the identifier follows (OBBall -> OBOrbiter).
- ASSIGN: object, target object | data | shape_keys, and slot or new_slot true (a slot of the holder's kind, named name or after the holder). Replies sharedWith - the other users of that slot.
- SEPARATE: one action per slot, named <action>_<slot name>.
- MOVE_TO_NEW: slots [..] and new_action: those slots and their curves move to a new action.
- MERGE: from_actions [..]: their slots and curves are copied into this action.
- REPLACE: new_action plays instead of this one through the slot with the same identifier (every build).
Every user - an active action or an NLA strip, on an object, its data, a Key or a node tree - is rebound, and the reply lists them. On 4.2 every op but REPLACE is refused by name. bl_assign_action binds an existing slot; bl_list_actions rows carry slots on 4.4+.
bl_set_modifier:
Change the settings of a modifier ALREADY on a Blender object's stack, or move it (index, or move UP, DOWN, TOP or BOTTOM) - the half bl_add_modifier left write-once. `settings` takes either the curated camelCase names bl_add_modifier and bl_list_modifiers use (foamCoverage, vertexGroup, offsetObject - validated exactly as bl_add_modifier validates them) or ANY writable RNA property by its identifier (foam_layer_name, spectrum, limit_method, show_render, use_axis), read off bl_rna at call time the way bl_set_constraint is: enums validated against their own items, finite numbers only, strict booleans, a datablock pointer by NAME with Blender's poll read back, a vertex group or UV map name checked against the object. Naming one attribute twice (foamCoverage and foam_coverage) is refused. ALL OR NOTHING: every attribute is snapshotted and restored if any key refuses. The effect is MEASURED: evaluatedChanged compares the evaluated mesh before and after, and evaluatedNote says when a setting moved no vertex - right for a render toggle or a layer name. Why it exists: an Ocean's foam is a colour attribute a material reads BY NAME, and its name (foam_layer_name) was settable by no op; re-tuning choppiness or a bevel's width meant removing and re-adding the modifier. A geometry-nodes modifier's group and inputs stay with bl_assign_node_group. A FLUID MODIFIER'S SETTINGS ARE ON ITS ROLE: its own property is only fluid_type, so a key it lacks is written on the live role's struct - domain_settings, flow_settings or effector_settings - e.g. use_dissolve_smoke, dissolve_speed, use_collision_border_top, vorticity, flame_vorticity, burning_rate, use_noise, time_scale on a domain; fuel_amount, temperature, surface_distance (in grid CELLS, not metres) on a flow. A key another role owns is refused naming that role; bl_list_modifiers(rna=True) reads the role back under its identifier. A cloth's, collision's or soft body's settings are on its structs - settings, collision_settings, point_cache - sent nested ({"collision_settings": {"distance_min": 0.01}}) or flat when one struct has the key, and read back as collision_settings.distance_min. The stack evaluates top to bottom, so order is behaviour: index or move places the modifier, read back in stackBefore and stackAfter; a move Blender declines, or one that changes nothing, is refused, and with settings the move is undone if a setting refuses.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): an OCEAN's viewport_resolution, foam_layer_name, use_spray, spray_layer_name, invert_spray, filepath, frame_start, frame_end and bake_foam_fade are written by RNA name and read back exactly with bl_list_modifiers(rna=True) on every build. A Subdivision Surface's adaptive dicing is the adaptive argument (test_blender_gaps_44_52_rest).
bl_set_nla_strip:
Edit an existing Blender NLA strip - frames, action range, repeat, scale, blends, mute, reverse, name, its slot (4.4+) and sync length - replying it before and after. Call mif_help("bl_set_nla_strip") first.

strip names it (default the track's only strip). frame_start moves the strip keeping its length; frame_end sets the length (not with repeat or scale); action_start / action_end choose the part of the action played; repeat and scale stretch it. slot (identifier or name) is the action slot the strip plays - a strip made on an object whose slot is not named for it plays none and moves nothing; given its first slot it takes that slot's key range. sync_length true sets the action range to the slot's keys now and keeps it synced. Every value is checked before any is written.
bl_export_mesh:
Export Blender objects to FBX for reimport into Unreal - object_name, or objects for one file in which every mesh keeps the scene origin as its pivot. The two axis arguments are the whole ballgame and are set for you: axis_up='Z', axis_forward='Y', which are NOT the operator defaults ('Y' / '-Z', the Maya convention) - the defaults produce a mesh that arrives in Unreal rotated. Unit scale is baked (apply_unit_scale with FBX_SCALE_NONE) so the file carries centimetre-magnitude numbers in a cm-declared scene; bake_space_transform stays OFF (experimental). The response re-stats the path and reports fileExists and fileSizeBytes, so a silent zero-byte write is a failure rather than an ok. SKELETAL EXPORT: object_types defaults to ['MESH'], which is why this used to write a rigged character as a static mesh - and worse, io_scene_fbx only preserves the REST POSE when ARMATURE is in that set, so without it the Armature modifier is evaluated like any other and the mesh is written DEFORMED INTO ITS CURRENT POSE, silently, in a perfectly valid file. Pass object_types=['MESH','ARMATURE'] for a skinned character; the deforming armature is added to the export selection for you, because naming it in object_types alone is not enough - the exporter gathers its objects from the selection. When a deformer is left out you now get deformerNotExportedWarning naming it rather than discovering it on import. add_leaf_bones defaults to FALSE here, deliberately disagreeing with Blender's True: a leaf bone is a synthetic chain-tip Blender adds to record bone length, and Unreal imports each one as a REAL extra <parent>_end bone that then shows up in every retarget chain and anim asset. armature_deform_only skips non-deforming bones. Nothing is needed on the Unreal side - UFbxFactory auto-detects skeletal versus static from the file. ON TRANSFORMS: an object transform that is not identity means the pivot moved, and bl_mesh_roundtrip gates on it - but do NOT reflexively apply one. See bl_apply_transform, which explains the case where applying is exactly wrong. LOCAL SPACE: local_space=True writes the file round the object's own origin - as if it stood at the origin, unrotated, its scale kept - and puts the object back, by value, before the call returns. Unreal's FBX import bakes each node's world transform into the vertices, so without it a tree standing at (5, 3, 0) arrives with its pivot meters from its trunk. The move is checked, and refused with nothing written, when a constraint, driver or animation holds the transform or when a modifier reads where the object stands (a Boolean against another object). The answer's localSpace block carries placementMatrix - the location and rotation left out - for placing the imported asset - and written, one row per mesh in the file's frame: its box, triangles, materialSlotCount and materialsUsed (the material in each slot at least one written polygon uses; an unused slot makes no slot in Unreal); mif_send_to_unreal does all of it in one call. An existing file is REPLACED by default and the answer says so: overwrote, and when true replacedBytes and replacedModified (UTC), measured off the old file before the write; overwrite=False refuses the path by name. A mesh with shape keys loses ALL of them when the export applies its modifiers (use_mesh_modifiers, the default): measured on 5.2.1, a keyed cube with a Displace came back with no keys, and so did one whose only modifier was an Armature with the rig left out of the file. Such meshes are named in shapeKeysDropped with shapeKeysDroppedWarning, before the write. ANIMATION: with bake_anim true, bake_anim_all_actions (Blender's default true: every action that fits the rig is its own take, named <object>|<action>), bake_anim_nla (default true), bake_anim_simplify (0-100, 0 keeps every key) and bake_anim_force_keying choose what is baked; all-actions and NLA both off write the one 'Scene' take of the timeline (measured on 5.2.1: all-actions off with NLA left on writes no curves at all). They are refused with bake_anim off. animations_only writes the skinned meshes' armatures alone with bake_anim on - the takes and no geometry - for the second file of a mesh-then-animations export; it is refused with object_types, with bake_anim false, or when no exported mesh is skinned. A mesh parented to a bone or held by a Child Of constraint is named in boneParented with boneParentedWarning: it is not skinned, and the engine's FBX importer can drop such a mesh without a word.

SCALE AND SEVERAL OBJECTS (2026-10-04). global_scale (0.001-1000, the exporter's own range) and apply_scale_options (the build's own list: FBX_SCALE_NONE, FBX_SCALE_UNITS, FBX_SCALE_CUSTOM, FBX_SCALE_ALL) change the pins only when sent: a call with neither writes FBX_SCALE_NONE and 1.0 exactly as before, so 1 Blender unit is 100 Unreal units. objects [names] writes one file from several meshes, each keeping the scene origin as its pivot (layout done in the engine is the other answer: one file gives every object that pivot); object beside objects is refused.

WHERE THE SCALE GOES, measured by reading the written files back with Blender's own FBX parser on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1 (identical): a 2 BU tall box at global_scale 0.25 - FBX_SCALE_NONE: node scale (Lcl Scaling) 25 x 25 x 50, UnitScaleFactor 1; FBX_SCALE_UNITS: node 0.25 x 0.25 x 0.5, UnitScaleFactor 100; FBX_SCALE_CUSTOM: node 100 x 100 x 200, UnitScaleFactor 0.25; FBX_SCALE_ALL: node 1 x 1 x 2, UnitScaleFactor 25. The vertices are never scaled; the scale rides on each node, which is the scaled-armature case the exporter warns about ("Some importers do not support scaled armatures!"), so a skinned export with a scale other than 1 under FBX_SCALE_NONE carries scaledArmatureWarning. All four are 50 cm once UnitScaleFactor is applied, and Blender imports each back 0.5 BU tall.

writtenHeight, on every export: the tallest mesh's heightBU, the fileUnits it is written as and the unitScaleFactor beside them, and centimetres (their product) - so a 4x error is a number before the import. An importer that ignores UnitScaleFactor reads fileUnits as centimetres.

WHAT DECIDES: the character's height in Blender units against the target (a 1.8 BU human is 180 uu with the pins), read with bl_object_info. Scale the data in Blender (an armature scale applied before export) or at import (mesh_options.uniformScale), not both. A rig that imported about four times too large was fixed by exporting at 0.25 and reimporting both the mesh and the animation; the first run reads the imported root bone's scale. Apply Transform (bake_space_transform) stays off: the exporter marks it experimental and broken with armatures and animation.

TEXTURES THAT TRAVEL WITH THE FILE (path_mode, embed_textures; 2026-10-05): path_mode is the exporter's own (AUTO by default, ABSOLUTE, RELATIVE, MATCH, STRIP, COPY). COPY with embed_textures=true writes each image file the exported materials read inside the .fbx - the reply's embeddedImages counts the images found in the written file by their own bytes, imagesNotEmbedded names any that were not (a generated or missing image has no file to embed). COPY alone copies the images into an <name>.fbm folder beside the file, named in texturesCopied. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: embed_textures with any mode but COPY writes no image anywhere - Blender ignores it - so that pair is refused before the write. An embedded file imports with its images packed.

facing_body (2026-10-05) - a body's name or {body, maxInwardShare (default 0.1), bandStep, reach} - measures each exported mesh as bl_mesh_quality facing_against does and refuses BEFORE the write when more than maxInwardShare of its faces near the body point into it; the reply's facingBody lists each mesh's share.

Tangent space (2026-10-05) is written by default (use_tspace true): a mesh with zero-area UV faces imported into Unreal 5.8.2 warning 'nearly zero tangents' without it and clean with it. The reply's tangentSpace {requested, inFile, skipped, note} is read off the file, and skipped names each mesh that got none and why - no UV map, or a face of more than 4 corners with use_triangles off (the exporter skips that whole mesh). zeroAreaUvFaces lists, per mesh, the faces with zero UV area on UV channel 0 (the one Unreal builds tangents from), with zeroAreaUvNote - reported, not refused, as bl_create_mesh reports zero-area faces.

RULE - MOVING A MESH TO THE ENGINE (2026-10-06). After an edit, export over the old file and reimport each asset (reimport keeps every reference and material assignment: mif_mesh_roundtrip with repoint, or reimport_asset) - the default whenever anything already uses the asset - rather than importing new assets and swapping them in the level. The pivot: local_space true writes the object round its own origin and moves nothing in the scene, instead of resetting its location. The skeleton: an existing Skeleton when animations are shared, a new one when the character stands alone. Materials: only the standard PBR slots survive; anything else is baked (bl_bake_texture), or the textures are imported and the materials rebuilt - embed_textures with path_mode COPY carries the images but the shader still needs correcting by hand; the shader's complexity decides.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): bake_anim_all_actions on an object and its shape keys writes one take per user: on 4.4+ that is one action with two slots (the object's and the Key's), on 3.6/4.2 two actions; bl_import_mesh reads them back as '<obj>|<obj>|<action>' and 'Key|<obj>|<action>'.

SHAPE KEYS AND UNREAL'S MORPH NORMALS (split_shape_corners, default on): Unreal reads no shape normals from an FBX - every import route reads a shape's positions only - and computes a morph target's normal change itself, PER POINT, from the last face corner listed at each point (LODUtilities.cpp 5.8 :3258-3263). On a hard corner that gives every face there one face's change - a cube turned about Z arrived with none. So a keyed mesh's points are split at its hard corners in the FILE (the scene is unchanged; the corner normals written are compared before and after, and a mesh whose normals would change is written unsplit and named): shapeCornersSplit reports pointsBefore -> pointsAfter per mesh. Unreal splits render vertices at hard corners anyway, so its vertex count does not grow. Measured on 5.3.2 and 5.8.3: the turned cube's 16 side-face corners arrive at 2 sin 15 = 0.5176, unsplit at 0. split_shape_corners=False writes the points unsplit (shapeCornersNote says what that costs).

sockets [names] writes those Empties too, so Unreal's FBX importer makes each a static-mesh socket: each must be an Empty named SOCKET_<name> whose parent is one of the exported meshes, or the export is refused. EMPTY joins the written object types only with them; the reply lists socketsWritten.
bl_export_vertex_positions:
Write a Blender mesh's vertex positions (or one shape key's, with shape_key) to a .json file in Unreal's mesh frame (cm, Y negated), in its own vertex order - the file set_skeletal_mesh_vertices reads. On an import of export_asset's FBX that order is the export order.

WHY (2026-10-09): set_skeletal_mesh_vertices takes positions in export_asset's FBX order, which a Blender import of that FBX keeps, and a skeletal mesh edited in Blender could go back only as a positions list built by hand - axis and unit included - through the caller. set_skeletal_mesh_vertices with blender_object runs this and the write in one call.

THE FRAME, measured on a 5.8.2 export_asset FBX imported by bl_import_mesh (Blender 3.6-5.2): an EMPTY named after the asset (scale 0.01, the importer's centimeters) holds the ARMATURE (scale 100), which holds the MESH (scale 0.01); the mesh's vertex co is the file's own centimeters, export index for index, Unreal's Y negated. So each position is taken through the object's matrix into root's frame - default the object's topmost parent, the import's empty - and its Y negated. Moving or turning the whole import changes nothing; moving the mesh against its armature does, and warnings says so (objectToRoot is the matrix). Name root when the import was re-parented under something else; root must be the object or one of its parents.

BASE MESH: the armature modifier poses the mesh, and the bind pose is what is wanted - other modifiers are not applied and are named in warnings; with shape keys the Basis is read and the others are named. Edit mode is refused (the live edits are in the edit BMesh). The file is {positions: [[x,y,z], ...], object, root, frame}; the reply: vertexCount, root, boundsCm {min, max}, and overwrote (an existing file is replaced by default; overwrite=False refuses it). A file that is not .json, a root that is not a parent, or a non-mesh is refused with nothing written.

SHAPE KEY (2026-10-11). shape_key names a shape key: that key's coordinates are written instead of the base mesh's, in the same frame and vertex order - with set_skeletal_mesh_vertices(blender_object, shape_key, morph_target) a sculpted key becomes an Unreal morph target in one call. A name the mesh lacks is refused with the ones it has; the reply's shapeKey names the key read.
bl_extrude_skirt: Extrude the selected boundary edge loops straight DOWN by depth_uu, forming a skirt - the fix for a flat-edged tile that hovers where the terrain falls away. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. depth_uu is in UNREAL units and is sent as depthUU; the addon does the one conversion. This is the SAFE edit for anything tiled along a spline: the extrude duplicates the loop IN PLACE and the only follow-up is a translate whose X and Y components are literal zeros, so the seam planes and the tile length are untouched by construction rather than by clamping. Verified on Blender 4.4.0 against a 10x3 BU tile: dX 0.0, dY 0.0, dZ = depth, zero verts moved off the X seam planes. The op REFUSES if the selection contains a non-boundary edge, because extruding an interior edge splits the mesh instead of skirting it - run bl_select_edges first and check interiorEdges. preserve_x still sends preserveAxes+assertAxes as a belt (it should always report 0 snapped verts and offSeamVerts 0 here; anything else means the selection was not a clean boundary loop). The same two-part assert as bl_bevel_edges applies - X size AND seam planarity - and the per-axis seamPlanarity block comes back for X, Y and Z whether or not they are guarded. direction is 'down' or 'up'; there is no sideways option by design. flip_normals inverts the new side faces - the default False gave outward-facing normals on the verified case. NOTE the new skirt faces carry no meaningful UVs, so expect stretched texturing until they are authored; nothing in this pipeline does that for you.
bl_face_info:
Which faces of a Blender mesh carry which material, how many, and where they are. The second most-escaped-to question - 15 of one day's 21 bl_run_python escapes were reading per-face material - and a pure read/write asymmetry: bl_assign_material_to_faces could WRITE that relation and nothing could read it back, so every 'operate on just the glass faces' job left the typed path for bl_run_python. AGGREGATE FIRST: per-slot counts, areas and bounding boxes answer most of it in a fixed-size response, and with_faces asks for rows once you know the slot. The bounding box comes in BOTH spaces, and the world one is built from all EIGHT corners rather than by transforming min and max, which is correct only for an axis-aligned matrix and plausible-but-wrong under any rotation. Empty material slots are reported: a slot holding a material with no faces is what a wrong slot index leaves behind, and it is invisible from the material list. Truncation is never silent. An object that draws instances - Geometry Nodes instances, particles, instancing - answers with instancesNote: instances are not part of any evaluated mesh, so this does not see them (measured on 3.6-5.2).

PARAMETERS. indices (list of whole numbers, default all faces): only these face indices are counted and listed, combined with material or slot when given; indices are of the base mesh, or of the modifier result when evaluated is true. limit (whole number, default unset, which the op reads as 200): the most face rows returned; it matters only with with_faces true, and the per-slot aggregates always cover every matched face.

OUT: ok, object, geometry (base or evaluated), faceCount (the whole mesh), facesMatched, materialSlots [{slot, material, faceCount, area, bboxLocal {min, max, size}, bboxWorld {min, max, size}}] (the boxes only on a slot with matched faces), slotsWithNoFaces [slot indices holding a material and no faces], instancesNote (null unless evaluated). With with_faces: faces [{index, slot, material, area, vertexCount, centerWorld, normalWorld, smooth}], facesReturned, facesTruncated, truncationNote when truncated. emptySlotNote when a slot holds a material and no faces. In edit mode: editModeStale, objectMode, staleNote (the figures are the mesh as last left in OBJECT mode). Read-only.

REFUSED: an object that is not a MESH; material and slot together; indices that is not a list, or holds a non-whole number; a face index out of range; a negative or fractional limit; no slot holding the named material (lists the slots); a slot index out of range. Each face row (with_faces) also gives vertices, the face's vertex indices in winding order - the indices bl_vertex_info reads - so a rule that needs topology no longer keeps its own copy of the face list.
bl_file_info:
What .blend this Blender session is, whether it has unsaved work, what it holds, and - the part Blender never volunteers - which datablocks a SAVE WOULD DELETE. Anything with no users and no fake user is purged on write, permanently and silently: an unlinked action, an unused image, a node group nobody instanced. Call this before bl_save_file if the session has been edited for a while. Cheap, no parameters.

It answers the two questions that decide whether a session can be resumed at all: is there a file on disk behind this (isSaved, fileExists, fileBytes), and is there work in memory that is not in it (isDirty).

orphanCount and orphans are the reason to call it before saving. They list datablocks with no users and no fake user, across actions, images, materials, meshes, node groups, textures, armatures, cameras, lights, worlds, curves, collections and objects. A SAVE DELETES ALL OF THEM, permanently and without a word. Seeing the list first is the only warning you get.

counts is a per-type census of the file, which is the cheapest way for a caller to orient itself in a scene it did not build.
bl_gen_asset: Prompt -> reference image -> mesh -> PBR texture -> imported into the scene. THE ONE CALL that produces something usable. License: Hunyuan3D-2 is not licensed in the EU, UK or South Korea; FLUX.1 [dev] is non-commercial. It sequences bl_gen_image, bl_gen_mesh and bl_gen_texture and hands back the finished object. Set texture=false to stop at geometry when you only want the silhouette. name prefixes the ComfyUI outputs so a run's artifacts stay identifiable; seed=0 is random, so fix it to reproduce a result. shape_steps/texture_steps/octree/guidance tune the individual stages and are worth leaving alone until a default disappoints. THIS IS THE LONGEST JOB IN THE TOOLSET - default 3600s, and it holds the single Blender transport socket for the whole run, so every other bl_* tool blocks behind it (bl_status will tell you which op is holding the line and for how long). Call bl_gen_status first. GENERATIVE, ON BY DEFAULT, WITH THREE OFF-SWITCHES: it runs unless the MCP server has MIF_GENERATIVE=off, the MifBlender preference 'Allow generative tools (ComfyUI)' is unticked, or the project's mode is non-generative (mif_project_mode - the user's choice, asked for once per project). Any one of them hides and refuses this tool, and nothing contacts ComfyUI. self_audit and bl_status report generativeAllowed and which switch holds it. MODEL LICENSES: in the image stage variant 'schnell' runs FLUX.1 [schnell], Apache-2.0 (https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell); variant 'dev' runs FLUX.1 [dev] under the FLUX.1 [dev] Non-Commercial License - the model may be used only for non-commercial purposes unless Black Forest Labs grants a commercial license, while its outputs may be used commercially (https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev/blob/main/LICENSE.md). The mesh and texture stages run Hunyuan3D-2, under the Tencent Hunyuan 3D 2.0 Community License - not licensed in the European Union, the United Kingdom or South Korea, and outputs placed in public must be identified as machine generated (https://huggingface.co/tencent/Hunyuan3D-2/blob/main/LICENSE). Every successful reply carries license, a list with one block per model that call ran ({model, licenseName, licenseUrl, restrictions, tellTheUser}): tell the user those terms, which they are responsible for following. It is not legal advice; read the license. MifBridge ships no model, and checks and sends nothing about where or how it is used.
bl_gen_image: Prompt -> reference image via Flux.1, left in ComfyUI's output folder. Stage ONE; bl_gen_mesh takes the returned image name. License: FLUX.1 [schnell] is Apache-2.0, FLUX.1 [dev] is non-commercial. variant selects the Flux model ('schnell' is the fast default; 'dev' is slower and follows the prompt harder), and steps defaults to whatever suits the variant, so leave it alone unless you are deliberately trading quality for time. seed=0 means random - set it to a fixed number when you want to iterate on the same composition while changing something else. bl_import_mesh:
Import an FBX or glTF/GLB file into Blender and report what arrived. Those two only - OBJ and everything else are hard-refused, because FBX and glTF are the formats whose axis and unit round trip is verified: glTF because its SPEC fixes the convention (+Y up, metres) and FBX because it carries its own metadata in the file. UE's OBJ exporter swaps Y/Z, de-indexes and writes no normals, and the file cannot tell you it did. NOTE for glTF: it has no shared-vertex-with-split-normals concept, so vertices are de-indexed per corner and a cube's 8 come back as 24 - the geometry is identical, so compare DIMENSIONS rather than vertex counts across a round trip. use_custom_normals is an FBX option and is refused for glTF rather than silently ignored. ANIMATION: the FBX importer is told use_anim:false by default, so an animated FBX arrives as a static mesh - pass import_animation:true to keep the action. glTF has NO animation option on any supported build and always imports them, so import_animation:false is refused for glTF rather than accepted and ignored. The response reports animationImported and actionsCreated, measured from what arrived rather than from what was asked for. CLEAR_SCENE DEFAULTS TRUE HERE and deletes the objects of the scene being imported into (clear_scope 'scene', the default) - an object also linked into another scene is kept and named in sharedKept; clear_scope 'file' deletes EVERY object in the file, every scene's. It runs after every parameter has been checked and just before the import; pass clear_scene=False to import into the scene as it is. The response lists what it deleted: clearedCount, clearedObjects, and clearedFromOtherScenes for the ones that were not in the active scene. Rigid bodies leave the physics world before they are deleted, as bl_clear_scene's do, and a rigid body bake the clear leaves stale is freed and named (freedRigidBodyBake, rigidBodyBakeNote).

Import an FBX or glTF/GLB file into Blender and report what arrived. Those two only - OBJ and every other extension are hard-refused, because FBX and glTF are the formats whose axis and unit round trip is verified (UE's OBJ exporter swaps Y/Z, de-indexes to three verts per triangle and writes no normals). Pass NO axis settings anywhere: with use_manual_orientation off the importer reads FrontAxis/UpAxis/CoordAxis out of the file, and an FBX written by Unreal declares Z-up / -Y-front / right-handed / cm, which reverse-maps to Blender's own system and applies an identity conversion - the mesh lands unrotated and 1 uu becomes 0.01 Blender units. The created objects are recovered by diffing bpy.data.objects before and after, because the import operators return nothing. clear_scene defaults TRUE so each run starts from a known scene; set it false to import alongside existing objects. The clear deletes every object in the FILE - every scene, not only the active one - and runs last, after every other parameter has been checked; the response lists what went (clearedCount, clearedObjects, clearedFromOtherScenes). Returns imported[] with a full object_info per object - MORE THAN ONE object means the FBX carried LODs, collision or an armature and the source should be re-exported with level_of_detail:false and collision:false.

CHANGE CAP: it has no preview, so a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct data-blocks (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) is refused, writing nothing, and says to split it or have the user raise the cap (docs/15 section 6).

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): this reads FBX through bpy.ops.import_scene.fbx on every build; 5.0+ also has wm.fbx_import, reachable through bl_call_operator - it makes one action holding both slots where this makes one per take (see bl_call_operator).
bl_join_objects:
Join Blender mesh objects into one. DESTRUCTIVE AND ASYMMETRIC: the sources are DELETED and everything lands in target. Armatures join too: clashing bones are renamed first (rename_suffix, default .001) and REPORTED, and the skinned meshes follow. WATCH THE MATERIAL SLOTS - join MERGES the slot lists and remaps every face's material_index, so the result's slot ORDER is neither input's order, and slot order is exactly what decides which Unreal material lands on which face. The response reports the slot list before and after for that reason. `consumed` is measured from which objects actually disappeared, since join silently ignores one it cannot merge. With keep_sources=True it joins copies and leaves every source, which the change cap counts as the one object it writes; a consuming join (the default) also counts each source it removes, so 29 parts at a cap of 25 is refused, naming keep_sources.

CHANGE CAP: it has no preview. The join counts as the one object it writes - the target - plus each source it removes; with keep_sources=True no source is removed (copies are joined, kept names the sources), so it is one write however many sources (2026-11-07, as the Unreal plugin's merge_static_mesh_actors counts its pieces only when keepInputs false destroys them). Over the open file's cap of distinct data-blocks (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) it is refused, writing nothing, and the refusal names keep_sources, joins of fewer sources, or the user raising the cap (docs/15 section 6).

ARMATURES. When target is an ARMATURE every source must be one. Each source bone whose name the target (or an earlier source) already holds is renamed BEFORE the join - name + rename_suffix (default .001; a suffix ending in digits counts up, .001, .002 ...) - through the bone's name, which Blender carries into the skinned meshes' vertex groups; renamed in the reply maps {source: {old: new}}. After the join every mesh whose Armature modifier pointed at a source points at the target (meshesRepointed), a child of a source is parented to the target where it stood (childrenReparented), and boneCount is checked against the bones that went in. Hidden or out-of-view-layer rigs are refused, as for meshes. rename_suffix on a mesh join is refused.
bl_list_actions:
Every action in the Blender file, who uses it, and whether it will SURVIVE A SAVE. An action with no users and no fake user is deleted the next time the file is saved - silently, by the save succeeding - so willBeDeletedOnSave names them before that happens. Each row carries curve and keyframe counts, frame range, and usedBy built by walking objects, because an action knows its user COUNT and not their names while 'which object is this clip on' is the actual question. Action names are also the CLIP NAMES glTF and FBX write into an engine, so an auto-generated 'Action.003' becomes a name somebody downstream has to live with.

THE FIELD TO READ IS willBeDeletedOnSave. An action with no users and no fake user is removed the next time the file is written - silently, and by the save SUCCEEDING. It is the same purge bl_save_file reports as purgedOrphans, seen from the other side, and an action is the easiest thing in Blender to leave in that state: unlink it from one object and it is already there.

usedBy is built by walking objects rather than by asking the action. An action knows its user COUNT and not their names, while 'which object is this clip on' is the question anybody actually has.

ACTION NAMES ARE CLIP NAMES. glTF and FBX write them into the engine, so an auto-generated Action.003 becomes a string somebody downstream has to live with and cannot easily change. Each row also carries curve and keyframe counts and the frame range.
bl_list_animation_data:
Every route by which a Blender object is animated - action fcurves, DRIVERS and NLA strips. bl_list_keyframes reads animation_data.action only, which is one of three places animation lives, so an object driven entirely by drivers came back with curveCount 0 from an op whose purpose is verification - a wrong answer, not a missing one. This reports animatedBy (action/drivers/nla), the action's name and whether it has a fake user (an action WITHOUT one is deleted on save), each driver's expression, validity and variable targets, and every NLA track and strip. invalidDrivers counts drivers whose variables point at something that no longer exists - the silent failure where a driver evaluates to zero and reports nothing.

Every route by which an object is animated. bl_list_keyframes walks animation_data.action, which is ONE OF THREE places animation lives - drivers are on animation_data.drivers and NLA strips on animation_data.nla_tracks, both separate collections. So an object driven entirely by drivers came back with curveCount 0 from an op whose entire purpose is verification. That is a WRONG answer, not a missing one, and a caller checking whether their driver landed was told it had not.

REPORTS: animatedBy (action / drivers / nla) and isAnimated; the action name and whether it has a fake user, because an action WITHOUT one is deleted on save and that is silent data loss; each drivers expression, type, validity and the objects its variables point at; and every NLA track with its strips and frame ranges.

invalidDrivers is the field to watch. A driver whose variable targets a deleted object stays in place, evaluates to zero, and reports nothing anywhere in Blenders UI or in any other op here.

DRIVER CURVES (2026-10-04): each driver row also carries curveModifiers - [{type, mute, mode, polyOrder, additive, coefficients, functionType}] as the modifier has them - curveKeyframes, and curveAt: the curve's evaluated value (modifiers and keys both applied) at the two ends of its input's range, with inputRangeFrom saying where the range came from: the UI min/max of the one custom property a single-variable driver reads, else 0 and 1, said so. WHY: a Rigify IK/FK switch drives the IK copy's influence through a GENERATOR POLYNOMIAL [1, -1], so which switch value means IK lives in that modifier and the expression alone ('1.0' or 's') hides it. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: a GENERATOR [1, -1] on a driver reading a 0-1 switch gives curveAt 1 at input 0 and 0 at input 1; a driver curve as bl_add_driver leaves it passes its input through (0 at 0, 1 at 1).
bl_list_bones:
The REST-POSE bone hierarchy of a Blender ARMATURE object; posed=True adds where each bone stands now (head, tail and matrix, world and armature space). It answers the question UE's list_bones answers for a Skeleton's ReferenceSkeleton, asked on the authoring side instead. object_name must be an ARMATURE; bl_list_objects with object_type:'ARMATURE' finds one. Each bone reports name, parent (name, null for the root), headArmatureSpaceBU/tailArmatureSpaceBU (ARMATURE-space, not parent-relative - these are head_local/tail_local, already composed through every ancestor, so they compare directly against a reference skeleton without walking the parent chain yourself), length, useDeform (false means this bone is a mechanism/control bone that does not skin any geometry), connected (the head is welded to the parent's tail - what bl_create_armature and bl_add_bones' connect writes) and childCount. name_contains filters. Read-only.

RIGIFY AND COLLECTIONS (2026-10-04): each bone also reports collections (its bone collection names; on 3.6 layers, the indices it is on) and rigifyType (its Rigify rig type, '' for none; null when the generator is not enabled in the session, because the property exists only while it is). Each row carries roll (radians, what bl_add_bones takes) and rollDeg, from the bone's rest matrix (2026-10-06).

POSED (1.4, 2026-11-07): posed=True adds to each row a `posed` block read through the depsgraph - where the bone stands now, constraints and actions applied: headWorld, tailWorld, headArmature, tailArmature, matrixArmature (the pose bone's 4x4) and matrixWorld, restHeadWorld, restTailWorld and tailMovedFromRest (world units). Before it a pose could only be checked by rendering it.
bl_list_cameras:
List every camera in the Blender file and, crucially, WHICH ONE the scene renders through. sceneCamera was unobtainable anywhere in the addon before this: bl_scene_info omits it, bl_set_render_settings reports a bare boolean, and bl_render_still names it only by blocking for a whole render. Each row carries the full optical set plus fovDegrees derived at the current render resolution - the number that actually determines framing, and which depends on sensor fit as well as focal length.

sceneCamera was unobtainable anywhere in this addon. bl_scene_info does not report it, bl_set_render_settings gives only a boolean saying whether one exists, and bl_render_still names it only as a side effect of blocking for an entire render. It is the first thing anybody needs to know about a scene they did not build.

Each row carries the full optical set - lens, sensor width/height/fit, clipping, shift, ortho scale, depth of field including its focus OBJECT - plus fovRadians and fovDegrees derived at the current render resolution. FOV is the number that actually determines framing, it depends on sensor fit as well as focal length, and computing it wrong is the usual reason a camera looks right in the numbers and wrong in the render.

hideViewport and hideRender are reported for the same reason bl_list_lights reports them: a hidden object reads as perfectly configured in every other field.
bl_list_constraints:
Every constraint on a Blender object or one of its pose bones, with each one's validity. invalidCount is the field to read: a constraint whose target has been DELETED stays in the stack, contributes nothing, and is indistinguishable from a working one everywhere except is_valid - Blender shows it red in the UI and reports it nowhere else an API caller can reach. Also reports influence, mute, target and subtarget per constraint, and how many are muted. `limit` bounds the rows at ~190 bytes each; invalidCount, invalid and mutedCount are computed from the whole stack whatever the limit, so a bound cannot hide a broken constraint. Call mif_help("bl_list_constraints") first.

Every constraint on an object or one of its pose bones, and whether each one is VALID.

invalidCount is the field to read. A constraint whose target has been DELETED stays in the stack, contributes nothing, and is indistinguishable from a working one everywhere except is_valid. Blender shows it red in the UI and reports it nowhere else an API caller can reach, so an agent looking at influence, type and target sees a perfectly healthy constraint that does nothing at all.

Also reports mute per constraint and mutedCount, because a muted constraint is the other way a rig looks correct and behaves as though it is not there.

Pass bone to read a pose bone's stack instead of the object's - constraints live on both and the API is the same, which is why one module covers them.

RNA (2026-10-04): rna=true adds each constraint's every readable RNA property by identifier - the type-specific settings bl_set_constraint writes (mix_mode, owner and target space, a limit's min/max, an IK's chain_count) - as bl_list_modifiers rna does for modifiers.

LIBRARY OVERRIDES (2026-10-05): on an override object each row adds isOverrideData (Blender's flag - measured FALSE for a library bone constraint on 4.2.23, true on 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2) and fromLibrary (that flag, or the constraint's path resolving on the library's object), with overrideNote: a library constraint cannot be removed (bl_remove_constraint refuses it naming the library file); one added locally can.
bl_copy_constraints:
Copy a Blender pose bone's constraints, every setting, onto other bones; each subtarget follows its bone by rename_subtarget ({'DF_': 'FK_'} or [[old, new], ...]) and must resolve before anything is made.

WHY: a deform rig driven by FK and IK chains carries two Copy Transforms per deform bone, each one's target found by swapping the deform prefix for FK or IK - 46 single bl_add_constraint calls with settings the caller must already know. Every writable RNA property of each source constraint is copied (influence, mute, spaces, the type-specific settings; list settings such as an Armature constraint's targets are not, and collectionsNote names them). THE SUBTARGET: for each source constraint the rule in rename_subtarget that turns the SOURCE bone's name into its subtarget (DF_arm -> FK_arm by DF_ -> FK_) is applied to each destination bone's name (DF_leg -> FK_leg); a subtarget no rule produces (a fixed root) is kept. A list of pairs allows two rules from one prefix ([['DF_', 'FK_'], ['DF_', 'IK_']]). Every new subtarget is checked against its target armature's bones before the first constraint is made. constraints narrows to named ones. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: DF_arm's FK, IK (influence 0.25, mix_mode BEFORE) and an Aim at root onto DF_leg gave FK on FK_leg, IK on IK_leg with both settings, Aim on root, all valid. Reply: made (bone, constraint, subtarget, the rule used, isValid, any property not copied), madeCount, invalid. Refused, NOTHING made: a non-armature, a missing source or destination bone, the source among the destinations, a constraint the source lacks, a subtarget that would not resolve, a malformed rename_subtarget.
bl_list_custom_properties:
Custom properties on a Blender object or pose bone, with their UI range. These are how a rig exposes controls, and glTF writes them into the engine as `extras` - so they are metadata that TRAVELS, not just annotations. The UI min/max is a separate store from the value and is reported alongside it, because a slider without a range is not a control. Blender's own internal keys (cycles settings, _RNA_UI) share the namespace and are named under skippedInternalKeys rather than silently folded into the count. `limit` bounds the rows - measured at ~132 bytes a property, so 200 on one object is 26 KB - while `count` stays the true total. Call mif_help("bl_list_custom_properties") first.

Custom properties on an object or pose bone, with their UI range.

These are how a rig exposes controls, and glTF writes them into the engine as extras - so they are metadata that TRAVELS, not just annotations on a file.

The UI min/max lives in a SEPARATE store from the value and is reported alongside it, because a slider without a range is not a control - it is a number somebody has to already know the bounds of.

Blenders own internal keys - cycles settings, _RNA_UI - share this namespace. They are named under skippedInternalKeys rather than folded into the count, which would be wrong, or dropped silently, which would leave a caller unable to tell an object with no metadata from one whose metadata was filtered.

data=true (2026-10-04) reads the object's DATA block's properties (an armature's Armature) instead; owner says which.
bl_list_keyframes:
Every animation curve on an object and/or its data, with the frames and values stored.

This is the read half of bl_set_keyframe and exists because a write is not verified by the writer. It also papers over a real API break: Blender 5.0 moved fcurves from action.fcurves to action.layers[].strips[].channelbag(slot).fcurves and REMOVED the old attribute, so the same question needs two different answers depending on version. Both are handled. A NODE TREE: target world, material or node_group with datablock (its name) works on that tree's own curves instead of an object's - data_path is the path on the tree, e.g. 'nodes["Mapping"].inputs[2].default_value'.
bl_list_lights:
List every light in the Blender file with its full state - type, energy, colour, cone, area size, shadow, transform - plus hideViewport/hideRender, because a perfectly configured light that is hidden from the render is the usual reason a scene comes back black. bl_object_info reports the same record under its `light` key; on Blender 4.0+ both carry lightLinking, the collections bl_set_light_linking limited the light to. sceneHasAnyLight answers the first question worth asking about a dark render.

FILTERS. `name_contains` is a case-insensitive substring; `type` is POINT/SUN/SPOT/AREA and is validated against this Blender's own enum, so an unknown type is refused rather than silently matching nothing.

PER-LIGHT FIELDS are the same shape bl_create_light and bl_set_light return, from one shared reader, so the three cannot drift apart: type, energy, color, location, rotationEuler, diffuseFactor, specularFactor, plus the per-type ones (shadowSoftSize for POINT/SPOT, spotSize/spotBlend for SPOT, size/sizeY/shape for AREA, angle for SUN) and `shadow` when this Blender still carries use_shadow on the light.

lightLinking (Blender 4.0+) names the collections bl_set_light_linking limited the light to - receiverCollection and blockerCollection, null when not set.

hideViewport and hideRender are included because a correctly configured light that is hidden from the render reads as perfect in every other field, and that is the usual reason a scene comes back black. `sceneHasAnyLight` answers that question directly.

WHAT IS NOT LISTED: a light DATABLOCK with no object. It cannot illuminate anything until something links it, and bl_clear_scene purges those.
bl_list_markers:
Every timeline marker, and which camera each one cuts to.

CAMERA BINDING is why markers matter beyond being labels. A marker with a camera bound makes the scene SWITCH to that camera at that frame, which is how a multi-camera edit is done in Blender and is invisible from everywhere else in this addon. bl_list_cameras reports which camera is active now; this reports which one each part of the timeline uses.

sceneCutsBetweenCameras says outright whether the scene changes camera mid-render. When it is true, scene.camera describes only the frames before the first binding - so a caller reading that alone is describing one shot out of several.
bl_list_materials: List every material in the Blender file with its user count. Reports `unused` - materials with zero users - because a material with no users is NOT written to an FBX at all, so one created and never assigned silently does not arrive in Unreal.
bl_list_modifiers:
The modifier stack on a Blender object - a mesh, curve, text, surface or lattice - in EVALUATION ORDER (top to bottom in the Modifier Properties panel, which is also application order) - answers 'what will bl_export_mesh actually produce' before spending an export to find out. rna=True adds every readable RNA property of each modifier by identifier - what bl_add_modifier and bl_set_modifier can write. A FLUID's rna also carries its live role's settings (domain_settings, flow_settings or effector_settings) - where bl_set_modifier writes them - without the simulation grids, whose getter crashes Blender on a domain that has not simulated.

Each entry reports name, type, showViewport, showRender (a modifier with both false changes nothing at export or in the viewport - it is present but inert, not absent) and a curated `settings` dict in camelCase for every type in bl_add_modifier's curated table (22 types - ARMATURE, ARRAY, BEVEL, BOOLEAN, MIRROR, OCEAN and SUBSURF among them) - not every property Blender exposes. rna=True adds EVERY readable RNA property of each modifier by identifier, which is what reads back a setting written by bl_add_modifier or bl_set_modifier outside that table (a BEVEL's limit_method, a WAVE's height - a WAVE has no curated fields at all). ARMATURE's settings.object is the SAME pairing bl_object_info's armatureModifier reports, seen here in context with the rest of the stack rather than in isolation. Read-only. A FLUID's rna also carries its live role's settings under domain_settings, flow_settings or effector_settings - where bl_set_modifier writes them - without the six simulation grids, whose getter crashes Blender on a domain that has not simulated (measured on 4.4.0).
bl_list_node_groups:
Every Blender node group in the file, by name, with its tree type, node count, user count and fake-user flag; type filters to GeometryNodeTree, ShaderNodeTree or CompositorNodeTree. bl_add_group_interface, bl_add_group_node, bl_assign_node_group, bl_link_group_nodes and bl_list_group_nodes all take a group NAME, bl_create_node_group makes one, and until 2026-09-08 nothing listed them: a caller had to remember what it had created or read the names out of a deliberate REFUSAL, since the not-found message prints them. Neither asymmetry audit caught it and both were right to pass - node_groups has a creator and is reached by a caller-supplied key, so the shape that was missing is a third one they do not ask about, CREATED AND CONSUMED AND NOT LISTABLE. users and fakeUser are reported because a group with neither is one the next save deletes, which is the same fact bl_file_info gives for orphans, said where somebody choosing a group will actually see it. Pass type to filter by tree type (GeometryNodeTree, ShaderNodeTree, CompositorNodeTree); omit it for all of them.
