limit (int, default None: unlimited) caps the rows returned; count stays the number that matched, and truncated, returned and a truncationNote say when rows were dropped. A negative or non-whole limit is refused. name_excludes (list of str, default None; a single string is also taken) drops every group whose name contains any of the terms, case-insensitive, before the limit applies - ['Mif'] hides this add-on's scratch groups. type is matched against the group's bl_idname as given and is not validated: an unknown type returns no rows rather than a refusal. Rows are sorted by name.

OUT: groups [{name, type, users, fakeUser, nodes}], count, filteredBy (the type, or null), totalInFile (every node group in the file, unfiltered), plus truncated and returned when limit is given, and truncationNote when rows were dropped.

Refused: an unknown key (name, group and tree are named and pointed at bl_list_group_nodes), a name_excludes holding a non-string, and a bad limit. It is a read and changes nothing.
bl_list_objects:
List objects in the Blender scene with their types. object_type filters to one Blender type ('MESH', 'EMPTY', 'ARMATURE', ...); omit it for everything. pattern filters by NAME and is echoed back in filteredBy, so a caller can tell an empty result from a filter that matched nothing. detail returns more per object. near {point, radius, by ORIGIN|BOUNDS} keeps those within the radius, nearest first, with distance. Read-only.

An FBX that brought in more than the mesh you wanted - LOD children, a collision shape, an armature - shows up here as extra rows, which is the usual reason a round trip refuses to continue. A MESH row's dimensionsBU is Blender's own obj.dimensions, not a measurement: it reads the base mesh's box for a stack that evaluates to nothing (4.2+) and a Subdivision Surface's cage when one is last in the stack (5.0+). detail:true and bl_object_info measure the evaluated vertices instead.
bl_list_shape_keys: Shape keys on a Blender mesh object - Blender's name for what Unreal calls morph targets (compare against UE's list_morph_targets on the same character). Each entry reports name, value (the current slider position), sliderMin/sliderMax, mute, isBasis (the neutral pose the others are relative to, not a real pose target itself) and relativeTo. A mesh with none reports hasShapeKeys:false and count:0 rather than an error - most game meshes have none; only facial/blend-shape ones need them. Read-only.
bl_list_vertex_groups:
Vertex groups on a Blender mesh (a skinned mesh's, one per deforming bone, named after it); region {box | sphere} adds each one's mean weight there. Each entry reports name, index and weightedVertexCount (how many vertices actually have a non-zero weight in this group) plus influencesGeometry (weightedVertexCount > 0) - a group with ZERO weighted vertices means this mesh will not deform at all on that bone, the same class of rigging bug UE's analyze_skeletal_split flags via influencesGeometry on the cooked side. A mesh with no vertex groups reports count:0 with a note rather than an error. Read-only.

REGION (2026-10-05): region {box: [[minX,minY,minZ],[maxX,maxY,maxZ]]} or {sphere: {center, radius}}, in rest space (the base mesh under the object's transform), adds regionMean to each group - its mean weight over every vertex inside, an unassigned vertex counting 0 - and regionWeighted, and the reply's regionDominant lists the groups by that mean, largest first (up to 20), with regionVertices. It is how a hood's back was found going straight from one spine bone to the head with almost nothing between. A region holding no vertex, and a vertexGroup region, are refused.
bl_list_worlds:
Every Blender world datablock in the file, by name, with usesNodes, user count, fake-user flag and a per-row current flag showing which the active scene uses - the FOURTH collection of this shape. bl_create_world makes one and ops take a world NAME, and the only enumeration of world names anywhere in the addon was inside bl_world_info's own refusal, so a caller discovered worlds by deliberately asking for one that does not exist. users and fakeUser are reported because a world with neither is one the next save deletes, and somebody choosing between worlds is exactly who needs that before choosing.

Parameters: limit (int, default None: every world) caps the rows returned, and the reply then carries returned and truncated (plus a truncationNote when rows were dropped); name_excludes (str or list of str, default None) drops worlds whose name contains any of the terms, case-insensitively, before the limit is applied.

OUT: worlds [{name, current, usesNodes, users, fakeUser}] sorted by name, count (the rows that matched after name_excludes, whatever the limit), current (the name of the active scene's world, or null), plus returned/truncated/truncationNote when limit was given.

Refused: an unknown key (name, world and current are refused with a note - bl_world_info reads one world, and each row already carries current); name_excludes holding something other than strings; a limit that is not a whole number or is negative. It only reads.
bl_move_keyframes:
Retime Blender keyframes - shift them by an offset, or scale the timing about a pivot. Retiming is a core animation operation and nothing here could do it: bl_delete_keyframe and bl_set_keyframe together can only rebuild an animation from scratch, losing every handle, interpolation and easing on the way, so 'make this 20% slower' meant re-authoring it. THE HANDLES MOVE WITH THE KEYS - a bezier handle is stored in ABSOLUTE frame coordinates, so moving only the key leaves its handles behind and silently reshapes the curve while the interpolation still reads BEZIER. Keys are moved in the direction of travel (later-first when shifting forwards) because Blender keeps them sorted and a key crossing one that has not moved yet makes the walk skip or revisit it. offset and scale are refused together as an ambiguous order. framesChanged reports whether the frame list actually differs, since an offset of 0 or a scale of 1 does nothing whatever the call said.

Retiming is a core animation operation and nothing here could do it. bl_delete_keyframe and bl_set_keyframe together can only rebuild an animation from scratch, which loses every handle, interpolation and easing on the way - so make this 20 percent slower, or push everything after frame 50 back ten frames, meant re-authoring it.

THE HANDLES MOVE WITH THE KEYS. A bezier handle is stored in ABSOLUTE frame coordinates, so moving only the key leaves its handles behind and silently reshapes the curve - the interpolation still reads BEZIER and the motion is different. That is the detail that makes a hand-rolled retime through other ops wrong.

KEYS ARE MOVED IN THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL: later-first when shifting forwards, earlier-first when shifting back. Blender keeps keyframe_points sorted by frame, and a key crossing one that has not moved yet makes the walk skip or revisit keys.

offset and scale are REFUSED TOGETHER, because applying both leaves the order ambiguous - call twice and see each result. A zero or negative scale is refused too: it collapses or reverses the timing and is never what is meant.

framesChanged reports whether the frame list actually differs. An offset of 0 or a scale of 1 does nothing whatever the call said, and that is worth knowing rather than reading as success. A NODE TREE: target world, material or node_group with datablock (its name) works on that tree's own curves instead of an object's - data_path is the path on the tree, e.g. 'nodes["Mapping"].inputs[2].default_value'.
bl_normalize_weights: Make every vertex's bone weights sum to 1 in Blender, and cap how many bones influence one vertex. WHY THE LIMIT MATTERS, AND IT IS NOT A BLENDER CONCERN: Unreal's GPU skin cache supports a bounded number of influences per vertex - 4 by default, 8 or 12 with the project setting raised - and the FBX importer DROPS the smallest weights past that limit and renormalises silently, so a mesh that deforms correctly in Blender deforms differently in Unreal and neither tool says why. Limiting here deliberately means the weights you tested are the weights that ship. ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING and handled for you: limit FIRST, then normalise - limiting drops the smallest influences and leaves the rest summing under 1, so normalising afterwards restores the sum; the other order renormalises and then throws part of the result away, which is exactly the bug the importer produces. UNWEIGHTED VERTICES ARE REPORTED, NEVER INVENTED - a vertex in no group cannot be normalised and guessing a bone for it would be a silent wrong answer of the worst kind because it deforms plausibly; they are counted and named instead (in Unreal they bind to the root bone). Pair with bl_list_vertex_groups, which is the read half. groups restricts the work to named vertex groups. On a rigged mesh only BONE groups count: with an enabled Armature modifier the default scope="bones" takes the groups named after the armature's deform bones and names the rest in groupsLeftOut - a cloth pin or a panel group is not an influence, and Unreal drops it. Pass scope="all" to count every group; a mesh with no armature keeps every group (scope reads "all (no armature)"). The groups and scope parameters are not passed together. respect_locked (2026-10-06; default true on 4.4+, false before, as Blender's own Normalize): groups whose lock is set keep their weights and the rest fill what is left of 1.
bl_object_info: Measurements for one Blender object, under an 'object' key: boundsLocalMinBU/MaxBU/SizeBU and boundsLocalSizeUU (the local bbox, already converted - use this one, do NOT multiply dimensionsBU yourself, that folds in object scale), dimensionsBU, locationBU, rotationEulerRad, rotationMode (with rotationQuaternion [w, x, y, z] on a QUATERNION object and rotationAxisAngle on an AXIS_ANGLE one - such an object ignores rotationEulerRad, and every glTF import is QUATERNION), scale, isIdentityTransform (read off the rotation the mode uses), vert/edge/face/tri counts, materialSlots in order, uvLayers, hasCustomSplitNormals, armatureModifier (the ARMATURE object's name if this mesh has an Armature modifier bound to one, else null - that is the rig actually deforming it at export time, and the name to pass bl_list_bones; a mesh merely PARENTED to an armature with no modifier is not deforming, so parenting alone does not set this). Read-only. This is the tool that answers 'did the FBX survive the trip': compare object.boundsLocalSizeUU against the boundsSizeUU export_asset reported for the source mesh (that one arrives as an {x,y,z} object, this one as a 3-list), and compare materialSlots against its materialSlots. isIdentityTransform must stay true - if it is not, something moved or rotated the object and the pivot is already lost. There is no matrix_world field; isIdentityTransform is the check that replaces reading one. Compare boundsLocalMinBU/MaxBU (x100) against export_asset's boundsMinUU/boundsMaxUU too, not just the size: the size is blind to a mesh that kept its dimensions and moved, and 'the pivot must not move' is half the tiling constraint. mif_mesh_roundtrip now does exactly that automatically. dimensionsBU is the EVALUATED size: on an object with a viewport modifier or shape keys it is measured off the evaluated vertices, and evaluatedVerts gives their count (0 means the viewport evaluation produced no mesh; instances a Geometry Nodes modifier outputs are not counted). Where Blender's own obj.dimensions disagrees it comes back as blenderDimensionsBU with a dimensionsNote - measured on 3.6-5.2: from 4.2 a stack that evaluates to nothing reads as the base mesh's box, and from 5.0 a Subdivision Surface last in the stack reads as its cage. boundsNote says when dimensionsBU and the base-mesh boundsLocal*/counts differ by design. On every object type: parent - {name, type (OBJECT, BONE, ...), bone, inverseIsIdentity} or null - and children, the names of its direct children sorted; bl_list_objects and bl_scene_info with detail carry the same. inverseIsIdentity is false after Blender's own Ctrl+P, which stores the parent's inverse; bl_set_parent leaves identity. A mesh also carries sharpEdges (edges marked sharp) and autoSmooth - {enabled, angleDeg} on Blender 3.6-4.0, null from 4.1 where bl_set_shading's angle is a Smooth by Angle modifier (bl_list_modifiers reads its Angle input) or marked sharp edges. A curve carries usePath and each spline's type, points, cyclic and handleTypes; a lattice its points, interpolation on each axis and useOutside; an armature its displayType and showInFront.
bl_open_file:
Open a .blend, DISCARDING everything currently in memory. There is no undo across a file load, so an open over a DIRTY session is refused unless discard_unsaved is passed - this is the one Blender op here that can lose work which was never on disk. Save first with bl_save_file if you want it. The response re-reads the session path and refuses to claim success if the session did not actually become the file you asked for.

AN OPEN OVER A DIRTY SESSION IS REFUSED unless discard_unsaved:true. There is no undo across a file load, so the guard is not optional - save first with bl_save_file if the work matters. A missing file is refused before anything is touched.

AFTERWARDS IT RE-READS bpy.data.filepath and refuses to report success if the session did not actually become the file you asked for, rather than trusting that a silent load means it worked. The response carries the datablock counts so a caller can tell immediately whether the file is what they expected.
bl_purge_orphans:
Delete every Blender datablock with no users and no fake user, NOW, without saving - and report what went, by type and by name. This is the ACT half of a report bl_file_info has always given: its purgeNote says a save deletes unlinked datablocks, and until 2026-09-08 nothing could act on that without either writing the file or clearing the scene. It is also why there is no bl_delete_material or bl_delete_image: Blender's lifecycle is unlink-then-purge, so a datablock with users cannot be removed without breaking what uses it and one without users costs nothing until the file is written - per-type deleters would be the wrong shape and this is the Outliner's own Purge. confirm:true is REQUIRED, matching bl_destroy_collection, because an unlinked material somebody spent an hour on looks exactly like scratch from here. With dry_run=True it previews what would go and returns a preview_id, no confirm needed; preview_id alone commits exactly that list in place of confirm. recursive repeats until nothing more is unused, reaching datablocks orphaned only because the first pass removed their last user - a deep clean, and more than a caller tidying up usually expects, so it is off by default. Counts are a before-and-after difference rather than the purge call's own return, because that return varies by build. ONLY SCOPES IT: only=['materials:Rust', 'node_groups:Leaves'] (the 'type:name' shape bl_file_info's orphans and purgedNames print, or a bare name when one datablock carries it) removes exactly those and leaves every other orphan - the file-wide pass takes a material made a moment ago and not yet assigned. Still unlink-then-purge: a named datablock with users, a fake user, a missing or an ambiguous name refuses the whole call, naming what uses it and how to unlink it; namesFreed confirms each name is free again (a re-create gets it back, not '.001'). This is how a material, node group, texture, world, font or action made through the bridge is removed on its own. clear_fake_user=true (only with `only`) clears the fake user on the NAMED datablocks and purges them - bl_create_action sets one by default, so without it an action can never be removed; without `only` it is refused.

CHANGE CAP: it has no preview, so a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct data-blocks (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) is refused, writing nothing, and says to split it or have the user raise the cap (docs/15 section 6).
bl_reload_image: Re-read Blender image datablocks from their files after a bake or another tool rewrote them - a re-written file changes nothing in the session until reloaded. Refuses a packed image, one with no file, a missing file, and one with unsaved pixels unless discard_unsaved. WHY: a 4K normal map re-baked to the same path kept its old pixels in every material that used it, and the garment work reloaded it through raw Python seven times. A packed image would reload its packed copy, not the file, so it is refused; an unsaved bake is UNSAVED pixels, which reloading discards. Each row reports sizeBefore, sizeAfter (read after the reload, which is what makes Blender decode the file) and the file's modified time; a file that decodes to nothing is named in a warning.
bl_remove_constraint:
Remove a Blender constraint by name, and report where the object went when it came off. Removing a constraint moves the object back to its own transform, and THAT movement is the proof the constraint was doing something - measured through the evaluated depsgraph for the same reason adding one is. The response counts constraints before and after with countsAgree, because constraints.remove() returns None either way.

Taking a constraint off moves the object back to its own transform, and THAT movement is the proof the constraint had been doing something. It is measured through the evaluated depsgraph for exactly the same reason adding one is: the object's own transform never changed, so nothing else would show it.

Constraints are counted before and after with countsAgree, because constraints.remove() returns None whether or not it did anything - the same reason bl_delete_keyframe counts keys instead of trusting a bool.

A name that is not on the stack is refused with the names that are, rather than treated as a successful removal of nothing. On a library override a constraint that came from the library is refused the same way as bl_remove_modifier's library modifiers; a locally added one is removed.
bl_remove_driver:
Remove a Blender driver and report what the property fell back to. A property with its driver removed returns to whatever it was last set to, which is NOT necessarily what it was displaying while driven - so the value is read back rather than assumed. A path with no driver is refused with a pointer to bl_list_animation_data rather than reported as a successful removal of nothing, and the removal is re-checked afterwards.

A property with its driver removed returns to whatever it was last SET to, which is not necessarily what it was displaying while driven - a driver holding a value does not write that value into the property. So valueNow is read back rather than assumed.

A path with no driver is refused, with a pointer to bl_list_animation_data, rather than reported as a successful removal of nothing. The removal is re-checked afterwards and the op refuses to claim success if a driver is still there.
bl_remove_modifier:
Remove a modifier from a Blender object's stack (mesh, curve, text, surface or lattice) WITHOUT applying it - the mesh data is untouched, and meshUnchanged in the response is measured rather than asserted (null on a non-mesh, which has no mesh data to compare). ON A LIBRARY OVERRIDE a modifier that came from the library (is_override_data) is refused, naming the source file: Blender's RNA remove returns, the stack reads it gone, and after a save and reload it is back (measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1). A modifier added locally on the override is removed and stays removed. A linked object with no override is refused as not editable.

Remove a modifier from a Blender object's stack WITHOUT applying it - the mesh data is untouched, and meshUnchanged in the response is measured rather than asserted. Use this to drop a Mirror or Subsurf that would otherwise change what bl_export_mesh writes, when you want the base geometry rather than the modified result. bl_apply_modifier is the opposite choice: bake it in. An unknown modifier name is refused with the list of what IS on the stack.
bl_rename_bones:
Rename Blender armature bones through a {old: new} map. Blender already renames the matching vertex groups and updates constraint and driver references by itself - what this adds is refusing the NAME COLLISION where that sync silently fails: renaming a bone onto a name another bone holds gives you 'Hips.001' and leaves the vertex group under its old name, matching no bone, so that part of the mesh stops deforming with nothing to say so. Collisions are refused before anything is written, every rename is read back, swaps are supported, and orphaned vertex groups are reported. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. See mif_help.

BLENDER ALREADY DOES THE OBVIOUS PART, measured against 4.4 rather than assumed. Setting bone.name renames the matching vertex group on every skinned mesh, updates constraint subtargets, and updates driver bone targets. This op does not re-implement any of that, and a 'also rename the vertex groups' parameter would do nothing.

IT EXISTS FOR THE CASE WHERE THAT SYNC SILENTLY FAILS - a name collision. Measured:

    bones ['Hips','Spine']  vgroups ['Hips','Spine']
    bones['Spine'].name = 'Hips'
    bones ['Hips','Hips.001']  vgroups ['Hips','Spine']

The bone is silently suffixed to a name nobody asked for, AND the vertex group keeps its old name, now matching no bone - so that part of the mesh stops deforming and the call reports nothing. A rig that looks fine and deforms wrong. Collisions are therefore refused BEFORE anything is written, and every rename is read back afterwards: a name that is not what was asked for means Blender suffixed it.

A target only counts as a collision when the name is held by a bone this batch does NOT rename away - otherwise a swap would be refused for no reason.

SWAPS WORK. A->B together with B->A cannot be done in either order directly, since whichever runs first collides, so the batch parks every source on a unique temporary name first and then moves each to its target. Invisible in the result; mentioned because retarget maps are full of left/right swaps.

ORPHANED VERTEX GROUPS ARE REPORTED whether or not this call caused them - a group matching no bone deforms nothing, and someone renaming bones is the one person certain to care. An empty orphan list is a positive result: it confirms Blender's group rename actually happened rather than assuming it.

dryRun runs every check and writes nothing.

NOT the retarget answer on the Unreal side: the IK Retargeter suite exists so that bone names do NOT have to match. This is for the case where you want them to.

MIRROR SUFFIXES (2026-10-11): one answer takes .L and .R only, another tolerates lowercase _l and _r; take the pair as a parameter and measure bpy.utils.flip_name on the build in use (arm.L, arm_l, Arm_L, Left_arm, L_arm) rather than assuming either.
bl_rename_object:
Rename a Blender object, REFUSING a name collision instead of letting Blender resolve it - because Blender resolves it in OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS across the 3.6/4.x line. Measured: with an existing 'Alpha', on 4.2/4.4/5.0 the incumbent keeps it and the renamer becomes 'Alpha.001'; on 3.6 whichever of the two names sorts first keeps the name - 'Zulu' renamed to 'Alpha' TAKES it and silently renames the INCUMBENT to 'Alpha.001', while 'Aardvark' renamed to 'Mango' becomes 'Mango.001' (3.6.23). So the same script renames a different object depending on the Blender running it, and on 3.6 it corrupts an object nobody asked it to touch. THE DATA NAME DOES NOT FOLLOW - obj.data.name keeps its old value, and a mesh named after the old object survives into the FBX - so rename_data defaults on. Pointers survive a rename (modifier targets, constraint targets, driver variables); STRING references do not, such as an exporter convention like UCX_<name>_00. The addon had bl_rename_bones and no way to rename an object.

allow_collision (bool, default None: false) lets Blender resolve a clash with an existing object's name its own way instead of refusing: on 4.2 and later this object becomes '<name>.001' (resolvedTo), on 3.6 the existing object can be the one renamed (otherObjectRenamed). to is also accepted as newName. rename_data (default true) sets obj.data.name to the name the object ended up with; an object with no data is skipped. Renaming to the name the object already has returns changed false and writes nothing.

OUT: ok, object (its name now), renamedFrom, changed, resolvedTo (only when Blender resolved a clash, else null), dataName, dataRenamed, otherObjectRenamed ({was, now} or null), note (pointers survive, string references do not).

Refused before anything is written: an unknown key; object or the new name missing, or the new name empty or blank; a non-boolean allow_collision or rename_data; an object not found; a library-linked object (overrides are allowed); a name another object already holds, unless allow_collision; and on Blender before 5.0 a name over 63 characters. One check comes AFTER the write: if Blender stored a different name with no clash allowed, the call is refused but the object has already been renamed to what Blender stored.
bl_render_info:
Everything that decides what a Blender render will look like - engine, samples and WHICH property they live on, effective resolution after the percentage multiplier, output format, colour management (view transform, look, exposure - the usual cause of 'washed out'), frame range, scene camera, world, and how many lights actually contribute. The read half of bl_set_render_settings, which reports only the five fields it can write. It also answers the black-render question directly: `blockers` is a measured list of reasons this render will produce nothing useful - no scene camera, no world datablock (a scene with no world contributes NO ambient light, so interiors go black and the lights get blamed), every light hidden or at zero energy - and `wouldRenderSomething` is the one-field answer. outOfProcessSimulations names the simulations bl_render_animation's saved-file render would not animate: an unbaked rigid body or soft body stays frozen, an unbaked cloth restarts when the render starts after its cache, an unbaked dynamic paint surface renders flat. No parameters. rna=True adds `eevee`, `cycles` and `render`: every readable setting of scene.eevee, scene.cycles and scene.render by identifier - the read half of bl_set_render_settings' eevee / cycles / render.

THE BLACK-RENDER QUESTION IS ANSWERED DIRECTLY. The 'blockers' field lists measured reasons the render will produce nothing useful, in the order they bite: no scene camera (nothing else will tell you - scene_info omits it); no world datablock, which means the scene contributes NO ambient light, so anything not lit by its own fixture is pure black and the lights get blamed; every light hidden from render or at zero energy; and a zero effective resolution. 'wouldRenderSomething' is the one-field version of the same answer.

SAMPLES ARE REPORTED WITH THE PROPERTY THEY LIVE ON. The count sits on cycles.samples or on eevee.taa_render_samples depending on the engine, and a caller comparing it against what they set needs to know it is the same field. 'samplesOn' names it.

'effectiveResolution' is the resolution multiplied by the percentage, which is the size the file will actually be and the number people get wrong, because percentage is a multiplier nobody remembers is set.

COLOUR MANAGEMENT is included - view transform, look, exposure, gamma, display device - because it silently changes every pixel and is the usual cause of 'washed out'. The default view transform differs by Blender version and a studio OCIO config renames all of them, so these are read off the scene rather than assumed. outOfProcessSimulations names the simulations bl_render_animation's saved-file render would not animate - an unbaked rigid body or soft body stays frozen, an unbaked cloth restarts when the render starts after its cache, an unbaked dynamic paint surface renders flat (measured on all five builds).
bl_render_status:
How far an out-of-process render has actually got, measured on disk rather than asked of the process. framesRendered counts only files whose mtime is at or after the job start. Keeps three answers distinct that must never be collapsed: unknownJob (never started here, or Blender restarted and the table went with it - NOT 'unfinished', which is how a caller waits forever), running, and exited-with-a-code, where a non-zero exit still reports the real frames already on disk. For a movie container it reports framesVerifiable:false instead of a frame count it never checked. Omit job_id to list the jobs this Blender knows about. gpuNote names gpu_backend CUDA when the log shows the OptiX kernel failing to load.

PARAMETERS. log_lines (whole number, default 20): how many lines of the job log's tail come back in logTail, read from at most the log's last 64 KB. It is not range-checked: 0 returns every line in that window rather than none, and a negative number drops lines from the front instead.

OUT, no job_id: ok, jobs [{jobId, pid, running, framesExpected, blendFile}], note (jobs are process-local). Unknown job_id: ok, unknownJob true, jobId, knownJobs, error - not a refusal, and not a report that the render is unfinished. Known job: ok, jobId, pid, running, exitCode (null while running), elapsedSeconds, framesExpected, blendFile, outputDir, logTail [lines], log (the log path), gpuNote, and job {memoryLimitBytes, peakTreeMemoryBytes, memoryMeasure, killedForMemory} when the job has a memory watch. Image frames: framesVerifiable true, framesRendered, framesRemaining, staleFramesIgnored, staleNote when older files sit on the expected paths. A movie container: framesVerifiable false, containerWritten, containerPath, note. Once the process has exited: complete (exit code 0 and every frame, or the container, written) and error on a non-zero exit or a memory-ceiling kill.

REFUSED: a log_lines that is not a whole number. Read-only, apart from closing the log handle of a job that has exited.
bl_run_python:
Run Python on Blender's main thread: code (bpy, bmesh and math imported) or a .py file; stdout, stderr and what the code assigns to `result` come back. Refused while the MifBlender add-on's preferences do not allow it. The escape hatch for everything MifBlender has no first-class op for - prefer a first-class op whenever one exists, because those have checked parameters and this does not. Names persist between calls until a .blend loads; fresh=True runs one call in a clean namespace, and namesFromEarlierCalls lists any earlier call's names the code read.

Pass EITHER code (a string) OR file (a path to a .py that Blender reads) - passing both is an error, as is passing neither. CONTRACT: whatever your code assigns to a module-level name `result` comes back in the response, coerced to JSON-safe values; a script that returns nothing useful is usually one that forgot to assign it. stdout and stderr are captured and returned. bpy, math, bmesh and mathutils are pre-imported into the namespace. An exception comes back as ok:false with the traceback and does NOT kill the connection, so a broken snippet is recoverable. GATED: the addon preference 'allow_run_python' must be ticked in Blender (Edit > Preferences > Add-ons > MifBlender) or every call refuses with instructions - that gate is the safety model, since this runs with Blender's full privileges, has no sandbox and no undo. It also holds the single serialised transport socket for its whole run, so an infinite loop here wedges Blender AND every other bl_* tool; bl_status is bounded at 5s precisely so it can still tell you that. Keep snippets short.

THE NAMESPACE IS SHARED BY DEFAULT, AND NEVER SILENTLY. Every name a call defines - a variable, an import, a function - is still there for the next call, as in a console, until a .blend is loaded; `result` alone starts each call as None. A value an earlier call left behind can therefore change a later run (it did, building a short film), so every reply carries `namespace` (shared or fresh) and `namesFromEarlierCalls`: each name this code read on or before the line that first binds it which an earlier call had left in the shared namespace, with a `warning`. fresh=True runs the code in a clean namespace of its own (bpy, bmesh, math, mathutils, Vector, Matrix, Euler, Quaternion and Color only) and leaves the shared one exactly as it was; nothing the fresh call defines carries over. The default stays shared because a fresh namespace per call cost more failed calls than it saved (benchmark round six: 4 of 9 failed Blender calls used a name an earlier call had defined).
bl_call_operator:
Run a registered Blender operator by id ('mesh.primitive_monkey_add'), each property checked against the operator's own ranges and enum items first; describe lists its properties and runs nothing; undo true runs it as the UI does, into the undo stack and Blender's operator log. Gated by Allow run_python, like bl_run_python.

WHY (2026-10-05): no op called bpy.ops by id, and bl_run_python reaches it but is never coverage. properties {name: value}: an unknown name, an enum item the operator lacks, or a number outside its hard range is refused - Blender clamps that in silence (measured on 4.2.23-5.2.2: primitive_monkey_add size -5 made a monkey of no size). context {object (made active and selected), selected [names], mode (EDIT etc., switched to before and back to OBJECT after)}: mesh.subdivide with {object, mode: EDIT} subdivides that mesh. A poll that fails in the context is refused by name. Refused by id: what quits Blender, replaces the session (the home file, factory settings, opening or reverting a file), saves the .blend or the preferences, or reloads add-ons - bl_save_file and bl_open_file are the typed calls and the add-on operators (bl_enable_addon). A CANCELLED result is a refusal. Reply: result, objectsAdded, objectsRemoved, activeObject, and typedOp when a typed tool does the same job with checks this generic call cannot make (bl_create_primitive, bl_add_modifier, bl_subdivide_mesh ...; the reply names the add-on op). undo true (MEASURED 2026-10-09 on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, headless included): bpy.ops's undo argument, so the operator finishes at undo depth 0 as a UI-run one does - an undo step is pushed and it enters WindowManager.operators, which bl_list_recent_operators reads; logged in the reply says whether it is now the log's last entry. undo false (the default, and bpy.ops's own) adds neither. An operator's reports reach the reply only through an error.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): object.modifier_copy {modifier} with context {object} duplicates the modifier on that object, and object.modifier_copy_to_selected {modifier} with context {object, selected [source, targets]} copies it onto the others - both run headless on every build and every property matches the source, as bl_add_modifier copy_from does natively. On 5.0+ wm.fbx_import (the new FBX importer) runs here by filepath: a bake_anim_all_actions FBX of an object and its shape keys comes in as ONE action holding both slots (OB<name>, KE<name>), where bl_import_mesh's importer makes one action per take ('<obj>|<obj>|<action>', 'Key|<obj>|<action>'); before 5.0 the operator is not registered and is refused naming the importers that are.

DYNAMIC ENUMS (2026-10-15, the settle pass): an enum whose items a callback makes reads as Blender's one-item placeholder [DEFAULT] from the operator's RNA, so it is not checked here - Blender checks the value when the operator runs, and a wrong one is refused with its own list and nothing done. rigidbody.mass_calculate {material: Iron} on a selected 2 m cube sets the mass to 62992 kg (7874 kg/m3) on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1 (test_blender_settle_routes BS403); before, every material was refused 'takes DEFAULT'.
bl_list_recent_operators:
Blender's log of the last operators run (WindowManager.operators: id, name, properties) and the calls made through bl_call_operator this session. An operator enters the log when run from the UI or by bl_call_operator with undo true. Gated by Allow run_python.

WHAT ENTERS THE LOG, MEASURED 2026-10-09 on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1 headless: an operator that finishes at undo depth 0 - run from the UI, or through bl_call_operator with undo true (bpy.ops's undo argument). bpy.ops's default, undo false - bl_call_operator's default, bpy.ops in bl_run_python, scripts - adds nothing. That is why the log read empty headless on 2026-10-05 and in a 5.2.1 GUI session on 2026-10-06 after a monkey and a cube made through Python: background mode keeps the log too. Blender keeps the last 32; an empty log says so in note. bridgeCalls lists {id, result, properties} for each bl_call_operator call. limit 1-200 (default 20).
bl_list_scenes:
Every Blender scene in the file, by name, with its object count, frame range, user count and a per-row current flag - the THIRD collection found created, consumed and not listable, and the first with no refusal to read the names out of either. bl_create_scene makes one and several ops take a scene NAME, but bl_scene_info reports the CURRENT scene and never touches bpy.data.scenes, so a caller in a multi-scene file had no way to learn what the others were called. The current flag rides on each row rather than sitting in a separate field, because 'what scenes are there' and 'which am I in' are asked together and answering them apart invites pairing them wrongly.

PARAMETERS. limit (whole number, default unlimited): the most scene rows returned, after sorting by name and after name_excludes. name_excludes (string or list of strings, default none): drops scenes whose name contains any of them, case-insensitively. Read-only.

OUT: scenes [{name, current, objectCount, frameStart, frameEnd, usePreviewRange, previewFrameStart, previewFrameEnd, users, fakeUser}] sorted by name; count (the scenes left after name_excludes, before limit); current (the current scene's name). With limit: truncated, returned, and truncationNote when rows were dropped. When usePreviewRange is true the preview pair, not frameStart/frameEnd, is the range playback uses.

REFUSED: a negative or fractional limit; a name_excludes entry that is not text. name, scene and current are refused with a note: this lists scenes, and bl_set_current_scene switches to one.
bl_enable_addon:
Enable or disable a Blender add-on by module, or install a .py, .zip or 4.2+ extension package (into repo, default user_default) and enable it; uninstall removes it. Replies its name, version and classes. Gated by Allow run_python.

MEASURED 2026-10-05 on 4.2.23-5.2.2, headless: io_curve_svg is bundled and enabled, and addon_utils.disable / enable take its import operator away and back; a file goes through Blender's own preferences.addon_install into the user's scripts/addons (installedTo says where - it stays for that user's Blender until uninstall) and is then enabled. enable false disables; persistent also records the state in the preferences, which keep it only if they are saved. An unknown module is refused with the near names; MifBlender itself is never disabled or removed here (the call would cut itself off); uninstall removes only a module that lives in the user's add-ons folder. Reply: module, enabledBefore, enabledAfter, name and version (bl_info), installedTo, uninstalled / removedPath, classesAdded / classesRemoved (bpy.types names). EXTENSION PACKAGES (measured 2026-10-06 on 4.2.23-5.2.2, headless): a .zip with blender_manifest.toml (at its root or in one top folder) goes through extensions.package_install_files into the local repository repo (default user_default; remote, disabled or system refused) and is enabled as bl_ext.<repo>.<id>; uninstall on that module uses extensions.package_uninstall. A non add-on manifest (a theme) or one with no id is refused. The reply adds extension {id, version, repo, type}.

REGISTERED WITH ITS PREFERENCES ENTRY (2026-10-15, the settle pass): an add-on is always enabled with an in-memory preferences entry (addon_utils default_set), because one whose register() reads its own entry fails without it - 'rigify' answered "reported no error and it is disabled" on 5.0.1 and left the generator half-registered. When persistent is false the preferences' dirty flag is put back as found, so an auto-save does not record the add-on. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1: enable rigify, then bl_create_armature metarig human and bl_generate_rigify_rig give 160 DEF, 159 ORG and 167 MCH bones (test_blender_settle_routes BS400).
bl_save_file:
Write the Blender session to a .blend on disk. Until this existed NOTHING the addon authored survived the process - every light, camera, keyframe, world and node group died when Blender closed, and the only artefacts were a mesh FBX, a baked texture and one rendered frame. SAVE-A-COPY BY DEFAULT: the session keeps its own filepath, so a later save still goes where it did before; pass repoint_session to make this the working file. An existing file is REFUSED unless overwrite is passed. The response reports purgedOrphans - what the save destroyed - which is data loss caused by the successful operation and invisible otherwise.

SAVE-A-COPY IS THE DEFAULT. Blender's own save-as normally REPOINTS the session at the new path, so a later save silently goes somewhere the caller never named. This passes copy=True unless repoint_session is set, leaving bpy.data.filepath alone; the response reports sessionFilepathUnchanged so you can see which happened.

OVERWRITE IS REFUSED BY DEFAULT. An existing file needs overwrite:true. Every refusal fires before anything is written, so a rejected call leaves the disk untouched. Missing parent directories are created.

THE FIELD TO READ IS purgedOrphans. Blender DELETES datablocks with no users and no fake user when it writes - an action unlinked from its object, an image nothing points at, a node group nobody instanced. That is permanent, silent, and caused BY the successful save. They are counted BEFORE the write, because afterwards they do not exist to count, and reported by type and name. Give one a fake user first if you want to keep it.

Success is stat'd off disk - a save that raises no error but leaves no file, or an empty one, is reported as a failure.
bl_save_image:
Write a Blender image datablock to disk (PNG 8/16-bit, JPEG quality, EXR half/full, any still format of the build) and point it at the file so a painted canvas survives a reopen; repoint=false writes a copy.

Parameters: filepath (str, required) is the file to write; '//' is relative to the open .blend and anything still relative resolves against the working directory, and the reply gives the absolute path. color_depth (int, default None: the image's own) is for PNG and OPEN_EXR only: a PNG is written at the image's own depth, 8 for an 8-bit image and 16 for a float one, so any other value is refused; an EXR takes 16 (half float, written through a temporary scene with the Standard view transform, and only for a Non-Color float image) or 32 (full float, the default). overwrite (bool, default None, read as true) replaces a file already at the path and reports what it replaced; false refuses a path that exists. format, when left out, comes from the extension (.png, .jpg, .exr, .tga, .tif, .bmp, .webp, .hdr, .jp2, .avif where the build has the format), else PNG; the accepted names are this build's still formats, read from the build's enum. image is also accepted as name.

OUT: image, file (absolute path), bytes, format, colorDepth, quality, route (save, or save_render for a half-float EXR), repointed, source, filepath (null when repoint is false), dirty, colorSpace, overwrote, plus replacedBytes and replacedModified when a file was replaced, and a note when a copy was written.

Refused, with nothing written: an unknown key; an image that does not exist or is a viewer image (render result or compositor viewer); a missing filepath, one with a control character or one naming a directory; a format this build lacks; a 0x0 image; quality on anything but JPEG, or outside 0-100; an EXR of an 8-bit image; an EXR depth other than 16 or 32; a 16-bit EXR of a color (not Non-Color) image; a PNG depth other than the image's own; color_depth on another format; an existing file with overwrite false; a folder that does not exist; repoint false for a generated image on a build whose Image.save has no save_copy; and a write Blender fails (the image's path and format are put back). A save Blender reports done with no file at the path is refused too.
bl_scene_info: Summary of the current Blender scene: objectCount, objectsByType, objects[] (names and types; detail:true swaps in a full object_info each), activeObject, selectedObjects, collections, blendFile, and unitSettings. Read-only. Use it to confirm what bl_import_mesh actually landed, or that a previous run's wreckage is still sitting in the scene - bl_import_mesh with clear_scene defaults to wiping it precisely because a failed run leaves its object behind on purpose, as the debugging artifact. It also warns when unitSettings.scaleLength is not 1.0, which is worth reading before any export: MEASURED on 4.4.0, the same 10 BU cube exported at scaleLength 0.01 reimports at 0.1 BU while UnitScaleFactor in the FBX header stays 1.0 either way - so a scene left at a non-default unit scale silently rescales the whole round trip and only the magnitudes give it away.
bl_select_edges: Resolve an edge selector against a mesh and report what it matches, WITHOUT modifying anything. seed_edge with loop=true or ring=true walks the edge loop or ring through one edge instead. trait NON_MANIFOLD, INTERIOR, LOOSE, BOUNDARY or DEGENERATE; max_reported 0 lists all. Always run this before bl_bevel_edges / bl_extrude_skirt: it runs the addon's SAME selector code, so what it reports is exactly what those two would act on, and a selector that matches zero edges makes both of them REFUSE rather than quietly no-op. selector is a small declarative predicate, not a script - {'boundaryOnly': true, 'axis': 'Y', 'side': 'both', 'tolerance': 1e-4} means 'boundary edges (one linked face) whose BOTH vertices sit within tolerance of the object's min-Y or max-Y', which is exactly the two long edges of a road tile. Accepted keys: boundaryOnly (alias boundary), axis, side ('min'|'max'|'both'), tolerance, minAngleDeg, maxAngleDeg, edgeIndices, allEdges - every criterion supplied is ANDed, and an unrecognised key is refused here with the accepted list rather than after a round trip. Omit selector entirely for the Y-boundary road-tile predicate. Returns count plus the boundary/interior/wire breakdown - a non-zero interiorEdges is why bl_extrude_skirt would refuse - and edgeIndices[] capped at max_reported. LOOPS AND RINGS (2026-10-04): seed_edge with loop=true walks the edge loop through it - at each vertex with four edges, the one sharing no face with the edge arriving; along a boundary, the next boundary edge - and ring=true the edge ring, across each quad to its opposite edge. Both ways, until the walk stops or closes (criteria.closed). The indices go to bevel, seam marking, transform and slide. With ring=true the reply's ringFaces lists the faces between the ring's edges - each quad the walk crossed, the row a separate or delete by faces takes (an iris row split from an eyeball); null for other selectors. TRAIT (2026-10-06): bl_mesh_quality lists the first 50 of each defect and nothing listed interior edges; trait selects every edge of one kind, alone or ANDed with selector. NON_MANIFOLD is not exactly two faces wound consistently (boundary, wire, an edge of 3+ faces, or flipped normals across it, as Blender's Select Non-Manifold); INTERIOR exactly two faces; LOOSE no face; BOUNDARY one face; DEGENERATE shorter than 1e-6 world. With trait the reply adds vertices {count, indices} - the edges' vertices, plus for NON_MANIFOLD the pinched ones (two fans of faces touching at one point), also listed as vertices.pinched - ready for bl_merge_vertices. max_reported 0 returns every index; edgeIndicesOmitted counts what a cap left out. trait does not combine with edgeIndices or seed_edge. STOPS (2026-10-06): stop_at with seed_edge ends the loop or ring at SEAM, SHARP or MATERIAL (a change of material across the walk), and a boundary loop at OUTER_CORNER (a vertex with one face), INNER_CORNER (three or more) or NGON; criteria.stopAt echoes them. A corner stop on a ring or an inner edge is refused.
bl_select_faces:
Find the Blender faces matching a description - the missing half of bl_assign_material_to_faces, which takes face INDICES that nothing could compute. Working out which indices you wanted was raw Python; bl_select_edges had no counterpart for faces. Criteria: material or slot, a WORLD-space normal direction (axis 'Z'/'-Z'/..., or direction as a vector [x,y,z], with a cone half-angle in DEGREES), area range, a world box (inside_box=[[minX,minY,minZ],[maxX,maxY,maxZ]], or box_min and box_max [x,y,z]; inside_box:true beside them is the same box), smooth/flat, and toward_point [x,y,z]: faces whose normal points at that world point within the angle (a hood's inner shell faces the head - hand the indices to bl_delete_mesh_elements), non_manifold (faces on an edge shared by more than two), trait (NON_MANIFOLD: on an edge not shared by exactly two faces; INTERIOR; LOOSE: sharing no edge; BOUNDARY; DEGENERATE: under 1e-9 m2), and uv_box [[u,v],[u,v]]: faces whose UV centre lies in that box, on uv_layer or the active map (a lining from its shell, by UV island). They AND together by default. Read-only - nothing is written and no selection state is touched. The NORMAL TEST IS WORLD SPACE through the inverse transpose, because a face pointing up in local space on a rotated object does not point up in the world and 'which faces are the floor' is a world question every time. The box test uses the face CENTRE, so a large face straddling the boundary is decided by its middle. matchedPerCriterion is returned so that 'nothing matched' names the culprit instead of being a dead end, and the count is always exact even when the index list is capped (limit 0 returns every index; indicesOmitted counts the rest). An object that draws instances - Geometry Nodes instances, particles, instancing - answers with instancesNote: instances are not part of any evaluated mesh, so this does not see them (measured on 3.6-5.2).

Parameters: min_area and max_area (float, default None each) keep faces whose area is at least / at most the value, measured as poly.area in the object's OWN (local, unscaled) units - not world area, unlike the normal and box tests; max_area below min_area is refused. Each counts as its own criterion in matchedPerCriterion. require_all (bool, default None, read as true) ANDs every given criterion; false ORs them, so a face matching any one is returned. Other defaults as the op reads them: angle 45 degrees, limit 1024 indices (0 = all), evaluated FALSE (the base mesh; true tests the modifier result).

OUT: ok, object, geometry ("base" or "evaluated"), faceCount, matched (exact), indices, indicesReturned, indicesOmitted, trait, mode ("AND" or "OR"), criteria (names that matched at least one face), matchedPerCriterion {criterion: count}, space, instancesNote (evaluated only, else null); note when nothing matched (names the criteria that matched no face); uvLayer and uvBox with uv_box; boxNote with a box; editModeStale, objectMode, staleNote when the object is in edit mode (the read is not refused; it reflects the mesh as of the last OBJECT mode).

Refusals (a read; nothing is written and no selection is touched): no object by that name; not a MESH; material and slot together; no slot holding that material (lists the slots); a slot that is not an integer or out of range; direction given as a string; axis with direction, or toward_point with either; an axis outside X, -X, Y, -Y, Z, -Z; a zero-length direction; angle outside (0, 180] when a direction or toward_point is used; max_area below min_area; inside_box true without both box corners, false, or malformed; only one box corner; a negative limit; an unknown trait; a malformed uv_box; uv_layer without uv_box; no such UV map (or no UV map at all) on the mesh tested; no criterion at all; any unknown key.
bl_set_bone_rest:
Move existing Blender bones' REST positions - bones [{name, head?, tail?, roll?}] in the armature's space, or apply_pose_as_rest - read back from the bones. Skinned meshes are not updated and are named; a proportion variant that keeps the bone names.

recalc_roll (1.3): {type POS_X | POS_Z | NEG_X | NEG_Z | GLOBAL_POS_X ... GLOBAL_NEG_Z | ACTIVE (with active: a bone to align to) | CURSOR, bones [names] or prefix, axisFlip, axisOnly} - Blender's Recalculate Roll on those bones, alone in the call; each bone's roll before and after (radians).
bl_set_vertex_weights:
Create a Blender vertex group and put weights in it - which NOTHING in the addon could do. BY POSITION TOO: by_axis {axis X|Y|Z, from, to, weightFrom (default 1), weightTo (default 0), space WORLD|LOCAL} gives every vertex (or just `vertices`) a weight from where it sits - weightFrom at `from`, weightTo at `to`, linear between, clamped beyond - which is how a soft body's base is pinned under a loose top, since no op returns vertex positions to weight by index. bl_list_vertex_groups, bl_normalize_weights and bl_transfer_weights all operate on vertex groups and nothing created one, so a rig imported with weights could be normalised and a rig built here could not be weighted at all. THE POSTCONDITION IS THE WEIGHTS, NOT THE GROUP: a group that exists with every weight at zero deforms nothing and reads back identically to a working one in bl_list_vertex_groups, so this reports verticesWithNonZeroWeight - the number that decides whether anything actually moves - and says so outright when every weight written was zero. Membership and a zero weight are DIFFERENT states and are distinguished: vg.weight() raises for a vertex outside the group rather than returning 0, so a vertex not in the group at all cannot be normalised or transferred. A duplicate group name gives the NEW group a .001 suffix and leaves the incumbent alone, uniformly on every build - unlike object renaming, which reverses across the 3.6/4.x line - and it is reported rather than refused. all_vertices weights every vertex; exclusive then takes them out of every other group (otherGroupsCleared names each) - a rigid piece on one bone.

mode CLEAN, INVERT, LEVELS (1.3), on group, or groups [names] | "DEFORM" (every group named after a deform bone of armature, default the Armature modifier's) | "ALL": CLEAN removes weights under threshold (default 0.01), keep_single (default true) keeping a vertex whose every weight is under it in its strongest group; INVERT writes 1 - w (auto_assign adds the group's missing vertices at 1, auto_remove takes 0s out - both default true, as Blender's); LEVELS writes (w + offset) * gain clamped to 0-1 (offset -1..1, gain 0..10). Per group counts in the reply.
bl_extract_deform_skeleton:
Make a deform-only copy of a Blender control rig (each deform bone under its nearest deform ancestor) and bake the rig's actions onto it through Copy Transforms - what a game engine keeps. Reports each baked action's measured motion error. Built from Blender's own steps: a new armature `name` (default <rig>_deform) with every deform bone at its rest, each parented to its nearest DEFORM ancestor (connections kept unless disconnect, for squash and stretch), a Copy Transforms per bone to the rig's bone of the same name, then each of `actions` (default: the rig's current action) put on the rig and baked over its frame range by bake_to_keyframes with visual keying. The baked action is named <action><suffix> (suffix '_deform') with a fake user. clear_constraints (default true) removes the Copy Transforms. THE MOTION CHECK RUNS WITH EVERY CONSTRAINT MUTED: the copy plays its baked keys against the rig at the first, middle and last frame, and maxBonePositionError, maxBoneRotationErrorRadians and motionPreserved come back per action - bake_to_keyframes' own check would read 0 whatever the keys held, because the constraints still drive the copy. The rig gets its own action back. A name in use, a missing action, a baked name in use or a rig with no deform bone is refused before anything is made. Export the copy with bl_export_mesh animations_only.

A FRAME CHANGE STEPS EVERY LIVE SIMULATION (2026-10-05): moving the scene's frame evaluates each unbaked cloth, soft body, emitter or dynamic-hair particle system, dynamic-paint canvas and rigid body world in the view layer, and a fluid domain whose cache type is REPLAY - on an object hidden with the eye or from the render too (only hide_viewport or the modifier's show_viewport off takes it out). A leftover cloth on a render-hidden object stepped against a body's collision during a pose check and asked for 58.7 GB. So a call that would move the frame past such a cache's first frame is REFUSED before anything changes, naming each simulation and the colliders it would step against; bake them, take them out of the depsgraph, or pass allow_simulation=true, and the reply's simulationsStepped and colliders say what stepped. A Geometry Nodes simulation zone is listed (geometryNodesSimulations) and not refused: Blender exposes no baked flag for it.
bl_fit_armature: Move a Blender armature's bones onto a character from landmarks {bone: [x, y, z]} (armature space), keeping names and hierarchy; unnamed bones follow their parent, symmetry 'X' fills the other side. Reports each bone's displacement and lengths. Each landmark puts that bone's HEAD at the point; a bone not named moves rigidly with its parent, so the fingers follow a moved wrist. A bone with a connected child takes that child's head as its tail (Blender keeps them together in edit mode); otherwise a bone whose only child was landmarked ends at that child's head, and any other bone keeps its head-to-tail offset. symmetry 'X' fills a named bone's missing partner ('_l'/'_r' or `pair`) with the landmark mirrored, and mirroredLandmarks names them. A landmark that would give a bone zero length, or connected children that would need different tails, is refused before anything is written. The rest is written by bl_set_bone_rest and read back; displacement, lengthsBefore and lengthsAfter come back per bone, and a skinned mesh is named (it deforms from the new rest). Landmarks found on a mesh automatically are not part of this call.
bl_create_armature_from_skeleton: Build a Blender armature from an Unreal skeleton's bones - list_bones with include_transforms. Its names, parents and parent-relative reference pose (cm) are composed to rest positions, mapped (x, -y, z) to metres, optionally scaled to height_m. The Unreal half is list_bones with include_transforms; pass its `bones` array as is. Each bone's component-space transform is composed down the hierarchy as FTransform does (rotation from FRotator::Quaternion, the parent's rotation and scale applied to the child's location), then mapped to Blender as (x, -y, z) x unit_scale (default 0.01, centimetres to metres). A bone's head is that position; its tail is its only child's head, or else its head plus its own forward axis (the engine's X) at leaf_length (default half the distance to its parent's head, at least 1 cm). height_m scales the rig so its heads span that height (heightScale comes back). The armature is named `name`, default 'root' - the engine's convention. Roll is not carried; Blender rebuilds a bone's roll from its axis. A list with no root or two, a parent missing from the list, a bone twice or a refPose without location, rotation and scale is refused and nothing is made.
bl_set_bone_properties:
Write existing Blender bones' properties - use_deform, parent (or clear_parent), connected, bbone_segments, inherit_scale - on bones by name, name_prefix or all. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. Previous and new values come back. WHY: bl_list_bones reads use_deform and connected, bl_add_bones and bl_set_bone_rest write positions, and nothing wrote the rest - deform off on a root and the IK targets before automatic weights (an engine keeps only deform bones), bendy segments back to 1 (the engine importer ignores them), a hierarchy reparented to its deform bones. Exactly one of bones, name_prefix or all. parent may not be the bone itself or one of its descendants (a loop is refused before anything is written); clear_parent removes it. connected on puts the head on the parent's tail, as Blender does, and is refused for a bone with no parent. bbone_segments is 1-32. inherit_scale is checked against this Blender build's own Bone.inherit_scale enum (FULL, FIX_SHEAR, ALIGNED, AVERAGE, NONE, NONE_LEGACY on 5.2.1). dry_run returns the bones and their current values without writing. Every value is read back off the bones after the write; changes lists each changed bone's before and after. DISPLAY: custom_shape (an object; "" clears it) with custom_shape_translation, custom_shape_rotation (degrees) and custom_shape_scale on the pose bone; color {normal, select, active} ([r, g, b] 0-1, palette CUSTOM) or color_palette (a theme set from this build's list). Bone colours are per bone from Blender 4.0 and refused before it.

BENDY BONE SEGMENTS, THE DESTINATION DECIDES (2026-10-11): about 10 to stop poke-through in a Blender render, 1 before an export to an engine (the importer ignores them) - set them for the purpose, not to a fixed value.
bl_step_simulation:
Step a Blender simulation frame by frame and stop BEFORE the next frame once it runs away: each frame reports the object's max and p99 vertex speed (m/s), its box, the process memory and the time; it stops at end, past max_speed, past max_memory_gb (default 12) or after max_seconds (default 60), says which in stoppedBecause, and names the fastest vertices. WHY: on 2026-10-03 a garment drape in an agent's Blender grew to 61.7 GB and a Movie Render Queue render died when the pagefile ran out. The agent's own stepper, run through bl_run_python, found the cause with memory flat: a cuff exploding at 3, 6, then 9 m/s from zero-length edges. A speed limit stops an explosion before it builds the collision pair lists that eat memory; the memory limit is the backstop. STEPPING IS IN ORDER: a cloth or soft body advances one frame at a time, so start defaults to the frame after the current one and a start that is neither that nor a cache's first frame is reported in jumpNote. Speeds are world-space metres per second through the scene's unit scale and fps; the first frame has no speed when the call did not start from the next frame (speedNote). memorySource says what was read: Windows private bytes, Linux resident, or a peak elsewhere. max_seconds is at most 600 - the call holds Blender's one socket - so a long sim is stepped in chunks, each call continuing from the frame the last stopped on. The scene is left on the last frame stepped. Rows past 500 are trimmed to the last 500 (framesTruncated); peakSpeed and peakMemoryGB cover them all.

colliderBlockers (2026-10-05) repeats physics_info's collider blockers before the first step: a collider no simulation can see (hide_viewport, a hidden or excluded collection, the modifier off in the viewport). looseVertices (2026-10-05): for a cloth or soft body, the base mesh's vertices no face uses - count and the first 50 with world positions - named before the first step: they fall on gravity alone and their speed reads as the cloth running away. The call still steps.
bl_transfer_face_materials: Give each face of a Blender target mesh the material of the nearest face of a source mesh, in world space - a high poly made from a low poly, or a remeshed garment, gets its panel materials back. Slots are matched by material name and added when missing; max_distance leaves far faces alone. WHY: a high poly made from a low poly (convert, subdivide, displace) came out with every face on slot 0, so its ID bake was one colour, and the garment work copied the materials across in raw Python six times. Each target face's centre finds the nearest point on the source's faces (a BVH of the source's base mesh, both transforms applied) and takes that face's material. The target's own slot order is kept; a material it lacks is appended (slotsAdded). The reply carries byMaterial, facesChanged, fartherThanMax, sourceSlotEmpty and the max and p95 distances - a large one means the wrong pair of objects. A call that would assign nothing is refused.
bl_transform_objects:
Rotate/translate independent Blender objects together around a WORLD-space pivot.

Angles are XYZ radians. The group mapping is translation + pivot + rotation; for example, pivot=[2,0,0], rotation=[0,0,-1.5707963267948966], translation=[-2,0,0] turns a group around its old center and recenters it. Refuses parent hierarchies and validates the whole list before writing. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. Mesh data is never baked.

CHANGE CAP: a call that would change more than the open file's cap of distinct objects, materials or collections (default 25; mif_project_mode change_cap, 0 off) writes nothing and answers ok:false, capped, the targets and a previewId; preview_id alone commits it once within 10 minutes, refused if a target has gone or moved since (docs/15 section 6).
bl_transform_selection:
Translate, scale or rotate (angle about axis X, Y, Z or [x,y,z]) selected vertices, edges or faces of a Blender mesh in place, with optional proportional falloff and a vertex-group mask. Edge and face selections transform the union of their vertices. Select with explicit indices, or use box_min/box_max for vertices. box_min, box_max, vector and pivot are interpreted in the requested local or world space. dry_run predicts and reports the exact affected coordinates without writing the mesh: on a dry run `changed` is false and `wouldChange` carries the prediction. WITH SHAPE KEYS and no shape_key, the edit moves the base mesh and the reference key, and every relative key by the same offset (measured on every build; shapeKeysNote says so). shape_key reshapes ONE key relative to its own vertices instead - selection, pivot and bounds are measured on that key, only it is written, and the reference key is refused. ROTATE takes angle (degrees) and axis (X, Y, Z or [x,y,z]) about pivot. falloff {type, radius, connectedOnly, projectAxis, seed} moves the vertices within radius of the selection too, by Blender's proportional-editing curves; mask (a vertex group, or {group, invert}) scales each vertex's move by its weight.

component_type is VERTEX, EDGE or FACE; indices selects those components explicitly, while box_min plus box_max selects vertices inside an inclusive box. operation is TRANSLATE, SCALE or ROTATE, vector is [x,y,z] (not for ROTATE), and space is LOCAL or WORLD; pivot is optional for SCALE and ROTATE and defaults to the selection center in the same space.

Invalid indices, empty selections, edit mode and non-mesh objects are refused before mutation. Linked duplicates intentionally share mesh data, so meshSharedWith and alsoChangedCount report every other object affected by a real write.

FALLOFF is Blender's proportional editing: every vertex closer than radius (in space units) to the nearest selected one moves by the same transform scaled by the curve at t = 1 - distance/radius - SMOOTH (default), SPHERE, ROOT, INVERSE_SQUARE, SHARP, LINEAR, CONSTANT or RANDOM (seeded by seed). connectedOnly measures along edges and reaches only vertices joined to the selection; projectAxis leaves one axis out of the distance, so a column moves together. It works inside shape_key, so a region moved in a key blends into its neighbors. falloffVertexCount and affectedVertexCount count the vertices moved beyond the selection and in all. A mask that weights every vertex 0 is refused; maskedOutSelected counts selected vertices the mask left still.

SHRINK_FATTEN AND TO_SPHERE (2026-10-05): SHRINK_FATTEN moves each vertex distance along its vertex normal (negative shrinks; in WORLD space along the world normal, in world units) - a thumb pad given volume after a loop cut. TO_SPHERE with factor 0 to 1 moves each vertex along its ray from the pivot (default the selection's centre) toward the sphere whose radius is the selected vertices' mean distance from it, Blender's To Sphere: at 1 every vertex is on the sphere, at 0.5 halfway; sphereRadius is reported. Both take falloff and mask like the others; neither takes vector, angle or axis, and SHRINK_FATTEN takes no pivot. Measured: a 2 m cube's corners fattened by sqrt(3) x 0.1 land at +-1.1.

With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.
bl_separate_mesh:
Split a Blender mesh into separate objects - mode 'loose' (each island), 'material' (one per material in use) or 'selection': faces (indices or a bl_select_faces reply), vertex_group or loop go to one new object; duplicate keeps the original whole. New objects are NAMED BY BLENDER as <source>.001, .002, so the response lists what actually appeared rather than predicting names. Separating a mesh with nothing to split on succeeds with createdCount 0 and says the zero is a measured result, not a failure.

MODE 'selection' (2026-10-05): faces (indices, or a bl_select_faces reply - refused when it listed fewer than it matched), vertex_group (the faces whose every vertex weighs min_weight or more, default 0.5) or loop (edge indices, or {near: [x,y,z]} | {vertex: i} | {edge: i} | {index: i}: an open boundary loop as bl_fill_mesh_loop names one) go to ONE new object - a sleeve's band split off as a cuff, a cup's rim loop copied out for the coffee surface - where a material slot and mode 'material' were the only route and left the slot behind. The new object is a copy of the source (transform, material slots, UV layers, vertex groups, modifiers) cut down to the selection; without duplicate the source loses those faces and the vertices only they used. A loop whose edges border faces is copied only (duplicate true): taking it out would delete those faces. new_name names the new object. Done in bmesh - no edit mode. Reply: created, and new / source with vertex, edge and face counts. Refused before any change: no selector or two, a selector with another mode, an index past the mesh, a vertex group the object lacks or that covers no whole face, every face without duplicate, a truncated select_faces reply, a new_name in use, shape keys.
bl_set_parent:
Parent a Blender object to another object, or to a bone of an armature (type BONE with bone), or clear its parent with clear:true - the hierarchy a prop on an empty, a camera on a rig or an FBX into Unreal needs. keep_transform (default true) keeps it where it is in the world, and the response MEASURES that: worldBefore / worldAfter and worldMoved. A cycle is refused before anything is written. type VERTEX or VERTEX_3 with vertices [i] / [i, j, k] or {near: [x,y,z]} rides one vertex or a triangle of a mesh parent. A button or pocket hung on a cloth follows the vertex as the cloth moves - the cloth-riding alternative to binding a deform modifier. near (world) picks the nearest vertex, or for VERTEX_3 the three corners nearest the point of the face nearest it; the reply's parentAfter.vertices names the indices used. keep_transform solves the local transform in the vertex parent's evaluated space (Blender's matrix_world setter measured one vertex position off on 5.2.2).

KEEP TRANSFORM IS MEASURED. keep_transform (default true) keeps the object where it is in the world; the response reads the world matrix before and after and reports worldMoved, so the claim cannot agree with itself by construction. keep_transform:false takes the object's current local transform into the parent's space instead (Blender's without-inverse), and worldMoved says so. The parent inverse is left as identity either way, so the local transform is the offset from the parent - what an exporter writes.

A CYCLE IS REFUSED before anything is written: an object as its own parent, or parented to one of its own descendants. type BONE needs an armature parent and one of its bones, named in the refusal when it is missing. clear:true with no parent to clear succeeds and says so; parent and clear together are refused. type ARMATURE_AUTO skins a mesh to an armature parent with automatic (heat) weights and an Armature modifier - Blender's Ctrl+P With Automatic Weights - and ARMATURE_NAME makes the modifier and one empty group per bone. Heat weighting fails per bone without an error, so the reply lists bonesWithNoWeights and verticesUnweighted, with a warning when vertices got no weight.

FALLBACK where heat finds no solution: with type ARMATURE_AUTO, fallback NEAREST weighs each vertex heat left with no deform-bone weight by 1/distance^2 to the nearest max_influences (default 4, 1-8) deform bone segments, normalised to 1; DIFFUSE spreads the weighted vertices' weights along the mesh's edges into the empty ones, one ring per pass, and gives NEAREST's to a piece with no weighted vertex at all. Only the empty vertices are written. Reply: verticesFilled, influencesPerFilledVertex [min, max] and verticesUnweightedAfter. A fallback or max_influences without ARMATURE_AUTO is refused.

CHOSEN BONES (2026-10-04): with type ARMATURE_AUTO, bones [names] weights those bones only - Blender's Assign Automatic from Bones (paint.weight_from_bones), run headless with the mesh in weight paint mode and the named bones selected, the modes and selections put back; every other group is left exactly as it was (checked, and refused if Blender changed one). include_parents (default true for AUTO) adds each named bone's nearest deform parent to the run: heat weighting gives a vertex to the nearest of ALL deform bones and writes only the selected ones, so a finger added to a weighted hand with the hand left out gets the tip while the hand keeps its old weight there - normalised, the finger then moves half as far (parentsNote says so when include_parents is false). Measured on a tube heat-weighted before the finger deformed: the tip ring went to the finger (> 0.5) and the hand's weight there dropped by more than 0.3, the arm untouched. With ARMATURE_NAME, bones makes an empty group per named bone only. The mesh is parented and given an Armature modifier first when it has neither (armatureModifierAdded). Reply: groupsWritten, groupsCreated, parentsIncluded, verticesChanged, weightRangeBefore/After on the vertices that changed, verticesUnweighted, bonesWithNoWeights (with a warning: a bone nothing of the mesh is nearest gets no vertex). Refused before anything is written: bones with another type, include_parents without bones, bones with fallback, only non-deforming bones, a bone the armature lacks. HEAD TO TAIL (2026-10-06; 5.2 adds the slider): head_tail 0 (the bone's head) to 1 (its tail, the default and Blender's own) says where a type BONE parent's space sits, written through the parent inverse on every build - a child parented at 0.5 with keep_transform false sits at the bone's middle. Refused on any other type.
bl_set_bone_pose:
Pose one bone of a Blender armature: location [x,y,z] in the bone's own space, rotation [x,y,z] euler radians or quaternion [w,x,y,z], scale [x,y,z], with rotation_mode applied first. Character animation had zero coverage here - bones could be listed and renamed and nothing else - and this was unreachable through bl_set_keyframe until the same day, because its dotted-path walk stripped subscripts so pose.bones["x"].location resolved to the bone COLLECTION. rotation (euler) and quaternion are refused against the bone's actual rotation_mode rather than silently ignored, and refused together. THE READ-BACK IS EVALUATED through the depsgraph: a bone with an IK chain, a Copy Rotation or a Limit does not end up where you put it, and pose_bone.matrix is the raw value. The response reports `written` and `evaluated*` separately - if they differ, that is the constraint working, not a fault. Call mif_help("bl_set_bone_pose") first. rotation_mode (QUATERNION, XYZ ... AXIS_ANGLE) is applied BEFORE the values: a new bone is QUATERNION and ignores a euler, so pass rotation_mode XYZ with rotation in one call. Changing the mode keeps the bone's current pose (measured on 3.6-5.2); rotationModeBefore reports what it was.

The evaluated read-back is evaluatedHeadWorld / evaluatedTailWorld, taken through the depsgraph, and when it differs from what was written the constraints list names the constraint that moved the bone.

MIRROR (2026-10-04): mirror {pair: 'FLIP_NAME' | [a, b] | {name: partner}, axis 'X', verify true} then writes the partner bone with the same values flipped across X - location x negated, an euler's Y and Z negated, a quaternion's y and z negated, scale kept (Blender's own paste-flipped rule) - and with verify reads both evaluated bones back: mirror.mirrorErrorUnits and mirrorErrorDegrees are the distance between the partner and the mirror image of this bone. The pair is required, never assumed: FLIP_NAME is Blender's bpy.utils.flip_name, measured identical on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1 (.L/.R, _l/_r, -l, 'arm l', L_arm, left_arm, Left_arm, armLeft, hand.L.001 -> hand.R.001); a pair swaps that suffix only; a table maps names. Measured on a mirror-image rig: error 0; with the partner's roll changed by 0.6 rad the error is tens of degrees and mirror.mirrorNote says the sides are not mirror images. Refused before anything is written: no pair, a bone with no side under it, a partner the armature lacks, a partner in another rotation mode (set its rotation_mode first), an axis other than X. Pose-mode X-Axis Mirror (bl_set_armature_properties x_mirror_pose) steers interactive transforms only and changes nothing for a typed write.

TURN AND IK (1.4, 2026-11-07): turn {axis: [x,y,z] | 'X' | 'Y' | 'Z' (WORLD), degrees, pivot 'head' | 'tail' | [x,y,z]} turns the bone about a world axis through its posed head (children follow), composed onto the pose as it stands, and reply.turn measures the angle back off the evaluated tail (measuredDegrees). ik {target: [x,y,z] (WORLD) | 'rest', pole: [x,y,z] (WORLD), keepRotation 'current' | 'rest' | 'none'} on an END bone (a foot) solves its parent and grandparent (shin, thigh) analytically and writes them as plain FK: the end's head lands on target ('rest' = where it stands in the rest pose, so lowering the root then ik target 'rest' on each foot is a crouch with the feet planted), the middle joint bends toward pole (default the chain's current bend, else its rest bend), and the end keeps its world rotation. reply.ik gives endErrorM, endRotationErrorDeg, jointWorld, reachM, distanceM and each chain bone before and after. Refused before any write: a target out of reach (distance and reach named), a chain whose joints do not meet, a straight chain with no pole, a pole on the line to the target, a constrained chain bone, ik together with channel values, a turn or a mirror.
