A turn about a pivot other than the head is refused on a CONNECTED bone: its head cannot leave its parent's tail, and Blender would drop the move and turn it about its head under ok.
bl_set_armature_properties:
Set a Blender armature's display and pose options - rest or pose position, display type, names, axes, X-mirror, auto IK - each read back with the previous values.

Set a Blender armature's display and pose options: pose_mode POSE|REST, display_type, show_names/axes/bone_shapes/bone_colors, show_in_front, x_mirror_edit, x_mirror_pose, auto_ik. Each read back; the reply gives the previous values.

WHY: they were written at creation only (bl_create_armature display_type and show_in_front) and pose_position was switched to REST and back inside two internal measurements with no call exposing it. The options live on three owners and this writes each where it lives: the Armature data (pose_position, display_type OCTAHEDRAL|STICK|BBONE|ENVELOPE|WIRE - read from the build's RNA, the same five on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2 - show_names, show_axes, show_bone_custom_shapes, show_bone_colors, which 3.6 calls show_group_colors, and the edit-mode use_mirror_x), the object's Pose (use_auto_ik and the pose-mode use_mirror_x) and the Object (show_in_front). pose_mode REST shows and renders the rest pose while the pose and its keys are kept; POSE brings them back - measured, a bone moved 0.3 along its own Y read back at its rest tail under REST and at the posed tail under POSE. x_mirror_pose and auto_ik steer interactive transforms in the viewport only and the reply says so (interactiveNote): a typed write is mirrored by bl_set_bone_pose mirror or bl_copy_pose flip. Reply: before, after and changed. Refused, NOTHING changed: an enum value this build lacks (the list is in the refusal), a non-boolean flag, nothing to set, a non-armature. A bad value beside a good one refuses both.
bl_key_pose:
Key Blender pose bones at a frame as they stand (bones, name_prefix or all): location, rotation in each bone's own mode, scale, and custom_properties (true or names); reset keys the rest pose.

WHY: bl_set_keyframe keys one path per call and needs a value, so keying a pose already there meant reading every channel with bl_evaluate_at_frame and writing it back path by path - a walk keyed on every control at contact, down, passing and up frames is hundreds of calls. This keys the values the bones hold with pose_bone.keyframe_insert, the same call on 3.6 to 5.2 (the keying-set operator changed between 3.6 and 4.2, so it is not used), in each bone's group. ROTATION ON THE BONE'S OWN MODE: rotation_quaternion for QUATERNION, rotation_axis_angle for AXIS_ANGLE, rotation_euler for an euler order - so a quaternion bone gets 10 keys (3 + 4 + 3) and an euler bone 9; measured 58 keys on a 6-bone rig with two euler hands. channels narrows to [location, rotation, scale]; custom_properties true keys every numeric custom property of each bone (an FK/IK switch), a list keys those names (a bone lacking one is listed in customPropertiesMissing; none at all is refused); a text property is never keyed. interpolation is read from the build's Keyframe enum and set on the keys at that frame. reset true writes location 0, rotation identity and scale 1 first - a rest pose keyed at a frame (a garment simulation that starts on a still body). Reply: bonesKeyed, keysWritten, and per bone its rotationMode and keys. A CONSTRAINED BONE's keys hold its own channels, not where the constraint puts it: constraintDriven names each such bone with how far its evaluated pose differs (units and degrees) - bl_bake_to_keyframes keys where it really is. Refused before any key: a named bone that does not exist, more than one of bones/name_prefix/all or none, an unknown channel or interpolation, a prefix that matches nothing, a non-armature.
bl_copy_pose:
Copy a Blender armature's pose from one frame to another, optionally flipped by name_rule (FLIP_NAME, a suffix pair or a table), keyed by default; reports the mirror error.

WHY: a walk's contact pose at 1 pasted flipped at 13 and plain at 25 to close the loop, then the down, passing and up poses at 3, 6 and 9 flipped at 15, 18 and 21 - Blender's pose.copy and pose.paste(flipped) need pose mode and a bone selection, so this is native - and it gives what they give: settled 2026-10-18 on 3.6.23-5.2.1, pose.paste(flipped) run headless and this op flipped arm.L onto arm.R with the same location and rotation. The mirror frame of a cycle is start + length / 2 of the rig's own range, never a constant: a 24-frame loop numbered 1..25 mirrors at 13, numbered 0..24 at 12. Each bone's own channels are read at from_frame (Blender's Copy Pose rule) and written at to_frame; with flip each bone is written onto its partner under name_rule - FLIP_NAME is Blender's bpy.utils.flip_name (measured identical on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1), a pair like ['.L', '.R'] or ['_l', '_r'] swaps that suffix only, a table {name: partner} maps both ways - with location x negated, an euler's Y and Z negated, a quaternion's or axis-angle's y and z negated and scale kept; a bone with no side is flipped in place, and a bone whose partner the armature lacks is left alone and listed in withoutPartner. A partner in another rotation mode is written through the basis matrix (rotationModeConverted). key (default true) keys location, rotation in the bone's mode and scale at to_frame; key false leaves the pose unkeyed and keyNote says an animated channel takes its value back at the next frame change. The scene is left at to_frame (frameBefore, frameNow). CHECKED THROUGH THE DEPSGRAPH: each written bone's evaluated matrix at to_frame against the mirror (or the copy) of its source's at from_frame - check.maxErrorUnits, maxErrorDegrees and the worst rows. Measured on a mirror-image rig: 0 error, hand.R's tail at 13 is hand.L's at 1 with x negated. A rig whose sides are not mirror images, or a constraint that moves a bone, shows as a large error and mirrorNote; a constrained source is listed in constrainedBones (its channels were copied - copying its evaluated pose would apply the constraint twice). Refused, NOTHING changed: flip without name_rule, a malformed rule, name_rule without flip, the same frame without flip, a missing bone, no named bone with a partner, two bones onto one, interpolation with key false.

A FRAME CHANGE STEPS EVERY LIVE SIMULATION (2026-10-05): moving the scene's frame evaluates each unbaked cloth, soft body, emitter or dynamic-hair particle system, dynamic-paint canvas and rigid body world in the view layer, and a fluid domain whose cache type is REPLAY - on an object hidden with the eye or from the render too (only hide_viewport or the modifier's show_viewport off takes it out). A leftover cloth on a render-hidden object stepped against a body's collision during a pose check and asked for 58.7 GB. So a call that would move the frame past such a cache's first frame is REFUSED before anything changes, naming each simulation and the colliders it would step against; bake them, take them out of the depsgraph, or pass allow_simulation=true, and the reply's simulationsStepped and colliders say what stepped. A Geometry Nodes simulation zone is listed (geometryNodesSimulations) and not refused: Blender exposes no baked flag for it.
bl_create_pose_asset:
Store a Blender armature's current pose (all bones, or bones / name_prefix) as a pose asset in this file or in an asset library by name, with a catalog path and a thumbnail; the rig's own action is kept.

WHY: a character-specific pose (a fist, a wave) stored by bone name and applied again later had no typed call. NATIVE ON EVERY BUILD, because Blender's own operator differs by build - a Python operator on 3.6 that puts the new action on the rig, native on 4.4 and 5.2 where it fails headless without an asset library reference (measured on 4.4.0: 'Unexpected library type. Failed to create pose asset') and needs PoseBone.select on 5.x. Here a new action named `asset` is put on the rig only while each bone's location, rotation (in the bone's own mode), scale and its ten bendy-bone pose properties (curve in and out x and z, roll in and out, scale in and out, ease in and out) are keyed at frame 1 in the bone's group, with any other property of those bones the rig's action keys on the current frame - the curves Blender's own operator writes (settled 2026-10-18 on 3.6.23-5.2.1 against poselib.create_pose_asset) - and the rig's action (and 5.x slot) is put back: rigActionKept names it. The action is marked as an asset with a fake user. library CURRENT_FILE (default) keeps it in this file; the NAME of an asset library from Preferences > File Paths writes <library>/<asset>.blend with it (never over an existing file), reads that file back to prove the asset is listed, and leaves no local copy. catalog is a catalog path ('Poses/Hands', found in or appended to blender_assets.cats.txt at the library's root - beside the saved .blend for the current file, so an unsaved file takes only a catalog UUID) or a UUID; catalogCreated says when a line was added. thumbnail GENERATE (default: Blender's own preview, 128 x 128 headless on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2), NONE, or an image file's path (its pixels become the preview). description is stored on the asset. Measured: arm.L and hand.L give 47 curves (19 before the bendy-bone channels were added, 2026-10-18). Refused, NOTHING made: a name an action in this file already has, a library not in Preferences, a file already in the library, a thumbnail file that does not exist, a catalog path in an unsaved file, a missing bone, a non-armature.
bl_apply_pose_asset:
Apply a pose asset to a Blender armature at a blend of 0 to 1, optionally flipped by name_rule, onto all its bones or bones; reports the bones moved and the largest change.

NATIVE, because Blender's poselib.apply_pose_asset reads the asset from an asset browser's context and cannot run headless on any build - measured: 3.6.23 and 4.4.0 'poll() failed, context is incorrect', 5.2.1 'Error: No asset in context'. The asset's bone curves are read at its first frame and written onto the rig's bones by name: location and scale blended linearly from the current value, rotation slerped as a quaternion and written in the bone's own rotation mode (an euler asset read in the bone's euler order) - measured: blend 0.5 puts a bone exactly halfway along the shortest arc. Only channels the asset keys are written; bone curves for other properties and non-bone curves are listed in notApplied. flipped with name_rule (FLIP_NAME is Blender's own flip_name, which its flipped apply uses; a suffix pair or a table) writes each bone's values onto its partner with Blender's mirror signs (location x, euler Y and Z, quaternion y and z negated) - writtenFrom lists the pairs. bones narrows the write to those rig bones (named after flipping). library reads the asset from that asset library's .blend files (appended, applied, and the appended copy removed again). The pose is written, not keyed: on a rig whose action animates those channels the next frame change puts the action's values back, and animatedChannels / animatedNote name them - key_pose keys the result. A plain action that is not marked as an asset applies too, with assetNote. Reply: bonesWritten, bonesMoved, largestChangeDegrees, largestChangeUnits, bonesMissing (asset bones the rig lacks). Refused, NOTHING changed: blend outside 0-1, flipped without name_rule or name_rule without flipped, an asset not in the file or the library, a bone the rig lacks, an asset with no bone channel, a non-armature.
bl_mark_asset:
Mark a Blender datablock (ACTION, COLLECTION, MATERIAL, NODE_TREE, OBJECT, WORLD) as an asset of this file with a catalog, description and tags, or clear the mark.

WHY: nothing marked a node group, material or object as an asset, so nothing made here showed in the asset browser (bl_append_from_file already covers reuse by name). kind is one of the six types the asset browser lists on 3.6 to 5.2; ID.asset_mark runs headless on all three builds and sets the fake user. catalog is a catalog UUID, or a catalog path found in or appended to blender_assets.cats.txt beside the saved .blend (an unsaved file is refused a path). tags are added (existing ones kept); description is set; preview=true generates Blender's preview (off by default - for an object it renders). clear=true calls asset_clear, which also takes the fake user OFF - measured - so an unused datablock is dropped at the next save, and warning says so. Reply: isAsset (read back), wasAsset, fakeUser, catalogId, catalogPath, catalogCreated, description, tags, preview. An asset of the current file shows in the browser's Current File library; for other files to use it, the file has to be saved inside an asset library's folder. Refused, NOTHING changed: an unknown kind, a missing datablock, a linked datablock, clear on a non-asset, clear with description/tags/catalog/preview, a catalog path in an unsaved file, tags that are not words.
bl_set_camera:
Change a Blender camera that already exists, including SWITCHING which camera the scene renders through - make_active was previously available only at creation, so choosing between two existing cameras was impossible without bl_run_python. sensor_fit is here because without it sensor_width is a half-answer and no real lens can be matched. Type-gated settings are validated against the type the camera will BE after the call, so retyping to ORTHO and setting ortho_scale together is legal. Every refusal fires before any write. The response carries before, after and changedFields, with FOV derived at the current render resolution. rotation and look_at are mutually exclusive.

SWITCHING THE SCENE CAMERA is the part that was genuinely unreachable. make_active existed only on bl_create_camera, so choosing between two cameras that already exist - ordinary shot work - meant bl_run_python or deleting and recreating one, which loses its name to Blender's .001 uniquify and drops any keyframes on the datablock.

sensor_fit is included because without it sensor_width is a half-answer. AUTO fits the focal length to the LARGER render dimension, so a portrait render silently changes which sensor dimension the lens is measured against, and no real-world lens can be matched without saying which.

TYPE-GATED SETTINGS are judged against the type the camera will BE after this call, so {type:'ORTHO', ortho_scale:5} works in one call while ortho_scale on a camera being retyped to PERSP is refused.

look_at and rotation are refused together - two answers to the same question. The response carries before, after and changedFields, with fovDegrees derived at the current render resolution.
bl_set_camera_panorama:
Configure a panoramic Blender camera - the settings bl_create_camera could accept a PANO type for and never reach. That made PANO a declared-and-unreachable: the type validated, the camera was created, and nothing in the addon could set a single panorama property, which is worse than not offering the type. A camera that is not PANO is refused rather than having the settings stored where they will never be used. Panorama settings moved between versions - camera.cycles in 3.x, the camera data in 4.x+ - so both are tried and storedOn reports which one this Blender uses. PANORAMIC RENDERING IS A CYCLES FEATURE: engineHonoursPanorama says whether the current engine will actually use any of this, rather than leaving it to be discovered when the render comes back rectilinear.

A DECLARED-AND-UNREACHABLE, CLOSED. bl_create_camera validates PANO against Blenders own enum and accepts it, and then nothing in this addon could set a single panorama property. So a PANO camera could be created and was unusable, which is worse than not offering the type at all - the same shape as bl_export_mesh accepting four objectTypes its selection could never contain.

A camera that is not PANO is REFUSED rather than having the settings stored somewhere they will never be read. Set the type first with bl_set_camera.

VERSION HANDLING: panorama settings lived on camera.cycles in 3.x and moved onto the camera data in 4.x+. Both are tried, newest first, and storedOn reports which one this Blender uses. A field this build does not have is refused by name rather than silently ignored, and every requested field is resolved BEFORE any is written.

PANORAMIC RENDERING IS A CYCLES FEATURE. On any other engine these values are stored and ignored, and a caller finds out when the render comes back rectilinear - so engineHonoursPanorama reports whether the CURRENT engine will use them.
bl_set_custom_property:
Set a custom property, and its UI range, on a Blender object or pose bone. THE TYPE IS REPORTED BACK because Blender coerces silently: an int written where a float was meant stays an int, and a driver or an exporter reading it later gets a different type than the caller thinks they stored - typeChanged names that. min/max set the UI range, without which a rig slider is not a control; if this Blender will not take the range the op says the value WAS written and the bounds were not, rather than reporting a clean success. Pass delete:true to remove one. Writing an internal key (cycles, _RNA_UI) is refused rather than allowed to collide with Blender's own storage. Call mif_help("bl_set_custom_property") first.

storedType, requestedType and typeChanged say what actually happened.

DATA (2026-10-04): data=true writes the property on the object's DATA block instead - an armature's Armature, the Armature tab's Custom Properties panel, where a rig keeps a limb switch or its rig_id and a driver reads it as data["name"] (the object and pose bones were reachable before). The range, tooltip and type report work the same; bone with data is refused, and data on an object with no data block (an empty) is refused. library_overridable (2026-10-06) marks the property overridable in the source file so an animator can key it on a library override of the object or bone; read back as libraryOverridable, and with no value it marks an existing key.
bl_set_frame_range:
Set the Blender scene's frame range, frame rate, step, current frame and PREVIEW RANGE. An end before start is REFUSED and the previous range restored - Blender accepts it and then renders nothing. fps_base is the other half of the frame rate and was previously unreachable: Blender stores 29.97 as fps 30 with fps_base 1.001, and 23.976 as 24 with 1.001, so every broadcast rate was impossible to set through fps alone. durationSeconds now divides by the TRUE rate (fps/fps_base) - it divided by fps alone until 2026-09-03, reporting every NTSC duration 0.1% short, which is a frame and a half over an hour. A preview range is for playback and viewport renders only: a render - bl_render_animation included - uses frame_start..frame_end (or bl_render_animation's own frame_start/frame_end) whatever the preview range, and the response's rendersFrames is that scene range. Call mif_help("bl_set_frame_range") first.

Set the scene frame range, fps and current frame, and report the duration in seconds.

An end before start is REFUSED and the previous range restored: Blender accepts that silently and then renders nothing, which is a confusing way to lose a render.

SYNC_MODE (2026-10-04): NONE (play every frame) | FRAME_DROP | AUDIO_SYNC, read from the build's scene.sync_mode enum (the same three on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1). Frame dropping keeps playback at real time while posing a heavy rig. It changes interactive playback only - renders and bakes evaluate every frame - and syncNote says so; syncModeBefore is the previous value. An unknown mode is refused before anything is written, with the range left as it was.

A FRAME CHANGE STEPS EVERY LIVE SIMULATION (2026-10-05): moving the scene's frame evaluates each unbaked cloth, soft body, emitter or dynamic-hair particle system, dynamic-paint canvas and rigid body world in the view layer, and a fluid domain whose cache type is REPLAY - on an object hidden with the eye or from the render too (only hide_viewport or the modifier's show_viewport off takes it out). A leftover cloth on a render-hidden object stepped against a body's collision during a pose check and asked for 58.7 GB. So a call that would move the frame past such a cache's first frame is REFUSED before anything changes, naming each simulation and the colliders it would step against; bake them, take them out of the depsgraph, or pass allow_simulation=true, and the reply's simulationsStepped and colliders say what stepped. A Geometry Nodes simulation zone is listed (geometryNodesSimulations) and not refused: Blender exposes no baked flag for it. fit_to_strips SCENE or PREVIEW sets the scene or the preview range to the first and last frame over every strip in the sequencer, metas included - what Blender's Set Range to Strips does without the Sequencer area it needs; refused with start/end (SCENE) or preview_start/preview_end (PREVIEW), and on a scene with no strips.

A LOOP'S FRAMES (2026-10-11): a 24-frame cycle keyed at 0, 12 and 24 with the range 1 to 24, against the same keys with the range 0 to 24, or keys at 1, 13 and 25: count the frames the range plays against the keyed period (bl_list_keyframes against this range), or the loop repeats or drops a frame.
bl_set_keyframe:
Key a Blender object at a frame: location, rotation (radians) or scale [x,y,z] key its transform; data_path + value key any other property - a list for an array, or index for one element. A data_path is routed to the object or its data automatically - a light's energy lives on the data datablock, not the object. keyframe_insert stores the CURRENT value, so the value is WRITTEN first and the object is left holding it. A list sent as text ('[0,1,0]') is refused: send the list itself. interpolation CONSTANT/LINEAR/BEZIER: a flicker needs CONSTANT or it eases and stops reading as a flicker. rotationModeNote says when rotation_euler keys land on an object or bone in QUATERNION or AXIS_ANGLE mode, where they move nothing - pose bones start in QUATERNION. Call mif_help("bl_set_keyframe") first.

WHAT GETS KEYED, THE OBJECT OR ITS DATA. A transform lives on the object; a light's energy, a camera's lens and a spot's cone angle live on the DATA datablock. keyframe_insert has to be called on whichever one owns the property, and calling it on the wrong one raises a bare RuntimeError naming a data path rather than the mistake. This routes it for you and reports which one it used; pass target explicitly only for a path it cannot place.

AN ARRAY PROPERTY TAKES A LIST. value on location, rotation_euler, rotation_quaternion or a color is the whole list - [0, -0.1, 0] - each element converted to the property's own type; with index it is one element. The same list sent as TEXT, "[0,-0.1,0]", is refused as "'value' must be a number".

INTERPOLATION MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. Blender's default is BEZIER, which eases between keys - a flickering light on BEZIER fades and stops reading as a flicker. Use CONSTANT for anything that should snap, LINEAR for constant-rate motion like a spinning fan.

Returns the fcurves read back off the action, so a keyframe that did not land is visible. rotationModeNote (per written path, and gathered at the top) says when rotation_euler or delta_rotation_euler keys land on an object or pose bone in QUATERNION or AXIS_ANGLE mode, where they turn it 0.0 degrees - measured on every build; pose bones start in QUATERNION, so key rotation_quaternion there. A NODE TREE: target world, material or node_group with datablock (its name) works on that tree's own curves instead of an object's - data_path is the path on the tree, e.g. 'nodes["Mapping"].inputs[2].default_value'.

modifier_input {modifier, socket} keys a geometry-nodes modifier's group input in place of data_path: socket is the input's name or identifier, modifier the NODES modifier's name (default the object's only one); the reply's modifierInput names the identifier. A simulation zone's Skip linked to a Bool group input is keyed this way - measured on 4.2 and 5.2, a zone stepped a frame at a time holds its state over the frames keyed true.

SETTLED 2026-10-14 on 3.6.23, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1 (headless): dataPath 'modifiers["Cloth"].settings.effector_weights.gravity' keys on the object (bl_list_keyframes lists one curve; bl_evaluate_at_frame reads 0.25, 0.625, 1.0 at frames 1, 6, 11 between keys 0.25 and 1.0, allowSimulation true while the cloth is unbaked), and 'shape_keys.key_blocks["Smile"].value' is re-rooted onto the Key datablock (listed as target shape_keys, path key_blocks["Smile"].value; 0, 0.5 halfway).
bl_set_light:
Change a light that already exists. Before this op a light could be created and never adjusted: there was no set path and no read path, and bl_object_info returns early for a light and reports only its transform.

WHICH LIGHT. `object` is required and names the light OBJECT, not the light datablock. A name that is not a LIGHT is refused by type, and a name that does not exist is refused with the lights that DO exist listed.

RETYPING. Passing `type` changes the light's kind (POINT/SUN/SPOT/AREA), and per-type settings in the same call are judged against the type the light will BE afterwards - so {type:'SPOT', spot_angle:0.5} is legal, while spot_angle on a light being retyped to POINT is refused. Blender DISCARDS a per-type property when you leave that type; changedFields is where that shows up.

PER-TYPE KEYS, refused on the wrong type rather than ignored: spot_angle/spot_blend are SPOT only, size/size_y/shape are AREA only, angle is SUN only, radius (the soft-shadow size) is POINT or SPOT. The same table guards bl_create_light.

REFUSALS FIRE BEFORE ANY WRITE. A call naming one bad key leaves the light in exactly the state it was in.

THE RESPONSE carries `before`, `after`, `changedFields` and `changedAnything`, all read off the datablock after view_layer.update(). Setting a value to what it already was reports changedAnything false, which is the honest answer rather than an assumed success.

RADIANS for rotation, spot_angle and angle, like every other op here.

BY STOPS OR A MULTIPLIER (2026-10-05): energy_scale multiplies the energy the light has (a rim copied from the fill and divided by 3 is energy_scale 0.333) and stops multiplies it by 2 to the power stops (+1 doubles, -1 halves) - lights are balanced that way, and the value no longer has to be read back first. One of the two, never with energy; energy_scale must be above 0. energyFactor in the reply is the multiplier used, and after.energy the result.
bl_set_light_ies:
Give a Blender light a real-world IES photometric profile, or clear it. An IES file is a MEASURED distribution from a fixture manufacturer - the shape of light a real luminaire throws - and it is how archviz and product lighting stop looking like computer graphics. No amount of energy, radius or spot-angle adjustment substitutes for one. A LIGHT'S DISTRIBUTION IS NOT A PROPERTY, IT IS A NODE TREE: Blender wires an IES Texture node into the Strength of an Emission shader, which is why this is its own op rather than a key on bl_set_light, and the addon had never touched a light's node tree at all. Pass filepath for an external .ies, or text for the data inline; both together are refused, and a filepath that does not exist is refused BEFORE the tree is built, because a half-built tree on a light that then renders black is worse than no change. linkedToEmission is the postcondition - an IES node sitting unconnected changes nothing and looks entirely correct in the node list.

An IES file is a MEASURED distribution from a fixture manufacturer - the actual shape of light a real luminaire throws. It is how archviz and product lighting stop looking like computer graphics, and no amount of energy, radius or spot-angle adjustment substitutes for one.

A LIGHTS DISTRIBUTION IS NOT A PROPERTY, IT IS A NODE TREE. Blender wires an IES Texture node into the STRENGTH of an Emission shader - three nodes and two links. That is why this is its own op rather than a key on bl_set_light, and why it did not exist: the addon had never touched a lights node tree at all.

Pass filepath for an external .ies, or text for the data inline as a text datablock. Both together are refused as two answers to one question, and a filepath that does not exist is refused BEFORE the tree is built - a half-built tree on a light that then renders black is worse than no change at all.

linkedToEmission IS THE POSTCONDITION. An IES node sitting unconnected in the tree changes nothing and looks entirely correct in the node list - the same right-looking, inert shape as an invalid constraint or a dead driver.

clear:true removes the node tree and returns the light to its plain properties. CLEAR removes the IES Texture node(s) and their link to the Emission strength and keeps the rest of the tree, then switches use_nodes off where the build honours it: on 5.1 and later a light always renders its tree and use_nodes reads True straight after False is written (useNodesSwitchHeld false), which is why turning the switch off alone left the profile in every Cycles render. Reply: iesNodesRemoved, iesNodesLeft and linkedToEmission (false once cleared).
bl_set_light_influence:
How far a Blender light REACHES and what it reaches into - the half neither bl_set_light nor bl_set_light_shadow covered. bl_set_light writes energy, colour, cone and size; bl_set_light_shadow writes the shadow settings; nothing wrote a light's INFLUENCE RADIUS, its volumetric contribution, an area light's spread, or a sun's shadow cascades - and those are most of what separates a lighting rig that renders well from one that merely exists. cutoff_distance is the performance knob: the distance past which the light is not evaluated at all, the direct equivalent of an attenuation radius in a game engine. A CUTOFF DOES NOTHING UNTIL use_custom_distance IS ON - Blender stores the distance either way, so setting it alone changes a number and not the render while every field reads back exactly as asked; passing cutoff_distance turns the toggle on unless you say otherwise, and the response says so. TWO AXES OF AVAILABILITY, and the refusal says WHICH failed: a property can be missing because this BUILD lacks it (transmission_factor and soft_falloff are 4.2 and later) or because this light TYPE lacks it (spread is AREA only, square and show_cone are SPOT only, the cascades are SUN only). Every row was read off bl_rna on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1 for all four light types. square and showCone (viewport display) change no pixel in EEVEE or Cycles on any build, and the cascade keys none under Cycles or under EEVEE from 4.2 (measured on 3.6-5.2); the reply names them under measuredNoEffect.

PARAMETERS. object (string, required): the light object (a non-LIGHT is refused). volume_factor (float, default unchanged): the light's contribution to volumetrics, every type and build. cascade_count (whole number), cascade_max_distance (float), cascade_exponent (float), cascade_fade (float), all default unchanged: a SUN's cascaded shadow map settings (shadow_cascade_count, _max_distance, _exponent, _fade), SUN only; they act under 3.6's EEVEE Legacy and were measured to change nothing under Cycles or under EEVEE from 4.2, which the reply names. At least one setting must be passed.

OUT: ok, light, lightType, engine, applied {key: value read back}, clamped {key: {requested, stored}} or null where Blender clamped a value, measuredNoEffect {key: why} or null, measuredNoEffectNote, useCustomDistance, cutoffWasEnabledAutomatically, note (when the cutoff toggle was turned on for you), blenderVersion.

REFUSED with "NOTHING was changed": an object that is not a light; no setting passed; a setting this light TYPE lacks (named with the types that have it - retyping with bl_set_light makes it available); a setting this BUILD lacks (named with the builds that have it). Both checks run before any write. Values are parsed as they are written, so a non-numeric, non-finite or fractional value (cascade_count) is refused with the settings before it in the call already written.
bl_set_light_linking:
Control WHICH objects a Blender light affects. 'This key light hits the product and not the backdrop' is routine in product and archviz work and cannot be faked - moving the light changes the look, flagging it with geometry changes the reflections, and turning it down changes everything. Light linking is the only correct answer and nothing here could reach it. receiver_collection limits what the light illuminates; blocker_collection limits what casts its shadows; both are created if they do not exist. Requires Blender 4.0+, and an older build is REFUSED BY NAME with the version rather than accepting the keys and doing nothing. litsNothing is reported because an EMPTY receiver collection illuminates nothing at all - a legitimate state mid-setup and a catastrophic one to render from, and identical to a correct link from every other field.

This key light hits the product and not the backdrop is a routine request in product and archviz work, and it cannot be faked: moving the light changes the look, flagging it off with geometry changes the reflections, and turning it down changes everything. Light linking is the only correct answer, and nothing here could reach it.

receiver_collection limits what the light ILLUMINATES. blocker_collection limits what casts its SHADOWS - a different question, and the one people forget exists. Both collections are created if they do not already exist.

BLENDER 4.0+. An older build has no light_linking at all, and this refuses BY NAME with the version it found rather than accepting the keys and doing nothing - which is what a hasattr-skip would do, and is the mistake bl_create_lights shadow key made until it was fixed the same day.

litsNothing is worth reading. An EMPTY receiver collection illuminates NOTHING AT ALL - a legitimate state to be in mid-setup and a catastrophic one to render from, and identical to a correct link from every other field in the response.

INCLUDE OR EXCLUDE PER MEMBER, AND AN EMISSIVE MESH (2026-10-05): receiver_members and blocker_members take {object or collection name: INCLUDE | EXCLUDE} and write each member's link_state in that collection (a name not in it yet is linked in, named in membersAdded); the reply's receiverMembers / blockerMembers read every member back with its kind and state. A key light that lights everything except a cove: the cove EXCLUDE in its receiver collection - measured in Cycles on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2, the excluded plane went from 0.6 to under 0.001 and the other stayed. object may be an object whose material emits (an Emission shader, or a Principled BSDF with emission strength above 0) as well as a LIGHT: a glowing plane receiving one of two planes left the other black (0.002), measured the same way; a mesh with no emission is refused. honoredBy names the engines that read it on the build (Cycles from 4.0; EEVEE from 4.4 by the shipped UI, not rendered here). Members with no collection to put them in are refused.
bl_set_marker:
Create, move, rename, camera-bind or delete a Blender timeline marker. Binding a camera makes the scene CUT to it at that frame. Markers are matched BY NAME and Blender permits duplicates, so the response reports how many matched - acting on several silently is how a caller ends up moving the wrong one. Binding a non-camera object is refused by type rather than accepted and ignored, and passing both a camera and unbind_camera is refused as two answers to one question.

Binding a non-camera object is refused by type rather than accepted and quietly ignored, and passing both a camera and unbind_camera is refused as two answers to the same question.

MARKERS ARE MATCHED BY NAME AND BLENDER PERMITS DUPLICATES. Two markers can share a name, and this op acts on ALL of them - so the response reports how many matched. Acting on several silently is how a caller ends up having moved the wrong one and not knowing.

A marker that does not exist is created only when a frame is given; without one there is nowhere to put it, and that is refused rather than guessed at.
bl_set_material_properties:
Write Principled BSDF values on a Blender material, or rename it (rename: refused when another material has the name). THE VERSION SPREAD IS THE WHOLE DIFFICULTY: Blender RENAMED these inputs between 3.6 and 4.0 - 'Specular' became 'Specular IOR Level', 'Emission' became 'Emission Color', 'Transmission' became 'Transmission Weight' - and this addon supports 3.6 through 5.0. Writing to a name that does not exist on the running version does not raise; the value lands NOWHERE and the material is subtly wrong with nothing to read back. So each property resolves through an alias list, one that resolves on NO alias is REFUSED by name with the inputs that do exist, and the response reports `resolvedInputs` naming the real socket each property landed on. Every name is resolved BEFORE any is written, so a bad one cannot leave the material half-applied. VIEWPORT DISPLAY (2026-10-05): viewport_color [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], viewport_metallic and viewport_roughness write Material.diffuse_color, metallic and roughness - what Solid view and an asset preview show, not the shader, so a linked asset is not grey there. They work without a Principled BSDF; bl_describe_material's viewport block reads them back. SUBSURFACE (2026-10-06): subsurface_weight, subsurface_scale, subsurface_radius [r, g, b], subsurface_ior and subsurface_anisotropy are Principled sockets (subsurface_scale is refused on 3.6, which has none); subsurface_method BURLEY, RANDOM_WALK or RANDOM_WALK_SKIN (5.2 adds RANDOM_WALK_LEGACY) is the node's own setting. Skin and wax: weight 1 and the radius reset to [1, 1, 1] so it stops reading red. bl_describe_material reads every one back. weathering splices wear in front of the Principled inputs, every mask driven by the mesh.

WEATHERING (1.4): weathering {edgeWear, grime, roughnessVariation, colorVariation, scale, seed} - its keys camelCase as the add-on takes them - splices wear in front of the Principled inputs, every mask driven by the mesh. edgeWear {amount 0.5, width 0.02 m, source bevel | pointiness, color, roughness, metallic, bump}: the convex edges, by curvature from a Bevel node (crisp on any mesh) or Pointiness (per vertex; needs a dense mesh) - color defaults to the surface's own color lighter and grayer, roughness to 0.6 x its own, metallic 1 for bare metal under paint, bump sinks the chips. grime {amount 0.5, distance 0.2 m, color, roughness 0.9}: where Ambient Occlusion (this object only) is low - creases and inside corners. Both are broken into patches by object-space noise (no UVs needed); roughnessVariation (0.15) and colorVariation (0.12) vary the whole surface. true takes every default; false removes the chain and puts each input back as it was. Whatever fed an input stays under the chain - a texture weathers in its own colors - and a later base_color / roughness / metallic writes the value under it. Bevel and Pointiness are Cycles nodes: Cycles renders the chain, and bl_bake_texture_set with types BASE_COLOR, ROUGHNESS, METALLIC, NORMAL and baked_material carries it to Unreal - a procedural chain alone reaches the send as nothing.

REGIONS FOR CLOTHES (1.4): weathering.regions [{region, strength, kind, vertexGroup | bones, radius, color, roughness}] wears a garment where the body works it. knees and seat (kind wear: the cloth's own color rubbed pale and 0.12 rougher) are a band radius (0.09, 0.15 m) along the leg at the knee joint on the front, and at hip height on the back; cuffs and hems (kind grime) a band (0.06, 0.04 m) along the open edges - every one for hems, those nearest a hand, forearm, foot or shin for cuffs; hands (kind grease: darker and glossier) where the hands hang with the arms down, the thighs beside them (0.2 m); chest (grease) the front at the top spine bone. kind wear | grease | grime, strength 0-1, color and roughness override the kind's. vertexGroup takes a group's weights; bones the named bones, radius from the bones' line. Each region is a float attribute 'MifWear_<region>' per vertex on every mesh using the material (weathering.objects names them; by default a mesh with no armature is passed over and listed in regionsSkipped), the bones read off weathering.armature or each mesh's Armature modifier; the shader reads it with an Attribute node, so the material on a mesh without it is untouched, and bl_bake_texture_set bakes it with the rest. A region whose mask reaches a quarter nowhere is refused before anything is written; calling again replaces the attributes, false removes them with the chain. bl_describe_material lists them under weathering.regions.
bl_set_material_settings:
The Blender material settings that are NOT Principled inputs - transparency, shadows, culling, refraction. bl_describe_material and bl_create_material have ALWAYS reported blendMethod and nothing anywhere could write it, which is a read/write asymmetry sitting in the middle of the most-used material op. It is also the property that decides whether a transparent material is actually transparent: an alpha of 0.2 on an OPAQUE material renders SOLID, and every field in every response still reads correctly. WHAT MOVES, read off bl_rna on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1 rather than from release notes: blend_method is on every build with the same four values; shadow_method is 3.6 and 4.2 ONLY, since EEVEE Next dropped it at 4.4; displacement_method, surface_render_method, use_transparent_shadow and use_raytrace_refraction are 4.2 and later and absent on 3.6. Anything this build lacks is REFUSED naming which builds have it, and every key is checked before any is written so a half-supported request does not leave half of it applied. THESE ARE EEVEE'S SETTINGS - Cycles decides transparency from the shader and ignores blend_method, so the active engine is reported and the keys it will not read are named.

Parameters (each None = not written; at least one setting must be given): backface_culling (bool) writes material.use_backface_culling - hide the faces that point away from the camera. alpha_threshold (float) writes alpha_threshold, the alpha cutoff for CLIP blending; Blender clamps it to the property's range and the clamped value is reported. screen_refraction (bool) writes use_screen_refraction (EEVEE screen-space refraction). transparent_shadow (bool) writes use_transparent_shadow and raytrace_refraction (bool) writes use_raytrace_refraction; both exist on 4.2 and later only. Any of them missing from the running build is refused. Enum values (blend_method, shadow_method, displacement_method, surface_render_method) are matched case-insensitively against the build's own enum, read from bpy.

OUT: ok, material, engine, applied {key: stored value, read back}, clamped ({key: {requested, stored, why}} for any value that did not land as asked - a float clamped by its range, or an enum the build remapped, e.g. blend_method OPAQUE or CLIP stored as HASHED from 4.2 - else null), inertUnderThisEngine (under Cycles, the keys it does not read: every one but displacement_method; else null), bothNote (displacement_method BOTH under EEVEE), note, blenderVersion.

Refusals ("NOTHING was changed." - every key is checked against the build and every value resolved before any is written): no material by that name (lists up to 25); no setting given; a setting this build does not have (names the builds that do); an enum value this build does not offer (lists them); a malformed bool or float; any unknown key.
bl_set_material_slots: Set a Blender object's material slot NAMES, in ORDER. Slot order is what decides which Unreal material lands on which face, so a reordered list renders the wrong material on an otherwise perfect mesh. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. This closes a gap the pipeline already DETECTED: mif_mesh_roundtrip compares the slot sequence before and after an edit and warns on a mismatch, and until now there was nothing it could call to fix one. Takes NAMES, not materials - the name is what lines up against Unreal's FStaticMaterial array on reimport, and a material's content is Unreal's business. A name with no existing material creates an EMPTY one and reports it in createdMaterials. A list whose length differs from the current slot count is REFUSED unless allow_resize=True, because changing the count re-indexes every polygon and a face left pointing past the end renders as the last slot with no error; when you do resize, polygonsOutOfRange reports exactly that. null means an empty slot. links (2026-10-06): per slot OBJECT or DATA (MaterialSlot.link), set before the material so it lands there - OBJECT keeps the material on the object, which is how an override of a linked mesh object keeps its own material across a reload; a DATA slot changed over linked, un-overridden mesh data is refused. The reply's links reads them back.
bl_set_object_visibility:
Control what a Blender object is visible TO - the viewport, the render, and each ray type separately. visible_glossy=false is how you stop a softbox appearing as a white rectangle in every reflection, which is the single most common adjustment in product and archviz lighting and was unreachable here. It also answers 'why is my object missing from the render', because hide_render and visible_camera are exactly where that answer lives - the response reports appearsInRender directly. Works on EVERY object type, because ray visibility is an object property and a mesh acting as a reflector needs it as much as a lamp does. Ray visibility moved off the Cycles addon onto the object in Blender 3.0, so both spellings are tried; a flag this build does not expose is REFUSED by name rather than silently ignored, and every flag is resolved before any is written.

THE ONE PEOPLE WANT IS visible_glossy. Setting it false stops a softbox or a bounce card appearing as a white rectangle in every reflection, which is the single most common adjustment in product and archviz lighting, and nothing in this addon could reach it.

IT ALSO ANSWERS WHY AN OBJECT IS MISSING FROM A RENDER. hide_render and visible_camera are exactly where that lives, and the response reports appearsInRender directly rather than leaving you to combine them.

For EVERY object type, not lights alone: ray visibility is an OBJECT property, and a mesh acting as a reflector, a holdout or a shadow catcher needs it as much as a lamp does.

holdout cuts the object out of the render as alpha; shadow_catcher makes it a Cycles shadow catcher (Object.is_shadow_catcher). Indirect Only is not an object setting: it is a collection's, per view layer, and bl_set_collection_visibility's indirect_only writes it. This tool took indirect_only until 2026-09-28 and wrote the shadow catcher under that name; the add-on now refuses it and says where it went.

VERSION HANDLING: ray visibility moved off the Cycles addon onto the object itself in Blender 3.0, so both spellings are tried, newest first. A flag this build does not expose is REFUSED BY NAME rather than silently ignored - the mistake the shadow key on bl_create_light made until it was fixed the same day - and every requested flag is resolved BEFORE any is written, so a build that lacks one refuses the whole call instead of applying half of them. hidden_in_view_layer is the outliner's eye for the ACTIVE view layer (Object.hide_set), not a datablock flag: an object outside that layer is refused. The before/after records carry hiddenInViewLayer and visibleInViewLayer (Blender's own is-it-drawn), and so does object_info's visibility block - hide_viewport False does not mean shown.

DISPLAY: display_as BOUNDS | WIRE | SOLID | TEXTURED (Object.display_type), show_wire, show_in_front, show_bounds with bounds_type BOX | SPHERE | CYLINDER | CONE | CAPSULE, and hide_select (the object cannot be clicked in the viewport) - a Boolean cutter shown as wire, a backdrop made unselectable. The enum values are checked against this build's own lists before anything is written, and the display fields come back in before and after with the rest.
bl_set_origin:
Move a Blender object's ORIGIN without moving its geometry in the world. The origin is what Unreal rotates and places the mesh around, it is baked into the FBX, and it CANNOT be fixed on the Unreal side - so it has to be right before export. mode defaults to 'geometry'; a location with no mode means 'point' (the response says modeInferred), and a location beside any other mode is refused rather than ignored.

The origin is what Unreal rotates and places the mesh around, it is baked into the FBX, and it CANNOT be fixed on the Unreal side - so it has to be right before export, and nothing could set it. Blender puts it wherever the object happened to be created: a prop whose origin sits mid-bounding-box cannot be floored by setting Z, and a door whose origin is not on its hinge edge cannot be rotated open. MODES: 'geometry' (default) the median point; 'bounds' the bounding-box centre, which differs from geometry on any mesh with uneven vertex density - that is most of them; 'bottom' the box centre in X/Y and its MINIMUM in Z, which is what a placeable prop almost always wants because it puts the pivot on the floor; 'cursor' the 3D cursor; 'world' the origin; 'point' an explicit location [x,y,z] in Blender units. A LOCATION WITH NO MODE MEANS 'point', and the response says so with modeInferred:true; a location beside any other mode is REFUSED - it used to be ignored, leaving the pivot in the middle while the call answered ok. THE GEOMETRY MUST NOT MOVE and that is asserted, not assumed - world-space bounds are measured before and after, and the response carries geometryMovedBU and geometryStayedPut so you can see only the pivot changed.

CORNER AND SIDE PIVOTS for modular pieces: mode 'bottomCorner' puts the origin on a bottom corner of the bounds - corner '-x-y' (the default: minimum X, Y and Z), '+x-y', '-x+y' or '+x+y' - the pivot a floor module tiles by, in whole-module moves from one corner. mode 'bottomSide' puts it at the bottom middle of one side face - side '-x', '+x', '-y' or '+y', required - so a wall module snaps flush against a line on the floor. Both read the bounds off the vertices in world axes (obj.bound_box can be stale after an edit), and the response carries pivotInBounds: where the origin landed as a fraction of each world axis of the bounds, 0 at the minimum and 1 at the maximum. corner beside any mode but 'bottomCorner', and side beside any but 'bottomSide', are refused rather than ignored. Small props usually want 'bottom' (bottom center); a centered pivot is 'bounds'.
bl_set_point_positions:
Move a Blender lattice's points, a shape key's vertices or a curve's control points by index. It is the edit that makes a lattice or a key deform. points is [[index, x, y, z], ...] in the object's LOCAL space; a lattice's index is u + v*pointsU + w*pointsU*pointsV, so a 3x3x3's centre is 13. On an object that has shape keys, shape_key is REQUIRED: the Basis key holds the rest shape and base points moved underneath it change nothing (measured on 4.4 for meshes and lattices). Every row is validated before any is written, positions are read back, and each object the points deform is fingerprinted before and after - evaluatedChanged names what actually moved, and note says when nothing could (a lattice nothing is bound to, a key at value 0). A curve takes radius too, and with nothing to write is READ. Call mif_help("bl_set_point_positions") first. handles [[index, [lx, ly, lz], [rx, ry, rz]], ...] places both handles of a curve's Bezier points exactly in the curve's local space, setting those points' handle types to FREE first; it is refused on poly or NURBS points and together with handle_type.

BOTH COULD BE MADE AND NEITHER COULD MOVE. bl_create_lattice makes a lattice and bl_add_modifier binds it, but a lattice deforms only by its points; scaling the lattice OBJECT moves the mesh and the lattice together and deforms nothing. bl_add_shape_key is the same one level down - without this op, every key it made was a copy of the basis.

POINTS are [[index, x, y, z], ...] in the object's LOCAL space. A lattice's point index is u + v*pointsU + w*pointsU*pointsV (the response reports resolution), so a 3x3x3's centre is 13, and a lattice at scale 1 spans -0.5 to 0.5.

SHAPE KEYS. On an object that has any, shape_key is required: the Basis key holds the rest shape, and base points moved underneath it change nothing - measured on Blender 4.4 for meshes and lattices. Name the Basis key to move the rest shape.

REFUSALS FIRE BEFORE ANY WRITE: a malformed row, a repeated index or an out-of-range index leaves every point where it was.

THE CONSEQUENCE IS MEASURED. Positions are read back (maxReadBackError), and every object the points deform - the mesh itself, or each object bound to the lattice by a LATTICE modifier or lattice parenting - is fingerprinted before and after. evaluatedChanged names what actually moved; note says when nothing could, such as a lattice nothing is bound to or a key at value 0.

CURVES (2026-10-05): a CURVE object's control points by index - every spline in order, a Bezier spline's points then the next spline's - with points [[index, x, y, z], ...] (a Bezier point's handles move with it, as dragging it does), tilt [[index, radians], ...] (the twist; nothing wrote or read it before) and handle_type {type FREE | VECTOR | ALIGNED | AUTO - this build's list, indices (default every Bezier point), side LEFT | RIGHT | BOTH} to change handle types after creation - a zip or thread curve smoothed by moving and twisting its points, then set to automatic handles. Any of the three may come alone. curvePoints reads every point back: co, handleLeft / handleRight and their types, tilt, radius (200 listed). Refused before any write: an index past the curve, a handle type Blender lacks, handles on a poly or NURBS point, curve shape keys; tilt and handle_type on a lattice or mesh.

radius [[index, r], ...] writes a curve point's radius (what a bevel and Curve to Mesh scale by; 0 or more). With nothing to write a CURVE is READ: curvePoints gives every control point's index, spline, co (local), world, tilt, radius, a Bezier point's handles in local and world space with their types, and a poly or NURBS point's weight; splines gives each spline's type, point count, cyclic flag and resolution. The first 10,000 points are read; truncated says when there are more.

handles [[index, [lx, ly, lz], [rx, ry, rz]], ...] (a CURVE's Bezier points, the curve's local space) places both handles exactly: each point's handle types are set FREE first, because an AUTO or ALIGNED handle is moved again by Blender when its partner or point changes. Refused on a poly or NURBS point and together with handleType; read back in curvePoints and maxReadBackError.
bl_set_shape_key:
Set a Blender shape key's influence, and optionally its slider range. It is the write half of bl_list_shape_keys, which could only read. The range is applied BEFORE the value, because setting a value outside the OLD range would be clamped to it and then look wrong even though the new range allows it. Blender CLAMPS SILENTLY: asking for 2.0 on a 0..1 key leaves 1.0 and reports nothing, so the response carries requestedValue, the actual value, and a `clamped` flag naming the difference rather than leaving it to be discovered in a render. remove true deletes the key instead (keys relative to it are re-pointed at the basis; the basis is refused while other keys remain).

THE RANGE IS APPLIED BEFORE THE VALUE. Setting a value outside the OLD range would be clamped to it and then look wrong even though the new range allows it - an ordering that matters and is easy to get backwards.

BLENDER CLAMPS SILENTLY. Asking for 2.0 on a 0..1 key leaves 1.0 and reports nothing at all, so the response carries requestedValue alongside the actual value and a 'clamped' flag naming the difference. Otherwise it is found later, in a render, as a shape that did not go as far as it was told to. vertex_group limits the key to one vertex group's region ("" clears it) and relative_key makes it relative to another key; both are checked before anything is written. A shape key has no invert flag on its group in Blender. move_to (an index from 1) | make_basis (5.0+) | apply_to_basis (2026-10-06), one alone: reorder the key, make it the basis (the mesh follows it), or add its offsets at its value into the basis and every other key and remove it.
bl_apply_shape_keys: Bake a Blender mesh's shape keys into its base mesh: the whole current mix (default) or keys [names] at their values, then remove them. keep_basis keeps a Basis holding the new shape. Replies keys before/after, maxDisplacement and mixDeviation. WHY: a mesh with shape keys refuses an Armature modifier apply and a join, so a morphed head and body joined for a bake needed every key applied first; bl_add_shape_key only adds. mix true (the default without keys) reads what the keys show now through Blender's own from-mix - each key's value, mute, vertex group and relative key honoured - writes it to the base mesh and removes every key (keep_basis true keeps one Basis holding the new shape). keys [names] bakes only those keys at their current values and removes them; every key left keeps its offset from the basis (the applied displacement is added to it too), and with keep_basis false the Basis is cleared when no other key is left. The Basis in keys, mix with keys, absolute (non-relative) keys and a non-mesh are refused before anything is written. Reply: applied [{key, value, mute}], keysBefore, keysAfter, maxDisplacement (how far the base mesh moved) and mixDeviation (the base mesh against the shape the applied keys showed: 0 when faithful). Remove one key without baking it: bl_set_shape_key remove true.
bl_status:
Health probe for the Blender backend, and the FIRST thing to call before any bl_* work. Returns the addon's op table plus bpy.app.version, background (blender -b has no event loop, so the addon runs jobs inline rather than on a timer) and the process pid. BOUNDED AT BOTH ENDS, 5s each, where every other bl_* tool waits 180s. (1) A short READ timeout: a ping does no bpy work, so silence means Blender's main thread is blocked by a modal operator, an open file browser or a render. (2) A short wait for the transport LOCK: the connection to Blender is one serialised socket, so this tool used to block behind an in-flight bevel for the full work timeout - the one thing you reach for when Blender is wedged was the one thing wedged Blender made unavailable. It now gives up and tells you WHICH op is holding the line and for how long, which is itself the diagnosis. A refused connection (Blender shut, or the addon not enabled) comes back effectively instantly with the install steps in the error. Version matters and is reported for a reason: the io_scene_fbx and bmesh.ops defaults this pipeline relies on were read from 4.4 and have moved between releases before. `pid` is worth reading whenever an edit seems to land nowhere: it identifies WHICH Blender owns the port, and the addon's N-panel prints the same number.

changeCap {cap, on, source, error?} is the change cap in force for the open .blend (docs/15 section 6).

handshake {verdict, agree, addonProtocol, serverProtocol, addonBuilt, missingEndpoints (ops this server calls that the add-on lacks), extraEndpoints, addonPath, siblingAddon, sameSourceAsSibling, update, note} is this server's version check of the add-on, read from this ping and again after a reconnect. verdict plugin means the add-on Blender loaded is older than the one beside this server (siblingAddon); sameSourceAsSibling false with no verdict is only a differing copy.

ANY PORT, NO RESTART (2026-10-12): each MifBlender writes where it listens (port, pid, Blender and add-on versions, the open .blend, background or not) into a per-user file (%LOCALAPPDATA%\MifBridge\Blender\listeners.json on Windows; MIF_BLENDER_LISTENERS overrides) and removes it when it stops. bl_status lists every OTHER live one in listeners - pid running and a ping handshake answered (answers) - and port=N or pid=N switches this session to that one after its handshake, answering switched {from, to, pid}. When the session's port refuses and exactly one live MifBlender is registered, every bl_* refusal names it and the switch call; with several it lists them and chooses none. Nothing switches unless you pass port or pid. MIF_BLENDER_PORT still sets where a session starts.

GENERATIVE (R85, 2026-11-06): generativeMode and allowGenerative are the ADD-ON's: the open .blend's own mode (unset until mif_project_mode records one on its scenes) and the add-on preference. The Unreal project's mode is not sent to Blender; this server enforces it, and generativeAllowedBy.unrealProject shows it - read from the project the running editor names, or, before any editor answers, from the MifBridgeProject.json of the project this server was started in (MIF_PROJECT_DIR, else the .uproject at or above its working folder). So a Blender saying unset with generativeAllowed false is a non-generative Unreal project holding the bl_gen_* tools off. The reply is the first text block of the result; a note (this file has no mode yet, the version handshake) comes as a later block, so a client must not join the blocks before parsing.
bl_transfer_weights: Copy vertex weights from one Blender mesh onto another by proximity - the op a retopology or LOD pass needs. A mesh that has been through bl_decimate_mesh or bl_clean_mesh comes out with its topology changed and its skinning destroyed, and re-rigging by hand is the expensive part; this maps the weights back from the original by nearest surface. IT REFUSES RATHER THAN GUESSES in the two cases where a plausible result would be wrong: a source with no vertex groups (producing an unskinned mesh while reporting success is the silent-success shape), and source == destination. IT DOES NOT NORMALISE, deliberately: a nearest-surface mapping interpolates between source vertices whose totals differ, so sums drift from 1 - call bl_normalize_weights afterwards, separately and visibly, and the response reminds you. THE POSTCONDITION IS MEASURED, not taken from the operator, which reports nothing useful: the response carries destinationGroupsBefore/After and destinationVerticesWeighted, and the call FAILS if no vertex ended up weighted (the usual cause being the two meshes sitting far apart in world space, since a nearest-surface mapping needs them roughly coincident). mapping accepts NEAREST, EDGE_NEAREST, EDGEINTERP_NEAREST, POLY_NEAREST, POLYINTERP_NEAREST (default) and POLYINTERP_VNORPROJ. With only_groups or exclude_groups only those source groups are transferred, and destination_mask (a vertex group on the destination) limits which destination vertices receive them - a hood takes the head and neck groups, a sleeve the arm's. Blender's data transfer cannot pick groups by name, so the destination's weights are snapshotted, the whole transfer runs, and every group outside the choice and every vertex outside the mask is put back as it was; a group the transfer created that was not chosen is removed (groupsTransferred, groupsKeptAsBefore, groupsNotCreated).
bl_transform_grease_pencil_points:
Translate, rotate and scale the points of a Blender Grease Pencil layer's strokes at one keyframe - written to the stroke data, no edit mode - for a head turn on its own layer, a drawing nudged or resized in place.

WHY (2026-10-11): turning a head drawn on its own layer, or nudging one drawing, meant edit mode and the transform tools, or raw Python per point - and a legacy point (3.6, 4.2) is co while a 4.3+ point is position. layer is required; frame is the keyframe edited (default the one shown at the scene's frame; a frame between keyframes is refused, its drawing being a hold of an earlier one); strokes [indices] (default all). translate [x, y, z] metres and rotate [x, y, z] degrees (XYZ Euler) in world space, scale s or [x, y, z]; pivot MEDIAN (default, the mean of the points moved) | ORIGIN | CURSOR | [x, y, z]. Order: scale, then rotate, about pivot, then translate. Reply: the points moved, the pivot and the world bounds before and after, read off the strokes. Refused: a frame that is not a keyframe, a stroke index outside the frame, no transform, a zero scale, an unknown pivot, a missing layer, a non-Grease-Pencil object.
bl_transform_object: Move, rotate or scale a Blender object WITHOUT baking the transform into its mesh data: location [x,y,z], rotation [x,y,z] in RADIANS, scale [x,y,z]; relative=True adds to the current values. bl_apply_transform and bl_set_origin both BAKE - they write the transform into the vertices and leave the object at identity, which is what an export pipeline wants and is NOT how you place a second object beside a first. The response reports the transform before AND after, because 'it moved' and 'it is where I asked' are different claims and only the second is worth making. Note this leaves isIdentityTransform false - bl_apply_transform is what bakes it in, and an FBX export writes the object transform unless you do.
bl_uv_info:
Read a Blender mesh's UVs per layer - the verification half of bl_uv_unwrap. bl_uv_unwrap can CREATE a channel and bl_object_info reports only that channels EXIST, so 'did the unwrap produce something Unreal can bake a lightmap into' had no answer short of opening Blender and looking. Reports per layer: name, the positional INDEX (what FBX writes and what Unreal's Lightmap Coordinate Index points at), islandCount, UV bounds, facesOutside01, zeroAreaFaces, overlappingIslandPairs, and texel density min/max/median. WHAT UNREAL ACTUALLY REQUIRES is why those numbers: a lightmap UV must lie inside 0-1 (Unreal clamps anything outside and it bakes as garbage) and must not have overlapping islands (two islands sharing UV space share lightmap texels, so one surface's light bleeds onto another). Both are legal and often deliberate on a TEXTURE channel, which is why lightmapReady is reported per layer with a named reason and a texture layer failing it is not a defect. OVERLAP IS CONSERVATIVE and says so: it is measured by island bounding box in bmesh, because bpy.ops.uv.select_overlap needs a UV editor area and cannot run headless - so every real overlap is counted, plus some pairs whose boxes touch while the islands do not. A pure read; it cannot damage the mesh it is diagnosing.

NEAR-ZERO UV AREA AND UNREAL'S ZERO TANGENTS, per layer. zeroAreaFaces counts faces with UV area at or under zeroAreaThreshold (1e-12); nearZeroUvAreaFaces (with the first 50 in nearZeroUvAreaFaceIndices) counts those at or under nearZeroUvAreaThreshold (1e-9 UV units squared, about 1/240 of a texel of a 2048 texture). nearZeroTangents predicts Unreal's import warning 'has some nearly zero tangents ... (Tolerance of 1E-4)': tangents are computed with MikkTSpace (mesh.calc_tangents) on a triangulated scratch copy, and a vertex instance (one position, normal and UV) with no UV area in any triangle around it is counted, because the MikkTSpace Unreal links leaves its tangent at zero - Blender's own calc_tangents substitutes a placeholder axis there (measured on 5.2.1), which blenderNearZero reports separately. It names the vertices and faces. Unreal builds tangents from UV channel 0 only, so unrealTangentWarning is set from that layer's count. The scratch copy is removed; the mesh is not touched.

ISLANDS AS DATA (islands=true, 2026-10-04): each layer also lists its islands, biggest UV area first and at most max_reported_islands of them (islandCount stays exact): faces, the first 50 faceIndices, uvArea, area3d (square world units, the object's scale and rotation applied), ratio (UV area per square world unit - the island's texel density squared), and its UV box; islandRatioMedian and islandRatioSpread (largest ratio over smallest; 1.0 when every island has one density) summarise them. Areas are unsigned per face, so a folded face counts whole. WHY: finding the island that steals texture space (a sleeve at 3x the density of the rest) was a recorded raw-Python read ten times in a short film's garment pass. bl_uv_pack equalize_by_area evens it out. FLIPPED ISLANDS (2026-10-06; 5.2's select by winding, native on every build): each layer reports flippedFaces (faces whose UV corners wind clockwise - a negative signed UV area, mirrored in UV space, so their tangents point the other way), flippedIslands and flippedIslandIndices (islands whose summed signed area is negative). STRETCH (2026-10-06): stretch AREA or ANGLE adds the UV editor's Display Stretch as numbers - per island the area-weighted mean and the worst face (worstFace): AREA is 1 - min(r, 1/r) with r a face's share of its island's UV area over its share of the world area, ANGLE the mean corner-angle error in degrees. 0 is undistorted; a relax is judged by it. overlapCheckCapped true means the search for overlapping islands stopped at its work limit, as it does on an atlas of stacked cards: the counts are lower bounds and lightmapReady is false.
bl_uv_set_texel_density:
Scale a Blender mesh's UV islands to a texel density you choose on a texture size, and say which texture size holds the layout. target with unit PX_PER_CM (default) or PX_PER_M - or from_screen {sizeCm, pixels}, the density an object that size needs to fill that many pixels of the frame at its closest; there is no default target. texture_size is a number or [w, h]. mode PER_ISLAND brings each island to the target, AVERAGE the selection as one with relative sizes kept; faces or islands pick which. Replies the density per island before and after (min, median, max, spread), uvFillPercent, each ladder size's fill and whether a pack at the target fits 0-1, smallestFittingSize, texelShape (1 = square texels) and, with pack, the islands left outside.

DENSITY is pixels per metre = sqrt(UV area x w x h / world area) per island, the UV area unsigned and the world area through the object's rotation and scale; 1 px/cm is 100 px/m, the unit bl_mesh_quality reports. A target is a game-art choice (10.24 px/cm is common for first-person props, 20.48 for a held weapon, 5.12 third-person, 2.56 top-down), so the call has none of its own. Each island is scaled about its own bounding-box centre. THE LADDER (default 256 to 8192, powers of two; a non-square texture_size keeps its aspect on every size) is a real pack, not an area sum: at each size the islands are scaled to the target for that size, Blender's pack_islands runs with scale off, and the size fits when no island lands outside 0-1; the UVs are put back after each trial, and a size whose islands need more than the whole tile is not packed (fits false, why). The trial packs the islands' bounding boxes - a concave pack with rotation took 15 to 23 s for a six-island cube on 3.6.23 - so a size it calls a fit holds the islands, and a tight layout may fit one size smaller packed by shape. pack=true then packs the layout at the target on texture_size (margin default 0.02), unrotated on a non-square texture. texelShapeNote appears on a non-square texture when the layout was unwrapped for a square one - bl_uv_pack texture_size squares it. Refused before any write: no target and no from_screen, or both; no texture_size; a face or island index the mesh lacks; faces with islands; margin without pack; no island with area.
bl_uv_transform_islands:
Move, rotate (degrees) and scale chosen UV islands of a Blender mesh one by one, each about its own pivot, or bring them to a texel density (match_texel_density {target, textureSize} or {toIsland}). Replies per-island UV area, density and box before and after. Also align_rotation, randomize and arrange.

islands takes indices from bl_uv_info islands:true; faces picks the islands those faces are on; one of the two is required. pivot CENTER (default, each island's box centre), MEDIAN (its mean UV corner) or [u, v] (one point for all). Applied in order: the density scale, scale (a number or [su, sv]), rotate (counter-clockwise), translate [u, v]. match_texel_density target is px/cm on its textureSize (default the call's texture_size, 1024); toIsland copies another island's density, texture-independent; it excludes scale. bl_uv_unwrap uv_transform moves the whole layer; bl_uv_set_texel_density also tries texture sizes and packs.

align_rotation: true turns each chosen island so its smallest-area bounding box is axis-aligned (Blender's Align Rotation AUTO, from the convex hull), the turn of smallest size; it adds to rotate. randomize {seed (whole number), translate [du, dv] (largest offset), rotate (largest turn, degrees), scale (largest change, 0 to below 1)}: each island gets its own offset, turn and scale from the seed (the same seed repeats them) - Blender's Randomize Transform, which breaks the repeat of a tiling material across a kit's identical pieces. arrange true or {columns (default the square root of the island count, rounded up), margin (default 0.01)}: last, the islands are laid out in a grid over the 0-1 tile in island order, one uniform scale for all of them so their relative texel density holds - Blender 5.0's Arrange Islands, on every build. perIsland and arranged report what was applied.
bl_uv_straighten_islands:
Straighten quad UV islands of a Blender mesh into a grid: GRID makes every quad a square, RECTIFY rectangles in world proportion; area and centre kept. Replies each island's worst corner off 90 degrees and edge spread before and after.

Blender's Follow Active Quads run on one island at a time from a start face set to a square (GRID, mode EVEN) or to its world edge lengths (RECTIFY, LENGTH_AVERAGE); active_face picks the start for one island, default the quad nearest square. Every face of a chosen island must be a quad. A pole or a seam inside the island bends the grid, and straightenNote names an island left more than 1 degree off square. Then the island is scaled back to its UV area and centred on its old box; bl_uv_transform_islands turns or moves it after.
bl_uv_move_vertices:
Move, scale or rotate chosen UV vertices of a Blender mesh, with an optional proportional falloff {type, radius} onto their neighbours and pinned vertices held. Replies the selection's box and the area or angle stretch before and after.

select is one of {faces: [i]}, {linkedFrom: face} (that face's whole island), {vertices: [i]} (every UV of those vertices) or {uvBox: [umin, vmin, umax, vmax]}. translate [u, v], scale a number or [su, sv] (0 on one axis flattens a row), rotate in degrees, about pivot CENTER (default, the selection's box centre), MEDIAN or [u, v]. falloff type SMOOTH (default), SPHERE, ROOT, SHARP, LINEAR or CONSTANT, radius in UV units: an unselected UV within radius of the selection moves by the falloff of its distance to the nearest selected one - the UV editor's proportional editing. pin [vertex indices] never move. stretch AREA (default) or ANGLE picks the measure (bl_uv_info stretch). bl_uv_transform_islands moves whole islands.
bl_uv_relax:
Relax a Blender mesh's UVs with Blender's Minimize Stretch over chosen faces (default all), island borders or named vertices held. Replies faces relaxed, the largest move and the stretch before and after.

select as bl_uv_move_vertices (a face counts when all its UVs are chosen). iterations default 20 (1-10000). pin_boundary pins each island's border for the run and unpins it after; pin [vertex indices] holds those. The operator runs headless in edit mode on every supported build and moves only the chosen faces' UVs. stretch AREA (default) or ANGLE is the measure reported before and after - a relax should lower it.
bl_set_skin_vertices:
Write a Blender Skin modifier's per-vertex data, which lives on the mesh: radius (a number or [x, y]) or scale (multiplies it), root (one per connected piece; the piece's old root is cleared) and loose (branches leave the vertex freely). Pick the vertices with vertices (indices), all or group. Replies the radii written, the roots and the loose count.

WHY ITS OWN CALL: bl_add_modifier makes the SKIN modifier, but each vertex's thickness is mesh data (mesh.skin_vertices), not a modifier setting - so a hand grown from one vertex (fattened, extruded into a forearm, the root at the wrist, the palm vertex loose so five digits branch from it, the digits slimmed) had no call. Put the Skin modifier before a Subdivision Surface; the other order does nothing. MEASURED 2026-10-05 on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: adding a Skin modifier makes the layer with radius 0.25 and the first vertex as root; radius [0.5, 0.25] on a 2 m chain evaluated 1.0 x 0.5 x 2.0; Blender's Mark Root moves a piece's root to the vertex marked and clears the old one, which root true does too - two roots asked in one piece are refused. With no layer yet one is made (radius 0.25, no root; the modifier picks its own) and hasSkinModifier false comes with a note. Edit mode is refused (the live mesh is in the edit BMesh). Refused before any write: none or two of vertices, all, group; an index past the mesh; a group the object lacks or that weighs nothing; radius with scale; a radius or scale not above 0; nothing to write.

read (1.3): true lists the Skin layer instead of writing it - each vertex's radius [x, y], root and loose (vertices narrows it, limit default 500) and the roots; mesh_stats attribute_values cannot reach it, because the skin layer is not a generic attribute (measured on 3.6.23 and 5.2.1). Face sets, by contrast, read through mesh_stats attribute_values {name: ".sculpt_face_set", domain: FACE}.
bl_uv_pack:
Pack a Blender mesh's existing UV islands into the 0-1 tile WITHOUT re-unwrapping - optionally equalising them by area first, so every island gets one texel density. Reports the density spread before and after (1.0 = equal), the layout's area and bounds. WHY: bl_uv_unwrap always unwraps before it packs, so a layout made by hand, or by an ANGLE unwrap from careful seams, could not be repacked without being replaced; the garment work packed in raw Python and evened island density in raw Python (Blender's average_islands_scale uses SIGNED areas, which a folded face reduces - it left a sleeve at 3x the density of the rest). equalize_by_area scales each island about its own UV centre to the median island's UV area per square world unit (unsigned areas, the object's scale and rotation applied); an island with no area is left and counted (islandsWithoutArea). The pack is Blender's pack_islands with every option pinned as bl_uv_unwrap pins them - margin (default 0.02), rotate (default true), all islands scaled together - so equal densities stay equal: measured, a 1 m and a 2 m quad on equal UV squares went from spread 4 to 1, the 2 m island exactly twice the 1 m one across. Without equalize_by_area the spread is kept. uv_layer picks the layer (default the active one); the active layer and the selection are restored. If the pack throws, the layer is put back as it was and the call fails. Refused before any write: no UV layer, an unknown layer, a margin outside [0, 1). texture_size packs for that texture: on [w, h] V is stretched by w / h so texels stay square and rotation is refused (the pack treats the tile as square). target_texel_density (needs texture_size, unit PX_PER_CM default) scales the layout to that density instead of the largest that fits. merge_overlap keeps overlapping islands stacked.

NON-SQUARE TEXTURES AND A TARGET DENSITY (2026-10-04).
