A pack treats the tile as square in a session without a UV editor: measured on 3.6.23 and 5.2.1, a rotating pack of an island stretched for a 1024 x 512 texture left its texels 2.65 times longer one way than the other, while an unrotated one kept them square - so a non-square texture_size refuses rotate=true and defaults it off. The reply then carries textureSize, vStretch, texelShape {median, max} (the longer side of a texel over the shorter per triangle) and densityAfter {min, median, max, spread} in densityUnit. With target_texel_density the layout is scaled about each island's centre to that area-weighted density and packed with scale off; layoutScale is the factor, outside01 and fitNote say when the tile no longer holds it. merge_overlap passes pack_islands' own option, present on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: two islands on one UV square stayed stacked. region [u_min, v_min, u_max, v_max] (2026-10-06) packs into that part of the tile, proportions kept on a non-square region; insideRegion says every UV landed in it.
bl_mark_seams:
Mark edges of a Blender mesh by rule without unwrapping: mark SEAM (default), SHARP, CREASE or BEVEL_WEIGHT, value true/false or 0-1. Rules: material or vertex-group boundaries, bone panels from skin weights (by_bones), the boundary loop nearest a point, the cheapest edge path {from, to, nearPlane {point, normal}} that hugs a plane, UV island borders (from_islands), or a bl_select_edges selector. Rules join; clear removes the mark first. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. WHY: a short film's garments were seamed in hand-written Python - plane cuts and material boundaries, panel boundaries with an underarm seam as a shortest edge path, every edge of a boundary loop - because bl_uv_unwrap could mark seams only inside an unwrap, by angle or index. THE RULES, any number in one call, their edges joined and each rule's own count reported in rules: by_material_boundary - edges between faces on different materials (two slots holding the same material are one); by_vertex_group_boundary - edges between faces wholly in a vertex group (every vertex at least min_weight, default 0.5) and faces that are not; boundary_loop_near [x,y,z] - every edge of the open boundary loop with the vertex nearest that world point (boundaryLoop says how many loops there were and how far the nearest vertex was); path - {from: [x,y,z], to: [x,y,z], nearPlane: {point, normal}, planeWeight (default 10)}: Dijkstra from the vertex nearest from to the vertex nearest to, each edge's length scaled by 1 + planeWeight x its mean distance from the plane over the mesh's mean edge length, so a back-centre seam follows the spine plane; without nearPlane it is the shortest path. The reply's path block lists the vertices in order, the edge count, the length and the farthest vertex from the plane. selector - bl_select_edges' grammar (minAngleDeg, boundaryOnly, edgeIndices, axis + side, allEdges). clear: true removes every seam first, or alone clears only. Seams are counted off the mesh before and after (seamsBefore, seamsAfter; marked is the new ones). dry_run writes nothing. World units with the object's origin as the working origin. Refused before any write: no rule and no clear, an unknown vertex group, min_weight without a group, a rule that matches no edge (an unwrap after it would act as if no seam had been asked for), a path missing from or to, a path whose ends are nearest one vertex, a plane with no normal, a path between separate pieces, a selector that is not an object, and boundary_loop_near on a closed mesh. Measured on a two-material, two-region 4x4 grid: 4 edges each, 8 together, and an ANGLE unwrap after them gives 2 and 4 islands.

BONE PANELS (by_bones, 2026-10-04): each face takes the deform bone with the most summed weight over its vertices (ties go to the name first in order; a face with none of the weighed bones is unlabelled), and a seam goes on every edge between two faces that differ. by_bones true weighs every deform bone of the armature; {bones: [...]} weighs only those, so the seam outlines their region; {panels: {name: [bones]}} weighs bones under a panel's name, the way bl_vertex_groups_from_bones groups them. armature defaults to the mesh's Armature modifier's object, then its armature parent; groups that are not deform bones (a pin group) are never weighed. The reply's bones block gives facesByLabel. Measured on an 8-sided tube skinned by band to A, A, B, B, C: 16 seam edges and 3 islands after an ANGLE unwrap; panels {Arm: [A, B], Hand: [C]} 8 edges and 2 islands. Refused: no armature to find, a bone that is not a deform bone, a bone in two panels, armature without by_bones, and a labelling with no boundary (one panel holding every bone). MARKS BEYOND SEAMS (2026-10-04): mark SHARP, CREASE or BEVEL_WEIGHT applies the same rules to that mark - a V-neck creased at 1, a fold held by a crease and released with value 0, a seam loop's sharp mark moved to its neighbor. value is true or false for SEAM and SHARP, 0 to 1 (default 1) for CREASE and BEVEL_WEIGHT; false or 0 clears the matched edges, clear removes the mark from every edge first. previousValues counts the matched edges' values before the write; markedBefore and markedAfter count the edges carrying the mark, read off the mesh (seamsBefore and seamsAfter stay for SEAM). Crease and bevel weight go where the build keeps them: the edge's own layer on 3.6, the crease_edge and bevel_weight_edge attributes from 4.0.

RULE - HARD EDGES UNDER SUBDIVISION SURFACE (2026-10-06): edge creases (mark CREASE, value 1; -1 clears, with a bevel weight beside it if wanted) against real support loops (bl_loop_cut). Creases shade oddly in some renderers and may not survive an export, so the destination decides: a render inside Blender can keep creases; a mesh that leaves Blender gets support loops or the applied shape. bl_mesh_stats on the evaluated mesh says what survives.

from_islands: true (the active UV layer) or a UV layer's name marks every edge on an island border of that layer - an edge between two faces whose UVs differ at either end, Blender's Seams from Islands. An imported mesh arrives with UVs and no seams; once they are marked a later unwrap or relax keeps the layout. The mesh's own open boundary is not marked.
bl_fill_mesh_loop: Make a face from Blender mesh vertices, or fill an open loop (edges, or loop_near [x,y,z]) as one NGON, TRIANGLES or a GRID of quads (span, offset). New faces take their neighbours' material and UVs. WHY: a coffee disc from a cup's rim loop, a handle join closed with a face, a boolean's opening closed with quads so subdivision stays clean. vertices make one face through them (bmesh contextual_create); a loop is named by its edges or by loop_near (world: the open boundary loop nearest). NGON (default) makes one face, TRIANGLES a beauty-shaped fan of triangles, GRID quads: the loop (an even vertex count of at least 4) is split into two opposite rails of span edges (default a quarter of the loop) starting offset vertices along it, and bmesh grid_fill fills between them - a loop of 2 x (span + m) vertices gets span x m quads. New faces take their neighbour's material and smooth flag, and (NGON, TRIANGLES) each corner's UV from that vertex in a neighbouring face. Measured: a 4-vertex hole filled with one face keeps the sheet one UV island with no zero-area face; an 8-vertex hole in a 4x4 sheet GRID-filled with 4 quads and a new centre vertex. Closing every hole up to N vertices at once is bl_clean_mesh fill_holes_up_to. Refused: more than one input, GRID or TRIANGLES from vertices, a span with no room, an edge that already has two faces, no open loop. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write.
bl_offset_edges:
Carve a buffer loop beside a Blender mesh edge loop, distance away across each face it touches - the room a bevel needs round a junction a Boolean left in n-gons. edges is one closed loop or open chain; the loop stays in place. side_face (a face touching a closed loop) keeps the buffer on that side only. Replies the rings' edges and measured distance, the buffer faces and maxOffSurface.

THE ROUTE (measured 2026-10-05 on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1, round the 56-edge junction of a cylinder unioned onto a sphere, 104 of its sides n-gons): Blender's bevel on the loop with two segments and a square profile, so the middle ring is the loop itself, every vertex in place, and the two new rings sit distance from it - 0.04998 to 0.05046 at 0.05. A round profile moved the junction; bmesh offset_edgeloops only stacks new loops on the old one; the editor's Offset Edge Slide needs a 3D view, and run without one it crashed 4.4.0. clamp_overlap is on, so a distance the neighbours cannot hold is shortened: each ring reports distance {min, median, max} and clampNote says so. side_face keeps one side: the other ring is welded back onto the loop, which put that side back on the surface to 1e-6 (closed loops only). An open chain works too: across a 5 x 5 grid both rings sat exactly the distance away. maxOffSurface is how far any ring vertex now sits from the mesh as it was: 0.00034 round that junction merged and clamped, 0.0035 unmerged and unclamped at 0.05. rings name their side LEFT or RIGHT of the walk loopVertices gives. Lengths in mesh units, or world units with space WORLD (uniform scale only). Refused before any write: a boundary or wire edge, edges that branch or are not one piece, two loop vertices on one position, a side_face that does not touch the loop or on an open chain, a distance not above 0.
bl_subdivide_mesh:
Cut a Blender mesh's chosen faces or edges, or all of it, into cuts + 1 pieces per edge - Blender's Subdivide (a plane cut 25 times is 26 x 26). smoothness 0-1 rounds the new vertices out; quad_corner STRAIGHT_CUT, INNER_VERT, PATH or FAN. Counts before and after, regionFaces.

WHY ITS OWN CALL (2026-10-05): a SIMPLE Subdivision Surface plus bl_apply_modifier doubles every edge of the whole mesh and nothing else, so a plane cut 25 times for a half pattern (26 segments) or one region cut finer had no call. faces (indices: every edge of those faces is cut), edges (indices) or all true pick what is cut; cuts is 1-100 (default 1) new vertices per edge. It runs bmesh.ops.subdivide_edges with the settings of Blender's own Subdivide operator (mesh.subdivide): grid fill on, a quad with two neighbouring edges cut split by quad_corner (STRAIGHT_CUT by default; INNERVERT is accepted for INNER_VERT), linear smoothing falloff. smoothness moves the new vertices toward the surface the old ones imply (a cube rounds out past its size); fractal with seed displaces them at random. A face beside the cut region is not split: it gains the new vertex on its shared edge (measured: the centre face of a 3 x 3 grid at cuts 1 becomes 4 quads and its four edge neighbours pentagons - 21 vertices, 12 faces). Reply: before and after counts, edgesCut, newVertices and regionFaces (the faces of the cut region, in the mesh's order after the write). Refused before any write: none or two of faces, edges, all; cuts outside 1-100; smoothness outside 0-1; a negative fractal; an unknown quad_corner; an index past the mesh; shape keys (the base mesh is what is written).
bl_cut_eyelets:
Cut eyelets through a Blender sheet at world points: round (inner_radius) or oval (size [w, h] along axis) holes at the mesh's density, each with a ring of faces ring_width wide in a material slot.

WHY (2026-10-02): eyelets on a hood band and the holes a drawcord exits by were cut with a circle primitive, an inset and a knife, or in raw Python - no op cut one. Each point of at is moved to the nearest point of the surface (refused past 10 cm). Faces whose centre lies inside the hole are deleted, and the new edge's vertices are moved onto the circle or ellipse in the surface's tangent plane, so the hole is round at the mesh's own density; axis (a world direction, default +Z) lays an ellipse's w into the surface. Faces within ring_width (default 4 mm) of the edge go to slot (a material, added as a slot when missing). min_boundary (default 8) refuses a hole with fewer edge vertices - subdivide the region first. Reply per eyelet: center, normal, facesDeleted, boundaryVertices, radius {min, max} as cut, ringFaces; boundaryLoopsBefore/After. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: two 5 mm holes in a 10 cm grid at 2.5 mm - boundary loops 1 -> 3, every edge vertex 5 mm from its centre. Refused before the write: a point off the surface, overlapping eyelets, a hole that deletes nothing or everything, a coarse mesh, size on a RING or inner_radius on an ELLIPSE, an unknown slot material, shape keys, a non-uniform scale. at entries may be vertex indices; mirror X|Y|Z adds each eyelet's twin across the mesh's centre on that world axis.

LAYERS (2026-10-06): layers OUTER (default) cuts the sheet the point is on; ALL also cuts every layer under it along the eyelet's inward normal within layer_depth (3 cm) - another layer of the same mesh and each object named in lining - the same shape round the point the line meets each, with its own ring and slot. Rows carry object and layer (OUTER or INNER), and linings their loop counts. Measured on 4.2.23-5.2.2: a two-layer band 5 mm apart and a lining 12 mm under it, two eyelets: band loops 2 -> 6, lining 1 -> 3, every hole 5 mm round. Refused: lining or layer_depth without ALL, a lining under none of the eyelets, ALL finding no layer, a point on the mirror plane.
bl_rip_edges: Rip (split) a Blender mesh along chosen edges: edges [i...] or selector {bl_select_edges' grammar}. A chain boundary to boundary, or a loop, cuts it into parts. fill bridges each rip with a face. Replies new vertex indices and parts before and after. WHY: cutting a garment into panels along its seams (collar, sleeve openings, hem, back pieces), each rip a UV island boundary, had no call - the EDGE_SPLIT modifier splits by angle or sharp marks only. Each edge becomes two, one on each face, and the vertices along the cut split with it; a slit that starts and ends inside the surface splits only its inner vertices. Every edge must have exactly two faces (a boundary or wire edge has nothing to rip). selector takes bl_select_edges' keys (seedEdge with loop, minAngleDeg, axis and side, ...) in camelCase, e.g. {"seedEdge": 4, "loop": true}. fill true (default false) bridges each ripped edge with a face, as Blender's Rip Fill does - the faces have no area until one side is moved. A mesh with shape keys is refused. Reply: newVertices, newVertexCount, islandsBefore and islandsAfter (connected parts), fillFaces, counts before and after. bl_separate_mesh mode LOOSE then splits the parts into objects.
bl_circularize: Make a Blender mesh loop (loop [vertex i...]) or a face region's rim (faces) a circle in its best-fit plane. flatten false keeps the host's curvature; regularize spaces vertices evenly; radius defaults to the mean. Replies deviation from a circle before and after. WHY: a round boss grown out of a curved surface needs its inset region turned into a circle with the host's curvature kept; bl_create_primitive circle only makes a new circle. LoopTools' Circle, headless. faces must be one region with one rim (a region with a hole, two regions touching at a corner, or a closed set of faces with no rim are refused); its rim is made round and the faces inside stay where they are. loop is a closed loop along edges, in any order (an open run is refused). The circle is centred on the loop's mean in its Newell plane. flatten (default true) puts the loop in that plane; false keeps each vertex's height off it. regularize (default true) spaces the vertices evenly, rotated to move them least; false keeps each one's angle. radius is in space units (LOCAL default, or WORLD on a uniformly scaled object). A mesh with shape keys is refused. Reply: loop (vertex indices in walk order), center, normal, radius, before and after {meanRadius, maxRadialDeviation, maxOffPlane, gapDegrees {min, max}}, maxMoved.
bl_build_vehicle_body:
A parked car's Blender body lofted from side-profile curves [[x, z], ...] (bottom, belt, roof) and a plan (half_width), each applying only in its own x range; lids, seams, bumpers, lamp/plate pockets, mirrors, lips, wheels.

WHY (2026-10-04): three street cars came from a ~1,000-line local loft script sent through bl_create_mesh, and its first version clamped the roof curve's end value - a roof held at 80 cm over a hood falling to 60 stood a 20 cm slab on a sedan's nose. Here a curve applies ONLY INSIDE ITS OWN x RANGE: outside the roof's range a section tops out at the belt. x runs along the car (front at the low x), metres. bottom, belt and half_width must share one length; stations (default 48) sections are taken along it, each sectionPoints (default 19, odd) per side: a superellipse quarter of exponents.lower (default 4, boxy) from the underside's centre to the belt, then where the roof applies one of exponents.upper (default 2.5) up to the roof's centre, its half width roof_width_ratio (0.72) of the belt's. Mirrored, skinned and capped into one closed solid, turned out by signed volume. arches [{x, radius, height (default radius)}] cut circles up into the bottom line; glass [[x0, x1], ...] puts the glasshouse faces in those ranges on slot 1 (materials {body, glass}). Reply: bl_create_mesh's, plus length, xRange, stationsWithRoof, roofRange, glassFaces, outwardCheck. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a 4.5 m sedan closed with no flipped edge, topping at the belt's 0.775 at x 0.5 (roof from 1.6) and at 1.45 under the roof, its underside 0.66 at an arch. Refused: x not rising, no common length, a belt not above the bottom, sectionPoints even or under 5, stations outside 4-400, a glass range past the body, an unknown material. Arches are cut into the bottom line; glass ranges go on a slot.

THE PARTS (2026-10-06), each optional, all in the body's local space and parented to it (moving the body moves them). lids [{x0, x1, inset 0.06, width 0.006, depth 0.004}]: a hood or boot lid where no roof applies, its shut line a groove (three cuts, the middle pressed in by depth) between the fender crowns, inset in from the plan's half width. seams [{x, zMin, zMax, width, depth, side BOTH|LEFT|RIGHT}]: a pressed vertical seam down the side. bumpers [{end FRONT|REAR, length 0.3, zMin, zMax, gap 0.01, thickness 0.03}]: a separate shell copied from the body's faces in that band, standing gap off it (gapMeasured). pockets [{kind LAMP|GRILLE|PLATE|HANDLE, at FRONT|REAR (HANDLE: LEFT|RIGHT|SIDES), center [y (x on a side), z], size [w, h], depth, mirror}]: the rectangle cut into the end cap or side and pushed in; a LAMP gets a lens shell clipped from the body surface (flush, lensThickness 0.008), an emissive band on the floor and (bowls, default true) two reflector bowls with a bulb in each, a GRILLE slats, a PLATE a plate with raised characters (text, charHeight, raise) from Blender's built-in font, a HANDLE a bar in its dish. mirrors [{x, z, size [along, out, up], reach}]: a housing on an arm each side, its rear face on the glass material. arch_lips {width, out, embed, segments}: a band round every arch each side. wheels {radius, width, rimRadius, inset, segments}: a tyre and rim through bl_build_lathe in every arch, standing on the ground. materials adds lens, lamp, trim and tyre. Reply: parts {lids, seams, bumpers, pockets, mirrors, archLips, wheels, objects}. Measured on a sedan with every part: the body still one closed solid faced out, 16 part objects each closed; shut line and seam 4 mm deep, lamp floors 6 cm in with 8 mm lenses flush with the nose, plate characters 2 mm proud, handle dishes 15 mm, wheels on the ground. Refused before anything exists: a lid under the roof, a seam outside the side, a pocket outside the end's outline or the side, overlapping another or in a bumper's band, a mirrored pocket crossing the centre line, a wheel that does not fit its arch, lips or wheels without arches; a part that does not build cleanly removes the body and every part made.
bl_build_lathe:
Revolve a profile [[r, h], ...] round an axis into a Blender solid of revolution (a can, a bottle, a post) whose every face points out, checked by signed volume. r 0 is a pole; caps close open ends.

WHY (2026-10-04): a trash can's profile was revolved in local Python, and that revolve turned each face away from the profile's centroid - on a tapered can the lower wall's radius sat under the centroid's, so 800 of 3,880 outer faces (20 %) faced inward and Unreal drew the band see-through, while bl_mesh_quality (non-manifold edges only) said nothing. Here every face winds by the profile edge's own direction, one orientation over the whole surface, and the finished part is turned so it faces out - by signed volume when closed, by the area-weighted radial direction when open (outwardCheck: signedVolume, closed, turnedOver). profile: two or more [r, h] points in order, r at least 0 (r 0 is a pole, one vertex). segments 3-512 (default 32); axis Z (default), Y or X; caps (default true) close an end whose r is above 0 with one face; smooth (default true); uv_scale metres per UV unit (u round the largest circumference, v along the profile); material names an existing material for every face. name, location, rotation, scale, collection, take_over_name and the reply are bl_create_mesh's. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a can tapered in or out, either walking direction, has 0 flipped edges and a signed volume within 1 % of the 32-sided frustum; a ray at its lower wall meets an outward normal. Refused before anything exists: under two points, r below 0, a repeated point, every point on the axis, segments out of range, an unknown axis or material.
bl_build_tube:
A round Blender tube along points (closed for a neon loop), laid on a surface mesh lift off it, or hanging between start and end with sag (a catenary): a cable, a pipe, a drawcord. Capped into a closed solid that faces out.

WHY (2026-10-04): neon signs, cables and pipes were swept in scratch scripts and a cable between two points hung by hand. points [[x, y, z], ...] gives the path (closed true joins the last point to the first); or start and end with sag (metres the middle hangs below the straight line, along -Z, solved as a catenary) sampled at samples segments (default 16). The ring of sides (default 12, 3-128) at radius is carried by parallel transport so it does not twist, and widened across each bend so the wall keeps its thickness. caps (default true) close an open tube into a solid; its winding is checked by signed volume and turned out if needed (outwardCheck). uv_scale: u round, v along, metres per UV unit. The reply adds pathPoints, pathLength, lowestPoint, closedLoop and capped to bl_create_mesh's. Measured: a cable from (0,0,3) to (4,0,3) with sag 0.5 bottoms at z 2.5 at x 2; an L-shaped pipe is closed with 0 flipped edges. Refused before anything exists: points with start/end or neither, under two points, a repeated point, radius not above 0, sag below 0, sag or samples with points, sides or samples out of range, closed with start/end. ON A SURFACE (2026-10-06): hoodie drawcords were rebuilt by ray-casting stations down the chest and sweeping a tube 3.5 mm off it. surface names the mesh (evaluated) the points are laid on: resampled every step metres, each moved to the nearest surface point and lift along its normal; surfaceGap {min, max} reads each station's distance back (2 mm asked, 2 mm within 0.1 mm on a 10 cm sphere) and channelLength the laid length. hang_ends [a, b] drops a and b metres straight down (-Z) from the start and the end, so a cord can hang unevenly past its eyelets. Refused: surface with start/end, lift or step without surface, hang_ends on a closed path.

CORD ENDS (2026-10-06): end_caps NONE|KNOT|AGLET|STOPPER for both ends or [start, end]: an aglet is a sleeve 1.3x the radius over the last 2 cm (or 6 radii), a knot a trefoil of the cord's own radius at the end, a stopper a barrel 8 radii long whose bore is the cord's radius - each a closed part in the cord's mesh. stoppers [{at, object, boreRadius, boreAxis}] slide a stopper onto the cord at metres along it: a model already in the file (origin on its bore's centre, the bore along boreAxis, default Z) copied, scaled so its bore is the cord's radius, turned along the cord and parented to it; without object a built-in barrel. Reply endCaps and stoppers rows (location, tangent, scale). Refused: an unknown cap, caps or stoppers on a closed tube, a stopper past the end, a model without boreRadius, boreRadius not above 0.
bl_build_trash_bag:
A tied rubbish bag in Blender standing on the floor: a pear on a flat contact patch, lumped by its contents, pleats twisting into the neck, a knot and two ears - one mesh, every part a closed solid facing out.

WHY (2026-10-04): a filled bin's bags were built by a local script and the loose ones stayed lumpy icospheres. height (m, default 0.7) is to the knot's top; width (default 0.48) the belly's diameter; contact (default 0.45) the flat patch's radius as a share of the belly's, at z 0, so the bag stands instead of rocking on a point. knuckles (default 8, 0-32) lumps of the contents with knuckle_depth (default 0.1 of the radius); pleats (default 9; 0 or 3-32) gather into the neck, turning twist turns (default 1); ears (default true) are two flat closed lobes leaning out from the knot, clear of it. seed (default 1): the same seed is the same bag. segments (48) and rings (40) set the density. color makes a near-black plastic (or material reuses one). The body is one ring surface - each ring a closed star at its own height - so nothing folds through itself; each part is turned out by its signed volume (outwardCheck). The reply adds parts, bag {knotTopM, earsTopM, bellyWidthM, contactRadiusM, neckRadiusM, knotRadiusM} measured on the built vertices, and materialSlots to bl_create_mesh's. Refused before anything exists: a value out of range, pleats 1-2, a bag wider than 1.5 x its height, material with color, a material that is not there.
bl_build_downspout:
Build a downspout down a wall in Blender: a hollow rect or round pipe from the gutter outlet over the eave (a gooseneck), down on screwed straps, out at a kick-out shoe. The wall is y 0, the pipe in +y.

WHY (2026-10-04): downspouts were built in scratch scripts. height (m, default 3, 0.8-30) is the outlet's; offset (default 0.3) its distance from the wall - from 0.15 m past the pipe's centre it crosses with two 45-degree elbows, under that it runs straight. section rect (width 0.076 x depth 0.051, 2 x 3 in) or round (width is the diameter; depth refused); standoff (default 0.02) the gap behind it. straps (default true) every strap_spacing m (default 1.5) on the straight run, each a formed sheet with two screws; shoe (default true) a kick-out at the foot. The pipe is ONE closed hollow solid - outer and inner walls swept with mitred elbows, joined by quad rims at both ends - so its ends are open to look into. Every part is turned out by its signed volume. The reply adds parts, boundsLocalM, materialSlots (pipe, straps) and downspout {outletM, footM, gooseneck, shoe, pathLengthM, straps, strapHeightsM, pipeBackYM} to bl_create_mesh's. Refused before anything exists: a value out of range, depth on round, strap_spacing with straps false, a spout too short for its gooseneck and shoe.
bl_build_wall_fixture:
Build a wall-mounted fixture in Blender - a wall pack light, a gooseneck barn light, or a junction box with its conduit run - every part a closed solid, the lamp its own emissive slot. The wall is y 0.

WHY (2026-10-04): wall lights and boxes were built in scratch scripts. kind wallpack (default): a slanted housing, a lens, fins. gooseneck: a backplate, an arm curving down at arm_length (default 0.45, 0.2-1.5), a socket, a dish shade (a thin sheet revolved and closed on itself) and a bulb. box: a junction box with a cover and screws, and conduit_length m (default 1, 0 for none, up to 5) of conduit going conduit down (default) or up, with a connector and one-hole straps. scale (default 1, 0.25-4) sizes everything. The fixture's back is on the plane y 0 and its mounting point at the origin; place it on a wall with location and rotation. Slot body (color) and, for a wallpack or gooseneck, slot lamp (lamp_color, lamp_strength default 5 - emissive). Every part a closed solid turned out by its signed volume. The reply adds parts, boundsLocalM, materialSlots and fixture {reachM, shadeRimM, conduitStrapsAtM, ...}. Refused before anything exists: an unknown kind, a key for another kind, a value out of range.
bl_call_log:
The calls this Blender ran through MifBlender, newest first - op, parameter keys and short values, ok or the error, milliseconds - so you can check what really went through the bridge. From memory by default, the last 64. disk=True reads the journal file instead: every Blender that wrote it and the sessions before a restart, with `unfinished` - a call whose start has no end, the one a crashed Blender died in - and each session's end: closed with its reason, restarted, or died (no shutdown record, and a later Blender came up with its pid). The file is per user (%LOCALAPPDATA%\MifBridge\Blender\journal.jsonl on Windows, `path` in the response) and each call is written before it runs; an add-on preference turns the file off. bl_run_python code is never written, only its size.

limit (int, default None): how many calls to return. From memory, None means every finished call in the ring (it holds the last 64, ringCapacity); with disk=True, None means 50. A fraction or a negative number is refused; when rows were dropped the reply says truncated and carries a truncationNote. Calls still running - this call_log and a batch it is part of - are left out of both sources.

OUT, always: path, diskEnabled, diskOpen, diskError, pid, proc, sessionStarted, totalCalls, ringCapacity, source (memory or disk), calls, count, and returned/truncated when limit was given. From memory each call is {seq, t (ISO time), op, ok, ms, error, keys, args, agent, generative}, plus batch and i for an op inside a batch and bulk for a bulk preview or commit. With disk=True each call is {pid, seq, t, op, ended, ok, ms, error, keys, args, agent, generative, session}, plus batch/i and sessionDied when its session died; also unfinished (up to 20 calls with a start and no end) and unfinishedCount, sessions (up to 20, newest first: {pid, proc, t, blender, port, background, generative, closed, reason, kind, restarted, died, diedEvidence, reopened} as they apply) and sessionCount, fileBytes, readBytes (the last 512 KB of the file is read), unreadableLines, previousFile when a rotated file exists, readError when the file cannot be read, and a note on how to read the fields. Argument values are shortened, and an error is cut to 160 characters.

Refused: an unknown key, a limit that is not a whole number or is negative, and a disk value that is not a boolean. It only reads.
bl_build_prop:
Build a wooden prop in Blender board by board: crate, pallet, barrel, table, bench, chair, shelf, with eased edges, worn corners and grain along each. kind is crate (default), pallet, barrel, table, bench, chair or shelf; depth sets its size with width and height in cm; wear (0-1) is how worn it is; detail is full or a lighter form; lid is a crate's; color2 is the wood's second tone and metal_color a barrel's hoops; collision adds a convex hull; collection and take_over_name place and name it as other builders do.

Sizes in cm, pivot at the bottom center, a hull, a lightmap layer. kind crate (default), pallet, barrel, table, bench, chair, shelf. width, depth, height in cm, each kind's common size by default (crate 70x50x50, pallet 120x80x14.4, barrel 60x60x88, table 150x80x75, bench 140x34x45, chair 44x46x90, shelf 100x36x180); a barrel's width is its bilge and it takes no depth. seed picks the bows, wear and tones. wear 0-1 (default 0.35) rubs the corners and, in the material, fades the boards apart, scuffs their edges and puts grime in corners and joints; the triangles stay the same; 0 is fresh-planed. That look is a Cycles node chain: bake_texture_set with uv_layer LightmapUV and baked_material carries it to an engine, on UV channel 1. detail full (default) or low: low is about a third of the triangles for a mesh without Nanite. lid (crate only, default true) adds the battened lid. color and color2 are the wood's two tones, metal_color a barrel's hoops. collision (default true) makes UCX_<name>_00, one convex hull round the whole prop. The name defaults to SM_<Kind>_01a, the first number free. UV0 is in meters with U along each board's grain, each board starting elsewhere on the texture, so a tiling wood material reads right whichever way a board lies; LightmapUV is the last layer; vertex color Col holds a tone per board in R and how faded it is in G. The reply lists the parts and sizeCm.
bl_build_dumpster:
Build a front-load dumpster in Blender: a lofted steel body with a sloped lower front, pressed ribs and dents, a rolled rim, fork pockets, skids or casters, lids opened by angle, and an optional fill checked against the walls.

WHY (2026-10-04): a dumpster came from a 330-line local script whose first heap poked three bags through its walls. width x depth x height (m, default 1.83 x 1.4 x 1.2 to the rim); front_slope (default 0.35) how far the lower front is set back at the foot; corner_radius (0.04); ribs (default 2) pressed into each side and the back; dents (0.3) a seeded dent field; seed. The body is one closed solid - outer sheet up, rim, inner sheet down to the floor - so the inside shows through an open lid. lid_angles [left, right] degrees (0-100) open the two moulded lids (domed, ribbed, skirted, with a grip and knuckles on the hinge rod). casters (default false: skids) puts it on four swivel casters. fill (0-1.2 of the inner height, over 1 heaps above the rim) places bags (bl_build_trash_bag's) and, with carton (default true), a carton; EVERY one is checked vertex by vertex against the walls and the floor, shrunk if it crosses and dropped if it still does - fillCheck says how many. The back is at y 0, the front +y, the origin at the back's foot. The reply adds parts, boundsLocalM, materialSlots, dumpster {capacityM3, capacityYd3, bodyFootM, ...} and fillCheck. Refused before anything exists: a value out of range, lid_angles not two numbers 0-100, carton with fill 0.
bl_measure_neckline:
Where a Blender body's neck column meets chest and shoulders, per angle (rays out from the neck's axis), as baseZ and a ring; trim {garment, distance} deletes a garment's faces above it near the neck.

WHY (2026-10-05): a shirt's neck edge and its collar sit where the neck meets chest and shoulders. On a stock mannequin that line is 1.50 m at the front, 1.545 m at the sides and 1.53 m at the back, so no plane follows it, and one sampling height fails both ways - high, a front ray from outside meets the jaw; low, a side ray meets the shoulder. Here the rays go OUTWARD from the neck's axis, so jaw and shoulders are never in the way. The axis: center [x, y] and neck_z (a height where every angle meets the neck column alone), or armature (+ neck_bone, default neck_01 / neck / Neck) whose posed bone's middle gives both. At each of angles (default 32, counter-clockwise from +X; -Y is a character's front) the column radius at neck_z is read, then rays step down z_step (0.0025) up to search_down (0.15) until the section leaves the column by tolerance (0.004): that height is baseZ. An angle that never leaves is filled from its neighbours (filledAngles); one more than clip (0.015) from the median of five is clipped to it (clippedAngles; rawBaseZ keeps it); smooth_passes (1) of [1, 2, 1] follow. The reply: angles [{angle, baseZ, rawBaseZ, columnRadius, baseRadius, point}], baseZ min/max and where, baseZAtAxes (+X, +Y, -X, -Y) and ring - the points bl_build_collar takes. trim {garment, distance (0.05), margin (0)} deletes the garment's faces whose centre stands above the neckline within distance of the column, and reports the cut edge's height against the neckline. Measured on a body built to a known answer: front, sides and back within 4 mm, a 4 cm dart clipped, a jaw in front of the neck ignored. Refused before anything: an axis outside the neck at neck_z, a column that does not end at a quarter of the angles, a trim of the body or one that deletes nothing or everything.
bl_build_collar:
A Blender shirt collar - stand, fold and fall, collar points and a front gap - as one ring at even angles on a neckline (bl_measure_neckline's ring, or its request), the fall laid onto shirt.

WHY (2026-10-05): a collar built in raw Python from the shirt's own ragged neck edge came out jagged three times. neckline is bl_measure_neckline's ring [[x, y, z], ...] or a measure_neckline request {body, center, neckZ | armature, ...} run first; it is resampled at segments (64) EVEN angles round center (default the neckline's; front_angle 270 = -Y, a character's front). The section at each angle: the STAND rises stand_height (0.03) straight up, ease (0.005) out from the neckline, in stand_rows (2); the FOLD turns over fold_gap (0.004); the FALL runs down and out fall_width (0.045) at fall_angle (20 degrees from vertical) in fall_rows (3). front_gap (0.02 m; 0 = a closed band) is left open at the front, where COLLAR POINTS grow over point_span (40 degrees): the fall lengthens by point_drop (0.02) and its tip swings point_angle (15 degrees, + toward the gap). shirt lays the fall on that mesh: a fall point inside it or within lay_reach (0.03) goes to its surface + lay_offset (0.002). One sheet - give it thickness with a SOLIDIFY modifier - with vertex groups CollarStand and CollarFall (pin the stand in a cloth sim), u along the neckline and v down the section in metres / uv_scale. The reply adds columns, angleStep, frontGapDegrees, front {gapAtNeckline, gapAtPoints} and laid {fallPointsMoved, gap} to bl_create_mesh's. Measured on a body built to a known neckline: the bottom row within 0.2 mm of it, every column at one angle step, a laid fall 1.5-2 mm off the shirt where the unlaid one went inside it. Refused before anything exists: a neckline under 8 points or not round its axis, a front gap as wide as the neck, sizes out of range, an unknown shirt or material.
bl_build_applique:
Lay a patch on a Blender surface where a ray meets it - a pocket flap, badge, name plate: a 2D outline (metres) cast on as a radial fan, lifted and walled into a closed solid. Resolution is the fan's spacing in metres, on the rim and between the rings alike: bigger is coarser and makes fewer faces - a 12 x 14 cm pocket is 286 faces at 2 cm, 950 at 1 cm and 3,626 at 5 mm. Left out, it is the coarsest of 4, 2 and 1 cm that follows the surface, and 1 cm on cloth no step follows, never finer; resolutionFrom (given, surface, floor) and resolutionTried (each step's spanDeviation) say which.

WHY (2026-10-05): pocket flaps, a badge, a name plate, epaulets and shoulder patches were each laid on a shirt in raw Python by rays from a 2D outline, as a radial fan (a grid kept inside the outline came out stair-stepped), lifted and given side walls. A ray from origin along direction meets target (world, evaluated); there the surface normal and up (default +Z, projected onto the surface; spin turns it, degrees) set the outline's frame: x right, y up. outline [[x, y], ...] in METRES round that hit point, star-shaped round its centroid, is resampled to resolution (the fan's spacing in metres; see above) and filled as a radial fan from the centroid at the same spacing; each fan point is cast back onto the target along the normal from reach (0.05) in front. The underside stands lift (0.001) off the surface along its interpolated normal, the top thickness (0.002; 0 = one lifted sheet) above it, with side walls, and bottom (true) closes the underside - checked by signed volume. material on top and bottom, side_material on the walls; vertex groups AppliqueTop and AppliqueBottom; UVs: the outline's box on 0-1, the wall along the rim. The reply adds hitPoint, normal, frame, outlinePoints, rings, rays, liftError and outwardCheck to bl_create_mesh's. Measured: a 10 x 6 cm patch on a cylinder stands 1.000 mm off it everywhere, closed and facing out, its edges following the curve. Refused before anything exists: a ray that misses, a fan point that misses (the outline runs off the surface), an outline not star-shaped, up along the normal, sizes out of range, an unknown material.
bl_build_band:
A stiff Blender band round a body from z0 to z1 - a belt, a waistband - by rays onto the garment: one radius per angle (the widest), closed top and bottom, with boxes (items) on it by angle and height.

WHY (2026-10-05): a duty belt was built in raw Python from rings sampled by rays onto the garment underneath; following the hip's taper made it slant like a tray, and what worked was ONE radius per angle over the band's height - the widest. Rays from outside toward a vertical axis through center (default the middle of around's vertices between z0 and z1) meet around (world, evaluated) at segments (64) angles and samples (5) heights. stiff (default true) takes the widest radius at each angle for the whole height - straight walls; false follows the surface at every sampled height. smooth_passes (2) of [1, 2, 1] round the band never go inside what was measured. The inner wall stands offset (0.003) out, the outer thickness (0.01) beyond, closed top and bottom - a closed solid checked by signed volume. items [{angle (degrees from +X; 270 = -Y, a character's front), dz (from the band's middle), size [width, height, depth], material?}] are boxes standing on the outer wall, their back flat at the widest outer radius they span. material on the band, item_material (or an item's own) on the boxes. The reply adds surfaceRadius, innerRadius, slant (top against bottom; 0 when stiff), taperFollowed (what the surface does) and items [{center, backRadius}] to bl_create_mesh's. Measured on a tapered elliptical garment: the stiff band's section is the same at its bottom and top, an ellipse like the garment, nothing nearer than offset; stiff false slants 2 cm with it. Refused before anything exists: a ray that misses, z1 not above z0, sizes out of range, an unknown material, an item material with no band material.
bl_mesh_from_outline:
A Blender mesh from a 2D outline [[x, y], ...] (and holes): a flat panel, or with height a closed slab with top, side and bottom slots and world-density UVs. edge_length adds an inner lattice (cloth). plane XY, XZ or YZ.

WHY (2026-10-02): street blocks and kerbs were extruded from plan outlines, and garment panels (a hood as a rounded rectangle, a sleeve from an armhole offset) were drawn as outlines and filled - each in raw Python round mesh.from_pydata. outline is one closed ring (the first point need not repeat; either winding - it is made counter-clockwise, so the panel or the top faces along the plane's normal); holes are rings inside it. plane XY (default, normal +Z), XZ (a front view: x right, y up; extrudes toward -Y) or YZ (normal +X). height 0 (default) is a flat panel; above 0 a closed slab - the outline's face at the plane (slot bottom), one at height along the normal (slot top) and the walls (slot side). edge_length resamples every edge to at most that length and fills the inside with a triangular lattice of that spacing kept half a step clear of the edges (cloth wants 10-20 mm; bl_add_cloth refuses under 16 vertices); walls are cut every edge_length up the height. Without it a ring with no holes is one n-gon; holes are filled with triangles (Blender's constrained Delaunay). materials {top, side, bottom} names existing materials for a slab's three slots (always made, in that order). uv_scale (default 1) is metres per UV unit: caps flat in the plane, walls along the perimeter by height, one density everywhere. boundary_group (default Boundary; null for none) holds the outline's vertices - a panel's sewing edge. name, location, rotation, scale, collection and take_over_name are bl_create_mesh's, and its reply comes back (counts, slots, groups, zeroAreaFaces) with outlineArea, boundaryVertices per ring and slots. Refused before anything exists: under three points, a repeated point, edges that cross (named by ring and edge), a hole outside the outline, a negative height, edge_length not above 0 or one making over 200,000 vertices, an unknown material, materials on a flat panel. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a 2 x 2 m slab 0.5 high with a 1 m hole is 16 vertices and closed; a 1 m panel at 0.1 is all triangles with 40 boundary vertices.
bl_mesh_sections:
Slice a Blender mesh across an axis (default Z) at heights or every step and read each cross-section: loops, closed or open, length, area, min/max/center and size in the other two axes. WORLD and evaluated by default. Read-only.

WHY (2026-10-02): a body's and a garment's widths at chest, waist and hip, and a car's profile at a few heights, were read by slicing in raw Python. heights [h, ...] or step (every step from the lowest point to the highest - the range comes back) along axis X, Y or Z, in space WORLD (default) or LOCAL, on the evaluated mesh (default; modifiers and the armature's pose applied) or the base mesh. Each slice: at, loops (largest area first) each with closed, vertexCount, length, area (closed loops), min, max and center in the two other axes (axes says which, in order), and the slice's min, max and size over all its loops; a plane that meets nothing is empty true - not an error, so a sweep past the top reads cleanly. A plane through a vertex counts it once. Measured: a 2 x 1 x 1 m box at z 0.5 is one closed loop, length 6, area 2, size [2, 1]. Refused: heights and step together or neither, a step not above 0, more slices than limit (default 200, at most 2000), a mesh with no faces.
bl_set_scene_units:
Set the Blender scene's unit system (METRIC, IMPERIAL, NONE), unit scale (1.0 is what the Unreal hand-off assumes) and display units; checked before any is written, before and after read back.

WHY (2026-10-02): a street scene and a character file were set to metric at scale 1.0 (one to centimetres for display) in raw Python; bl_scene_info reported these fields and warned on a scale that is not 1, and nothing wrote them. system NONE, METRIC or IMPERIAL is written first, because Blender resets the unit choices when it changes; then length_unit, mass_unit, time_unit, temperature_unit (each must be one Blender takes for that system - CENTIMETERS needs METRIC, INCHES IMPERIAL), rotation_unit DEGREES or RADIANS, separate (compound units) and scale_length (above 0; 0.01 is the centimetre convention, and FBX export multiplies by it). A value Blender refuses puts every setting back as it was, so a refusal changes nothing. The reply: before, after, changed, and a note whenever scale_length is not 1.0.
bl_sculpt_stroke:
Sculpt a Blender mesh along a stroke of world points: brush DRAW, CLAY, INFLATE, SMOOTH, FLATTEN, CREASE, GRAB, SNAKE_HOOK, BOUNDARY, CLOTH, CLAY_STRIPS, SCRAPE, FILL, PINCH, LAYER, BLOB, DRAW_SHARP, NUDGE, ELASTIC or POSE, falloff, symmetry, masks, a shape key, dyntopo detail or a Multires level. Mesh space.

WHY MESH SPACE (measured 2026-10-05): Blender's sculpt.brush_stroke poll fails headless with no 3D view and passes once the startup screen's VIEW_3D area is overridden - but the stroke then segfaulted Blender 4.4.0 and 5.0.1, and on 5.2.2 answered FINISHED and moved nothing (its dabs are screen positions). So the brushes run on the vertex positions: the same on every build and repeatable, Blender's falloff curves by formula (SMOOTH default, SPHERE, ROOT, SHARP, LINEAR, CONSTANT over distance / radius) - not its brush engine, spacing or pressure. path [[x,y,z], ...] world (one point is a dab; spacing resamples it every spacing x radius); radius in world units; strength 0-1 (default 0.5). Per dab: DRAW moves along the area normal by 0.25 x radius x strength x falloff; INFLATE along each vertex normal; SMOOTH toward the neighbours' mean; FLATTEN toward the area plane; CLAY toward that plane raised, from below only; CREASE sinks (invert: raises) and pinches toward the dab; GRAB moves what is within the radius of the first point by last - first (strength not applied); SNAKE_HOOK does that segment by segment, re-picking round the moved point, so a region is pulled out along the path. BOUNDARY (2026-10-06) acts on the open boundary nearest the dab and the vertices within radius of it along the edges: boundary_deform BEND (default; 90 degrees at strength 1 about the region's far edge), EXPAND, INFLATE, GRAB or SMOOTH. stabilize (world length) trails the dabs on a string. dyntopo {detailSize} (world) triangulates under the brush and splits every edge there longer than detailSize first (never collapses). multires_level sculpts the Multires modifier's top level (adding levels up to it) and writes it with Blender's reshape - the base mesh stays. symmetry mirrors across the object's own axes; mask {vertexGroup, faceSets [ids]} weights; shape_key writes the stroke into that key (required on a mesh with keys). Reply: dabs, verticesMoved, maxDisplacement, boxBefore, boxAfter, and dyntopo / multires counts. Measured: a DRAW dab at a 2 m grid's centre, radius 0.5, strength 1, raises the centre 0.125 and nothing beyond 0.5. Refused before any write: a level below the Multires top level, dyntopo with a shape key or Multires, a face set the mesh lacks, BOUNDARY with no open boundary near, an unknown brush or falloff, radius 0, strength outside 0-1, an empty path, GRAB with one point, an unknown mask group or shape key, a non-uniform scale, a stroke that reaches no vertex. CLOTH (2026-10-06) is NATIVE mesh-space cloth, not Blender's cloth brush (its stroke and cloth_filter do not run headless): per dab the vertices under it take cloth_deform DRAG (default, along the path), GRAB (first point to last), PUSH, PINCH_POINT, INFLATE or EXPAND (rest lengths grow) and are held by their weight while every edge within cloth_area x radius (default 2.5) is pulled back to its rest length; outside, and where the mask is 0, vertices are pinned - so the cloth drags and folds instead of stretching. deform_target CLOTH_SIM on the other brushes lets the area round what the brush moved follow as cloth (GEOMETRY, the default, does not).

1.3 brushes (2026-10-19), with w = falloff x strength x mask weight: CLAY_STRIPS toward CLAY's raised plane from both sides (it fills and cuts); SCRAPE toward the area plane from above only, FILL from below only (invert swaps them); PINCH toward the dab in the surface's plane by w / 2 (invert: away); LAYER out to ONE height - 0.25 x radius x strength x falloff above where each vertex began - however many dabs pass; BLOB along each normal by 0.25 x radius x w and drawn toward the dab by w / 4; DRAW_SHARP along each vertex's normal at the stroke's start with the falloff squared; NUDGE pushes along each segment in the surface's plane (two points at least); ELASTIC moves every vertex by (last - first) x strength / (1 + (d / radius)^2)^1.5 from the first point - no hard edge; POSE takes path [pivot, from, to] and turns the part past the pivot (within |from - pivot| + radius) by the rotation from from to to, blended over half a radius at the pivot (spacing and stabilize refused with it).
bl_cloth_filter:
Run a cloth filter over a Blender mesh: GRAVITY, INFLATE, EXPAND, PINCH or SCALE with its edge lengths held as cloth, masked vertices pinned, colliders pushed out of. Native mesh-space cloth, not Blender's filter. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.

WHY NATIVE (probed 2026-10-06): Blender's sculpt.cloth_filter answers PASS_THROUGH headless and moves nothing (4.2.23, 5.2.2), and sculpt.mesh_filter segfaults both. Per step every free vertex moves by strength x the mean edge length - GRAVITY along direction (world, default [0,0,-1]), INFLATE along its normal, PINCH toward center (world, default the origin) - or EXPAND grows every rest length 5 % x strength (SCALE also moves the vertices out from center); then position-based constraints pull each edge back to its rest length (40 passes a step, 200 after the last) and a vertex inside a collider (or nearer than collision_offset, default 0.005) goes to its surface, its slide cut by friction (0-1, default 0.8). steps default 20 (1-500). mask {vertexGroup, faceSets [ids]} - weight 0 pins. Reply: verticesMoved, maxDisplacement, strain before/after, collisionPushes, the box before and after; dry_run writes nothing. Refused, nothing changed: shape keys, a mask holding nothing, the object as its own collider, strength outside 0-10, steps outside 1-500, a zero direction.
bl_merge_vertices: Merge chosen Blender mesh vertices: all of them into one, each of pairs [[a, b], ...], or those closer than distance among the vertices given. at CENTER (default), FIRST or LAST says where a merged vertex lands. WHY: welding chosen vertices - a collar defect closed by merging two vertices at their centre, straggler vertices after a merge by distance, seams welded pair by pair - was raw Python; bl_clean_mesh merge_distance welds the whole mesh. vertices alone collapse into ONE vertex; pairs [[a, b], ...] merge each pair (a vertex may be in one pair only); vertices with distance merge, among those vertices only, every two closer than distance (mesh units) - a weld kept to a seam. at CENTER (default: the mean), FIRST or LAST (the first or last vertex named; for a pair a or b); a merge by distance keeps Blender's choice and takes no at. Faces that collapse are removed (four inner vertices of a 3x3 sheet merged into one take the middle face with them). The reply names each merged vertex and where it landed. Refused: vertices with pairs, distance with pairs, at with distance, a distance not above 0, fewer than two vertices, a vertex in two pairs, and a distance that merges nothing. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked first; a mesh with shape keys is refused. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1.
bl_add_control_rig: Add FK and IK control bones over an existing Blender deform skeleton, its names kept: per limb an FK copy, an IK copy with target and pole, two Copy Transforms on each deform bone and a driven FK/IK switch property. Reports the controls, constraints, switches and how far IK sits from the rest. preset LIMBS_FK_IK finds the engine's limbs (upperarm/lowerarm/hand, thigh/calf/foot, _l and _r), or chains [{name, bones [upper, lower, end], default FK|IK}]. Per limb: FK_ and IK_ copies of the three bones (not deforming), an IK constraint on the IK lower bone (chain 2) aimed at IK_<chain>_target (a copy of the end bone, parented to target_parent, default 'root' when there is one) with a pole IK_<chain>_pole in front of the middle joint and the pole angle computed from the rest pose; on each deform bone a Copy Transforms from its FK copy, then one from its IK copy whose influence a driver reads off the object property <switch_property>_<chain> (ik_fk_arm_l): switch_direction IK_AT_ZERO (default: 0 = IK) or FK_AT_ZERO. Arms start on FK, legs on IK. The deform bones keep their names, parents and rest. A deform bone that already has a constraint, a control name in use or an existing switch property is refused before anything is made. restError is how far the IK chains sit from the deform chains at rest with every switch on IK.
bl_import_scene:
Read OBJ, USD/USDA/USDC/USDZ, Alembic, STL, PLY, an image (as a textured plane) or SVG (as curves) - the other half of bl_export_scene, which on its own left the addon able to WRITE six formats and read three. FBX and glTF are read by bl_import_mesh and are refused here by name: two ops reading one format is how they drift apart, and that one knows things this does not - that useCustomNormals is an FBX option with no glTF equivalent, and that an axis conversion applied to glTF is applied twice because the spec already fixes +Y up. THE POSTCONDITION IS WHAT ARRIVED, by set difference, because every import operator returns FINISHED and none returns the objects it made: a file that parses and holds nothing importable - an animation-only USD, a camera-only export - reports success and adds nothing, and that is refused rather than returned as ok:true. A named collection is resolved BEFORE the import, so a bad name cannot leave objects already in the scene. An SVG comes in as Grease Pencil strokes with svg={'as': 'GREASE_PENCIL'}.

IMAGES AS PLANES, SVG AS CURVES (2026-10-05): a .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .exr, .tif or .tiff arrives as a mesh plane in the image's aspect with a material reading it (Blender's Import Images as Planes operator, core from 4.2; the bundled add-on's before) - image_plane {shader PRINCIPLED | EMISSION | SHADELESS, height (sets sizeMode ABSOLUTE), sizeMode, alignAxis}, each checked against the build's importer; the reply's plane block gives the object, dimensions, aspect and material. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a 200 x 100 PNG is a 2 x 1 plane, 6 x 3 at height 3. The material is named after the image and a second import of it rebuilds that material (the importer's overwrite), so both planes share the last shader. EMISSION is a Principled BSDF whose Emission Color the image drives. A .svg arrives as curves (the bundled SVG importer add-on, enabled for the session when off - svg.addonEnabled says so): svg {scale} scales the curves about the origin; the reply's svg block gives curveObjects, splineCount and world bounds - three paths gave three splines. An SVG comes in as Grease Pencil strokes with svg={'as': 'GREASE_PENCIL'}.

BVH (1.3): a .bvh makes an armature with its action through the bundled io_anim_bvh (enabled for the session when off); bvh {rotateMode, scale, frameStart, useFpsScale, updateSceneFps, updateSceneDuration, cyclic}. Reply: armature, bones, action, frameRange, sceneFps, fileInfo (joints, frames, frame time read from the file).
bl_assign_node_group:
Attach a Blender geometry node group to an object as a Nodes modifier and set its exposed inputs. The modifier addresses inputs by IDENTIFIER (Socket_2), not by name, which is the most confusing thing about driving geometry nodes from script - this resolves names to identifiers for you and reports anything it could not place. A DATABLOCK INPUT TAKES A NAME: an Object, Collection, Material or Image socket is resolved from the name you pass, because assigning the raw string is ACCEPTED by Blender, stored, and then ignored - the modifier reads an empty socket and the effect silently does nothing. REUSE IS THE DEFAULT: calling this twice for the same object and group used to stack a second modifier, so an assign-look-adjust loop tripled the stack invisibly. It now updates the modifier already holding that group and reports reused:true; pass reuse:false to force a second instance deliberately. A DIFFERENT group always gets its own modifier. output_attributes {output name: attribute name} writes a field output out as a named attribute on the evaluated geometry (a mask a shader reads): mod.properties.outputs on 5.2, '<identifier>_attribute_name' before. The Geometry output and an unknown name are refused before the modifier is made. AN INPUT FED BY AN ATTRIBUTE (2026-10-05): inputs {socket: {attribute: name}} switches a field input to read a named attribute - a vertex group as a density mask - and inputsApplied answers {attribute: name}: mod.properties.inputs.<id>.type ATTRIBUTE and attribute_name on 5.2, the '<id>_use_attribute' and '<id>_attribute_name' properties before (a Boolean on 4.4.0 and 5.0.1, an int on 4.2.23). Measured on all four: an Offset fed by a vertex group lifts each vertex by its weight, and moves when the weights do. A plain value puts the input back on its value. Geometry, datablock and single-value inputs cannot read an attribute and are refused in inputsRefused. A GROUP FROM AN ASSET LIBRARY (2026-10-06): library DEFAULT (the assets this Blender ships - Scatter on Surface from 5.0, Smooth by Angle on 4.2-4.4, the hair groups on every build), an asset library's name from the preferences, or a folder or .blend path - the asset-marked geometry group named `group` is found, appended (a copy appended earlier from the same file is reused) and attached; a name the library lacks is refused with what it holds, and a name it holds only as a shader or compositing group is refused saying so. The reply's asset names the file and exposedInputs lists every input with its identifier. Inputs are keyed by name or by identifier; a name two inputs share (Scatter on Surface has two 'Randomize Scale') is refused naming both identifiers. A Menu input takes its item's name on every build (an int property on 5.0, an enum on 5.2).

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): an EMPTY takes a geometry-nodes modifier on 5.2 only; 3.6-5.0 return no modifier and the call is refused saying so.
bl_run_node_tool:
Run a geometry-nodes node TOOL (a group marked with bl_create_node_group tool) once on a mesh, curves or points object, with its inputs by name or identifier; mode EDIT runs on the edit-mode selection. Replies counts before and after.

WHY (2026-10-07): nothing ran a node tool and nothing marked a group as one. A tool changes the object's own geometry once, the way its menu entry does, instead of living on the modifier stack. tool is the group's name; with library (DEFAULT, an asset library's name, or a folder or .blend path - as bl_assign_node_group) the asset is appended first. inputs {name or identifier: value}, a menu by its item's name, each checked before anything runs; they are NOT kept - the group's own defaults are as they were afterwards. mode OBJECT or EDIT (default the object's own); the object is back in the mode it started in, and the scene's active object is put back.

THE ROUTE DEPENDS ON THE BUILD, measured on all five: 3.6 has no node tools (refused naming 4.0). 4.2, 4.4 and 5.0 run Blender's geometry.execute_node_group, with the inputs as temporary interface defaults (its operator takes none) and, in EDIT mode, a 3D view in the context (without one it finds no object and changes nothing). 5.1+ has no execute_node_group - each tool registers its own operator, and only a GUI session's event loop registers it - so there the group is applied as a Nodes modifier, first in the stack, with its Tool Selection reading the edit-mode vertex selection through a temporary attribute that is removed after; any other tool-only node (Set Selection, Active Element, Face Set, 3D Cursor, Mouse Position, Viewport Transform) is refused there by name. The reply names the route.

REFUSED, NOTHING run: a group not marked as a tool (the tool groups in the file are listed), a tool not made for this mode or object type, a tool that reads the selection run in OBJECT mode (Blender would hand it every element as selected), an unknown input, a value of the wrong kind, an object whose data another object shares (5.1+ route), another object in edit mode (4.x-5.0 EDIT runs on every object being edited). Reply: route, readsSelection, inputsApplied, countsBefore / countsAfter (vertices, edges, faces; points and curves for curves and point clouds), countsChanged.
bl_set_material_texture:
Put an IMAGE from disk into a Blender material - the write half of what bl_describe_material has always been able to read. Nothing else in the addon could do it: bpy.data.images.load appears once, in the world/HDRI path, so a material could be given numbers and never a map. `input` takes any bl_set_material_properties name plus 'normal' and 'displacement'. TWO TRAPS ARE HANDLED RATHER THAN LEFT TO THE CALLER. Colour space is chosen per input - sRGB for base_color and emissive, Non-Color for everything else - because Blender decodes from the IMAGE's setting, not from where it is plugged in, so a roughness map loaded as sRGB comes back through the transfer curve and every value the shader reads is wrong while looking plausible. And 'normal' is wired through a Normal Map node, because the Principled Normal socket takes a VECTOR and a tangent-space map is RGB; linking the image straight in is the usual mistake and reads as correct in every field of every response. A MISSING FILE IS REFUSED BEFORE ANYTHING IS CREATED: Blender would make the datablock anyway and render it MAGENTA, which is loud on screen and completely silent to anything reading a response. The link is verified off the socket afterwards, and the nodes are removed again if Blender rejected it. TILING is scale / offset (a number, or [u, v]) and rotation in DEGREES, through a Mapping node - per-texture and non-destructive, where the only alternative was bl_uv_unwrap's uv_transform, which scales the MESH's UVs and is therefore shared by every texture on the object and undone by the next unwrap. The addon has accepted these three since the day the Mapping support landed and no tool sent them, so the capability existed and was unreachable. For a pattern rather than a file, see bl_add_procedural_texture, which shares this vocabulary. A uvMap naming a UV layer the material's meshes lack is accepted and answered with uvMapNote: a UV Map node naming a missing layer renders a fixed fallback, not the active layer (measured on 3.6-5.2). ANY SOCKET OF THE TREE: to_node + to_socket instead of input wires the image into any node's input (a node name, or a node type such as colorRamp, mapRange, mix, math, invert or displacement to create one), link=false leaves the node free, node_name names the Image Texture node or reuses one to swap its image, invert=true puts an Invert node on the way, and from_socket takes Alpha. alpha_mode sets the image's alpha: STRAIGHT, PREMULTIPLIED (Blender's PREMUL), CHANNEL_PACKED or NONE, from this build's list - premultiplied keeps a logo's outline from showing. Written on the image, last, so a refused call leaves it as it was; alphaMode and alphaModeBefore come back. DISPLACEMENT (2026-10-06): input 'displacement' wires the image (Non-Color) into a Displacement node's Height and that node into the active Material Output's Displacement - not into Normal. displacement_scale and midlevel set the node. The reply names displacementMethod: BUMP only shades; bl_set_material_settings displacement_method BOTH moves the surface, on a mesh with enough faces. input 'subsurfaceWeight' takes a mask. normal_convention OPENGL | DIRECTX (2026-10-06), normal input only: a DirectX (Unreal) map read with green flipped - the Normal Map node's own switch on 5.2+, a 1 - G step before it earlier (normalConventionRoute says which).

RULE - PAINTED LAYERS (2026-10-06). The neutral first paint depends on the layer's role: a layer mixed over another starts at alpha 0, a roughness layer starts white at alpha 1, a mask attribute starts white and is painted black. Combining: multiply two colour layers through a Mix (Multiply) with an alpha as the factor, or mask whole materials with painted alpha images driving Mix Shader nodes - the second only when the layer must change roughness or metalness too.
bl_set_material_volume:
Give a Blender material a VOLUME shader - smoke, fire, fog - as a Principled Volume on its output's Volume socket. bl_add_fluid could build a smoke or fire simulation and nothing could make it appear, because every other material op writes the Principled BSDF on Surface. MEASURED on 3.6, 4.2, 4.4, 5.0 and 5.2: a GAS domain with no material renders as a SOLID BOX in EEVEE and as NOTHING in Cycles, and a Principled Volume with no surface shader renders the rising smoke in both. SURFACE IS EXPLICIT (keep | disconnect, default keep): a surface shader renders in front of the volume inside the mesh - bl_create_material's Principled BSDF left on Surface hid the smoke completely in both engines - so pass surface='disconnect' for smoke, fire or fog, and keep it only for a surface meant to be seen, like glass around the volume; surfaceNote says whenever a surface is still linked. density_attribute left out is left as it is - a new Principled Volume starts at Blender's 'density', which is what a smoke domain writes; an empty one measured as a filled box in EEVEE and nothing in Cycles, and densityAttributeNote says so when a GAS domain (listed in gasDomains) uses the material. A Principled Volume already on the output is edited in place; any other node there - Volume Scatter, a Mix Shader - is refused by name. Every value validates before anything is created or written. remove=True unlinks the volume shader from the output and deletes the node unless another node reads it (keptBecauseReadBy names them); it takes no other setting. Put the material on the domain with bl_set_material_slots (allow_resize=True when the mesh has no slots yet).

Every value is optional (default None: left as the node has it; a new Principled Volume starts at Blender's own defaults). color, absorption_color, emission_color and blackbody_tint take [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] (alpha 1 when omitted): color is the scattering colour, absorption_color the absorbed colour. anisotropy is -1 (scatters back) to 1 (forward). emission_strength, blackbody_intensity and temperature (kelvin) are >= 0, as is density. density_attribute, color_attribute and temperature_attribute are grid attribute names as strings ("" for none) written to the node's Density, Color and Temperature Attribute inputs. The volume goes on the ACTIVE Material Output (else the first). remove unlinks the Principled Volume and deletes it only when no other node reads it.

OUT: the material summary (name, users, useNodes, blendMethod, settings, viewport and its shading read), then volumeNode, createdVolumeNode, applied (keys written), before (values before, null if new), volume (every value read back; a linked input as {linkedFrom}), volumeLinked, surfaceLinked, surfaceShaders, surfaceDisconnected, gasDomains, and surfaceNote, densityAttributeNote, note, outputNote when they apply. With remove: removed, deleted, keptBecauseReadBy, before, volumeLinked.

Refused before anything is written: an unknown key; no such material; no node tree; surface other than keep or disconnect; a bad value (wrong type, wrong component count, negative, anisotropy out of range); no Material Output with a Volume socket; a node other than a Principled Volume already on Volume; remove with any other setting, or with no volume shader present; a value for an input that is linked to another node.
bl_import_pbr_texture_set:
Wire a folder of PBR maps into one Blender material in one call, each found by its file name and set in the colour space it needs: base colour, normal, roughness, metallic, displacement, AO, opacity, emission, subsurface. Replies what was wired and every file skipped, with why.

WHY (2026-10-05): bl_set_material_texture wires one map a call and could not do ambient occlusion, displacement or subsurface, so a downloaded set was six calls and raw-Python steps. MAPS ARE FOUND BY THE WORDS IN THEIR NAMES, CamelCase or separated: basecolor / albedo / diffuse / color, normal / nrm, roughness / rough, metallic / metal, displacement / height, ao / occlusion, opacity / alpha, emission, subsurface / sss. Only base colour and emission are sRGB; every other map is Non-Color. normal goes through a Normal Map node; displacement through a Displacement node into the Material Output's Displacement (Cycles shades it as bump unless the material's displacement method moves the surface - the reply says which); ao is MULTIPLIED into the base colour by a Mix node (a free node when there is no base colour); subsurface drives the Principled subsurface weight. ONE FILE PER MAP: several candidates (a 4K and an 8K roughness, an OpenGL and a DirectX normal) choose by resolution ("4K"), then an OpenGL normal over a DirectX one (Blender reads OpenGL green; a DirectX map chosen anyway is named in notes), then name, and every file not used is listed in skipped with the reason - as is an image whose name carries no map word. UDIM: a name holding 1001-2000 is a tile; it loads as ONE image by default (measured on 4.2.23-5.2.2: bpy's image load does not detect UDIM sets) and is named in udimFiles; udim true makes it a TILED image, which finds the set's tiles. include limits the kinds; mapping {scale, offset} drives every image through one shared Mapping node. Refused before any node is made: no such folder or material, a folder with no map in it, an unknown kind, an included kind with no file, a mapping that is not {scale, offset}; a failure while wiring removes everything the call made.
bl_add_shape_key: Add a Blender shape key - the other thing several ops consumed and nothing produced. bl_set_shape_key drives a key's value and bl_list_shape_keys reports them; nothing could CREATE one, so a mesh without shape keys could never be given any. THE FIRST KEY IS THE BASIS AND IT IS NOT A SHAPE: Blender makes the first key added to a mesh the rest position and stores every later key RELATIVE to it (verified on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.0), so a caller adding one key to a bare mesh gets something that holds the shape the mesh already has and moves nothing. basisCreated reports that separately rather than letting it look like the key you asked for. from_mix captures the current evaluated mix instead of the rest shape - how a corrective key is made - and is OFF by default, because a key silently capturing whatever the sliders happened to be set to is a surprise rather than a convenience. from_object is Join as Shapes: the key takes another mesh's evaluated vertex positions (same vertex count, refused otherwise), carried from that object's world space into this one's; a mesh with no keys gets a Basis first so the named key is the shape. maxOffsetFromBasis says how far it moves. vertex_group and relative_key as bl_set_shape_key: a key whose points all move moves only the group's vertices.
bl_add_soft_body:
Add a SOFT BODY simulation to a Blender mesh - the deformable one, between cloth and a rigid body: jelly, a beanbag, a sagging cable, flesh over a rig. GOAL IS ON BY DEFAULT AND IT IS WHY NOTHING MOVES: Blender ships use_goal=True with goal_default=0.7, which pins every vertex toward its ORIGINAL position, so a soft body added with defaults sags a little and stops - and reads as a simulation that does not work. That default is NOT overridden, because silently inverting what the engine chose is worse than reporting it; the response says useGoal and carries a goalNote explaining it. Pass use_goal=false for a free-falling body, or lower goal_default to loosen the pin. TO PIN PART OF THE MESH - a jelly's base on its plate, a tail's root - pass goal_vertex_group (an existing vertex group, made with bl_set_vertex_weights): each vertex's goal becomes its weight there TIMES goal_default, mapped into goal_min..goal_max, so weight-1 vertices hold at goal_default's strength and weight-0 ones move; goal_friction damps them. goal_default=0 beside a group is refused, since every weight would multiply to zero and pin nothing. Without it every vertex shares one goal and the body sways as one lump. An unknown group, a group beside use_goal=false, or goal_min above goal_max is refused with nothing added. Settings live on the OBJECT (object.soft_body), not on the modifier as cloth's do, which is the trap that makes a value look like it landed when it did not - this writes and reads back the same place. Refused on a mesh under 16 vertices, since a soft body deforms the geometry it is given and a quad has nothing to bend, and refused on an object that already has one, because a second solver does not make a stronger simulation, it makes two fighting over the same vertices. `gravity` is a WEIGHT on the scene's gravity, not an acceleration - 1.0 normal, 0.0 floats. Every attribute this writes was verified present on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17 LTS, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1, so there is nothing version-gated here. Like any simulation it is stepped forward: bake_physics before jumping to a late frame.

Parameters (all default None in the wrapper; a key left out keeps the value Blender gives a new soft body, and every value is written to object.soft_body): mass (float, the mass of each vertex), friction (float, the general media friction on vertex movement), speed (float, the simulation speed scale), goal_spring (float, the goal spring stiffness), pull (float, edge spring stiffness when stretched), push (float, edge spring stiffness when compressed), use_edges (bool, use the mesh's edges as springs) and self_collision (bool, collide the body with itself). Each float must be finite; a text boolean must be one of 1/true/yes/on or 0/false/no/off. These are read and checked before the modifier is added.

A goal group does not replace goal_default: each vertex's goal is its weight TIMES goal_default, mapped into goal_min..goal_max, so a weight-1 vertex holds at goal_min + goal_default x (goal_max - goal_min) and weight-0 vertices move freely.

OUT: object, modifier, mass, friction, speed, pull, push, bend, useGoal, goalDefault, goalSpring, goalVertexGroup, goalMin, goalMax, goalFriction, useEdges, selfCollision, gravityWeight, vertices, bakeNote, plus goalVertexGroupNonZero (the vertices with a non-zero weight in the group) when a goal group was given, and goalNote whenever the goal is on. Every value is read back from object.soft_body.

Refused with nothing added: an object that does not exist, is not a MESH or is not in Object mode; a mesh under 16 vertices; an object that already has a soft body modifier; a goal_vertex_group the object lacks (the refusal lists its groups); a goal group beside use_goal=false; goal_default 0 beside a goal group (it pins nothing); goal_min above goal_max; a non-finite or non-numeric number or an unknown boolean word. gravityWeight is refused as an input key, with a note to send gravity.
bl_mirror_shape_key: Mirror Blender shape keys across an axis onto new keys named for the other side (smile_L -> smile_R, or new_name): each offset goes to the mirrored vertex. Reports the vertex pairs matched and the unmatched vertices; drivers are not carried. One of key, keys or prefix (the basis never). Each key's offsets from the basis go to the mirrored vertex - the nearest basis vertex to the mirrored position within tolerance (1e-4) - with the axis (X default) component negated. The new key's name swaps the side at the end (pairs, default _l/_r, _L/_R, .l/.r, .L/.R, Left/Right), or is new_name for one key; an existing key of that name is refused unless overwrite. A new key starts at value 0. Reply: pairsMatched, unmatchedVertices with their indices, matchedShare, and a symmetryWarning under 100 percent.
bl_create_curve:
Create a Blender curve - a path to follow, a profile to bevel, or a cable. bl_add_constraint accepts FOLLOW_PATH and nothing could make the one object it requires.
