THE SPLINE TYPE DECIDES WHAT THE POINTS MEAN: POLY and NURBS points live in spline.points with a 4th weight component while BEZIER points live in spline.bezier_points with handles - different collections with different lengths, so building into the wrong one produces a curve with no points and no error, and the point count is checked afterwards. use_path defaults ON because a Follow Path constraint evaluates to NOTHING without it while the constraint and the curve both read back perfectly. radii is one radius per point, scaling the bevel there: a stem, branch, horn or cable that TAPERS is radii [1.0, ..., 0.1] (read back as `radii`; bl_mesh_stats measures the tube it builds). Every coordinate and radius must be a finite number. bevel_object and taper_object (a CURVE object's name) give the new curve a cross-section (bevel mode OBJECT) and a taper; refused before anything is made when the name is not a curve.

PATH ANIMATION (measured 2026-10-05). Curve.path_duration defaults to 100 frames, use_path_follow to off and eval_time to 0.0 on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1. bl_set_keyframe with target data reaches both eval_time and path_duration on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1 (keys 0 at frame 1 and 100 at frame 96 on eval_time made one curve). An object following the path (Follow Path) travels the whole path when eval_time runs 0 to the path's own duration - 100 unless written - so a 96-frame shot keys eval_time to 100 at frame 96, or sets path_duration to 96 first.
bl_create_curves:
Create a Blender CURVES object (the hair/curves type a geometry node group fills; not bl_create_curve's legacy CURVE). With surface and count it grows real guide curves on a mesh. With surface_deform it is Blender's own Empty Hair, and preset 'fur' is its Quick Fur. Call mif_help("bl_create_curves") first.

Create a Blender CURVES object - the modern hair/curves type, driven by geometry nodes. NOT bl_create_curve, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT OBJECT TYPE: that one makes a legacy CURVE - a Bezier or NURBS path with control points you set directly, the thing you extrude a profile along. This makes the CURVES type, which holds no editable control points of its own and is filled by a geometry node group. The one-letter difference is Blender's naming, not ours. WITHOUT surface IT ARRIVES EMPTY AND THAT IS THE OBJECT TYPE, not a failure: the response says pointCount 0 and isEmpty true outright, because a caller believing an object is populated when nothing has filled it is the exact failure this addon refuses elsewhere. Fill it with bl_create_node_group plus bl_assign_node_group, and note that the group's OUTPUT must be CURVE geometry - a mesh-outputting group evaluates without error and lands nothing on a CURVES object. WHY THIS TYPE AND NOT THE OTHER SIX unbuilt ones: measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1, an empty one accepts a node group and evaluates to real geometry, and the ops that fill it were already here. A metaball, a volume and a grease pencil have no such op, so they would be empty containers with no way to fill them. bl_object_info reports both the stored and the evaluated counts, which is how you tell 'nothing has filled this' from 'the group generated it'.

GUIDES ON A SURFACE (2026-10-06): surface (a mesh) parents the object to it at its origin - the curves live in its space, so location, rotation and scale are refused with it - and sets Curves.surface and surface_uv_map (uv_map, default the surface's active UV map). count (0-100000; 0 leaves an empty groom on the surface) guides are rooted by face area, times density_group's weight (a vertex group on the surface, 0-1) when given, from seed (the same seed, the same roots); each runs length world meters (default 0.1, whatever the surface's scale) straight along direction - NORMAL (the face's, default), UP (world +Z) or CUSTOM with custom_direction [x, y, z] - in points_per_curve points (2-128, default 8). Written through the Curves datablock's own add-curves method (Blender 4.2 and later; an older build is refused by name), with surface_uv_coordinate (FLOAT2 per curve) the surface's UV at each root, which a shader reads so a painted surface colors the groom. The reply adds curveCount, pointCount, surface, surfaceUvMap, surfaceUvAttribute, lengthM, direction, densityGroup, seed and parent; bl_object_info's generated.stored counts the guides. Refused before anything is created: a guide key without surface, a missing or non-mesh surface or one with no faces, an unknown UV map or vertex group, CUSTOM without custom_direction (or custom_direction without CUSTOM), a zero direction, points_per_curve outside 2-128, length outside (0, 10] m, count outside 0-100000; a density group weighing 0 on every face is refused and the object removed.

EMPTY HAIR AND QUICK FUR (2026-10-06), both run Blender's own operator on the surface and adopt what it makes under your name. surface_deform (with surface) is object.curves_empty_hair_add: parented to the surface, Curves.surface and surface_uv_map set, and the build's deform modifier - measured "Surface Deform" on 3.6-5.0, "Hair Dynamics" on 5.2, which also adds "Capture Rest Geometry" to the SURFACE (surfaceModifiersAdded names it). count and the other guide keys then write guides into it as without it (4.2 and later). The reply lists deformModifiers. preset 'fur' is object.quick_fur: density LOW (1000 curves) | MEDIUM (default, 10000) | HIGH (100000) over the whole surface, length (default 0.1 m), radius (default 0.001 m), view_percentage (0-1), apply_hair_guides, use_noise, use_frizz (default true). It needs a UV map on the surface - refused without one, because Quick Fur skips such a mesh, reports success and leaves an orphan material - and does not take count, uv_map, direction or surface_deform. The reply gives curveCount (the stored guides, 11-17 at LOW), evaluatedCurveCount (what the modifiers interpolate, 997-1124 at LOW on all five builds), the modifier stack and the material it made.
bl_create_empty:
Create a Blender Empty - the most-used object in Blender that this addon could not make. An Empty is what a Track To or Copy Location constraint points AT, what a rig is controlled by, what a camera is aimed at, and what objects are parented to for one shared pivot. bl_add_constraint and bl_aim_object both take a target and neither could create the object people overwhelmingly use as one, so a constraint could only be set up against something that already existed. It has no geometry and renders nothing; display_size is viewport only. IMAGE BACKDROPS (2026-10-05): image {file | name} makes an IMAGE empty holding it, with opacity (0-1), depth and side (Blender's image-empty choices; a wrong one is refused with the list), show_perspective, show_orthographic, offset [x, y] and selectable; images [{view FRONT | BACK | LEFT | RIGHT | TOP | BOTTOM, file | name, scaleToCube, location} - keys as written] places one per entry, rotated to face that numpad view, the shared settings on all - front, side, top and back drawings in one call; scaleToCube sizes the longer side to 2 (the default cube). bl_object_info's empty.image reads every setting back. A reference image on an empty, compared in viewport captures - not the camera's background images (declined 2026-09-03).

Parameters: rotation (default None = [0, 0, 0]) is Euler XYZ in RADIANS, written straight to rotation_euler; it takes [x, y, z] or a partial {x, y, z} dict (missing axes are 0, a dict naming none of them is refused), like location. display_type (str, default None) is one of PLAIN_AXES, ARROWS, SINGLE_ARROW, CIRCLE, CUBE, SPHERE, CONE, IMAGE, case-insensitive; it defaults to PLAIN_AXES, or IMAGE when image is given (any other type with image is refused). collection (str, default None) links the new Empty into that existing collection instead of the scene's root collection. name defaults to "Empty" (with images, to "Reference", and each empty is named <name>_<View>, e.g. Reference_Front). With images, location and rotation for the set are refused - each entry carries its own location and its view sets the rotation; display_size still applies to entries without scaleToCube.

OUT: ok, name, type "EMPTY", collection, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, location, rotation, displayType, displaySize, note. With images: created [{ok, name, type, collection, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, location, rotation, view, image, displaySize}], count, note.

Refusals, each before anything is made ("NOTHING was created."): a display_type Blender does not offer (the message lists them); image with a non-IMAGE display_type; opacity, depth, side, show_perspective, show_orthographic, offset or selectable without image or images; image and images together; images empty or not a list, an entry with other keys, a view outside FRONT, BACK, LEFT, RIGHT, TOP, BOTTOM, or not exactly one of file and name; location or rotation beside images; a collection that does not exist; a malformed or non-finite vector; any unknown key.
bl_create_force_field:
Create a Blender FORCE FIELD that simulations respond to - type WIND, TURBULENCE, VORTEX, FORCE, DRAG, MAGNET, HARMONIC, CHARGE, LENNARDJ, TEXTURE, GUIDE, BOID or FLUID_FLOW. bl_add_cloth, bl_add_soft_body and bl_set_particles all read and write effectorWeights, which scales how much the fields in a scene affect that sim; with no field present the only effector is gravity, so those were dials on something that could not exist. type: WIND | TURBULENCE | VORTEX | FORCE | DRAG | MAGNET | HARMONIC | CHARGE | LENNARDJ | TEXTURE | GUIDE | BOID | FLUID_FLOW - refused by name if the running Blender does not offer it, and the list in the refusal is read off that Blender rather than quoted, so it cannot go stale. NEGATIVE STRENGTH PULLS instead of pushing, which is how you make a drain or an attractor out of a WIND or FORCE field. `max_distance` sets the flag AND the number together: Blender ignores distance_max unless use_max_distance is on, so setting the number alone reads back as the value you asked for and changes nothing. The object is created with bpy.data and a name you choose, then made a field - the obvious route, bpy.ops.object.effector_add, works but names the object after its type and drops it at the 3D cursor, so your name and location would only be suggestions. `shape`: POINT | LINE | PLANE. WIND and VORTEX DEFAULT TO PLANE, and a PLANE field reaches everything on either side of its own plane - max_distance is measured perpendicular to it, so it never stops at the sides and fields placed in a row overlap completely; the response carries a shapeNote saying so. Pass shape POINT for a field that ends in every direction. SURFACE and POINTS are refused: they take their shape from a mesh, and this makes an empty. Verified on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17 LTS, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1: all four attach the field, take every setting, and offer the same 14 types. A field affects a simulation only as far as that simulation's effector weights allow. Rigid bodies listen too, through the rigid body world's weights - but a simulation baked BEFORE the field existed ignores it, so bake with bl_bake_physics rebake=True after adding one.

rotation [x, y, z] (list, default None: [0, 0, 0]) is the empty's Euler rotation in radians; location and rotation also take {x, y, z} with any subset of the axes. collection (str, default None) links the new empty into that existing collection instead of the scene's root collection. strength (float, default None: Blender's default for the type) is the force; negative pulls. flow (float, default None) is the field's flow value; WIND and FLUID_FLOW first get flow 1.0 (and inflow 1.0, WIND also wind_factor 1.0) as type defaults, which an explicit flow overrides. noise (float, default None) is the field's noise amount. seed (int, default None) is the noise seed; a fraction is refused. falloff_power (float, default None) shapes how the force fades with distance. Blender's own defaults stand for anything omitted; TEXTURE also gets size and rest_length 1.0.

OUT: ok, name, type 'EMPTY', collection, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, location, rotation, fieldType, shape, typeDefaultsApplied (the per-type values written, or null), strength, flow, noise, seed, falloffPower, useMaxDistance, maxDistance (all read back off the field), note, and shapeNote when the shape is PLANE.

Refused before anything is created (NOTHING was created): a malformed location or rotation; an unknown key (object, target and radius are named with what to use instead); a type or shape the running Blender does not offer, with its list; shape SURFACE or POINTS; a non-number strength, flow, noise, falloff_power or max_distance, or a non-whole seed; a collection that does not exist. If Blender cannot attach the field to the new empty, the empty is removed and the refusal says NOTHING was left behind.
bl_set_curve: Write Blender curve data settings - bevel_mode, bevel_object, taper_object, fill_mode, resolution_u, bevel_resolution, bevel_depth, extrude, offset - on one curve, a list or a collection at once. Values before and after; triangles adds the evaluated triangle count. The curve counterpart of bl_set_camera and bl_set_light. One of object, objects or collection (every CURVE object in it). bevel_mode ROUND | OBJECT | PROFILE, taper_radius_mode and fill_mode are checked against this build's own enums; bevel_object and taper_object name a CURVE object (an empty string clears it) and are refused when missing, not a curve, or one of the curves being set; resolution_u and bevel_resolution are 1-64. Every value is checked before anything is written. Objects sharing one curve datablock are named in sharedDataNote. triangles true counts the evaluated mesh's triangles before and after - lowering the resolution before converting cards to meshes is where the polygons go.
bl_physics_info:
What the Blender physics setup IS - the read half of a family that could only write. bl_add_rigid_body, bl_add_cloth, bl_add_collision and bl_bake_physics all set and nothing reported what they had set; bl_scene_info carries no physics at all, and a rigid body is NOT a modifier (it lives on obj.rigid_body) so bl_list_modifiers cannot see it either. Catches the inert state that settings cannot reveal: an object can carry a fully configured rigid body - mass, friction, shape, all reading back perfectly - and never simulate, because the sim only acts on objects in the RigidBodyWorld's COLLECTION, so it hangs in the air. Reported as inSimulation. Also flags unbaked caches (a late frame shows the REST state and a render of it is simply wrong) and BAKED-BUT-SHORT ones, where a bake made before the frame range was extended stays valid while the frames past its end silently fall back. A geometry-nodes modifier whose group holds a simulation zone (the 5.2 node cloth among them) is listed under nodeSimulations: modifier, group, bake target and the exposed inputs with the identifiers the modifier is keyed by.

COLLIDERS (2026-10-05): `colliders` lists every object in the scene with a Collision modifier, whatever `object` asked: seenBySimulation, visibleGet, hideViewport, hiddenInViewLayer, hideRender and the modifier's showViewport, with `why` when it is not seen and a blocker naming it. Measured on 4.2-5.2 with a cloth dropped on a floor: an eye-hidden (hide_set) or render-hidden collider still stops the cloth, so visibleGet false is not the failure; hide_viewport, a collection hidden in viewports or excluded from the view layer, or the modifier's show_viewport off lets the cloth fall straight through. ignoredBy names a cloth or soft body whose collision collection does not hold the collider.
bl_bake_physics:
Bake Blender's physics point caches so a given frame shows the simulated state rather than the rest state - or one fluid domain stage by stage (stages GUIDES, DATA, NOISE, MESH, PARTICLES; resume; free_stages). BLOCKS for the length of the bake. Reports which caches actually hold frames, because bake_all returns success even when nothing in the scene has a cache to bake. An EXISTING bake is kept (keptExistingBake, staleBakeNote) - pass rebake=true to free and bake again. Before any bake that starts from nothing it rewrites a force-field setting (fieldsRefreshed) and a rigid body world setting (rigidBodyWorldRefreshed): measured, a body added after a bake stayed frozen through a rebake that only freed, and moved once a world setting was written. allBaked says whether every cache ended up baked; `baked` only says bake_all ran. Each Mantaflow domain gets a caches row of kind fluid - cacheType, cacheDirectory, framesOnDisk per subfolder, framesStored, isBaked - read off its cache folder: bake_all simulates a REPLAY cache by stepping frames and bakes nothing for MODULAR or ALL, and fluidNote names a domain with no frames. A liquid's FLIP display system is not listed as a point cache. start/end reach a Mantaflow domain too (its cache_frame_start/end, written only when they differ), and a domain is listed in rangeAppliedTo or rangeNotHeld by the frames its cache folder holds. With clear=true it also empties caches that hold frames WITHOUT a bake - a cloth stepped frame by frame into a disk cache, which the next run replayed - and leaves the scene at their start frame, because going back re-fills them (framesBefore, framesAfter, unbakedFramesFreed, frame, frameBefore).

ONE FLUID DOMAIN, STAGE BY STAGE (2026-10-04). Passing object, stages, resume or free_stages bakes one Mantaflow domain - the named one, or the scene's only one - and nothing else: no point cache is baked. The cache must be MODULAR (bl_set_modifier {cache_type: 'MODULAR'} or bl_add_fluid cache_type). stages [GUIDES, DATA, NOISE, MESH, PARTICLES] run in that order, only the ones asked, each through Blender's own fluid.bake_* operator in this thread (bake_guides included: FINISHED in 0.09-0.25 s on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1). free_stages frees first, then the stages bake. Reply: per stage the operator, seconds, the pause frame, framesOnDisk [first, last, count] of its subfolder (data, noise, mesh, particles, guiding), and resumedFrom; filesOnDisk per subfolder, freed (by which setting, files before and after), the range, timeScale and resolutionMax.

WHAT IS REFUSED, before anything is freed or baked: GUIDES unless use_guide is on with guide_source EFFECTOR (a DOMAIN-source guide follows its parent's data and has nothing of its own); DATA while an effector guide is unbaked, or a DOMAIN guide has no guide_parent (Blender's panel withholds Bake Data then; its operator runs regardless and bakes data that ignores the guide - measured); NOISE, MESH or PARTICLES on a cache with cache_resumable off (the panel withholds them; the operator wrote frames anyway on every build, which the panel does not stand behind) or without baked data; a stage the domain does not have (NOISE needs a GAS domain with use_noise, MESH a LIQUID with use_mesh, PARTICLES a LIQUID with spray, foam or bubbles); a stage that is already baked unless it is freed in the same call or resumed - its operator starts at the pause frame, so on a finished stage it would redo the last frame only; use_adaptive_domain with effector guides; clear or rebake beside stages.

RESUME. resume: true continues a baked stage whose pause frame is before the end, from that frame - the same operator again, as Blender's Resume button does; it needs cache_resumable. With no stages it resumes every stage that can be. Raising end extends a finished bake this way: liquid data baked 1-6, then end 10 with resume, continued from frame 6 to 10 (10 files) and left the mesh at 6 (measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1).

THE PER-STAGE FREE writes one domain setting onto itself, whose RNA update frees that stage's cache synchronously (rna_fluid.cc: noise_strength frees noise, mesh_particle_radius the mesh, sndparticle_potential_min_wavecrest the particles, time_scale the data, guide_parent the guides). Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: each took exactly its own folder to 0 files and its pause frame to 0, and the stage baked again afterwards. Freeing DATA takes noise, mesh and particles with it, and freeing GUIDES takes everything - the sets Blender's own free operators use. Blender's fluid.free_* are not used: headless on 3.6.23 and 4.4.0 they answered FINISHED in 0.0 s and freed nothing (their work is a window-manager job).

RULES WHERE THE WORKFLOWS DISAGREE, and what decides:
(a) Adaptive Domain: on for an unguided gas domain (a 120-division, 3 m box); off for guided sims. Blender removes the panel for effector guides, so a stage bake with use_adaptive_domain and effector guides is refused; with DOMAIN guides the reply carries adaptiveNote, since that case is unmeasured.
(b) Resolution: an unguided domain can be iterated at 64 and raised to 128 or more for the final bake (resolutionNote). With guides, the final resolution is chosen BEFORE the guide bake: writing resolution_max or time_scale after it frees the data and KEEPS the guides (measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1), leaving guides made at the old setting - the reply's guideNote says so. Free GUIDES before changing either.
(c) Domain time scale: 1.0 for a faucet at real scale, 0.5 for a 3 m smoke box or a liquid jet (the default looks too fast at 24 fps), 0.3 for a liquid guided by smoke. A look tied to scene scale and fps: bl_add_fluid time_scale writes it, nothing here changes it, and the reply reports it. bl_set_physics_world time_scale is the rigid body world's, a different setting.
(d) Spray, foam and bubbles: spray only for a faucet or a sink, all three for an open-water splash. Each adds particle work to the PARTICLES stage (its row lists particleKinds); the choice is the caller's (bl_set_modifier use_spray_particles, use_foam_particles, use_bubble_particles).
(e) The cache folder: a domain made in an unsaved file caches in Blender's session temp folder, deleted when Blender closes - the reply carries cacheNote then. A bake meant to survive sets cache_directory first (bl_add_fluid cache_directory), one folder per domain: two domains sharing a folder free each other's frames.

AN OCEAN MODIFIER (2026-10-05): object (and modifier, the Ocean's name) bakes it with object.ocean_bake - disp_####.exr per frame from frame_start to frame_end into the modifier's filepath, foam_####.exr with foam on and normal_####.exr with normals - and waits for the files, which a job thread writes after the operator returns. The row (kind ocean) answers filesWritten, filesExpected, maps, missing and isCached; free=true frees the cache and leaves the files on disk (Blender's own free, measured), counted in filesOnDisk. Set the Ocean's settings first with bl_set_modifier (viewport_resolution, use_foam, foam_layer_name, use_spray, filepath, frame_start, frame_end, bake_foam_fade). HEADLESS: measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2 under the bpy module, the maps are written and is_cached stays false - the job's end step, which sets it and points the modifier at the files, runs on a window-manager timer a background session never ticks - so there the modifier keeps simulating live; cacheNote says so. An Ocean without a filepath is refused, as are toFrame and diskCache on one.

RULE - SIMULATION SCALE (2026-10-06). A cloth scene built at about 5 times real size and one whose collider and garment were scaled up 10 times and applied are both valid; what is not is scaling the objects and leaving the distances. Whatever factor is chosen goes onto the objects (applied) and the same factor onto every distance setting - collision distance, self-collision distance, shrink, thickness. bl_object_info's dimensions before and after the scale are the check, and bl_physics_info reads the distances back.

bake_node (1.3, Blender 4.2+): object + the geometry-nodes Bake node's name or bake id (modifier when two share one) bakes that node alone - bake_mode STILL | ANIMATION, disk_cache, free deletes its bake. Measured: the whole-cache node bake does NOT bake Bake nodes (0 files on 4.4.0 and 5.2.1); 4.2 needs the .blend saved first.
bl_link_group_nodes: Wire one node's output into another's input inside a Blender node group - or, with remove=true, take links OUT. links.new returns a link object even when Blender immediately drops it as invalid (mismatched socket types), so the link is read back and `linked` is a measurement rather than the call's return. A LINK INTO AN INPUT THAT ALREADY HAS ONE REPLACES IT and Blender says nothing: the displaced link comes back in replacedLinks (with replacedNote), in full, so it can be restored; a multi-input socket such as Join Geometry keeps both. remove=true needs to_node plus to_socket and/or from_node (from_socket narrows further), removes every link matching that scope and lists each one in removedLinks - a scope matching nothing is refused rather than reported as a success. Before this a link could only be undone by deleting a node. The `group` argument also addresses trees that are OWNED by something rather than living in bpy.data.node_groups: 'scene:compositor', 'scene:world', 'material:<name>' and 'world:<name>'. That is how a MATERIAL's shader graph is authored. An unpaired zone input (a Simulation, Repeat or For Each input made on its own) is refused: nothing passes through it until it is paired, which bl_add_group_node zone does.
bl_add_group_interface: Expose a value as a group input or output - what turns a Blender node tree into a modifier with sliders on it. socket_type is a NodeSocket id such as NodeSocketFloat. EDIT THE EXISTING SOCKETS: rename {old: new}, move {name: index} and remove [names] act on the in_out side (INPUT by default; index counts that side's sockets, 0 first). A rename and a move keep the socket's identifier, so the modifier's stored value and every link stay - rebuilding a socket gives a new identifier and breaks them. A remove that would cut a link inside the tree is refused unless confirm is true (linksCut says how many went). A name that is missing, or on two sockets of that side, is refused; name, socket_type, default, min and max make a new socket and are refused beside an edit. Reply: the order, and each socket's identifier with its name before and after. default_input (2026-10-06): what an unlinked input reads - INDEX, POSITION, NORMAL, and from 5.2 SCENE_FRAME or SELF_OBJECT - checked against this socket type's list on this build. It is read where the group is a node inside another tree; a Nodes modifier's own input keeps its value.
bl_add_group_node:
Add a node to a Blender node group. `inputs` is {socketName: value} and a name that does not match a real socket is refused with the sockets the node actually has - a value written to a socket that is not there vanishes without a word. A vector or colour value needs ALL its components ([r,g,b] into a colour keeps its alpha) and only finite numbers: until 2026-09-20 a NaN was stored, a long list died as a raw IndexError and a short one was written in part and echoed as applied. bl_set_node_property writes the same inputs on a node that already exists. The `group` argument also addresses trees that are OWNED by something rather than living in bpy.data.node_groups: 'scene:compositor', 'scene:world', 'material:<name>' and 'world:<name>'. That is how a MATERIAL's shader graph is authored - bl_describe_material could read one in full while bl_set_material_properties could write only the Principled BSDF's own sockets, so the addon could describe a graph in detail and not add a node to it. NESTING: pass node_group to make a Group node CONTAIN another tree - without it a Group node points at nothing, has no sockets at all and does nothing, while reporting success. Set it in the same call as `inputs`, because the node has no sockets to write until it holds a tree. A RECURSIVE nest is refused: Blender rejects one SILENTLY, leaving node_tree empty and raising nothing, so the assignment is read back and the node removed rather than left inert. PROPERTIES: operation/data_type/domain/mode are friendly spellings of four common knobs; `properties` writes ANY node property by its real RNA name, dispatched on the property's own declared type - an enum is validated against its own items and reported as the identifier Blender stored, not the string you sent. That is what reaches a Math node's use_clamp, a Noise texture's noise_dimensions or a Map Range's interpolation_type, none of which a curated list of four was ever going to cover. parent puts the new node inside a Frame node of the same group (layout only); its location then reads relative to the frame. A parent that is not a Frame, or not in the group, is refused and the node removed. ZONES: zone {kind SIMULATION | REPEAT | FOR_EACH | CLOSURE, items [{name, type}], link (true)} makes both nodes (no type), pairs them with input.pair_with_output(output) - two nodes made one by one stay unpaired - places them 150 either side of location, links the input's first Geometry output to the output's first Geometry input, and adds the items (types from this build's own list: FLOAT, INT, BOOLEAN, VECTOR, RGBA, ...). Repeat arrived in 4.2 and For Each Element in 4.4; an earlier build refuses naming the version. With name, the nodes are '<name> Input' and '<name> Output'. Reply: both node names, paired, the items with their socket identifiers on both nodes.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): the compositor's Glare, Translate and Denoise keep their controls as node PROPERTIES on 3.6 and 4.2, have BOTH properties and new input sockets on 4.4, and only input sockets from 5.0 - so set them with properties before 5.0 and inputs from it. Bundle and closure nodes (NodeCombineBundle, NodeSeparateBundle, NodeJoinBundle, NodeEvaluateClosure), GeometryNodeListLength and GeometryNodeListGetItem add on 5.0+; GeometryNodeList on 5.0 only (5.2 lists through Field to List and the other list nodes); GeometryNodeBoneInfo and GeometryNodeSampleSoundFrequencies on 5.2. zone {kind: CLOSURE} (5.0+) makes the paired Closure Input / Output, zone.items being its parameters (input_items).
bl_set_view_layer:
Turn Blender render passes on or off - what decides WHAT THE COMPOSITOR CAN SEE, since a Render Layers node only offers sockets for passes the layer actually outputs. Ask for a Z-depth composite with the Z pass off and there is nothing to connect. Pass names drop the use_pass_ prefix ("z", "normal", "mist", "cryptomatte_object") and are validated against THIS layer rather than a list in the addon, because the set depends on the Blender version and render engine - a hard-coded one would refuse passes that exist. Every requested pass is read back individually: several use_pass_* properties are read-only under a given engine, so the write is accepted and the value does not move. cycles / eevee write view_layer.cycles / .eevee by identifier (denoising_store_passes gives a Denoise node its Albedo and Normal), cryptomatte_depth sets the Cryptomatte levels, lightgroups and aovs ([{name, type}]) are made when missing, and material_override renders the layer with one material (null clears it).

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): the Cycles render-time pass is cycles {pass_render_time: true} on 5.0+ (refused by name before, listing view_layer.cycles' settings); it is not one of the use_pass_* names enable_passes takes.
bl_set_viewport_shading: Set the Blender 3D viewport shading: WIREFRAME, SOLID, MATERIAL or RENDERED. This is what makes lighting work VISIBLE - SOLID ignores materials and lamps entirely, so a correctly lit scene looks grey. MATERIAL preview uses a studio light and does NOT show your scene's lamps; only RENDERED runs the render engine, so it is the only mode in which a flickering light actually flickers. The reply reads the shading back, colorType and studioLight included, and a call with no arguments changes nothing and reports the current shading. show_xray (see and select through surfaces) and show_cavity (cavity shading, which shows creases and topology mistakes) are written on every 3D viewport and read back. show_grid turns the floor grid overlay off or on - the perspective floor (overlay.show_floor) and the orthographic grid (show_ortho_grid) together - so a backdrop image is judged without it; showGrid reads true when either shows.
bl_set_viewport_view:
Place the Blender viewport's own view - the orbit pivot (focus), how far back, and the angle. The viewport is an ORBIT, not a camera: there is no eye position to set directly, so pass look_from and it derives the pivot, distance and rotation for you. azimuth/elevation are RADIANS; azimuth 0 looks along +Y and positive elevation looks DOWN at the focus. Use this to drive a walkthrough without the human touching the viewport.

Parameters: perspective (str, default None: left as it is) is the view's projection - PERSP, ORTHO or CAMERA (look through the scene camera), matched case-insensitively. lens (float, default None: left as it is) is the viewport's own focal length in millimeters (the 3D view's lens, not a camera's); it must be finite, has no range check here, and the reply reads back what Blender stored. Only the first 3D viewport of the current screen is changed. With azimuth or elevation alone, the other one is taken as 0 (azimuth) or 0.35 (elevation); distance must be positive; a focus left out keeps the current pivot. focus and look_from take [x, y, z] or {x, y, z}. Everything is validated before anything is written.

OUT: focus [x, y, z], distance, eye [x, y, z] (the eye position derived from the orbit), perspective, lens - read back off the view.

Refused with nothing changed: an unknown key; no 3D viewport in this Blender (a headless run); look_from together with azimuth, elevation or distance; look_from equal to the focus; a malformed or non-finite focus or look_from; a distance that is zero or negative; a non-finite azimuth, elevation, distance or lens; a perspective other than PERSP, ORTHO or CAMERA; CAMERA with no scene camera.
bl_relax_loop: Even out a Blender mesh run of vertices (one path or one loop along edges): mode SPACE puts them at equal distances along it (interpolation LINEAR or CUBIC), RELAX averages each with its neighbours; on_surface keeps them on the mesh. Edge lengths before and after. vertices may be named in any order: they must form ONE path or ONE closed loop along the mesh's edges (a branch, two pieces or fewer than three vertices is refused). SPACE moves them to equal distances along the run - LINEAR along its own segments, CUBIC along a Catmull-Rom curve through them - and an open run's two ends stay. RELAX moves each vertex halfway to the midpoint of its two neighbours on the run, iterations times (default 1); the ends of an open run stay. on_surface puts each moved vertex on the nearest point of the mesh as it was before the call. Reply: the order walked, closed, verticesMoved, and edgeLengthBefore and edgeLengthAfter (max, mean, min along the run). A mesh with shape keys is refused. FLATTEN (2026-10-06, 5.2's mesh.flatten, native on every build): mode FLATTEN projects the vertices - any set, not a run - onto their least-squares plane; reply plane {point, normal} (local) and maxDisplacement. Six vertices up to 0.1 off a plane land within 1e-6 of it. It takes no interpolation, iterations or on_surface.
bl_dissolve_mesh_elements:
Dissolve Blender mesh vertices, edges or faces (indices) and keep the surface - the faces around them merge into one instead of leaving a hole. WHY: removing the two inner loops after a corner reroute, a vertex where a seam parted, three edges meeting where two should - bl_decimate_mesh DISSOLVE works on the whole mesh by angle. elements VERTS, EDGES (default) or FACES; use_face_split keeps a merged face split where it would be concave; use_boundary_tear tears a boundary vertex out; also_verts (edges and faces, default true) dissolves the vertices left with two edges. regionFaces lists the merged faces. Measured on a 3x3 sheet: four faces into one (9 -> 6 faces, 16 -> 13 vertices); one inner vertex (9 -> 6 faces); all 12 inner edges into one face of 4 vertices. An edge without two faces (a boundary or wire edge) is refused before anything is written: it has nothing to merge, and builds disagree on it - measured on a sheet's corner rim edge, 3.6.23 and 5.2.1 change nothing while 4.4.0 dissolves the corner vertex instead and answers ok. A dissolve that changes nothing is refused, as are use_boundary_tear on edges and use_face_split on faces. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write. mode LIMITED is Limited Dissolve by angle (degrees, default 5) over the whole mesh or the indices given, with delimit and dissolve_boundaries; it splits the n-gons it merges unless keep_ngons.

LIMITED DISSOLVE (mode LIMITED, 2026-10-05). bmesh.ops.dissolve_limit: every edge between two faces meeting flatter than angle and every vertex between two edges running straighter than it are dissolved. angle is in DEGREES (default 5, as Blender's own operator; angleRadians is echoed). Without indices the whole mesh is the candidate set; with indices, elements says what they are and faces bring their edges and vertices. delimit (NORMAL, MATERIAL, SEAM, SHARP, UV - read from this build; default the build's own, NORMAL; [] for none) keeps the edges between such regions. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: a flat 5 x 5 grid goes from 25 faces to 1; with delimit MATERIAL and two materials, to 2; a 64-sided cylinder cut once around its middle loses the cut at 0.1 and at 5 degrees (384 to 128 vertices) and its 5.625-degree sides only at 6. dissolve_boundaries (default false) dissolves an open rim too - on the flat grid it left no face at all, which is refused. Reply: facesDissolved, verticesDissolved, regionFaces, the counts before and after. use_face_split, use_boundary_tear and also_verts are refused with LIMITED; angle, delimit and dissolve_boundaries without it.
bl_join_boundary_loops:
Join two open boundary loops of one Blender mesh: BRIDGE (a band of faces), FUSE (weld into one seam) or SEW (loose edges for cloth sewing). Each loop is {near: [x,y,z]}, {vertex}, {edge} or {index}. WHY: a cup handle's two loops bridged, a jumpsuit's two waist loops fused into one seam, two garment panels sewn at the shoulders - nothing paired two loops. Both loops must be closed rings on the same object (bl_join_objects first). Vertices are paired by the rotation and direction that put the pairs closest in total, plus twist; BRIDGE uses bmesh bridge_loops, which pairs them itself and takes unequal counts; FUSE moves each pair to its midpoint and welds; SEW adds a loose edge per pair inside the mesh for a cloth's sewing springs (wrap a sewing trial in bl_step_simulation's guards). pairDistance reports the closest and farthest pair. Measured on two 8-sided tubes 1 apart: BRIDGE 8 faces, SEW 8 loose edges, FUSE 32 -> 24 vertices with the seam at the middle. Refused: one loop twice, FUSE or SEW of unequal loops, a loop that is not a clean ring, a mesh with fewer than two loops, an unknown loop reference. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write.

DIFFERENT SIZES, CUTS AND CURVES (2026-10-04): match RESAMPLE splits the shorter loop's longest edges at their middles until the counts match (verticesAddedByResample), so FUSE and SEW join a 4-vertex rim to an 8-vertex one; match EQUAL (default) refuses that for FUSE and SEW, while BRIDGE joins unequal loops with triangles. BRIDGE of equal loops takes cuts (0-64): that many rings across the band, each rung split at even shares (interpolation LINEAR) or along a cubic curve that leaves each rim the way its own surface runs (SMOOTH). Measured on two 8-sided tubes offset 1 sideways: 2 LINEAR cuts slant straight (ring centres x 0.333333, 0.666667); SMOOTH ones leave each tube along it (0.259259, 0.740741), the rings at z 1.364016 and 1.635984. OPEN RUNS - pattern seams: a flat panel has ONE boundary loop, so a side or shoulder seam is a stretch of it. run_a and run_b (or runs_b, several runs sewn to run_a in order - a hood edge to both neckline halves, a band in segments) are each {from, to} by vertex index or {near: [x,y,z]}; a run follows the boundary loop holding both ends the shorter way round (way LONG for the other side) or the cheapest edge path (along EDGES - an internal line such as a drawcord's centerline). SEW (default for runs) adds loose edges pair by pair, FUSE welds the pairs at their midpoints; match RESAMPLE splits the shorter run's longest edges until the counts meet; B is paired in whichever direction puts the pairs closest (reversedB). seam reports lengthA, lengthB (the sum of the B runs), lengthsB, the difference and flagged against tolerance (0.001, world units); report_only measures and writes nothing. BRIDGE, loop_a/loop_b, twist and cuts are for whole loops and are refused beside runs.
bl_knife_cut: Cut across Blender mesh faces between points (a polyline; each lands on the nearest vertex or edge), or join vertices by vertex_pairs or vertex_path - across the faces between them. Returns the cut's edges and vertices. WHY: rerouting a support loop round a corner, a diagonal cut across a square, a repair cut into one face - bl_bisect_plane slices the whole mesh. points: each lands on the vertex nearest it when one is within tolerance (default 1e-4, mesh units), else on the nearest point of the nearest edge, which is split there; space WORLD (the default here) or LOCAL. Consecutive points are joined across the faces between them (bmesh connect_vert_pair), which adds a vertex on every edge the cut crosses. vertex_pairs [[a, b], ...] and vertex_path [a, b, c, ...] join existing vertices the same way - a pair in one face splits that face (connect_verts). Measured on a 3x3 sheet: points from the left edge to the right edge of the first row split its 3 faces (16 -> 20 vertices); a corner-to-corner path cuts the 3 diagonal faces. pointsLanded, cutEdges and cutVertices come back. Refused: more than one input, under two points, a vertex to itself, a pair on separate pieces, every pair already joined. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write.
bl_inset_faces: Inset Blender mesh faces: a ring thickness wide inside the region (or each face with individual), the inner face moved depth along the normal. Returns the inner and ring face indices. WHY: a cup's base n-gon pinches into a star under subdivision until it is inset; a plate's centre collapses; a boss grows out of an inset face - and nothing inset. bmesh inset_region (the region's outer edge inset as one; boundary inset open edges too, default true; outset grows outward) or inset_individual (individual=true). even (default true) keeps the ring's width at corners; relative_offset scales it by the neighbouring faces' size. The faces given stay and move in (innerFaces); the ring is new (ringFaces). space WORLD takes world lengths (uniform scale only). Measured: the middle face of a 3x3 sheet of 0.5 squares inset 0.1 and raised 0.2 has its corners at 0.6/0.9, z 0.2, with 4 ring faces. Refused: thickness not above 0, outset or boundary with individual. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write.
bl_slide_edges: Slide a chain or loop of Blender mesh edges along the edges beside it by factor (-1..1, the sign picks the side); clamp=false slides past the rail's end. WHY: tightening a loop toward an edge, and turning a cuff or hem back past the original edge, are edge slides. Each vertex moves along its rail - the edge at it, not in the chain, in the face on the chain's + or - side, read off the faces' winding so the side is the same all along - by |factor| of the rail's length. Measured on a loop at z 0.5 of a tube 1 high: +0.5 to z 0.25, then -0.5 to 0.625 (the other rails are 0.75 long by then); clamp false with -1.5 from 0.5 to 1.25. A vertex with no rail on that side is left and counted (verticesWithoutRail). Refused: factor 0, |factor| over 1 with clamp on, edges that branch or are not one chain, no rail on that side at all. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write.
bl_loop_cut:
Cut edge loops across the ring of quads through a seed edge (index, or edge_near [x,y,z] world) on a Blender mesh: count loops, slid by slide (-1..1). Returns each loop's vertex and edge indices. WHY: a support loop near a rim, loops near a part's ends, even loops that become seams - bl_bisect_plane cuts everything a plane crosses and has no seed, count or slide. The ring runs across each quad to its opposite edge, both ways, until a boundary, a face that is not a quad, or the start again (closed round a cylinder). Loops are evenly spaced along every ring edge; slide moves them all by that share of the spacing toward the seed edge's second vertex (negative: its first). Measured on an 8-sided tube 1 high: one loop at z 0.5, 16 -> 24 vertices; count 2 with slide 0.5 at z 0.5 and 0.833333. bl_select_edges seed_edge + loop=true on a reply edge finds the same loop. Refused: count outside 1-64, slide at or past +-1, a seed with no quad beside it. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write.

EVEN AND SMOOTHNESS (2026-10-04): even=true puts each cut at the same distance from the ring's first side - the seed edge's share times the seed edge's length - instead of the same share of every ring edge, so the loop runs parallel to that side; on ring edges 1, 1.5 and 2 long one even cut sits 0.5 from the side on each (shares give 0.5, 0.75, 1.0). A cut that would pass a shorter edge's end is refused. smoothness (-1 to 1) moves each new vertex that share of the way from the straight edge to a cubic curve whose end tangents lie in each end's tangent plane, so on a curved surface the loop follows the curve: on a radius-1 octagon's 45-degree edge the midpoint goes from radius 0.92388 (the chord) to 0.997103. Measured identically on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1.
bl_extrude_mesh: Extrude Blender mesh faces, edges or vertices (indices) along the normal (distance) or a vector (offset), with scale and rotate {angle, axis} about each step's median, repeated steps times; mode REGION or INDIVIDUAL. Returns each step's new indices. WHY: the most-used hand-modelling step had no typed call - bl_extrude_skirt extrudes boundary loops straight down only. elements FACES (default), EDGES or VERTS; mode REGION (faces together, their shared edges kept) or INDIVIDUAL (each face on its own). Each step extrudes the previous step's new geometry, then moves it by offset [x,y,z] or distance along the normal (a region's area-weighted normal, each face's own for INDIVIDUAL, the averaged vertex normal for edges and vertices), scales it about its median by scale (a number or [x,y,z]) and turns it by rotate {angle degrees, axis [x,y,z]} about its median. space WORLD gives the vectors and the distance in world units (the object's rotation and scale applied; the distance needs a uniform scale). A face extrude removes the original faces, as Blender's own does, so a lone quad becomes an open-bottomed box; perStep lists each step's new vertices, edges and faces (a face a later step extruded is gone), and topVertices / topFaces / topEdges are the last step's, ready for the next call. Measured: a cube's top face 1 along its normal gives 12 vertices, 10 faces, closed; two steps of up 1, scale 0.5 and 90 degrees on a 2 x 1 quad end at x +-0.25, y +-0.125, z 2. Refused: a step that neither moves, scales nor rotates (the new geometry would sit on the old), offset with distance, INDIVIDUAL edges, a 0 scale, steps over 100, a distance with no normal. Indices come from bl_select_faces, bl_select_edges or bl_vertex_info and are checked before anything is written; the edit runs on a scratch copy and is written once, so a refusal changes nothing. A mesh with shape keys is refused (the base mesh is what is written). The reply carries counts before and after and the indices of what was made, in the mesh's order after the write.
bl_uv_unwrap:
Generate a UV layer on a Blender mesh. Closes a gap the addon could already SEE: object_info and gen_status both report uvLayers, and the quality check says outright 'no UVs - texturing and lightmaps will both fail until it is unwrapped', with nothing able to unwrap. THREE METHODS for different jobs: SMART (default, bpy.ops.uv.smart_project) cuts its own seams by angle and is the one for imported geometry that has none; LIGHTMAP (lightmap_pack) makes non-overlapping islands inside 0-1, which is what Unreal wants from a LIGHTMAP channel specifically; ANGLE (unwrap, angle-based) respects seams you have already marked and WARNS if the mesh has none, because without them it flattens as one unusable island. uv_layer NAMES THE TARGET CHANNEL and matters more than it looks: Unreal reads lightmaps from a SECOND UV channel, so a LIGHTMAP pass usually wants uv_layer='Lightmap' rather than overwriting the base UVs - and the layer is made active BEFORE the unwrap, or the operator writes into whichever channel happened to be active, which is how a lightmap lands on top of the base UVs and nobody notices until the bake. An existing layer name is REFUSED unless replace=true. The response reports uvLayersBefore and uvLayersAfter BY NAME plus activeLayer and createdLayer, so 'did it land on the channel I meant' needs no second call. dry_run reports and modifies nothing. Verified headless on Blender 4.4.0 and 5.0.1 - unlike bpy.ops.mesh.bevel, the UV operators do run under blender -b. With seam_rules it marks seams by rule before an ANGLE, CONFORMAL or MINIMUM_STRETCH unwrap (refused with the methods that cut their own or ignore seams): {rule: head, bone (default the one named head), armature (default the mesh's Armature modifier or parent), back (default [0,1,0])} rings the head where its skin weights meet the neck's - under the chin, round the nape - and runs a seam up the back of the skull to the crown; {rule: garment, prefer: inner | back | [x,y,z], preferWeight, midPlane {point, normal}, splitAtMidPlane} cuts every piece open from loop to loop along its preferred side (inner: the inside of a sleeve or leg) until it is one disc, gives a closed piece one slit, and with splitAtMidPlane halves it at the mid-plane first. With pack_fill (0-1) it packs to a fill target: every island scaled to one texel density, then packed at smaller margins until the layout uses that share of the tile, keeping the fullest; packFill gives target, achieved, met and every attempt. Every unwrap's layout gives fill, islands and texel density (pixels per metre at 1024) with the spread between islands - on a test character's head the automatic unwrap was 70 islands at 56% fill, and the head and garment rules 4 islands at 75%.

SEAMS, PACK AND TRANSFORM LANDED 2026-08-31, in that order and no other - seams, then the unwrap, then pack, then transform. Packing before unwrapping packs the OLD layout, which looks like it worked and is just the previous islands rearranged; seams marked afterwards do nothing until the next unwrap.

mark_seams IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS, because this endpoint has always refused to pretend an ANGLE unwrap works without seams - it warns 'NO seams marked ... the whole mesh flattens as a single island' - and nothing in the addon could set edge.use_seam. So ANGLE was a method its own callers could not use. Pass the same selectors bevel_edges takes: {minAngleDeg: 40} for every edge sharper than 40 degrees, {boundaryOnly: true}, {edgeIndices: [...]}, {allEdges: true}. The angle is the DIHEDRAL angle between the two faces an edge joins, which is what 'sharp edge' means and what you cut a mesh along.

mark_seams:true is REFUSED as ambiguous - 'every edge' and 'the sharp ones' are different meshes and guessing would silently pick one. A criterion matching no edge is refused too, because marking nothing and then unwrapping would behave exactly as if seams had never been asked for.

uv_transform takes scale and offset, each a number or [u,v], applied to the layer just written. Rotation is deliberately absent: rotating a packed layout moves islands out of 0-1 with nothing to put them back. The response reports the layout bounds BEFORE and AFTER, read off the layer rather than computed from the request, and warns when the result leaves 0-1 - legal for a tiling texture, wrong for a lightmap channel.

METHOD BOX, FOR KIT PIECES AND PROPS THAT MUST SHARE ONE TEXEL DENSITY: a box projection in meters - each face takes the two axes across its dominant normal axis, divided by meters_per_tile (default 1.0), or set it the other way with texel_density pixels per meter on a texture_size (default 1024). A 4 m wall and a 1 m block unwrapped this way get the same pixels per meter, and pieces laid side by side on a grid that is a multiple of the tile continue the same texture. box_space OBJECT (default) projects the object's own axes with its rotation and scale, about its origin - put the pivot on the module grid (bl_set_origin bottomCorner) and the tiles line up; WORLD adds the location, so the texture runs on across pieces wherever they stand, and moves under a piece moved later. The UVs are written straight to the layer, no operator and no edit mode; the layout runs outside 0-1 by design (a tiling texture), so a lightmap belongs on its own layer (method LIGHTMAP). uv_pack is refused with BOX - a pack rescales the islands to the tile. The answer's box block carries the tile used and the density MEASURED off the layer per face (measuredTexelDensityMin/Median/Max at texture_size), facesByAxis, facesMirrored (0: every face reads the right way round from outside) and facesSlanted - a face at 45 degrees gets about 0.84 of the density along its slope, a box projection's own limit. The four BOX keys beside another method are refused, as are meters_per_tile with texel_density, texture_size alone and any size that is not a finite number above 0. MORE METHODS (2026-10-06): CONFORMAL and MINIMUM_STRETCH unwrap on your seams like ANGLE (MINIMUM_STRETCH on 4.4 and later; refused by name on 4.2, where bl_uv_relax is the nearest); fill_holes (default true) for those three. FOLLOW_ACTIVE_QUADS lays a quad mesh out as a grid from active_face (default the first quad), sized from its world edges and scaled into 0-1. keep_bounds (2026-10-06, unwrap in place): each new island fitted, uniformly and centred, into the UV bounds its faces had before; refused with uv_pack, uv_transform and BOX, and on a new layer.

RULE - UNWRAPPING FOR PAINTING (2026-10-06). Island margin 0.05 against SMART's default: a margin keeps a stroke near an island's edge from reaching the next island, so measure the gap with bl_uv_info and keep the margin that holds islands apart at the texture size in use. An image canvas needs UVs and a saved file; vertex colours need neither but are limited by the vertex count - bl_mesh_stats says which the mesh can carry. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.
bl_vertex_groups_from_bones: Make Blender vertex groups from bone weights: groups {name: {bones: [...], threshold (default 0.5), value 'one' or 'sum'}} - each holds the vertices whose summed weight on those bones reaches the threshold. A region mask (hood, cuff, pin rim) from a skinned mesh. WHY: garment region groups (hood, cuffs, hem, a self-collision band, a pin rim) were built in raw Python twenty times; bl_set_vertex_weights takes explicit vertex lists. 'bones' are vertex group names (a skinned mesh's bone groups). value 'one' (default) writes 1.0, 'sum' the summed weight clamped to 1. Every group is computed before any is written: an unknown bone, an existing group without replace, or a group that would come out empty is refused and nothing changes. Each group's vertex count and minimum weight are reported.
bl_world_info:
What the Blender world actually IS - the read half of bl_set_world, which had none. The family was write-only: bl_scene_info omits the world entirely and bl_render_info reports only its NAME, so 'what is my world set to' was unanswerable on the one datablock that decides whether an interior renders black. Every answer is taken from the LINK rather than the node, because that is where a shader tree's effect lives: backgroundConnected (a Background node not wired to the world output accepts every write and contributes nothing), and environmentTextureDriving, found by walking backwards from the Colour socket so a Mapping in between still counts while a texture left unlinked correctly does not. Also reports useNodes, because a world with it off IGNORES the whole tree and renders its flat colour while every node reads perfectly. blockers is the diagnosis, not the inputs to it. A scene with no world returns a blocker rather than an error - that is the commonest black-render cause, not a failure. A LINKED COLOUR RENDERS ITS LINK: colorLinked says whether anything drives the Background's Colour, colorDrivenBy names it, skyTextureDriving names a Sky Texture as environmentTextureDriving names an HDRI, and `color` is then the socket's unused value (colorNote says so). Until 2026-09-20 a sky-lit world whose socket value was black read contributesLight:false.

Parameters: name (str, default None) reads that world datablock by its exact name instead of the current scene's world; an empty name also means the scene's world. isSceneWorld says whether the named world is the one the scene renders with.

OUT: ok, world (name, or null), isSceneWorld, worldsInFile [names], contributesLight, blockers [plain-language causes of no light]. With a world: useNodes, flatColor [r, g, b] (what renders when useNodes is false), mist {use, start, depth}, aoDistance, cyclesVisibility {diffuse, glossy} (null when the build has none). With useNodes on: nodeCount, surfaceDrivenBy (node type feeding the world output), backgroundConnected; and when a Background node exists: color (the Colour socket's own value), colorLinked, colorDrivenBy ("<node> (<TYPE>)"), skyTextureDriving, colorNote (when linked), strength, environmentTexturePresent (any Environment Texture node in the tree, linked or not), environmentTextureDriving, hdri (its image filepath), rotation (the Z rotation of the FIRST Mapping node in the tree, wherever it is wired, or null).

Blockers (reported, not refused): no world on the scene; use_nodes off; no Background node; the Background not wired to the output; an environment texture driving with no image; strength 0; an unlinked black colour; Cycles visibility diffuse and glossy both off. contributesLight is true only with no blockers.

Refusals (a read; nothing is changed): no world by that name (lists them); any unknown key.
bl_wrap_to_target:
Fit a Blender mesh onto a target surface keeping its topology (a template head onto a scan): landmark pairs moved first, pinned vertices held, relaxed and re-projected; the distance to the target before and after. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.

WHY (2026-10-06): a custom head or body is conformed by wrapping the template-topology mesh onto it; SHRINKWRAP, pin weights and apply_modifier reached it in several calls with no landmark pairs and no measure of the fit. object keeps its vertices, edges and faces and takes target's shape (world space; the target as it evaluates). In order: landmarks [{vertex: i | from: [x,y,z], to: [x,y,z]}] move that vertex (or the one nearest from) to to, spread over landmark_radius with a smoothstep falloff, and hold it; every free vertex goes onto the target by wrap_method NEAREST_SURFACEPOINT (default), PROJECT (along its normal either way, within reach; a miss stays put and is counted) or NEAREST_VERTEX, plus offset along the target's normal; smooth_iterations passes move each free vertex half way to its neighbours' mean and back onto the target. pins {vertexGroup, minWeight} holds a group's vertices. dry_run measures and writes nothing. Reply: before and after {maxDistance, meanDistance}, landmarks [{vertex, error}], pinned, missed, edgeLengthCV {before, after}, counts. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a UV sphere wrapped onto an ellipsoid goes from 0.30 off to under 1e-5, and five relax passes even its edge lengths. Refused, nothing changed: the object as its own target, a bad method, a pin group missing or empty, a malformed landmark, a non-finite offset or reach, smooth_iterations over 100, shape keys.
bl_retopo_panels:
Quad-grid retopo of flat Blender pattern panels: each outline split at four corners and filled by a Coons patch at edge_length, the panel's UVs sampled on, and seams [[{panel, near}, {panel, near}]] given equal vertex counts. A hole is ringed by closed quad loops; rings [{panel, near, loops}] sets how many, or lays rows along a curved side.

WHY (2026-10-06): the cleanest game mesh of a draped garment is the FLAT panels retopologized, their UVs copied on, then moved onto the drape by UV (bl_transfer_by_uv); the grid had no typed call. panels: names or {object, edgeLength, corners [[x,y,z] x4]}, each a flat mesh with a UV map. Corners default to the outline's four sharpest turns (20 degrees or more). Segments per side = length / edgeLength; opposite sides share a count and a seam ties two sides, each tied set taking its largest count. A grid point off the panel takes the nearest UV and is counted (uvOutside). One mesh holds every panel (vertexStart per panel), UV map named uv_map or UVMap. HOLES AND CURVES (2026-10-08): a panel with a hole (an armhole cut out) gets the hole resampled to 2 x (nu + nv) vertices, loops closed rings at edge_length apart round it (default 1), then four Coons patches out to the four sides (an O-grid), so every ring is a closed loop of quads and seam counts still hold. A rings entry whose near is nearest the hole sets its loops (0-16); on a panel without a hole it lays loops rows at a constant distance along the outline side nearest near (pass a concave armhole curve as one side by its corners). Each panel replies foldedQuads, holes and rings [{kind, loops, ...}]. Refused, nothing created: a panel not flat, closed, listed twice or without a UV map; a seam on a side twice; edgeLength not above 0; over 250,000 faces; more than one hole in a panel; loops past the outline, folding or filling every row; a side band on a holed panel or a second one on a panel; any quad of a ringed panel folded over.
bl_transfer_by_uv:
Move a Blender mesh's vertices to the point of a source surface at the same UV (a flat retopo onto its drape), weld seam pairs at their centre, and make an upward LOD chain (levels: subdivide, transfer again).

WHY (2026-10-06): a DATA_TRANSFER modifier samples by position, not by UV, so a retopo made on the flat panels (bl_retopo_panels) could not be put on the draped garment. Each vertex takes its uv_map UV (a vertex on a UV seam takes its first corner's and is counted) and moves to the source's point (as it evaluates unless evaluated is false) whose source_uv_map triangle holds that UV, by barycentric weights; a UV outside every triangle takes the nearest and is counted (uvOutside). weld_distance merges boundary vertices closer than it at their centre. levels 1-4 adds object_up1..N, the flat mesh subdivided once more each level, moved and welded the same way (196 / 784 / 3,136 / 12,544 quads from a 14 x 14 retopo). bl_audit_placement:
Sweep a whole Blender scene for objects that stick out of the room, float, sink into the floor, or collide - the level-dressing question, which bl_objects_overlap cannot answer because it asks about ONE pair and dressing asks about every object at once, hundreds of round trips away. IT CAUGHT A REAL DEFECT: two camp cots authored 0.75 x 1.95 were rotated 90 degrees about an object origin still at the world origin, swinging them from x 11.13 to 13.08 - straight through an east wall at x 13.0, which nothing in the render made obvious. EVERY TEST HERE IS AABB, and said so in the response: a cage and the pallet inside it share a bounding box without touching, so treat 'overlaps' as CANDIDATES and settle the ones that matter with bl_objects_overlap, which tests real geometry. A FLOATING OBJECT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY WRONG - lights, wall fixtures and anything hung read as floating because they are - so 'floor' is opt-in and 'ignore' takes name prefixes, letting the caller say what is meant to rest on the ground. Bounds and floor are both optional and each enables its own test; with neither, this reports only what it audited. check_overlaps is off by default because it is O(n^2). Lists are capped at max_report and every one is returned beside its untruncated *Total, so a cap can never read as a clean scene. An object that draws instances - Geometry Nodes instances, particles, instancing - answers with instancesNote: instances are not part of any evaluated mesh, so this does not see them (measured on 3.6-5.2).

Parameters: bounds (default None) is the room every object should sit inside, either the flat list [x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1] or {min: [x, y, z], max: [x, y, z]} (the shape the bounds readers return; only those two keys). Without it no containment test runs. floor_tolerance (float, default None, which the op reads as 0.02) is the slack for the floor tests: an object whose lowest world point is more than this above floor is floating, more than this below it is sunken. prefix (str, default None) audits only objects whose name starts with it; collection (str, default None) audits only the objects linked directly in that collection (coll.objects). Only MESH objects are ever audited; ignore prefixes are skipped. max_report defaults to 40 and evaluated to true.

Boxes are world AABBs built from the vertices (of the modifier result unless evaluated is false); a mesh with no vertices is skipped and listed. Each list is sorted worst first.

OUT: ok, audited (count), outsideBounds [{object, outsideBy {x-|x+|y-|y+|z-|z+: distance}, worldMin, worldMax}], outsideBoundsTotal, floating [{object, gap}], floatingTotal, sunken [{object, depth}], sunkenTotal, overlaps [{a, b, aabbVolume}], overlapsTotal, overlapNote, notAuditedNoVertices [names], notAuditedNoVerticesTotal, drawnInstances {name: count}, instancesNote (null when none), floorNote (null without floor).

Refusals (a read; nothing is changed either way): bounds not one of the two shapes, a dict with keys other than min and max, a non-finite value, or min greater than max on an axis; a non-finite floor; ignore not a list; no collection by that name; any unknown key.

find_tools:
Search every MifBridge tool, loaded here or not, by a keyword or a few words: each row gives the tool's summary and parameters, and an unloaded tool's pack.

Ranking, ignoring case: the whole phrase in a tool's name first, then the phrase in its description, then - for several words - tools that have every word somewhere, most of them in the name first. When no tool has every word, the answer is marked partial and lists the tools with two or more of the words as whole parts of their names, most first (each row's matched counts them); when not even that, it says which single words do match.

This is LOCAL: it reads this server's own registered tool metadata and needs no running editor,
so it works even before the bridge is reachable. It does not call describe_endpoint or the
bridge's self_audit - those report the UNREAL-side C++ handler surface (parameter guards,
read-only/transacted bucket, build signatures); this reports the MCP TOOL surface as this Python
process actually registered it, which is the thing an MCP client is choosing between.

No matches is real information, not a failure: it means try a different word (e.g. "bone" instead
of "skeleton", or "widget" instead of "UI") rather than that nothing exists for the concept.

WHAT EACH ROW NEEDS, AND WHETHER IT CAN RUN NOW (2026-10-14). Each of the first fifteen rows carries needs - unreal, blender, unreal+blender, "unreal or blender" (run_python: the app argument picks), or "unreal for part of it" (a tool that runs offline and hands work on, like mif_synth_audio's import) - and a row that cannot run here says why in unavailable: no Unreal editor answers (at this server's port), Blender does not answer, the tool's description says UE 5.N+ and the editor runs an older engine, or the editor's MifBridge plugin (or Blender's add-on) is older than this server and lacks the tool's endpoint - the version handshake's measurement, taken now if it was due. A tool that reaches no backend (the offline audio, REAPER and file tools) has no needs. now says what each backend is doing: connected with the engine and project (or the Blender version), or not answering at its address; unrealPlugin is there when the handshake found the plugin older. What a tool needs is read from server.py itself - its pack's backend, the _post and _blender calls in its body and the helpers it calls - never a hand-kept list; the state is reused for 20 seconds, and a port nothing listens on is not pinged.
mif_project_mode:
Read or record this project's settings - ask the user. mode: generative | non-generative. change_cap: items one call may change before it previews (0 off). roadmap: the plan it follows. Empty reads. project: all|unreal|blender.

THE ROADMAP. roadmap is goal words or a catalog id (refused when none fits, naming the closest), your own plan as {goal, steps}, or {done: [step ids]} and {undone: [...]} for the steps done outside any check; 'none' clears it. mif_roadmap with no words then follows it. It is kept where the other settings are, so it survives a restart and moves with the project: on Blender, save the file to keep it. A refusal changes nothing on either project.

WHAT THE TWO MODES MEAN. generative: the bl_gen_* tools may create images, meshes and textures with AI models (Flux and Hunyuan3D-2, in a ComfyUI the user runs). Each model has its own license, which the user is responsible for following, and the note that asks names the limits: say them when you ask. non-generative: MifBridge only drives the editors and nothing is AI-generated - the bl_gen_* tools leave the tool list, find_tools and every pack, and a call by name, through mif_call or inside a bl_batch is refused before anything is sent.

IT IS THE USER'S CHOICE. A project with no mode works as generative, and the first MifBridge reply from it in a session carries one note asking you to ask the user and record the answer here. Record what they said; do not choose for them, and do not change a recorded mode unless they ask.

WHERE IT IS KEPT. For an Unreal project, MifBridgeProject.json in the project folder beside the .uproject - kept when Saved/ is deleted, shareable through source control, and never staged into a cooked build; the editor's MifBridge Setup tab and its startup log line show it. For Blender, a custom property on every scene of the open .blend (the add-on's project_mode op): it travels with the file, so save the file to keep it. project=all records it in every editor this session has reached, or tries both when none has.

THE OTHER TWO SWITCHES stay off-switches whatever a project says: MIF_GENERATIVE=off on the MCP server (or the older MIF_ALLOW_GENERATIVE=0), and the MifBlender preference 'Allow generative tools (ComfyUI)'. Either project being non-generative holds the bl_gen_* tools off, because they make content for the project being worked on. The answer reports each project's mode, generativeAllowed and generativeMode, as self_audit does.

THE CHANGE CAP (change_cap). One call that would change more than this many distinct targets - actors, assets, objects, DataTable rows, Blender objects, materials, collections; ten properties on one actor is one target - writes nothing and answers the list with a previewId to commit, or is refused where it has no preview. 25 when a project has none (or MIF_CHANGE_CAP in the editor's or Blender's environment); 0 switches it off. Kept beside the mode: changeCap in MifBridgeProject.json (the file is merged, never rewritten whole) and on the .blend's scenes. It is the user's choice: raise it only when they ask. self_audit and bl_status report the cap in force (docs/15 section 6).

WITHOUT AN EDITOR (R85, 2026-11-06): the Unreal project's recorded mode holds the bl_gen_* tools off even when no editor answers - read from the MifBridgeProject.json of the project this server was started in (MIF_PROJECT_DIR, else the .uproject at or above its working folder), and again whenever that file changes. Recording a mode still needs the editor, which names the project's folder.
mif_call:
Call any MifBridge tool by name, loaded in your client or not - no client refresh needed; args is an object of that tool's own parameters, which mif_help(tool) lists. Any call also takes _select/_omit (paths), _page (n, then _cursor) and _wait (seconds, on a job-status tool): mif_help('mif_call').

RESPONSE CONTROLS. Reserved keys that work on every tool, inside mif_call's args or in a direct call's arguments; they are this server's, never the tool's, and no schema lists them. _select ['actors.name', 'count'] keeps only those dotted paths - a path through a list applies to each row - and selectMissing names a path found nowhere, so a typo is not an empty answer. _omit ['actors.transform'] drops paths. ok and error always survive both. _page 50 returns 50 items of the result's longest list (_pageField 'a.b' picks another) with page {field, offset, returned, total, nextCursor}; send {'_cursor': nextCursor} (alone, or with _select/_omit) for the next page. Every page comes from the first call's one read, kept in this server's memory for 15 minutes - the tool is not called again, so no row is skipped or repeated while the level changes, and a fresh read needs a fresh _page call. _wait 120 on a job-status tool (render_sequence_status, package_status, render_movie_capture_status, frame_capture_status, gpu_profile_status, request_status, mocap_performance_status, lighting_build_status, shader_compile_status, ui_scenario_status, live_coding_status, bl_render_status, kr_reconstruct_status) polls it every 2 s until the job ends or the seconds pass (600 at most), with an MCP progress notification per poll for a client that sent a progressToken; the last reply comes back with waited {seconds, polls, ended}. A refusal ends the wait at once. _image is for a tool that shows a picture (capture_camera, capture_viewport, capture_level_map, render_thumbnail, preview_animation, preview_widget, preview_composite_widget, render_graph_image, bl_render_viewport, bl_preview_garment, bl_render_still with return_image, mif_view_image): by default the picture comes as an image block, at most 1024 px and 512 KB and four to a call, with its path in the text. _image false sends the path alone; _image 'data' keeps bl_render_still's base64 in the text. A bad control is refused before anything runs.

A SERVER OLDER THAN THE PLUGIN (1.3). A name this server has no tool for, which the running editor registers (self_audit's endpoint list), is forwarded to that endpoint as it is: args are the endpoint's own JSON keys (snake_case keys go camelCase, named in argsRenamed), the editor's own guard refuses an unknown one, and the reply carries forwarded:true, serverOlderThanPlugin:true and forwardNote - update or restart the MCP server for the typed tool. Response controls are not applied to a forwarded call (controlsIgnored).
bl_compose_atlas:
Tile rendered frames into one flipbook atlas PNG (left-to-right, top-to-bottom, the order Unreal's SubUV reads). Call mif_help("bl_compose_atlas") first.

ALPHA IS A DECISION (alpha_mode): film keeps the rendered alpha - for absorbing subjects on a transparent film (smoke, dust); luminance sets alpha = clamp(max(R, G, B) x alpha_gain) of the LINEAR colour and divides the colour by it - for emissive subjects rendered over black (fire, flashes, glows), whose film alpha is about 0 because emission absorbs nothing; dividing makes a translucent material's Emissive x Opacity give back the rendered emission. hybrid takes BOTH from two renders of the same frames - `frames` over black on an opaque film (the light) and alpha_frames on a transparent film (the absorbing smoke's coverage), one per frame in the same order: alpha = max(the film's alpha, the light's luminance alpha), the colour the light divided by it - so a fireball's flame and the dark smoke it turns into are one sheet (luminance alone gives dark smoke no alpha; film alone loses the flame). alpha_frames is refused with any other mode, and hybrid without it. All arithmetic is in linear light.
alpha_floor (default 0.01) is a black point: alpha = (a - floor) / (1 - floor). A volume render is never exactly empty - measured on a 5.2.1 fire sheet, 3% of all pixels sat at alpha 0-0.01 in areas holding nothing, which a sprite draws as a dirty square. Colour is written only where the stored 8-bit alpha is not 0: dividing by a tiny alpha had left saturated noise (RGB up to 0.84) under alpha 0, which compression and mip maps bleed into the edge.
loop_blend K crossfades the last K cells with the K frames rendered before the first cell (premultiplied, in linear light), so a looping sheet has no pop at the wrap; it needs columns x rows + K frames. normal_output writes a second sheet, a tangent-space normal (green-down, Unreal's convention) derived from each cell's alpha gradient, normal_strength its slope.
REFUSED, each saying nothing was written: a frame count that is not columns x rows + loop_blend, more than 256 cells, frames of two sizes (cells are the frames' own size - render at the size you want; nothing is resampled), a sheet past 8192 px, a missing frame, an output that is not a .png, is one of the frames, already exists (without overwrite), or is the normal sheet's path.
