RETURNS: atlas, wroteFile and fileBytes (stat'd off disk after the save), width, height, cellWidth, cellHeight, coverage per cell, emptyCells, repeatedCells (a cell pixel-identical to the one before - a held frame) and frozenNote when every cell is one image (measured on 5.0.1: EEVEE's background animation render drew a baked fluid frozen that way). Adds nothing to the scene and leaves no image datablock. Verified on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1.

MOTION SHEET (motion_output, 2026-10-11): a third PNG, each cell's optical flow toward the next cell (pyramidal Lucas-Kanade on the cells' alpha, numpy only), RG = 0.5 + flow / (2 x motionScalePx) in pixels of the cell, green DOWN (a uv's v), B 0, A 1. The flow comes from the frames, not a render pass: a fluid domain is a static box, so a vector pass holds no gas motion. motion_scale (pixels) fixes the encoding; by default the sheet's own 99th-percentile motion. The last cell's motion is toward the first when loop_blend makes the sheet loop, else 0. motionAtlas in the reply: path, motionScalePx, motionStrengthUV (what a material multiplies the decoded motion by - create_particle_material's MotionStrength), maxMotionPx, meanMotionPx, residual per cell (how much of the change to the next cell the flow leaves unexplained, under 1 when the motion is real), meanResidual. Import it with sRGB off and no mipmaps.
bl_compositor_info:
What the Blender compositor IS, and every way it can be on and doing nothing. The whole subsystem was unreachable before: bl_create_node_group can make a CompositorNodeTree, but that is a node GROUP in bpy.data.node_groups, while the scene's compositor is scene.node_tree - a different tree nothing could address - so glare, grading, denoise, cryptomatte and file output were outside the typed path. Reports four distinct blockers because the fix differs for each: use_nodes off; use_compositing off (the classic - backdrop updates, file untouched); no Composite node linked (a Viewer is NOT a substitute, it feeds the backdrop only, which is why it looks right in the compositor and the saved file is wrong); and no Render Layers feeding it. Also muted nodes, VSE strips that replace the compositor's output wholesale, and which view-layer passes are actually enabled.

PARAMETERS. view_layer (string, default the active view layer): whose enabled and available passes are reported. limit (whole number, default unlimited) and name_excludes (string or list of strings, case-insensitive substring) bound the nodes rows only; nodeCount, nodesByType and every blocker are still computed from the whole tree. Read-only: nothing is created or changed.

OUT: ok, scene, useNodes, useCompositing, useSequencer, viewLayer, addressAs ('scene:compositor'), compositorApi, nodeCount. With a tree: treeName, nodesByType {bl_idname: count}, nodes [{name, type, label, muted}] (plus nodesTruncated, nodesReturned, nodesTruncationNote when limit is passed), linkCount, compositeNodes, compositeConnected, renderLayersNodes, renderLayersFeeding, invalidLinks ["a.out -> b.in"], mutedNodes, outputNodeTypes. sequencerStrips when use_sequencer is on. Always: enabledPasses, availablePasses (use_pass_* names off the view layer), blockers [sentences], compositorAffectsRender (true when there are no blockers). Invalid links and a VSE holding strips are blockers too.

REFUSED: a view_layer that is not in the scene (the refusal lists the ones present); a negative or fractional limit; a name_excludes that is not text.
bl_set_scene_audio:
Set the Blender scene's 3D audio: distance model, Doppler speed and factor, master volume. Call mif_help("bl_set_scene_audio") first.

Works on the active scene (bl_set_current_scene switches it). With no arguments it only reads. Every call returns distanceModel, dopplerSpeed, dopplerFactor and volume as Blender stores them, `changed` (the keys this call moved), `before`, and distanceModels - read from this Blender's own RNA, never from a list kept here: NONE, INVERSE, INVERSE_CLAMPED (Blender's default), LINEAR, LINEAR_CLAMPED, EXPONENT and EXPONENT_CLAMPED on 3.6 through 5.2.
distance_model decides how a speaker's level falls with its distance from the listener: NONE keeps every speaker at full level wherever it stands, and under INVERSE_CLAMPED with a speaker's default reference distance and attenuation (1 and 1) a speaker 10 m away plays at a tenth of one at 1 m (measured in a mixdown). doppler_speed is the speed of sound in m/s (default 343.3, at least 0.01); doppler_factor scales the Doppler pitch shift of moving speakers (0 turns it off); volume is the scene's master volume, 0-100.
REFUSED, with nothing written: a distance model this build does not offer (the refusal lists the valid ones), and any value outside the property's own range - Blender would clamp it without a word. Every value is checked before any is written.
THE LISTENER IS THE SCENE CAMERA: Blender takes the listener's position and rotation from it, so `listener` names it and listenerNote says when the scene has none (bl_set_camera make_active picks another). volumeNote says when the scene's volume is animated - its keys then set the level, not this value.
Place sounds with bl_add_sound; hear the result with bl_mixdown_audio.
bl_add_sound:
Put a sound file in the Blender scene at a frame, as a 3D speaker or a sequencer strip. Call mif_help("bl_add_sound") first.

mode is required: speaker makes a Speaker object heard in 3D from the scene camera (the listener); strip makes a sequencer sound strip, heard as it is. file must exist and decode - it is read by Blender's own audio module BEFORE anything is created, because Blender's loader accepts a missing file or a text file named .wav without a word. frame is where the sound's first sample plays (default the current frame): in a mixdown that is sample (frame - frame_start) x rate / fps, to the sample. name defaults to Blender's own ("Speaker"; a strip takes the file's name), and a clash is suffixed and reported (requestedName, nameWasSuffixed).
SPEAKER: location [x, y, z] (default the origin), volume 0-1, pitch 0.1-10 (2.0 plays an octave up in half the time, measured), distance_reference, distance_max and attenuation (how its level falls with distance, under the scene's distance model - bl_set_scene_audio), cone_angle_inner and cone_angle_outer in DEGREES 0-360 (the inner may not be wider than the outer) and cone_volume_outer 0-1. Blender plays a speaker only through an NLA sound strip - one made through the data API alone is silent - so this uses Blender's own speaker operator, which makes that strip at the start frame, and rebuilds the dependency graph so Blender LOADS the sound: a sound set on a speaker from Python otherwise mixes to silence, measured on every build. soundLoaded reports it; a speaker that would be silent is removed and refused instead. The reply also gives distanceToListener, the NLA strip and the distance model.
STRIP: channel 1-128 (default the lowest channel free over the strip's frames; a channel another strip occupies there is refused, naming it and a free channel), volume 0-100, and volume_keys [[frame, volume], ...] keyed on the scene's action, LINEAR between keys - volume OR volume_keys, not both. Blender samples a strip's volume curve once a frame, so a key's value is heard from between half a frame before its frame to one frame after it (measured; which, depends on the frame and the build). No build's sound strip has a pitch (3.6-5.2), so pitch on a strip is refused. A strip lasts round(seconds x fps) frames.
BOTH: the file is loaded with check_existing, so a sound already in the file is reused (sound.reusedExisting) and never copied. The reply carries the sound's rate, channels and length in seconds and frames. A key of the other mode is refused by name, and every value is checked against Blender's own range before anything exists - a refusal leaves no object, speaker, sound or strip. Hear it with bl_mixdown_audio; bl_file_info counts sounds, speakers and sequencer_strips.

SCENE (2026-10-08): scene names the scene whose sequencer gets a strip. With none, on 5.0+ a strip goes to the workspace's sequencer scene when one is set - what the Sequencer shows - else the window's; the reply says which (sceneSource named | sequencerScene | window). A speaker is always the window scene's, and scene with mode speaker is refused.
bl_mixdown_audio:
Render the Blender scene's audio to a WAV or FLAC file, measured off the file. Call mif_help("bl_mixdown_audio") first.

Mixes every sequencer sound strip and every speaker of the active scene, in stereo unless channels names another layout, from frame_start to frame_end (default the scene's range). container is WAV or FLAC, taken from the file's extension when omitted, and the extension must match it. bit_format is U8, S16 (default), S24, S32, F32 or F64 for WAV, and S16 or S24 for FLAC - Blender writes a U8 FLAC as 16-bit and an S32, F32 or F64 FLAC as 24-bit without a word (measured on every build), so those are refused. sample_rate is 8000-192000, default 48000 (on 3.6 and 4.2 it is set through the scene's FFmpeg audio rate and put back).
CHANNELS: STEREO by default, or any layout this build's mixdown offers - MONO, STEREO, SURROUND4, SURROUND51 and SURROUND71 on every build, STEREO_LFE, SURROUND5 and SURROUND61 from 4.4 (on 3.6 and 4.2 the layout is set through the scene's FFmpeg audio_channels and put back). A layout the build lacks is refused with the build's own list. The reply carries layout, channels read off the header, and a WAV's channelMask. Where a mono strip lands, measured on 3.6.23 to 5.2.1 with one strip at each pan: STEREO pan -1 is left only and 0 is -3 dB each side; SURROUND51 pan 0 is the center channel alone, -1 splits front left and back left, 2 or -2 is back left and right equally, and the LFE is silent. For SURROUND61 and SURROUND71 the file's channel mask misnames where the sound is, and the reply says so in layoutWarning: in 7.1 a source behind lands in channels 7-8, which the mask calls side left and right.
TIME: sample 0 of the file is frame_start, so a sound placed at frame F starts at sample (F - frame_start) x rate / fps. A WAV runs a few hundred samples past the range; a FLAC does not.
MEASURED, NOT TRUSTED: wroteFile, fileBytes, bitsPerSample, sampleFormat, sampleRate, channels, samples and durationSeconds are read off the written file's header. It writes a temporary file beside the target and renames it over the target once complete, so a failure never leaves half a file (replacedExisting says whether one was there). soundStrips and speakers name what was heard; speakersReloaded names speakers whose sound Blender had not loaded (set after the dependency graph was built - silent until reloaded), and silentSpeakers the ones that still cannot play, with the reason; silentNote and mutedNote say when the result is silence. Blender steps every frame of the range first, to capture animated volume and moving speakers, so a heavy scene mixes slowly.
BLENDER 5.2 mixes down in a job and answers before the file exists; this waits for it (ranAsJob). A background Blender (-b) never retires that job, so it runs ONE mixdown per session and suspends every later one - refused with that reason after 3 s. Mix down in a fresh background Blender, or in one with a window.
REFUSED before anything is written: a control character or a directory as the path, an extension that is not the container's, MP3, OGG, AAC and the other containers, a FLAC format Blender would rewrite, a rate or frame outside Blender's range, an inverted range, and a path that is one of the scene's own sounds (overwriting a source while Blender reads it). Loudness is not measured here - mif_measure_audio does that.

MUXED INTO A VIDEO, NORMALIZED: the render carries the scene's audio when bl_set_render_settings has file_format='FFMPEG' and ffmpeg={'audio_codec': 'AAC' (or FLAC, PCM, ...)}; bl_normalize_audio measures this mixdown against EBU R 128 or ASWG-R001 and sets the scene's master volume so the render lands on the target; bl_extract_audio reads the video's sound back out to measure it.

SCENE (2026-10-08): scene names the scene to mix; with none, on 5.0+ the workspace's sequencer scene when one is set, else the window's (sceneSource in the reply). The mixdown runs with that scene as the context's scene, measured on 4.2.17, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1 (a second scene's strip mixed while the window showed another).
bl_bake_sound_keys:
Key a Blender property from a sound's loudness, one key per frame. Call mif_help("bl_bake_sound_keys") first.

data_path is the property from the object - scale, location, rotation_euler, data.energy - and it is keyed on the datablock that owns it (data.energy on the light, as `energy`), on every build including 5.0's layered actions. index picks one element; -1 (default) keys every element. frame_start is the frame the sound starts at (default the scene's start): frame frame_start + k holds the level of the sound's k-th 1/fps slice, at the scene's own fps. mode rms (default) is the level over each slice, peak the largest sample in it. attack_ms and release_ms (default 0) smooth it with a one-pole follower that starts from silence - how fast the level may rise and fall. The smoothed level is scaled so the loudest frame maps to max_value and silence to min_value (min_value defaults to 0, max_value to 1; a min above the max inverts the mapping), and a silent file keys min_value throughout and says so.
The keys are LINEAR and written in one pass (keyframe_points.add + foreach_set), replacing any keys already in that frame range and keeping the rest (replacedKeys). RETURNS keyCount, keysPerCurve, frameStart and frameEnd, envelopeMin and envelopeMax (linear, 0-1 of full scale) and envelopePeakFrame, the owner and the path keyed, and the sound's rate, channels and length. Read them back with bl_list_keyframes (target data for a data path) or bl_evaluate_at_frame.
REFUSED, leaving every key as it was: a missing or undecodable file, a missing object, a path that does not resolve, a property that is not a number or cannot be animated, an index past the property's length, min_value equal to max_value, a mode other than rms or peak, smoothing past 60 s, and a range the property's own limits would clamp (a speaker's volume past 1).
bl_set_render_settings:
Configure the Blender render: engine (EEVEE/CYCLES aliases resolve to whatever THIS build calls them), resolution, samples, output path and format. The sample count lives in a different property per engine and writing the wrong one is a silent no-op, so this routes it and says which property it used. Warns when there is no scene camera, since a render would then fail. COLOUR DEPTH: bl_render_info has always reported colorDepth and nothing could set it, so an 8-bit normal map or HDR pass was quantised, existed, and looked roughly right. Two things make it awkward and both are handled. The enum LIES - bl_rna.properties['color_depth'].enum_items reports 8, 10, 12, 16 and 32 for EVERY format including JPEG, measured on 3.6 and 5.0 - while Blender validates on ASSIGNMENT and raises naming the real set, so the attempt is the validation and its own message is passed through. And order matters: the format is applied FIRST, so file_format='OPEN_EXR' with color_depth=32 works in one call. If the depth is then refused, the format AND the depth are put back, because changing format clamps depth and restoring one without the other leaves half the state. eevee_raytracing turns EEVEE's SCENE raytracing on or off - eevee.use_raytracing from 4.2, use_ssr + use_ssr_refraction on 3.6 - which glass and water need to refract the scene rather than the world (measured: a glass ball's render moves ~25/255 when it is toggled); the material's refraction flags come from bl_set_material_settings. The response reports it before and after and names the property written. EEVEE AND CYCLES' OWN SETTINGS: eevee={identifier: value} and cycles={identifier: value} write any writable property of scene.eevee / scene.cycles by its RNA identifier, each checked against its own type (enums against their items, finite numbers, strict booleans) - e.g. eevee={'volumetric_tile_size': '2', 'volumetric_samples': 128} (EEVEE draws volumes on an 8-pixel grid by default, which turns smoke and fire into soft blobs) or cycles={'volume_step_rate': 0.5}. They are written last and inside the call's snapshot, so any refusal puts the whole call back; a setting this tool also names (samples, eevee_raytracing, use_denoising) is refused if given both ways. render={identifier: value} does the same for scene.render - motion blur (use_motion_blur, motion_blur_shutter) lives there from 4.2 - and refuses fps and the compositing switches, naming bl_set_frame_range / bl_set_compositing, which own them. bl_render_info(rna=True) reads them back. IMAGE AND NESTED SETTINGS: image={identifier: value} writes scene.render.image_settings - exr_codec, use_preview, color_management - and a dotted identifier reaches a nested settings struct in any group: image={'color_management': 'OVERRIDE', 'linear_colorspace_settings.name': 'ACEScg'}, eevee={'ray_tracing_options.resolution_scale': '1'} (4.2 and later); the format, depth and mode stay file_format, color_depth and color_mode.

VIDEO AND ITS SOUNDTRACK: ffmpeg={identifier: value} writes scene.render.ffmpeg the same way - format (the container: MPEG4, MKV, QUICKTIME, WEBM, ...), codec (H264, AV1, FFV1, ...), audio_codec (AAC, FLAC, PCM, OPUS, MP3, ... or NONE), audio_bitrate (kbps), audio_mixrate (Hz), audio_channels and every other setting there, each checked against this build's own items; the container is written before the codec, because Blender offers the codecs a container takes. A video with audio_codec NONE is SILENT whatever the scene plays - that is the setting that muxes the scene's audio into the render. file_format='FFMPEG' is accepted on every build: from 5.0 a format belongs to a media type and FFMPEG is refused until the media type is VIDEO, so the build is asked which media type takes the format and the answer says which it set (mediaType). after.video reports the container, codecs and carriesAudio. THE MUX, measured 2026-09-23 on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1: file_format='FFMPEG', ffmpeg={'format': 'MPEG4', 'codec': 'H264', 'audio_codec': 'AAC'}, bl_save_file, bl_render_animation - the MP4 carries the scene's audio at the scene's master volume; bl_extract_audio reads it back out, bl_normalize_audio sets that volume for a loudness target.

HAIR IN CYCLES (cycles_curves, 2026-10-05): {shape, subdivisions} on scene.cycles_curves, a struct the Cycles add-on registers outside scene.cycles - shape RIBBONS (flat strips facing the camera) or THICK (3D curves), and THICK_LINEAR from 5.0 (measured: offered on 5.0.1 and 5.2.2, refused with the enum on 4.2.23 and 4.4.0). Written and read back like the other groups; bl_render_info {rna: true} lists it; refused by name when the Cycles add-on is off.

THE CYCLES TEXTURE CACHE, 5.2 AND LATER (texture_cache, 2026-10-05): GENERATE runs render.generate_texture_cache, which writes a tiled, mipmapped .tx file for every image the shader nodes use into a blender_tx folder beside the image; CLEAR deletes them. The reply's textureCache block names txFilesWritten / txFilesRemoved and useTextureCache (render {use_texture_cache: true} is the switch a render reads; on by default on 5.2). texture_cache_memory=true with GENERATE renders a 64 px, 1-sample CPU preview with the cache off and then on and replies memoryMB {cacheOff, cacheOn} - the largest Mem/Peak Cycles reported; the render settings are put back and Render Result holds the last preview. Measured on 5.2.2: a 2048 px texture on a plane peaked at 17 MB off and 1 MB on. Refused by name on 5.0 and earlier, which have neither the operators nor the switch.

RULE - EEVEE BOUNCE AND STEPS, where the recipes disagree (2026-10-06). Two step counts are easy to confuse: Fast GI's (fast_gi_step_count, 1-64, default 8) and the shadows' (shadow_step_count, 1-16) - "raise the steps to the maximum of 16" is the SHADOW maximum. Write the value and read `applied` back: the clamp says which count a number belongs to (100 reads 64 on Fast GI, 64 reads 16 on shadows - test_blender_workflow_rules R101, on 4.2-5.2). What decides the values: a still can take the maximum (rays 16, steps 64), an animation the cheap pairs (rays and steps 2 and 8, or 4 and 16 - measured once at about 30 s and 45 s a frame against 193 s), and an interior with walls wants a baked volume probe carrying most of the bounce, with Fast GI used sparingly (distance 1 to 2) or Fast GI plus screen tracing and a coarse probe (about 4 points per axis). Compare render seconds (bl_render_still's elapsed time) on the shot before trusting a recipe.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): ffmpeg {codec: H265} on 4.4+; fileFormat AVIF, image {exr_codec: HTJ2K} and eevee {direct_light_intensity, indirect_light_intensity} on 5.2 - each refused by name, with the values the build has, where it lacks them, and every earlier write in the call put back. The 5.2 texture cache switches are test_blender_texture_cache's.
bl_extract_audio:
Write a file's audio - a rendered video's soundtrack or any sound file - to a WAV, with an optional gain. Call mif_help("bl_extract_audio") first.

filepath is decoded by Blender's own audio library (aud) through its FFmpeg: a video's soundtrack (MP4, MKV, MOV, WebM), WAV, FLAC, OGG, MP3. out_path is the WAV written (it must end in .wav and cannot be the source), bit_format S16 (default), S24 or S32 integer PCM, at the source's own rate and channels. gain_db (default 0, -120 to +60) is added to every sample; a sample it pushes past full scale is clipped and counted in clippedSamples - to raise a level safely, bl_normalize_audio computes the gain against the true peak.

WHAT IT IS FOR: reading a rendered video's sound back so it can be measured (mif_measure_audio) - a mux is only proved by the file - and writing a normalized copy of a mixdown. Measured 2026-09-23 on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1: an AAC track read out of a one-second MP4 as 48 kHz stereo at the level the scene rendered it. The file is read in whole-second chunks and written beside the target, then renamed over it; every number in the answer (sampleRate, channels, bitsPerSample, frames, durationSeconds) is read off the written header, beside the source's own specs, peakDbfs after the gain, and framesNote when the decoder delivered fewer frames than it reported. A video rendered with audio_codec NONE has no soundtrack and is refused by name. It reads through aud, not the mixdown job, so it runs any number of times in a 5.2 background session.
bl_normalize_audio:
Normalize the Blender scene's audio or a file to EBU R 128 or ASWG-R001 loudness without passing the true-peak ceiling: a normalized WAV, and the scene volume a video render reads. Call mif_help("bl_normalize_audio") first.

TARGETS, read in the standards (2026-09-23): 'ebu_r128' - EBU R 128 (2023): -23.0 LUFS, true peak at most -1 dBTP; 'aswg_home' - ASWG-R001 home platforms: -24 (+/-2) LKFS, -1 dBTP; 'aswg_portable' - ASWG-R001 portable platforms: -18 (+/-2) LKFS, -1 dBTP; or a number of LUFS (-70 to 0). true_peak overrides the ceiling (-20 to 0 dBTP) - lower it for lossy delivery, where the encoder adds peaks.

WHAT IT DOES: with no filepath it mixes the scene down (bl_mixdown_audio, the session's one mixdown on a 5.2 background Blender), measures it (integrated loudness and true peak, the meter mif_measure_audio uses), and computes ONE linear gain: target minus measured, unless that would lift the true peak past the ceiling - then the ceiling wins, peakLimited is true and the result sits under the target by the amount it says. Nothing is compressed or limited. The gain is then applied without mixing again: out_path gets a normalized WAV (bl_extract_audio with that gain), measured and checked to land within 0.2 LU of the prediction and under the ceiling (output.verified, output.withinStandard); and set_scene_volume (default on when the scene was mixed, off for a filepath) multiplies the scene's master volume by it and reads it back, so the next video render comes out on target. With a filepath (WAV, FLAC or a video's soundtrack) the file is measured instead.

THE NORMALIZED MUX: bl_normalize_audio(); bl_set_render_settings(file_format='FFMPEG', ffmpeg={'format': 'MPEG4', 'codec': 'H264', 'audio_codec': 'AAC'}); bl_save_file; bl_render_animation and poll bl_render_status; then bl_extract_audio the video and mif_measure_audio the WAV. The scene volume's range is 0 to 100 on every build, so a quiet mix is raised up to +40 dB; a gain past it is refused with the file route offered instead. ASWG-R001 asks for at least 30 minutes of representative gameplay to be measured - the answer says how much was.

MEASURED 2026-09-23 on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1 (tools/test_blender_audio_mux.py, 18/18 on each): a 1 kHz tone strip mixed down at -30.16 LUFS; the gain +7.16 dB; the normalized WAV -23.00 LUFS; the scene volume 1.0 -> 2.2803; then rendered, read back with bl_extract_audio and measured - MKV + FLAC -23.01 LUFS, MP4 + H264 + AAC -23.01 LUFS, the tone starting on its frame to the sample. Identical on all five builds.
bl_build_tree:
Build a tree in Blender with real geometry leaves - one object with a bark slot and a leaf slot, its pivot at the trunk's base, the same tree for the same seed. Call mif_help("bl_build_tree") first.

WHAT IT MAKES: one mesh object in meters at the height asked for - slot 0 bark and slot 1 leaves (materials <name>_Bark and <name>_Leaves, node materials for Blender's own renders), a UV layer UVMap, a color attribute Col on face corners and, with collision on, a UCX_<name>_00 convex hull round the trunk below the crown, drawn as a wire and hidden from renders. The pivot is the trunk's base at the object's origin, Z up; the root flare reaches rootDepthM below it (about 3% of the height), so the tree sits into uneven ground. Every branch is its own closed-tip tube, not welded into its parent; bark UVs tile along each stem at 0.6 m per unit, round the girth and along it alike; each leaf maps the whole 0-1 UV square, stalk at v 0 and tip at v 1. The hull is a separate object at the tree's transform: move, export and delete the two together.
PRESETS are tree forms, not species: broadleafRound (the default - 12 m, a round crown on a trunk forking into three leaders, 100000 ovate leaves of 12 cm), broadleafTall (18 m, a tall crown on two leaders, 110000 lanceolate leaves of 11 cm), conifer (20 m, conical, drooping tiers, 160000 needle sprays of 13 cm), youngTree (5 m, 20000 ovate leaves of 8 cm), shrub (2.2 m, nine stems from the ground, 25000 round leaves of 5 cm, no hull by default), pyramidal (14 m, one leader to the top, level limbs drooping low and rising high, 19000 lobed leaves of 14 cm - a pin oak's or a linden's form), vase (13 m, a low fork into four spreading limbs, 10500 pinnate leaves of 20 cm - a honey locust's, an elm's) and oval (10 m, five steep leaders, a dense upright crown, 75000 ovate leaves of 7.5 cm - a callery pear's). A species is a form plus its leaves: pick the preset, then set leaf_shape and leaf_size (a London plane is broadleafRound with palmate leaves of about 19 cm; a linden pyramidal with cordate leaves of about 9 cm).
PARAMETERS: name (default Tree; at most 56 characters with collision on, so UCX_<name>_00 fits the 63 characters Blender 3.6-4.4 keep; a taken name is suffixed, and nameWasSuffixed says so). seed (0 or more, default 1): the same seed and parameters give the same tree, vertex for vertex, on a given Blender. height (0.5-60 m): the whole tree's, top leaf included. trunk_radius: the base radius before the flare, by default the preset's share of the height (1.8-4.2%). levels (1-3): branch levels below the trunk. crown_shape: conical, spherical, hemispherical, cylindrical, taperedCylindrical, flame, inverseConical or tendFlame - the envelope the first-level branches follow, by the height each starts at. leaf_shape: ovate, lanceolate, round (6 triangles, folded along the midrib), needle (a spray of three blades, 6 triangles), palmate (a plane's or a maple's outline, 26 triangles), lobed (an oak's, deep sinuses, 32), cordate (a linden's heart, 12) or pinnate (a compound leaf: a rachis and 7 pairs of leaflets, 58; each leaflet maps the whole 0-1 square). The outlined leaves crease along the midrib, each half triangulated on its own. leaf_size (0.5-60 cm): the leaf's length; each leaf varies by up to 25% either way. leaf_count (0-400000; 0 is a bare tree). leaf_clusters (default false): true groups the leaves into twig-and-leaf clusters of about 80 triangles - a 6-triangle twig carrying as many leaves of leaf_shape as fit (12 ovate, lanceolate, round or needle, 6 cordate, 3 palmate, 2 lobed, 1 pinnate), each leaf keeping its own 0-1 UV square and its own R value, the twig a UV sliver at u 0.49-0.51, v 0-0.016 - fewer, richer parts than single leaves; leaf_count stays the number of leaves, so a tree has leaf_count / leaves_per_cluster clusters, rounded up. leaves_per_cluster (1-16, only with leaf_clusters) overrides the count. leaf_color and leaf_color2 ([r, g, b], linear 0-1): the two greens vertex color R picks between, per leaf. bark_color ([r, g, b], linear 0-1). collision (default on, off for shrub). location and rotation ([x, y, z] or {x, y, z}), collection.
VERTEX COLOR Col (BYTE_COLOR, face corners) carries what a wind and variation material needs without textures: R a random value per leaf (0.5 on bark), G the wind weight - 0 at the trunk's base, rising along every branch, 1 at each leaf's tip - and B a phase shared by a main branch and everything on it, so a limb sways as one. A is 1. Each byte is the value x 255, stored in sRGB space as a painted mask is: the FBX that bl_export_mesh writes carries the numbers, and Unreal's VertexColor node reads them as written. Blender's own shading and bl_mesh_stats read them linearized - 0.5 reads 0.216 there.
RETURNS the object's name, type, collection, location and rotation, preset, seed, heightM, rootDepthM, trunkRadiusM, crownWidthM, stems per level, leaves and trianglesPerLeaf, clusters (count, leavesPerCluster, trianglesPerCluster, twigTriangles, spanM) or null, vertices, faces, triangles (bark, leaves, total), materialSlots, uvMap, colorAttribute, collisionHull (object, topM, vertices, volume) or null with collisionNote saying why, pivot and elapsedSeconds. The hull is audited as bl_create_collision_hull's is - closed, manifold and convex - and one that fails is removed rather than kept; a hull whose name is taken is not made.
MEASURED 2026-09-27: the default tree is 747,610 triangles (600,000 leaf, 147,610 bark) and builds in 6-15 s; a young tree in about 1 s. Checked on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1.
REFUSED before anything is created: an unknown preset, crown or leaf shape, a blank name or one with a control character, a negative or fractional seed, a height outside 0.5-60 m, a trunk wider than a quarter of the height, levels outside 1-3, a leaf outside 0.5-60 cm, more than 400000 leaves, leaves_per_cluster without leaf_clusters or outside 1-16, a color that is not three numbers from 0 to 1, and a collection that does not exist.
bl_build_rock:
Build a rock in Blender - a boulder, a slab or a cliff face - as one mesh with its own stone material, sized in centimeters, its pivot at the bottom center, the same rock for the same seed. Call mif_help("bl_build_rock") first.

WHAT IT MAKES: one mesh object at the size asked for (size is the mesh's bounds, sunk part included), one material slot <name>_Stone (a procedural stone node material for Blender's own renders), UV layers UVMap and UVLightmap in that order, a color attribute Col on face corners and, with collision on, a UCX_<name>_00 convex hull (at most 48 vertices, 96 on a cliff) drawn as a wire and hidden from renders. The pivot is the bottom center at the object's origin, Z up; the rock reaches sink (cm) below it so it sits into the ground. A cliff's face looks down -Y; its back is flat, for setting against a slope.
KINDS: boulder (default 140 x 110 x 85 cm, 30000 triangles) - fracture planes bent so faces curve and edges wander, a few large faces, small chipped facets at the corners, a flatter base; slab (240 x 170 x 55 cm, 30000) - two to four strata, each set back by its own amount, bedding planes between them, a top layer broken off across part of it, fine laminae on the rim, joints across the top; cliff (800 x 300 x 600 cm, 120000) - layers of very different thickness, thin ones eroded back and thick ones standing out as ledges, vertical joints that do not line up from layer to layer, the ends turning back and down into the slope.
PARAMETERS: name (default Rock; at most 56 characters with collision on). kind. seed (0-2147483647, default 1): the same seed and parameters give the same rock, vertex for vertex, on a given Blender. size ([length, width, height] in cm, each 5-5000, at most 40 to 1). triangles (500-1000000): the count the rock is reduced to by collapse decimation, which keeps triangles on edges and ledges; the dense end is for Nanite. sink (cm, 0 to half the height; default 6% of the height for a boulder, 8% for a slab, 3% for a cliff). weathering (0 fresh-broken and sharp to 1 worn round; default 0.2, cliff 0.25). strata (default on for slab and cliff, off for boulder). stone_color and stone_color2 ([r, g, b], linear 0-1): the stone's dark and light tones. moss (0-1, default 0): moss on up-facing exposed faces in the preview material. collision (default on). location ([x, y, z] or {x, y, z}) in METERS - Blender units, not centimeters like size and sink. rotation ([x, y, z] or {x, y, z}) in RADIANS, XYZ Euler. collection.
UNITS: size and sink are centimeters; location is meters and rotation radians, written to the object as given - so a rock 2 m to the side is location [2, 0, 0] and size [140, 110, 85].
UVs: one smart unwrap. UVLightmap is its 0-1 layout without overlaps (uv_info reports it lightmapReady); UVMap is the same islands scaled to one unit per meter of surface, for a tiling rock texture.
VERTEX COLOR Col (BYTE_COLOR, face corners), each byte value x 255 in sRGB space, so bl_export_mesh's FBX carries the values and Unreal's VertexColor node reads them as written: R cavity (0 on open faces, toward 1 in cracks and hollows, from the rock's own distance field), G up-facing and exposed (where moss or dust settles), B ground contact (1 at the pivot's height, 0 from about 12% of the height up), A a value per stratum or block for tint variation (0.5 on a boulder). Blender reads R, G and B back linearized; A is not color-managed.
TIME: a default boulder builds in about 6 s, a slab in 10-13 s, a cliff in 25-35 s.
bl_build_plant:
Build ground cover in Blender - a grass tuft, a fern, a broadleaf plant, a bush, a tile of lawn or a piece of clipped hedge - as one mesh of real geometry blades and leaves, sized in centimeters, its pivot at the base, the same plant for the same seed. Call mif_help("bl_build_plant") first.

WHAT IT MAKES: one mesh object whose every blade and leaf is geometry (no alpha cards, no opacity mask), a UV layer UVMap in which each blade and leaf spans the whole 0-1 square (base at v 0, tip at v 1), and a color attribute Col on face corners. Materials are the ones bl_build_tree makes: <name>_Leaves, and for a bush <name>_Bark first (slot 0 stems, slot 1 leaves); a hedge has <name>_Bark, <name>_Leaves and <name>_Litter (its fallen leaves, in browns); a turf tile with weeds has a slot per weed after <name>_Leaves. The pivot is the base at the object's origin, Z up; blades and stems start sinkCm below it so the plant sits into the ground. No collision hull: ground cover is walked through. No lightmap UV: foliage is not lightmapped.
KINDS and defaults: grass (35 cm tall, 60 cm spread, 60 blades, about 1,100 triangles) - tapered, V-creased blades, the outer ones leaning further out; fern (55 cm, 130 cm, 10 fronds, about 3,500) - arching fronds with paired pinnae, longest a third of the way up; plant (30 cm, 60 cm, 14 leaves, about 500) - a rosette of stalked leaves, inner ones standing and outer ones lying out; bush (110 cm, 130 cm, 2000 leaves, about 22,000) - stems from the ground forking twice, leaved on their outer two thirds. turf (9 cm, a 100 cm tile, 3000 blades, 15,000 triangles: 5 a blade) - a square of lawn that TILES: blade roots fill the square by a density that repeats with it and is the same under a quarter turn, so copies laid edge to edge, each at any quarter turn (turning them hides the repeat), show no seam, and blades lean over the edges as over the next tile; its thin and lush places are 20-70 cm across, never as wide as the tile, so the tile's repeat does not show (larger wear belongs to the ground material); the blades grow in shoots, 1-4 leaves from one crown fanning out and curving outward, as lawn grass does; a share lean far or lie where trodden (a trodden shoot as one), more as height grows. hedge (120 cm clipped, 60 cm thick at the foot, a 100 cm piece, about 12,000 leaves of 10 triangles and the stems: about 170,000 triangles a meter) - a privet or box hedge as sheared: a row of plants about 30 cm apart (two staggered rows past 45 cm thick), each 3-5 stems from the ground forking into branches and twigs that reach the leaves; the leaves in a shell a few centimeters deep under the clipped face, turned out and up to the light, in soft patches of tone and paler toward the top; inside, a thicket of fine dead twigs with brown leaves caught in it, so the hedge is opaque and dark, not a hollow shell; the foot drawn in and thinning out, stems showing; the face's top edges rounded and the sides cut a tenth narrower at the top, with a centimeter or two of the shears' unevenness; fallen leaves along the foot. A middle piece TILES along X: its plants stand a whole number of steps apart, its twigs reach past its ends as the next piece's reach into it, and the unevenness fades out at its ends, so pieces of any seeds laid end to end meet with no seam. For a hedge, height is the clipped top, width the thickness at the foot, and it is NOT fitted: new shoots stand out of the outline. For turf, width is the tile's side and height the longest blade, and the tile is NOT fitted to them as the other kinds are (the answer's tileCm is the step to lay tiles at, widthCm the blades' spread past it).
PARAMETERS: name (default Plant). kind. seed (0-2147483647, default 1): the same seed and parameters give the same plant, vertex for vertex, on a given Blender. height (cm, 2-600, the top) and width (cm, the wider plan side, 2-1000): the plant is fitted to both, centered on the pivot; the defaults are each kind's grown proportions, and a height and width far from them stretch the form. count: blades for grass (1-400), fronds for a fern (1-40), leaves for a plant (1-60) or a bush (50-20000), blades on the whole tile for turf (100-100000); the triangle count scales with it. bare (turf only, 0-0.9, default 0): the share of the tile left as bare, soft-edged patches (worn ground), from a second repeating field, so patches run on across tiles laid at the SAME turn (that field is not the same under a turn: four-fold patches look made, so a tile with bare patches is laid unturned); the blades left keep the tile's density, so count x (1 - bare) are made (the answer's blades). weeds (turf only, 0-0.6, default 0): the share of the tile its broadleaf lawn weeds cover - white clover in patches 30 cm to a meter across (about 1,200 three-leaflet leaves a square meter in a patch's middle, on stalks up into the grass), broadleaf plantain (a flat rosette of broad oval leaves on channelled stalks) and dandelion (a flat rosette of narrow leaves with teeth pointing back toward the root, cut deep or shallow); the blades thin out under them (nearly bare under a rosette, about two thirds under clover) and that share comes off the blades made. Each weed lies whole where it grows and reaches over the tile's edge as blades do, so a tile with weeds still meets neighbors at any quarter turn. weed_mix ([clover, plantain, dandelion], shares of 0 or more, not all 0; default [0.5, 0.3, 0.2]) splits weeds among them. flowers (0-1, default 0): clover heads over the patches and 1-3 yellow heads on that share of the dandelions. Each weed of the mix gets its own material slot after <name>_Leaves - <name>_Clover, <name>_Plantain, <name>_Dandelion, then <name>_Flowers (vertex color R near 0 a clover head, near 1 a dandelion's) - with preview colors: the look is set on those slots. The weeds come after the blades in the vertex order. The answer's weedsGrown counts the patches, rosettes, leaves and heads and each slot's triangles. weeds, weed_mix and flowers are refused off turf, out of range, or (the last two) without weeds. length (hedge only, cm, 20-1000, default 100): the piece's run along X, the step to lay pieces at. ends (hedge only): none (default; a middle piece that tiles), start (clipped at -X), end (clipped at +X) or both (a hedge on its own) - a clipped end is cut square with rounded corners and nothing reaches past it. shag (hedge only, 0-1, default 0.3): the growth since the last cut - 0 freshly sheared, 1 a summer's shoots standing up to a third of a meter out of the face (upright on the top, arching out of the sides), their leaves in opposite pairs each a quarter turn on from the last, paler (R toward 1). leaf_length (hedge only, cm, 1-8, default 4): privet's ellipse at about 4, box's small oval at about 2, blended between. A hedge's count, unless given, is its clipped face's area in leaves twice over, and is refused past 400,000 (a small leaf on a large hedge); the answer's hedge block counts plants, stems, branches, twigs, inner twigs, shoots, leaves, litter and each slot's triangles. These four are refused off a hedge, and out of range. leaf_color and leaf_color2 ([r, g, b], linear 0-1): the two greens vertex color R picks between. location and rotation ([x, y, z] or {x, y, z}), collection.
VERTEX COLOR Col (BYTE_COLOR, face corners), each byte value x 255 in sRGB space as bl_build_tree writes: R a random value per blade, frond or leaf (0.5 on a bush's stems), G the wind weight - 0 at the base rising to 1 at the tips - B a phase shared by a blade, a frond or a stem and its leaves, A 1 - except on a hedge, where A is how open the corner lies (1 on the clipped face and outside it, toward 0.1 twenty centimeters in, less at the foot): an ambient occlusion a material can read.
bl_create_collision_hull:
Build a convex hull collision MESH named for Unreal's UCX_<RenderMesh>_## convention. NOT bl_add_collision, which is a rigid-body PHYSICS setting evaluated by Blender's own simulation - same word, unrelated job, and the addon had that one and not this. THE RECIPE EVERY TUTORIAL GIVES IS WRONG AND LOOKS RIGHT: bm.from_mesh(source) then convex_hull then delete geom_interior returns, on Suzanne, the SAME 66 vertices as a correct hull plus 51 non-manifold edges, 4 boundary edges, Euler 16 instead of 2, 22 convexity violations and an 8% inflated volume, with nothing raised - measured on 4.4.0 and 5.0.1. This builds from POINTS ONLY and then AUDITS: closed, manifold, no loose verts, Euler 2, positive volume, and genuine convexity tested by checking every vertex against every face plane. A hull failing any of those is DELETED and refused, because a broken hull imports, looks like collision, and things fall through it. Degenerate input produces silent garbage rather than an exception - collinear points give an empty mesh, coplanar points a zero-volume sheet - which is why the audit refuses instead of warning. max_vertices simplifies to a hull that still ENCLOSES every point - the exact hull's own face planes, each added where the simplified hull sticks out most - never by decimating (a decimated hull is no longer convex: 24 violations at ratio 0.1) or by merging points (merged points lie inside, so the hull shrank and the mesh poked through it - 12 cm on a bl_build_rock rock at 40 vertices). Each hulls[] row's sourceOutsideM says how far any point lies outside. A name collision is REFUSED, not uniquified - Blender's .001 suffix survives FBX export and makes the engine parse the base name wrongly. The UCX naming convention itself is engine-side and is NOT verified here.

BOXES, ONE HULL PER PART, AND A HULL LIMIT - the few simple primitives a kit piece collides with. shape='box' makes the 8-corner box of the points' bounds in the hull's own axes (the source's local axes, or world with world_space): 6 faces, audited like a hull; max_vertices beside it is refused. per_part=true makes one hull per LOOSE PART (vertices joined by edges), numbered from index up - UCX_<object>_00, _01, ... - so a wall with a doorway built from separate jambs and a lintel keeps its doorway, where one hull round the whole wall fills it. A part that encloses no volume (a flat card, a single face, fewer than 4 vertices) gets no hull and is listed in skippedParts with the reason; a mesh whose every part is flat is refused. max_hulls (per_part only) caps the count: past it the parts are merged two at a time, always the pair whose combined box grows least, so touching and nearby pieces join first, and each group gets one hull round all its parts - which covers the space between them. partsPerHull says which parts each hull holds. Every name is checked before anything is made, a taken one refuses the whole call, and a hull failing its audit removes every hull the call made: a refusal always means NOTHING was created. EVERY ANSWER NOW CARRIES hulls[] (one row per hull: object, parts, vertices, simplifiedTo, audit, withinEngineLimit), hullCount and primitiveCount; without per_part the rest of the answer is as before. name beside per_part, max_hulls without per_part and max_hulls below 1 are refused. UE's importer reads each UCX_ mesh as one convex element; the UBX_ box prefix is prefix='UBX_'. vertex_group | vertex_indices | selected (2026-10-06): a hull or box round that subset only (a head-only box); subsetVertices counts them. Not with per_part.
bl_mesh_quality:
Measure the objectively checkable things that get an asset REJECTED from a store: ngons, non-manifold edges, loose verts and edges, zero-area faces, unapplied scale and rotation, empty material slots, UV loops outside the 0-1 tile, and texel density spread across faces. Returns every NUMBER plus `concerns`, which lists only defects with a defensible objective threshold - it says NOTHING about whether the asset looks good and does not pretend to. READ notMeasured BEFORE TRUSTING A CLEAN REPORT: a mesh with no UV layer gets no UV verdict at all, which is an absence of data rather than a pass, and an empty concerns list beside a skipped check is not a clean bill of health. Measures the mesh AS AUTHORED, not the evaluated result, because that is what exports and what a store inspects - a subdivision modifier would make every ngon and density figure describe something the file does not contain. texel_density_for takes a size or [w, h]. game_ready {triangleBudget, allowNgons, uvOneTile, allowFloating, allowWaste} adds gameReady: pass or fail, each reason a measured number with its limit and the call that fixes it, or `choices` where only you can tell: floating parts, and triangles over the size class's number, the budget when no triangleBudget is given. Parts 2% or more of the longest side away, slivers under 10 micrometers, near-zero tangents and wasted faces fail it: 90% flat with no painted colors, or half out of any ray's reach.

CONVENTIONS - HOW A PIECE HOLDS TO THE WAY GAME PIECES ARE USUALLY BUILT, checked before export instead of after import. conventions=true (or kind, or module_cm, alone) adds a `conventions` block; checks and concerns are unchanged and none of these findings is added to concerns. Every finding carries what was MEASURED, the convention it is held to, and `follows` - true, false, or null where the convention does not decide: sizeClass (by the longest side: small under 100 cm, medium 100-300, large 300 and over); kind (wall, floor or prop read off the bounds - a floor both sides at least 1 m and under a tenth as thick, a wall at least 1 m long and tall and under a tenth as thick as it is long - or given as kind); pivot (where the origin sits, z bottom/center/top/below/above/inside and xy corner/side/centered/inside/outside, with pivotInBounds: a floor on a bottom corner, a wall on a bottom corner or the bottom of a face, a small prop centered or bottom-center, any other prop bottom-center - bl_set_origin bottomCorner, bottomSide or bottom sets each); uvLayers (UV0 for the texture and the LAST layer for the lightmap, found by a lightmap-like name or by position, lightmapIsLast and lightmapReady as uv_info reads it; one layer is null, because Unreal's importer can generate the lightmap from UV0); module (with module_cm: each long side's modules and offModuleCm, a side shorter than one module called a filler); triangles (the count and per square meter of the box's surface against the usual range for the size class, and where it falls - above is ordinary on a Nanite mesh); materialSlots (one is usual, and a slot still named a modeling tool's default - Material, lambert1, Default - was never named); thickness (walls and floors: a single plane has none and is seen from one side only); transform (scale and rotation applied); collision (UCX_/UBX_/USP_/UCP_<name>_NN hulls found, each under 255 vertices; none is null, since collision can be made on import); name (SM_<Words>_NNa). notes lists a sentence for each finding that differs, followCount and differCount count them. A convention is how pieces are usually built, not a defect: a piece can have a reason to differ. kind other than auto/wall/floor/prop, a module_cm that is not a finite number above 0, and kind or module_cm beside conventions=false are refused.

TANGENTS AND NEAR-ZERO UV AREA. checks.uv carries nearZeroUvAreaFaces, nearZeroUvAreaFaceIndices and nearZeroUvAreaThreshold (1e-9) for the judged layer. checks.tangents is always read from UV channel 0, the one Unreal builds tangents from, whichever layer uvLayer judges: nearZeroVertexInstances, vertices and faces predict Unreal's 'has some nearly zero tangents ... (Tolerance of 1E-4)' import warning (MikkTSpace via calc_tangents, plus mikktspace's rule that a vertex instance with no UV area around it gets a zero tangent - see bl_uv_info). A non-zero count adds a concern: Unreal warns on import and shades those vertices wrongly.

BOUNDARY LOOPS AS DATA (boundary_loops=true, 2026-10-04): the reply gains boundaryLoops - each open boundary loop (a connected run of one-face edges) with its edges, vertices, closed (false where a bow-tie vertex joins two), length, centroid and box in WORLD units, biggest first, 50 listed and loopCount exact. bone names a bone (armature: its armature, default the mesh's Armature modifier's object or its armature parent) and adds each loop's span along that bone's REST axis - from, to and span in world units from the bone's head: a cuff ring spans about 0, a cuff torn open along the forearm its torn length. WHY: bl_mesh_quality counted boundary edges, and finding which loop was a torn cuff (17.7 and 13.5 cm along the forearms of a draped hoodie) took a recorded script. bone without boundary_loops, armature without bone, an unknown bone, a non-armature and a bone with no armature to find are refused. POLES: poles true adds interior vertices of valence 3 and of 5 or more, with their indices (200 listed) and a count per valence - a boundary vertex is not a pole. JOINT RINGS: joint_rings {bone, armature, range (0.1 world units)} counts the closed edge loops that go round the bone's axis with their centre within range of its head, each with its vertex count and its distance along the bone - a clean bend wants closed rings at the neck base, the shoulders and the leg roots. An open loop (through a pole or along a boundary) is not a ring. texel_density_for takes a size or [w, h]. With [w, h] each face's density is sqrt(uv area x w x h / world area) and forTextureSize echoes [w, h].

FACES THAT POINT INTO A BODY (2026-10-05): facing_against - a body's name, or {body, bandStep (default 0.1 m), reach (default 0.2 m)} - adds facingAgainst: for each face within reach of the body (the mesh as its base under its transform, the body as it evaluates), whether its normal points toward the nearest body point; facesMeasured, inward, inwardShare, the first 50 inwardFaces and bands by height. A rebuilt cuff and hem band that faced inward shipped and showed as holes in an asset viewer under a one-sided material (a recorded check: 25.4% inward before the fix, 6.0% after - the folded-under edges, which face the body by design). Flip them with bl_clean_mesh flip_normals. Nothing within reach is refused. WINDING (2026-10-06): windingFlippedEdges counts edges whose two faces walk them the same way - one face of each pair points the other way, which a one-sided material draws see-through (a revolve that turned faces away from its profile's centroid left 20 % of a tapered can's wall facing in, closed and manifold, and nothing here flagged it); insideOutParts lists closed parts whose faces agree and whose signed volume is negative - the whole part faces in. Both are added to concerns. Measured: a cube with one face reversed has 4 such edges; a cube wound inward is one inside-out part.

FOLDS (2026-10-06): flipped_against - the name of a copy kept before a reshape, with the same faces vertex for vertex - adds flippedAgainst: faces whose normal now points against the same face's normal in the copy (flipped, share, the first 50 flippedFaces). A copy with other faces is refused.

A KIT (2026-10-06): collection in place of object measures every mesh in the collection and its child collections (UCX_/UBX_/USP_/UCP_ hulls listed as hulls, other types as skipped) with conventions on - kind, module_cm, texel_density_for and uv_layer apply to each piece - and answers pieces (each piece's conventions differs, notes, concerns and texelDensityMedian, as bl_mesh_quality says of it alone), unmeasured (a piece that could not be measured, with why) and kit: texelDensity (the pieces' medians, lowest and highest, follows when within 1.25 x - pieces of one kit meet at seams), namesClashingWithoutCase (one asset in Unreal), differByFinding (each finding that differs, with its pieces), piecesFollowingAll and notes. A collection with no mesh piece, or one beside object, the one-mesh reports or conventions false, is refused.

THICKNESS (thickness=True or {method BOX|MEAN|LOCAL|ALL (default ALL), samples (2000), seed (0)}, thickness_min_cm). The piece's thickness in centimeters three ways, from the mesh as authored in world space: boxCm, the thin side of the bounds (exact for a slab, blind to a hollow); meanCm, twice the volume over the surface area of a CLOSED mesh (null, with meanNote, when an edge is open or shared by more than two faces); and the local thickness - rays from area-weighted random surface points, inward along the reversed face normal, to the first far-side hit - as localMinCm, localP5Cm (5th percentile), thinnestAt [x, y, z] and hitRate (a low rate means an open or non-manifold piece). The tool never picks the threshold: follows is held against thickness_min_cm when given (judged by localP5Cm, else meanCm, else boxCm - judgedBy says which), and null without one, because the figure a renderer needs depends on its tracing mode and settings. Measured: a 2 m cube 200 / 66.667 / 200; a kit floor 7 / under 7 / about 7.

GAME READY (game_ready {triangleBudget, allowNgons, uvOneTile}, or true): a pass or fail for a game engine, read off the checks this tool takes anyway - no second checker. Each reason in gameReady.reasons is {check, measured, limit, why, fix}: triangles over triangleBudget (fix bl_dissolve_mesh_elements mode LIMITED, then bl_decimate_mesh targetTris), ngons unless allowNgons (bl_clean_mesh triangulate), nonManifoldEdges (bl_clean_mesh mergeDistance with dissolveDegenerate), looseGeometry (bl_clean_mesh removeLoose), uvMissing (bl_uv_unwrap SMART), uvOutOfBounds only with uvOneTile, for a bake or an atlas (bl_uv_unwrap SMART on that layer, replace), scaleNotApplied (bl_apply_transform scale), inconsistentNormals - wound-opposite edges plus inside-out parts (bl_clean_mesh recalcNormals) - and degenerateFaces (bl_clean_mesh dissolveDegenerate). Each fix's args name the object and can be sent as given; check again after, since one fix can bring back another reason. measured has every number whether it failed or not; notJudged lists what was not held to a limit (triangles with no budget, n-gons under allowNgons, UVs outside 0-1 without uvOneTile - right on a tiling texture - boundary edges - right on a sheet - and unapplied modifiers: the base mesh is judged). A mesh with no faces, or one in edit mode, is refused rather than passed; so is game_ready with collection.

GAME READY, SECOND PASS (1.4, 2026-10-30) - efficiency, not only validity. With no triangleBudget the budget is the top of the usual triangle range for the mesh's size class - the same numbers as conventions' triangles for the size (small under 100 cm: 1070, medium to 300 cm: 3364, large: 25652) - and gameReady.triangleBudgetFrom says where it came from; a Nanite mesh past it is ordinary, so give triangleBudget to judge it by another number. A given number is a ceiling: a pass under it past the usual top says so in notJudged, with both numbers. Three more reasons: floatingParts - face-connected parts under 10% of the largest part's surface that touch no other part (no vertex within 1/10000 of the mesh's longest side of another part, no face crossing one) and stand 2% or more of the longest side away, or a group of touching parts under 10% of a body holding over half the surface and standing nearest it, 1% of the longest side and 5% of the group's own size away, or 3% whatever its size, or 0.4% and 20% of the thickness of a solid at least 0.5% of the longest side thick, with the gap measured exactly; no fix is named, only `choices`; sliverFaces - faces narrower than 1/10000 of the mesh's longest side and 100 or more times longer than wide (the needles a cut or a triangulated n-gon leaves), fixed by clean_mesh dissolveDegenerate at the distance named; nearZeroTangents - checks.tangents' vertex instances Unreal gives nearly zero tangents, fixed by the sliver fix when they are all on slivers, else by a fresh uv_unwrap. Measured on a one-prompt castle tower that passed the first verdict: 8 sliver faces under 3.4 micrometers wide, 18 near-zero tangent vertex instances, 0 floating parts among 17; clean_mesh dissolveDegenerate 1e-05 cleared both and it passed at 1598 triangles (budget 25652, large).
bl_build_kit_piece:
Build a modular kit piece in Blender - a wall (with a door or window opening), a floor, a pillar, or a roll-up shutter or door leaf for a wall's opening - on a module grid, with bevels, trim, a lightmap UV layer and UCX_ hulls. Call mif_help("bl_build_kit_piece") first.

NO TWO FACES Z-FIGHT. The builder keeps the rules that stop kit pieces flickering in the engine (from use; checked with bl_coplanar_overlaps, which finds no visible overlap on any kind it builds, nor between a door wall and its door leaf or shutter): parts butt and never overlap - the plinth, its band and an opening's casing are boards on each face that butt the slab with square backs, not boxes run through it, whose bottoms lay in the slab's bottom plane; anything sitting on a face stands 2 mm or more proud of it (1 mm still fights at a distance) - the plinth stops 3 mm short of the wall's ends, the kick plate stands 2 mm off the leaf, the drip cap 3 mm off the wall; the lining stands in the reveal between the casings, so no part's face lands in the wall's planes at the opening. For pieces you assemble yourself the same rules apply: two parts of one kind in one plane (braces from one point, consecutive stair stringers) offset 3-4 mm, and a part set into a wall (a plinth, a band) cut 3 mm wider than the wall's openings so its reveals do not land in the wall's planes.

WHAT IT MAKES: one mesh object in meters, built from centimeters. Sides are counted in modules (module, default 100 cm): a wall's length and height (default 4 x 3, 400 x 300 cm), a floor's length and width (default 4 x 4), a pillar's height (default 3). A fractional count is a fitted filler, and the answer's onModule and fittedFiller say which sides are off the grid. thickness is in cm: a wall's slab (default 12), a floor's (default 7), a pillar's side (default 40). A wall is built along +X with its thickness along +Y.
PIVOTS: pivot corner (walls and floors), side (the middle of the -Y side) or center (a pillar's default). Every pivot is at the bottom: a floor placed at z 0 has its slab from 0 up to its thickness. The answer's pivotAt says where it is and boundsLocalCm where everything is round it.
OPENINGS (a wall only): opening door (default 110 x 220 cm, to the floor) or window (default 100 x 120 cm, sill 90 cm); openingWidth, openingHeight, sillHeight and openingOffset (cm from the wall's center along X) shape it. openingWidth and openingHeight are the CLEAR opening a character walks through: with trim the 2 cm lining sits outside it, in the slab's reveal, so the slab's cut (roughOpeningCm) is 4 cm wider and 2 cm taller. The answer's clearOpeningCm is the opening measured by rays on the built mesh, and a warning names any difference from the request. The wall's face is split on a grid round the opening - every face a quad, no boolean - and an opening must keep 10 cm of wall, plus its casing, at every edge.
THE LOOK: every edge bevelled (bevel cm, default 1; 1.5 on a pillar; bevelSegments default 3), shaded smooth across the rounding with sharp edges keeping flat faces flat. With trim on (default): a plinth with a band along its top on both faces of a wall, broken at a door; a two-step casing and a lining round an opening; a window's sill, apron and a frame with a mullion and a transom; a pillar's stepped base and capital. Trim parts are separate closed shells standing proud of the slab, and no two parts share a face plane where they overlap.
SLOTS: slot 0 the surface (material, or color for the one made here), slot 1 the trim (trimMaterial or trimColor) - a floor, or a piece with trim off, has slot 0 only. The made materials are for Blender's own renders; in Unreal each slot takes the kit's material.
PAINT GRID: gridCm (default 50, 0 for none) adds grid lines across the slab's faces (a pillar's shaft's), and with trim on a support line where trim meets the slab and another 10 cm out, so a vertex-color mask (bl_set_vertex_color_by_rule) has vertices to vary across instead of ramping over a whole 3 m face.
UVS: UVMap is a box projection in meters, uvTileCm (default 200) per repeat, so pieces laid on the module continue one texture when the module divides the repeat (uv0.continuesAcrossModule). LightmapUV is made LAST - the channel Unreal's Lightmap Coordinate Index points at - by bl_uv_unwrap and judged by bl_uv_info: lightmap.lightmapReady, with resolutionSuggested by size (128 at 3 m and over, 64 at 1-3 m, 32 below).
COLLISION: with collision on (default), UCX_<name>_NN boxes of the slab, audited closed, manifold and convex - one for a plain wall, floor or pillar; beside, above and (for a window) below an opening, stopping at the clear opening, so the opening stays open. Each hull is its own object at the piece's transform, a wire hidden from renders.
NAME: default SM_<Kind>_<size in cm>_01a (SM_Wall_400x300_01a, SM_WallDoor_400x300_01a, SM_WallWindow_..., SM_Floor_400x400_01a, SM_Pillar_40x300_01a), the first model number free. A name given that is taken is refused, never suffixed - a kit piece's name is its asset name.
WHAT FILLS AN OPENING: kind shutter or door_leaf is built in the frame of the wall it fills - pass that wall's length, height, thickness, opening, openingWidth/Height, sillHeight, openingOffset, trim and pivot and the same location and rotation, and it lands in the wall's opening. A shutter (opening door, default, or window) is closed on the wall's face, in front of its casing: roll-formed slats with an interlock curl (slatPitch cm, default 6.7, 3-15), a bottom angle bar on a bulb astragal, channel guides on jamb angles, a hood with a rounded front (hoodRadius cm, default 8, 0-15) over the coil, end brackets; refused when its hood would stand above the wall. A door_leaf (opening door) is a 4.45 cm hollow-metal leaf with hemmed edges, 3 mm clear of the jambs and head, 15 mm undercut; louver true adds a chevron louver. hardware (default true): a shutter's bolts and lift handle; a leaf's hinges, lever and deadbolt on both faces, kick plate, astragal and drip cap. Slot 0 is the curtain or leaf, slot 1 the hardware; every part a closed quad solid. gridCm is refused on a shutter.
Rotation is in radians. Every value is checked before anything is created; a refusal says NOTHING was created.

RETURNS: name, kind, opening, moduleCm, sidesCm, onModule, fittedFiller, thicknessCm, pivot, pivotAt, boundsLocalCm, parts, bevelCm, bevelSegments, trim, gridCm, vertices, faces, triangles, ngons, uvLayers, uv0, lightmap {layer, index, method, lightmapReady, reason, islands, resolutionSuggested}, materialSlots, collisionHulls, collisionNotes, openingCm, clearOpeningCm {width, height, left, right, foot, top} and roughOpeningCm (with an opening), warnings (when the measured opening differs), elapsedSeconds; a shutter or leaf adds partCounts, fills, and curtain {slats, pastOpeningCm, spanZCm} and hood {depthCm, heightCm, topCm, coilDiameterCm}, or leaf {widthCm, heightCm, thicknessCm, clearanceCm, louverCm}, measured on the built mesh.

minThicknessCm (min_thickness_cm): a thickness the caller holds the piece to. The reply adds minThicknessCm, belowMinThickness and, when the piece is thinner, a note - never a refusal and never a changed default (a wall stays 12 cm, a floor 7 cm, until the user says otherwise).
bl_set_vertex_color_by_rule:
Write a 0-1 mask into a Blender mesh's color attribute by a rule - up (faces that look up), height, cavity or random per part - for a material to blend moss, dirt, grime or variation with. Also rules dirt, fromWeight and adjust. Call mif_help("bl_set_vertex_color_by_rule") first. group names the vertex group whose weights rule fromWeight writes into the channel (required for that rule, refused by any other rule, and refused by name if the object lacks it).

WHAT IT WRITES: 0-1 into one channel of a color attribute (channel R, the default, G, B, A, or RGB for all three), as 8-bit BYTE_COLOR stored in sRGB space - each byte is the value x 255, which bl_export_mesh's FBX carries and Unreal's VertexColor node reads as written (Blender's own shading and bl_mesh_stats read the same bytes linearized, so 0.5 reads back there as 0.2159). A new attribute (name, default Col) is made on face corners with the other channels at 0 and alpha 1; an existing BYTE_COLOR attribute keeps its domain (CORNER or POINT) and its other channels. combine sets how the value meets what the channel holds: replace (default), multiply, max, min, add - so several rules share one attribute (R dirt, G grime, B moss).
RULES: up - the shading normal's world Z per face corner (sharp edges keep a hard box's top face up to its edges), mapped through range (default 0.5 to 0.9): moss on tops. height - world Z from the object's lowest point (0) to its highest (1), or through range in meters; invert gives dirt at the foot. cavity - the share of `rays` short rays (default 24) over each vertex's hemisphere that meet the mesh within `distance` meters (default 5% of the object's largest side), mapped through range (default 0.1 to 0.5): grime in crevices and where parts meet. random - one value per connected part (element part, the default) or per face (element face), uniform in range (default 0 to 1), from seed. space local reads up and height in the object's own axes. A key another rule reads is refused, not ignored. range [from, to] with from > to reverses the mask; invert writes 1 - value.
RESOLUTION: values live on vertices and blend across each face, so a band narrower than the faces it crosses becomes a ramp. The answer's resolutionNote says so with the numbers (height: an edge taller than the range; cavity: an edge longer than 8 x distance). bl_build_kit_piece's gridCm (default 50) and its support lines where trim meets the slab give kit pieces the vertices a mask needs.

RETURNS: object, rule, attribute, made, domain, dataType, channel, combine, invert, range (as used), written, readBack {channel: min, max, mean, atLeastHalf} read from the stored bytes, resolutionNote, stored; distanceM and rays (cavity), seed, element and elements (random), space (up, height), elapsedSeconds.

Rule dirt (Blender's Dirty Vertex Colors, the bundled algorithm): per vertex the angle between its normal and the mean direction to its connected vertices, clamped between dirt.dirtAngle and dirt.cleanAngle (degrees, default 0 and 180; dirt.dirtOnly skips the clean clamp), blurred over the edges dirt.blurIterations times (0-40, default 1) at dirt.blurStrength (0.01-1, default 1), and mapped between the lowest and highest tone (dirt.normalize, default true). dirt is that object: {blurStrength, blurIterations, cleanAngle, dirtAngle, dirtOnly, normalize}. The value written is the DIRT: 1 in a crease, 0 on open or worn surface; invert gives Blender's own tone. Rule fromWeight: group names a vertex group, its weights go into the channel through range (default 0-1). Rule adjust changes the attribute's existing values with no mask computed: adjust {levels {offset, gain}: gain x (value + offset); hsv {hue (0.5 leaves it), saturation, value}: needs channel RGB; brightnessContrast {brightness, contrast} -100 to 100, Blender's formula}, applied in that order, then invert; the attribute must exist, and range or combine with adjust is refused.
bl_build_lod_chain:
Make hand LODs for a Blender mesh that Unreal's FBX importer reads as its LODs - decimated copies under an Empty whose fbx_type is LodGroup, the object itself LOD0 - and optionally write them to an FBX. Call mif_help("bl_build_lod_chain") first.

WHEN: Unreal reduces LODs itself and most pieces are Nanite, so hand LODs are for a piece that needs them - a non-Nanite mesh whose automatic reduction breaks its silhouette, or LODs shaped differently from LOD0.
WHAT IT MAKES: <object>_LOD1, <object>_LOD2, ... - edge-collapse decimations of the object's EVALUATED mesh (its modifiers applied), each keeping ratios[i] of LOD0's triangles (default [0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.45]; falling, each above 0 and below 1, at most 7) and every UV layer and color attribute - and an Empty <object>_LODGroup with the custom property fbx_type = LodGroup, which Blender's FBX exporter writes as the node's type on 3.6-5.2. The group takes the object's place and transform; the object (LOD0, under its OWN name, so UCX_<object>_NN hulls still attach) and every LOD are its children with no offset. Unreal takes the group's children in order as LOD0, LOD1, ...
Each LOD's edges sharper than 30 degrees are marked sharp (auto smooth on up to Blender 4.0), so a smooth-shaded piece's flat faces still shade flat after the collapse.
file: writes the group, its LODs and the object's UCX_/UBX_/USP_/UCP_ hulls (beside the group, not under it) to that .fbx with bl_export_mesh's settings - centimeters, Z up, modifiers applied. Import it with Import Mesh LODs on. overwrite (default true) replaces an existing file and says what it replaced.
REFUSED: an object with a parent (the group would replace it) or with children (under a LOD node they would be merged into LOD0), a LOD or group name already taken (Blender would suffix .001), ratios that do not fall, a file that is not .fbx. Every value is checked before anything is made.

RETURNS: object, group, fbxType, lods [{lod, object, ratioAsked, triangles, ratioAchieved, uvLayers, colorAttributes, sharpEdges}] - triangles measured on each LOD, LOD0's the evaluated count that reaches Unreal - collisionHulls, order, file {path, bytes, objects, overwrote}, notes (a modifier on the object), elapsedSeconds. SKINNED MESHES (2026-10-06): a mesh with an Armature modifier or an armature parent gets a skinned chain - each LOD decimated from the REST shape (the basis key, no modifiers), then given every vertex group's weights and every shape key (values, ranges, relative keys) by barycentric interpolation from the nearest point on LOD0's rest surface, LOD0's parent and an Armature modifier on the same armature. No LodGroup: Unreal imports a skeletal mesh's LODs one file each, so file writes <file>_LOD0.fbx, _LOD1.fbx ... each with the armature. Each row reports vertexGroups, unweightedVertices, shapeKeys and poseDeviation - the LOD's largest distance from LOD0's surface in the pose the armature holds now (measured: a bent two-bone cylinder at 0.5 and 0.25 of its triangles, 0.0 and 3.9 cm, the last mostly the decimation's own chord error). A skinned mesh parented to anything but its armature is refused.
bl_build_pass_composite:
Rebuild a Blender render from its light passes in the scene compositor: (Direct + Indirect) x Color per pass, summed, then Emission and Environment, with optional denoise, AO, glare and mist.

PARAMETERS. view_layer (string, default the active view layer): whose passes are read; a Render Layers node already showing that layer is reused, else one is made. passes (list, default every one of DIFFUSE, GLOSSY, TRANSMISSION, VOLUME, EMISSION, ENVIRONMENT the layer outputs in full): summed in that fixed order whatever order you send. group (bool, default true): each light pass goes through a reusable "MifPassMixer" compositor group (direct, indirect, color), reused when it exists; false builds plain Mix nodes instead. denoise (string, default NONE): NONE, FINAL (one Denoise at the end) or PER_PASS (one after each light pass); Albedo and Normal are wired when the layer stores denoising data. extras (object): {ao {ramp [a, b], cryptomatteObject}, emissionGlare (bool), mist {ramp [a, b], color [r, g, b]}}; each ramp is two rising stops inside 0-1, default [0, 1]; mist color defaults white. output (string, default COMPOSITE): COMPOSITE (the Composite node, or the Group Output's Image from 5.0; links already into it are removed and named), VIEWER (a new Viewer node) or FILE_OUTPUT (a new File Output node). file_path (string): the File Output's folder and name, required with FILE_OUTPUT. file_format (string): from the build's ImageFormatSettings enum, FILE_OUTPUT only.

OUT: scene, viewLayer, tree, addressAs, compositorApi, passes, group (mixer name or null), groupCreated, denoise, denoiseAlbedoNormal, denoiseNote, extras, output, outputNode, replacedLinkFrom [node names], nodesMade [names], linksMade ["a.out -> b.in"], linkCount, note.

REFUSED with "NOTHING was built": no such view layer; a bad denoise, output, passes or file_format value; file_path or file_format without FILE_OUTPUT, or FILE_OUTPUT without file_path; a pass, AO, Cryptomatte object or Mist pass the layer does not output (naming the bl_set_view_layer switch); emissionGlare without EMISSION; a malformed extras, ramp or color; a scene with no compositing tree (not made here). A failure during the build removes the nodes this call added, and a mixer group it created.
bl_recipe_game_ready:
THE BORING PIPELINE, BANKED: apply transforms, ensure a UV layer, then MEASURE the result with the same battery bl_mesh_quality exposes. Composes existing ops rather than reimplementing them, so every guard they carry - shared mesh data, linked libraries, edit mode - still applies; it does nothing you could not do by hand, it does it in the right ORDER and then checks. Order is the whole value: unwrapping before the scale is baked lays UVs out against the unscaled mesh, so a non-uniformly scaled object ends up with a texel density that is wrong the moment scale is applied. forceUnwrap defaults FALSE because re-unwrapping a layout somebody made by hand is destructive and silent. If a step fails half way it reports leftBehind saying what already happened and is NOT undone - a partial composition that stayed quiet would be the worst outcome. Read quality.notMeasured before treating concernCount:0 as a clean bill of health. THE FULL PASS for Unreal (full=true, or each key alone): pivot by kind, a Lightmap UV layer last, UCX_ hulls, an SM_ name, then bl_mesh_quality's conventions. Call mif_help("bl_recipe_game_ready") first.

THE FULL PASS - every step off unless asked for, so a call without these keys does what it always did. The order is the one that works: transform, pivot, UV0, lightmap, name, hulls, check - the hulls after the rename that names them and after the pivot whose transform they copy.
full=true turns every step on at its default: pivot 'kind', lightmap, collision 'auto' with one hull per part, ue_name 'auto'. A key given beside it wins (collision='none' drops the hulls).
kind: auto (default: read off the bounds once the transform is baked - floor: both sides at least 100 cm and under a tenth as thick; wall: at least 100 cm long and tall and under a tenth as thick as it is long; anything else a prop), wall, floor or prop. The pivot, the hull shape and the conventions check go by it.
pivot: 'kind' puts a floor on its -x-y bottom corner (it tiles by whole-module moves from there), a wall on the bottom middle of the face across its thickness (-y for a wall running along X, -x along Y) and a prop on its bottom center; bottom, bottomCorner and bottomSide name one outright. Read off the vertices, not the stale bound_box; the geometry does not move.
lightmap=true makes a layer named 'Lightmap' LAST with uv_unwrap LIGHTMAP - Unreal's lightmap coordinate index points at a channel by position - and measures it with uv_info lightmapReady (pass.lightmap). A lightmap layer already last and ready is kept; one last and not ready is laid out again; one that is not last is refused before anything changes (Blender cannot move a UV layer). UV0 stays the active layer. Refused with no UV layer and unwrap=false, because the lightmap would become UV0.
collision: auto (box for a wall or floor, convex for a prop), convex, box or none, through bl_create_collision_hull; per_part (default true under full) makes one hull per loose part so a doorway stays open, max_hulls caps them. Hulls already named for the object are kept and the step says so.
ue_name: 'auto' puts SM_ in front (every run of other characters one underscore: 'Mif RF-Crate' becomes SM_Mif_RF_Crate), or the exact name. A taken name is refused before anything changes; hulls named for the old name are renamed with it.
module_cm: the kit's module, for the conventions check's sides.
THE ANSWER gains pass (kind, pivot with pivotInBounds, lightmap, collision hulls and primitiveCount, renamedFrom), conventionNotes - mesh_quality's conventions notes, each difference in a sentence with its number - and conventionsFollowed / conventionsDiffer. Notes, not concerns: they do not count in concernCount. A step that fails raises 'recipe stopped at <step>' and names every step that already ran (WHAT IS LEFT BEHIND); nothing is undone. A triangle budget (bl_decimate_mesh) is not a step: reducing is left to the engine's LODs or Nanite unless asked for by hand.
bl_create_mesh:
