Build a Blender mesh object from vertex, face and loose-edge lists, with optional per-face material slots, UV layers, vertex groups and smooth flags; bad input is refused before anything exists. Call mif_help("bl_create_mesh") first.

PARAMETERS: vertices [[x,y,z], ...] (required; local space, meters). faces [[i,j,k,...], ...] - three or more distinct vertex indices each, wound counter-clockwise seen from the side the normal should face. edges [[a,b], ...] - loose edges; one that is already a face edge is reported in edgesOnFaces. material_indices - one slot index per face; without materials the slots are made empty for bl_set_material_slots or bl_assign_material to fill. materials - existing material names, one per slot, in order. uvs {layer: [[[u,v], ...], ...]} - one row per face, one [u,v] per corner in the face's own order; the first layer is the active one; at most 8 layers. vertex_groups {group: [[index, weight], ...] or [index, ...]} - a bare index means weight 1, weights run 0-1. smooth - true/false for every face, or one boolean per face; default flat. name (default "Mesh"; Blender appends .001 on a collision: nameWasSuffixed for the object, meshNameWasSuffixed for its mesh, and nameHeldBy names each object or mesh already holding the name with its users and whether it is an orphan - an object deleted without purging leaves its mesh holding the name). take_over_name (default false): true removes the ORPHAN object and/or mesh holding the name (no users, no fake user) so both get it exactly, listed in nameTakenOverFrom; a holder in use is refused by name and nothing is created or removed. location, rotation (radians), scale, collection.

REFUSED BEFORE A DATABLOCK EXISTS, so a refusal leaves nothing behind: a face index out of range, a face with under three vertices or a repeated corner, a duplicate face (Blender's validation would delete it and shift every per-face list after it), an edge that is not [a, b] or repeats another, NaN or Infinity anywhere, a per-face list of the wrong length, a UV row whose corner count is not its face's, a vertex weight outside 0-1, a material that does not exist. After the build Blender's own mesh.validate runs; if it had to change anything the object is removed and the call refused.

THE REPLY READS EVERY COUNT BACK OFF THE BUILT MESH: vertexCount, edgeCount, faceCount, looseEdgeCount, uvLayers and activeUvLayer, materialSlots, smoothFaceCount, vertexGroups with their vertex counts, and zeroAreaFaces (area under 1e-12 m2) - legal in Blender, but the Unreal hand-off refuses zero-area faces.
bl_create_node_group:
Create a Blender node group (geometry by default) whose Group Input and Group Output are NOT linked: until something reaches Group Output, an object it drives evaluates to nothing. Both sit on a Geometry socket pair; a geometry group with no geometry sockets cannot drive a modifier at all. Group sockets moved to tree.interface in Blender 4.0 and the old tree.inputs/outputs are GONE rather than deprecated; both are handled. tool: true (OBJECT and EDIT, MESH) or {modes: [OBJECT|EDIT|SCULPT], types: [MESH|CURVES|POINTCLOUD]} marks a geometry group as a node tool (Blender 4.0+), run by bl_run_node_tool.

name (str, default None, which the op reads as 'MifNodes') is the group's name; Blender suffixes it on a collision (nameWasSuffixed). 'scene:compositor', 'scene:world' and names starting 'material:', 'world:' or 'light:' are refused, because those address trees owned by a scene, material, world or light. type (str, default None: GeometryNodeTree) is GeometryNodeTree, ShaderNodeTree or CompositorNodeTree, exactly as spelled. with_group_io (bool, default None: true) adds the Geometry input and output sockets and the Group Input and Group Output nodes; it acts on a GeometryNodeTree only - a shader or compositor group is created empty either way. tool works on a GeometryNodeTree in Blender 4.0 or later only.

OUT: group (the name it got), type, nodes (names of the nodes made: Group Input and Group Output, or []), requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, interface [{name, inOut, identifier, socketType}] (the identifier is what a modifier key uses), nodeCount, tool ({modes, types, operator} or null), apiNote.

Refused before anything is created: an unknown key; a reserved name; a type outside the three; a with_group_io that is not a boolean; a tool spec on Blender before 4.0, on a non-geometry type, or not true or {modes, types} with modes from OBJECT | EDIT | SCULPT and types from MESH | CURVES | POINTCLOUD.
bl_create_point_cloud:
Create a Blender POINTCLOUD object - points with attributes, driven by geometry nodes. Same argument and same measurement as bl_create_curves: on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1 an empty pointcloud accepts a NODES modifier and a generating group evaluates to real points. IT ARRIVES EMPTY AND BLENDER HAS NO UI FOR PLACING POINTS IN ONE BY HAND EITHER - the type exists to be generated. The response says pointCount 0 and isEmpty true rather than staying quiet about it. Fill it with bl_create_node_group plus bl_assign_node_group, and the group's OUTPUT must be POINT geometry (a Mesh Grid into Mesh to Points, for instance) - a mesh-outputting group evaluates without error and lands nothing. bl_object_info reports the stored and evaluated counts separately, which is the only way to see that it worked.

PARAMETERS. name (string, default "PointCloud"): the object and data name; Blender suffixes it on a collision (nameWasSuffixed). location ([x, y, z] or {x, y, z}, default origin) and rotation (Euler XYZ in radians, same forms, default zero): written to the object. scale (same forms, default [1, 1, 1]): written to the object, not echoed in the reply. collection (string, default the scene's root collection): an existing collection to link into. Every vector needs finite numbers, and a dict must name at least one of x, y, z.

OUT: ok, name, type (POINTCLOUD), collection, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, location, rotation, dataName, pointCount (always 0), isEmpty (always true), note (how to fill it with a node group).

REFUSED with nothing created: a malformed or non-finite location, rotation or scale; a collection that does not exist (lists the ones present); a build with no bpy.data.pointclouds. points, count, radius, nodeGroup and material are refused with a note on where each one is set instead.
bl_add_rigid_body:
Make Blender objects (object, objects or a collection) ACTIVE (falls) or PASSIVE (is landed on) rigid bodies, or update existing ones: deactivation, the Dynamic flag (enabled), copy_from and a mass from density or material. The simulation lives in a scene-level rigid body world that Blender creates on demand, so this goes through the operator with a context override - assigning obj.rigid_body directly is not possible. A rigid body is stepped forward from the start frame, so jumping to a late frame shows it at REST: call bl_bake_physics before rendering that frame. A body added to a world that is ALREADY BAKED is not in those frames and does not move at all - the response carries bakedWorldNote, and bl_bake_physics rebake=true is the fix. BOUNCINESS NEEDS BOTH SURFACES: measured on every supported build, a sphere at 0.99 rebounds 0.00 m off a floor at 0 and 2.29 m off a floor at 0.99, so bouncinessNote names the bodies in the world that have none.

MANY BODIES IN ONE CALL (2026-10-04). Pass exactly one of object, objects [names] or collection (every object in it and its children). A non-mesh in a list or collection is skipped and named in `skipped` (Blender's own Copy from Active skips them too, while its objects_add refuses the whole call when one non-mesh is selected - measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1). The bodies are made by one rigidbody.objects_add per type, so a 300-piece slab is one operator call. A list or collection replies one row per object (`objects`, `count`); a single object keeps the flat reply.

UPDATE, AND WHY A SECOND ADD IS REFUSED. update: true writes the settings of bodies that already exist and keeps each one's type unless `type` is given. Without update an existing body is refused: rigidbody.object_add on a body that exists re-types it to the call's type - ACTIVE when none is given - and keeps its mass (measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: a PASSIVE floor added again became ACTIVE).

COPY FROM. copy_from names a rigid body whose 18 settings - Blender's own Copy from Active list (type, kinematic, mass, collision shape, margin and its switch, friction, bounciness, the four deactivation settings, both dampings, collision collections, mesh source, deform, enabled) - every target takes first; the call's own settings are written over them.

DEACTIVATION AND THE DYNAMIC FLAG. use_deactivation, start_deactivated, deactivate_linear_velocity (Blender's default 0.4) and deactivate_angular_velocity (0.5) are written and read back here and by bl_physics_info. start_deactivated turns use_deactivation on with it, since the panel greys it while deactivation is off. enabled is Blender's Dynamic checkbox: an ACTIVE body only, refused on a PASSIVE one. Measured: a cube 3 m up with start_deactivated stayed at z 3 over a 20-frame bake while the same cube without it fell (3.6.23, 4.4.0, 5.2.1).

HOW TO KEEP A WALL INERT UNTIL IT IS STRUCK - three recipes, and the purpose decides. (1) start_deactivated (with use_deactivation) on every piece, plus an Animated trigger body that wakes the pieces it touches: nothing moves on play and no timing is needed - right when the striker's arrival frame is not fixed. (2) The wall PASSIVE, only the bricks near the impact ACTIVE, and their Dynamic flag (enabled) keyed on at the impact frame with bl_set_keyframe on 'rigid_body.enabled': exact timing and the cheapest simulation - right when the strike frame is known. (3) Every brick ACTIVE from the start: bricks without support topple on frame 1. To tell which one a wall needs, bake and read a sample of unstruck bricks at frame 1 and at the frame before the strike (bl_evaluate_at_frame); any drift means (1) or (2).

A MASS FROM A DENSITY. density (kg per cubic metre) or material (one of Blender's mass presets, matched in any case) sets mass = density x the volume of the EVALUATED mesh in world scale. The mesh must be closed - every edge joining exactly two faces - or it is refused naming the mesh, since an open mesh has no volume. The preset names are read from rigidbody.mass_calculate on the running build (46 on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2, plus Custom; its enum is dynamic, so the static RNA lists only DEFAULT), and a preset's density is measured on the first body with the shape set to BOX for one run and put back (Concrete 2320, Gold 19282). Blender's own Calculate Mass uses the COLLISION SHAPE's volume instead: a 2 x 1 x 1 box read 4640 kg of Concrete as BOX, CONVEX_HULL or MESH and 9718 kg as SPHERE (measured) - this call uses the mesh, and says so in massRule. The reply carries volume per object, density, material and totalMass. A mass applies to ACTIVE bodies only. The preset name is checked against the operator after the bodies exist (its poll wants an active rigid body); a refused name takes back the bodies and the world the call made.

A RIGID BODY AND CLOTH (rule d, measured 2026-10-05 on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1). Cloth does not see rigid bodies: it collides only with objects that carry a Collision modifier, and it never pushes a rigid body back - a 0.4 m ball dropped onto a pinned cloth sheet fell through it to z -27.6 by frame 60 whatever its shape. For the cloth to react, add bl_add_collision to the same object and use collision_shape SPHERE: with SPHERE the sheet moved as the ball passed; with CONVEX_HULL or MESH plus the Collision modifier it read exactly as with no ball. Something that must land and rest on cloth is a soft body or a pressure cloth, not a rigid body.
bl_add_rigid_body_constraint:
Join Blender RIGID BODIES with physics joints - type FIXED, POINT (a chain), HINGE (a door), SLIDER, PISTON, GENERIC, GENERIC_SPRING or MOTOR - two (object1, object2) or many (objects, pattern, pivot, collection), or edit joints (update, names). GENERIC limits make a ragdoll. bl_add_rigid_body could make things fall and bl_set_physics_world could tune the solver, and nothing could join two bodies. NOT the same as bl_add_constraint: those are OBJECT constraints (Track To, Copy Location) evaluated in the depsgraph, while these are solved by the rigid body world. type: FIXED | POINT | HINGE | SLIDER | PISTON | GENERIC | GENERIC_SPRING | MOTOR, refused by name if the running Blender lacks it. BOTH objects must ALREADY be rigid bodies - call bl_add_rigid_body on each first, or this refuses naming the one that is not. THE JOINT IS AN EMPTY AND ITS LOCATION IS THE PIVOT: a HINGE swings about the constraint object's origin, so put `location` on the hinge line or the door swings about the wrong axis - nothing here can guess where that is. THE JOINT'S ROTATION IS THE AXIS: a HINGE turns about the joint's local Z and SLIDER, PISTON and MOTOR work along its local X (measured on all five Blender builds), so an unrotated hinge is VERTICAL and a plank on it swings like a door and never falls. `rotation` is the joint's Euler XYZ in RADIANS ([1.5708, 0, 0] lays a hinge axis along world -Y), and the response reports axisLocal and axisWorld read off the joint. `breaking_threshold` sets use_breaking AND the number together, because Blender ignores the threshold unless the flag is on and the number alone reads back as asked while never breaking. A constraint is COLLECTION MEMBERSHIP rather than a modifier: the object is linked into scene.rigidbody_world.constraints and Blender creates the settings, which is why this needs no operator. Verified on Blender 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1. Rigid bodies are stepped forward - bake_physics before jumping to a late frame.

MANY JOINTS IN ONE CALL (2026-10-04). objects [names] (every one a rigid body) with active (default the first) joins them the way Blender's Connect does (bl_operators/rigidbody.py, the same on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2): pattern SELECTED_TO_ACTIVE (default) joins each object to active; CHAIN_DISTANCE starts at active and joins each to the nearest one left, with no maximum distance. pivot CENTER (default, between the two), ACTIVE (at the first of the pair) or SELECTED (at the second); the enums are read from Blender's own Connect operator. Written natively with world positions, so the joints' empties go into `collection` (made under the scene's collection when it does not exist) instead of the scene's own. A pair a joint already holds is skipped (pairsSkipped); a call that would make nothing is refused. Every joint takes the call's type, rotation, disable_collisions, breaking_threshold, use_breaking, enabled and solver_iterations. Reply: joints [{object, constraintType, object1, object2, location, ...}], count, worldJointCount (bl_physics_info reports it too, as rigidBodyWorld.constraintCount).

EDITING JOINTS THAT EXIST. update: true with names [joint objects] or collection writes breaking_threshold (and use_breaking with it), use_breaking, enabled, solver_iterations and disable_collisions on every joint at once - Blender's Alt-click edit - and replies each joint with its before values. Anything else in an update call is refused.

SOLVER ITERATIONS. solver_iterations N turns the joint's own override on (use_override_solver_iterations) with N; 0 turns the override off and the world's count applies. Raise it for stiffer, smoother joints.

A KEYED BREAKING SCHEDULE goes through bl_set_keyframe on the joint's 'rigid_body_constraint.use_breaking' and 'rigid_body_constraint.breaking_threshold' - measured keyable on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1 (use_breaking off at 40 and on at 41; threshold 100 at 41 and 1 at 50). Key the threshold with interpolation CONSTANT: under Blender's default Bezier the threshold read 58.7 at frame 45, between the two keys. bl_assign_action shares one schedule across joints. A threshold of 1 breaks easily; 100 holds.
bl_add_fluid:
Make a Blender mesh a fluid DOMAIN, FLOW or EFFECTOR - smoke, fire and liquid. FLUID has been in the addon's _SIM_MODIFIERS since that list was written, so bake_physics and physics_info always handled one and nothing could create one: the same consumer-with-no-creator shape as soft body. bl_add_modifier can add the FLUID modifier but not configure it - the modifier carries exactly ONE writable property, fluid_type, and everything that matters lives on domain_settings/flow_settings/effector_settings. THIS DOES NOT BAKE, deliberately: a fluid bake is minutes to hours and blocks Blender's main thread for all of it, so call bl_bake_physics when the setup is right and expect it to be slow. TWO DEFAULTS MAKE A CORRECT SETUP LOOK BROKEN and are reported rather than overridden - resolution_max is 32, Blender's default and low enough that smoke is visibly blocky; and flow_behavior defaults to GEOMETRY, which turns the MESH into fluid ONCE, a single puff, where the continuous emitter people mean by 'add smoke' is INFLOW. Neither is changed for you, because picking a simulation resolution or guessing which behaviour you meant is not this op's business, but the response says so. A SETTING SENT TO THE WRONG ROLE IS REFUSED naming the role that owns it: resolution_max with type=FLOW is a caller who believes they set a resolution, and dropping it quietly would leave them believing it. One object is one role - a domain that is also a flow is not something Mantaflow solves. Verified on 3.6.23, 4.2.17 LTS, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1. A LIQUID domain gets mesh generation ON (use_mesh) on every build: 3.6 starts it off, which simulates a liquid with no surface - useMeshNote says when this op turned it on; use_mesh:false keeps it off. A GAS DOMAIN WITH NO VOLUME SHADER renders as a solid box in EEVEE and as nothing in Cycles (measured on every build), so the response's volumeNote says when one is missing and names the calls: bl_create_material, bl_set_material_volume with surface='disconnect', then bl_set_material_slots. EVERY OTHER SETTING of the role - smoke dissolve, the domain's border collisions, flame and vorticity, noise upres, time scale, a flow's fuel and temperature - is written afterwards with bl_set_modifier(object, modifier='Fluid', settings={identifier: value}). surface_distance is in grid CELLS (Blender's default 1.5): 0.08, read as metres, emits almost nothing from a thin burner and the domain stays empty.

A DOMAIN SET UP FOR A STAGED BAKE (2026-10-04): time_scale, cache_type (the build's own list: REPLAY, MODULAR, ALL), cache_directory and cache_resumable are written in the call that makes the domain, and read back. time_scale is a look tied to scene scale and 24 fps - 1.0 for a faucet at real scale, 0.5 for a 3 m smoke box or a liquid jet, 0.3 for a liquid guided by smoke - so it is a named parameter and the default is never changed for you. cache_resumable must be on BEFORE the data bake: writing it afterwards frees every stage (measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1), and without it Blender's panel withholds the noise, mesh and particle bakes. Give each domain its own cache_directory: left empty in an unsaved file the cache goes to Blender's session temp folder, which is deleted when Blender closes, and two domains sharing a folder free each other's frames. Guides (use_guide, guide_source, guide_parent, guide_alpha, guide_beta, guide_vel_factor) and spray, foam and bubbles are set with bl_set_modifier; bl_bake_physics stages bakes and frees them stage by stage - see its help for the rules where the workflows disagree.
bl_set_bone_collections:
List, create, rename, remove, move, assign, unassign, show, solo and nest a Blender armature's bone collections and set their Rigify UI rows (SET_UI); collection is a name, or a layer index 0-31 on 3.6. WHY: nothing read or wrote bone collections - bl_list_bones returned neither collections nor layers, and bl_create_armature's collection is a SCENE collection. A rig is organised by them, Rigify's generator gates on them, and a weight fix wants only the deform set showing.

THE BUILD DECIDES THE FORM. 4.x and later: named, nested armature.collections; collection is a NAME and a layer index is refused. 3.6: 32 fixed layers; collection is an INDEX 0-31, and CREATE, RENAME, REMOVE, MOVE, SET_SOLO and SET_PARENT are refused there with what does exist (layers have no names, nesting or solo). A 3.6 bone must stay on one layer and one layer must stay visible - both refused before anything changes.

ACTIONS: LIST (default; collection optional), CREATE (parent, bones or name_prefix, and the UI keys), RENAME (new_name; Root, DEF, ORG and MCH are refused - the generator finds them by name), REMOVE, MOVE (index among its siblings), ASSIGN / UNASSIGN (bones or name_prefix; a bone may be in several collections, and the reply lists alreadyMembers / notMembers), SET_VISIBLE (visible, default true), SET_SOLO (solo, default true), SET_PARENT (parent, '' for the top level; a loop is refused), SET_UI (ui_row, ui_title, selection_set, color_set). A key the action does not read is refused.

THE RIGIFY ROW: ui_row (0 = no button; 3.6 rows are 1-32), ui_title, selection_set and color_set (a color set NAME on 4.x, the group number 0-32 on 3.6) exist only while the Rigify generator is on, so they enable it for the session when it is off (enable_rigify false refuses instead). The generator refuses on 4.4 and 5.2 when no collection but Root, DEF, ORG and MCH has a row above 0; 3.6 generates without one (measured). 3.6 layers 28-31 are the generator's Root, DEF, MCH and ORG and take no button.

A GENERATED RIG: the reply says generated true and 'regenerate erases this' - the generator removes every collection of the target rig before rebuilding it, so an edit there belongs on the metarig.

Reply: collections [{name, parent, boneCount, visible, solo, uiRow, uiTitle, selectionSet, colorSet}] (3.6: layers [{layer, boneCount, visible, reservedFor, uiTitle, uiRow, ...}] for the used ones), collection (the one acted on), rigifyEnabledNow.
bl_set_rigify_type:
Write Rigify rig types and their parameters on metarig bones (bones or chain_from), copy_to {bones | chainChildren | mirror}; a parameter the type does not define is refused. WHY: a metarig bone is only a bone until pose_bone.rigify_type names what to build from it, and rigify_parameters is ONE property group holding every rig type's parameters in a single namespace - so a parameter of another type is accepted by Blender and does nothing. The type's own parameters are found by running the rig type's own parameter definition against a recorder (what the generator's own validator does at registration), and a name outside them is refused naming the ones it has.

Targets: bones [names] or chain_from (the bone and its connected children while each has exactly one - the generator's chain). type: a key of THIS build's generator (27 types on 3.6, 28 on 4.4 and 5.2 - limbs.spline_tentacle is new); '' clears; omitted keeps each bone's type so parameters alone can be written. parameters {name: value}: enums by identifier, booleans, numbers, 3.6 layer lists (32 booleans), and on 4.x a bone-collection reference (fk_coll_refs, tweak_coll_refs...) as a list of collection NAMES. copy_to (one of): {bones: [...]}, {chainChildren: '<bone>'} (every direct child of that bone - e.g. each hair strand's base under the head), {mirror: true} (Blender's flip_name: .L/.R, _l/_r, Left/Right; collection references are flipped when the other side's collection exists). Every value is checked and a failed write rolls every touched bone back. Refused on a generated rig (types belong on its metarig).

Measured on 5.2.1: limbs.arm defines rotation_axis (x, z, automatic), auto_align_extremity, segments, bbones, make_custom_pivot, ik_local_location, limb_uniform_scale, fk_layers_extra, fk_coll_refs, tweak_layers_extra, tweak_coll_refs, make_ik_wrist_pivot; on 3.6 the *_coll_refs are fk_layers / tweak_layers (32 booleans). The build's generator decides: 3.6.23's limbs.leg has no extra_toe_roll (it has extra_ik_toe and foot_pivot_type), so there it is refused naming those. The knee's Rubber Tweak is NOT a parameter: it is a generated property rubber_tweak on the rig's tweak bones (bl_set_custom_property).

Reply: bones [{bone, type, parameters (every one the type defines, read back)}], typeParameters {type: [{name, kind, default, items}]}, copiedTo.
bl_generate_rigify_rig:
Generate or regenerate a Rigify rig from a metarig after checks the generator skips (scale, UI rows, leftover face bone, straight limbs); reports bones by collection, IK/FK switches, erased bones and the backup. With dry_run=True it previews a new rig by the name it will get and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since. WHY: Generate Rig is the one step between a fitted metarig and a usable rig, and it fails in ways a caller cannot see. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: it reports a failure with report(ERROR) and returns FINISHED, so it surfaces only after a half-built rig exists; it has no scale or rotation check; and a regenerate removes every bone and collection of the target rig first, so a bone added only to the rig is gone. It runs headless: the human metarig makes 706 bones in 3.4-4.1 s and regenerates in 7-9 s.

REFUSED BEFORE RUNNING (dry_run true runs only these and returns checks and limbBends): the armature is itself a generated rig (it holds rig_id); its world scale is not 1 or rotation not 0 (bake it: a new metarig takes height or scale on bl_create_armature; an existing one takes bl_apply_transform scale and rotation, which applies an armature with the meshes it deforms); no bone has a rig type; on 4.x and later no collection but Root, DEF, ORG and MCH has a UI row above 0 (the generator's own 'No bone collections have UI buttons assigned' - 3.6 generates without one); a faces.super_face bone with no children (measured: "key 'ORG-nose' not found" and a 68-bone partial rig on all three builds); and a limb, finger or tentacle chain so straight that the generator orients it by the bone's ROLL instead of its bend. The rule is the generator's own (compute_chain_x_axis, unchanged 3.6-5.2): |first.y x (last.tail - first.head)| < first.length / 100. Measured on an arm of two 0.3 m bones: bent 0.55 degrees the IK elbow did not bend when the hand was pulled in (0.001 m), bent 0.6 degrees it bent the intended way (0.163 m), on all three builds; a leg's FK axis flips sign across the same line; at 0 degrees generation throws 'zero length vectors have no valid angle'. allow_straight_chains true lets it through when the roll is set on purpose. It applies to limbs.arm, leg, paw, front_paw, rear_paw, super_limb (first two bones), super_finger and simple_tentacle (the whole chain) while their axis parameter is automatic. And a chain told to connect to its parent rig (rigify parameter connect_chain - a spine's head or tail) whose first bone sits neither on the parent chain's last tail nor on its first head (the generator's 1e-5 rule, rigs/chain_rigs.py, unchanged 3.6-5.2): settled 2026-10-18 on 3.6.23-5.2.1, a human metarig with spine.004 disconnected and moved 5 cm throws "Bone 'spine.004': Cannot connect chain - bone position is disjoint." and leaves a 159-bone partial rig; the check is disjointChain.

name: the new rig's name (rigify_rig_basename; the default turns 'metarig' into 'rig', 'META' into 'RIG', else RIG-<name>); refused when the metarig already has a target. target_rig: regenerate into that rig. collection: where a NEW rig goes (must be in the view layer). backup (default true when regenerating): a hidden copy '<rig>_backup' of the old rig, made before the generator empties it.

Reply: rig, rigId, boneCount, bonesByCollection {Root, DEF, ORG, MCH, controls} (3.6: bonesByLayer), deformBoneCount and deformBones, ikFkSwitches [{bone, property, value}], uiScript, uiRegistered (the rig's panel and snap operators exist in this session), autoRunAllowed (a re-opened file needs Auto Run Python Scripts to register them), regenerated, and on a regenerate erased (bone names gone), erasedCollections and backup. A generator failure is ok false with failure {bone, text} parsed from 'RIGIFY ERROR: Bone ...', partial true and leftBehind {rig, boneCount} - nothing is cleaned up behind the caller.
bl_rigify_snap:
Snap a generated Rigify rig's limb IK_TO_FK or FK_TO_IK with its own UI operators (optionally keyed, switched or baked), or LIST its snap buttons and which IK_FK value means IK. WHY: a generated rig's snap buttons are operators of ITS OWN UI script, named with the rig's random 16-character id (rig.data['rig_id']): pose.rigify_limb_ik2fk_<id>, pose.rigify_generic_snap_<id> (FK->IK) and their _bake_ forms, with the bone lists as JSON text that exists only in the rig's UI text. This reads the buttons from that text and runs the one the panel would, with the same properties. Measured headless in OBJECT mode on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2: IK->FK took an arm's chain gap from 0.339 to 0.0006, FK->IK from 0.47 to 0.0001.

WHICH WAY THE SWITCH RUNS is read, never assumed: the limb's settings bone (upper_arm_parent.L, thigh_parent.L) holds IK_FK, and drivers of type SUM with a GENERATOR POLYNOMIAL [1, -1] modifier feed the influence of the ORG bones' constraint copying the IK chain - so the driver curve is evaluated at 0 and 1 and the reply says ikAt 0, fkAt 1 on a generated rig (unchanged 3.6-5.2), with the curve's modifiers. A hand-built switch can run the other way and is read the same way.

direction LIST (default) | IK_TO_FK (the IK controls moved onto the FK pose) | FK_TO_IK (the FK controls moved onto the IK result). limb: the UI's name (hand.L, foot.R) or the settings bone. frame: go there first. key true: key what moved (the operator keys only under auto-keying, so it is switched on for the call and restored - and Preferences > Animation > Only Insert Available, on by default in 5.2, is turned off for the call and restored, since with it on the operator keys nothing on a rig with no curves yet: settled 2026-10-18); keysAdded counts the keys the call made. switch true: also set IK_FK to the side snapped to (FK_TO_IK -> FK, IK_TO_FK -> IK), keyed with key. bake {start, end}: the _bake_ operator over that range (it re-snaps the keyed frames of the source chain and needs an action). Refused when the rig's script never ran in this session (a re-opened file without auto run: run the text or allow auto-run).

Reply: LIST: limbs [{limb, switch {bone, property, value, ikAt, fkAt, mode IK|FK|blend, curveModifiers}, ikToFk, fkToIk (operator, label, properties)}], uiScript, uiRegistered, autoRunAllowed. A snap: operator, frame, chainGapBefore / chainGapAfter (largest head distance between the two chains), chains, switch.

A FRAME CHANGE STEPS EVERY LIVE SIMULATION (2026-10-05): moving the scene's frame evaluates each unbaked cloth, soft body, emitter or dynamic-hair particle system, dynamic-paint canvas and rigid body world in the view layer, and a fluid domain whose cache type is REPLAY - on an object hidden with the eye or from the render too (only hide_viewport or the modifier's show_viewport off takes it out). A leftover cloth on a render-hidden object stepped against a body's collision during a pose check and asked for 58.7 GB. So a call that would move the frame past such a cache's first frame is REFUSED before anything changes, naming each simulation and the colliders it would step against; bake them, take them out of the depsgraph, or pass allow_simulation=true, and the reply's simulationsStepped and colliders say what stepped. A Geometry Nodes simulation zone is listed (geometryNodesSimulations) and not refused: Blender exposes no baked flag for it.
bl_create_armature:
Create a Blender armature with its bones - without which the whole rigging family could only EDIT. ops_rig has twelve ops and not one creates an armature, so nothing could be rigged from scratch. BONES ONLY EXIST IN EDIT MODE (armature.edit_bones is absent outside it), so this switches mode, builds, and switches back - and restoring the mode is a POSTCONDITION, not a courtesy, because being left in edit mode strands every op that follows. Every bone is validated in full BEFORE any mode change, so a bad entry cannot leave a half-built rig with Blender stuck in an editor. Bones are counted from data.bones after leaving edit mode, not from the edit_bones the op made, since those only exist inside it. Parents must be listed before their children. Each bone takes name, head, tail, parent, connect and rotationMode (the pose bone's, default QUATERNION); any other key in a bone is refused. rotationModes reads every bone's mode back.

METARIG (2026-10-04): metarig names one of the Rigify generator's bundled metarigs (human 159 bones 1.98 m, basic_human 29, basic_quadruped, bird, cat, horse, shark, wolf - read from the build's own metarigs folder, so an unknown name is refused before anything is enabled). location places it (default the origin, not the 3D cursor the generator's operator uses); height (meters) or scale sizes it, BAKED into the bone positions with the object left at scale 1 and rotation 0, because the generator copies bones without the object's scale and an unapplied one gives a rig of the wrong size with no message. The ends are computed before any is written: a connected child's head is its parent's tail, and scaling bone by bone moved the shared joints twice (the human at 3x came out 17.3 m, measured on 5.2.1). rotation, bones, display_type and show_in_front are refused with metarig. The generator is enabled for the session when off (enable_rigify false refuses): addon_utils.enable('rigify', default_set=False) half-registers it on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2 (its register() reads its preferences entry), so it is enabled with an in-memory preferences entry and preferences.is_dirty is put back, so an auto-save of preferences does not record it. Reply: boneCount, heightM, naturalHeightM, scaleBaked, rigTypes {bone: type}, collections [{name, uiRow, ...}] (3.6: layers), generateReady with notReadyBecause and limbBends, rigifyEnabledNow.
bl_add_bones:
Add bones to an armature that ALREADY EXISTS. bl_create_armature builds bones and every other rigging tool edits what is there - bl_list_bones, bl_rename_bones, bl_set_bone_pose, the weight tools - so edit_bones appeared in exactly one place in the whole addon and a skeleton that arrived through bl_import_mesh could be renamed, posed and weighted but never given another bone. Adding a socket bone, or an ik_hand_gun beside the hand, is ordinary skeletal work for a game engine and had no typed path. A parent may be a bone that was already on the rig OR one created earlier in the same call. `bones` is [{name, head:[x,y,z], tail:[x,y,z], parent, connect, roll}]. TWO REFUSALS WORTH KNOWING: a bone whose head equals its tail has ZERO length and Blender DELETES it when edit mode is left - silently, with no error - so it is refused up front rather than surfacing later as a confusing count mismatch. And a name already on the rig is refused, because Blender would add '.001' beside it and everything looking that name up afterwards, including the vertex groups that skin it, would find the wrong bone. Restoring OBJECT mode is a postcondition rather than tidy-up: left in edit mode, every call after this one fails on an editor nobody asked for, so the mode is asserted afterwards and reported. REMOVE: remove [names] deletes bones (children reparented; merge_weights moves their weights).

SAMPLE (2026-10-04): sample {rigType, origin [x,y,z], scale} adds one Rigify rig type's sample bones through the generator's armature.metarig_sample_add in edit mode (its poll needs EDIT_ARMATURE; the sample lands at fixed coordinates about the armature's origin, measured identical on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.2 - limbs.arm makes upper_arm.L, forearm.L and hand.L with the type on upper_arm.L only), then moves it to origin and scales it about it, ends computed before any is written, and restores object mode. A type with no sample is refused naming the ones with one. On 4.4 and 5.2 the sample's bones are in NO collection (put them in one with a UI row before generating); on 3.6 on layer 0. A name already on the armature gets Blender's .001 and is listed in suffixed. Reply: added, bones [{name, head, tail, parent, rigType, collections}], rigTypes, modeAfter, generateReady. rename_from {find: replace} (2026-10-06) instead of bones copies every bone whose name holds a find under the replaced name (DEF- to CTRL-), keeping head, tail, roll, connect and deform, each copy parented to its parent's copy; a taken new name is refused, so no .001 appears.

REMOVE. remove [names] deletes bones instead of adding them: each child of a removed bone is reparented, unconnected so its head stays, to the nearest ancestor that stays; OBJECT mode is restored and the count asserted. The vertex groups named after a removed bone are left on every mesh skinned to the armature and named in warning, or with merge_weights=true added into the group of the bone that takes over (created when missing; dropped for a removed root). actionsKeyingRemoved names the actions still keying a removed bone - Blender leaves those curves. remove goes alone: not with bones, rename_from or sample.
bl_set_world:
Set the Blender world background - a flat colour or an HDRI, plus strength and mist. A scene with no world contributes no ambient light at all, so an interior renders pure black outside its own fixtures and the lights get blamed. strength multiplies emission: 1.0 with mid grey is roughly overcast and washes out a dark interior, which usually wants 0.02-0.1. Passing both an hdri and a colour is refused - the texture would silently override the colour. useAsLight writes the world's Cycles ray visibility, which EEVEE does not read (measured no change on 3.6-5.2); under EEVEE the reply says so with inertUnderThisEngine and an engineNote.

THE WORLD'S SUN AND PROBE RESOLUTION (EEVEE, Blender 4.2 and later; 2026-10-04). sun {threshold, angle, shadow {enabled, jitter, overblur}} writes World.sun_threshold, sun_angle, use_sun_shadow, use_sun_shadow_jitter and sun_shadow_jitter_overblur; probe_resolution writes World.probe_resolution from the build's own list (128 to 4096). All are read back under after.sun, with sunBefore. On 3.6 the World has none of them (measured) and the call is refused naming the build, with nothing changed. sun_threshold defaults to 10: light in the world above it is extracted into a sun with a shadow. For an HDRI used only as skylight beside a real sun lamp that owns the sun's height and direction, set the threshold to 0. The threshold acts after the Background node, so a strength change moves the extracted sun - retune it after the strength (sunNote says so). The scene-level Spheres Resolution is bl_set_render_settings eevee {gi_cubemap_resolution}.
bl_set_light_probe:
Write an existing Blender light probe's own settings by RNA identifier - bake settings such as surfel_density, surface_bias, normal_bias, view_bias, use_data_display - each checked against this build's probe and read back; all or nothing.

WHAT IT REACHES (2026-10-04). Any writable property of the probe's own datablock, read off its bl_rna as bl_set_modifier reads a modifier's: enums checked against their items, numbers finite, booleans strict, each value read back into `written`, the old values in `before`. An absent name is refused with the names this build's probe has. All or nothing: a refusal puts back every value the call had already written. The probe classes differ by build: 3.6 has one LightProbe class (CUBEMAP, PLANAR, GRID; intensity, visibility_bleed_bias, visibility_blur, show_data and the rest); 4.2 and later have LightProbeSphere, LightProbePlane and LightProbeVolume, and the volume one carries the bake settings - bake_samples, surfel_density, the four capture settings (distance, world, indirect, emission), surface_bias, escape_bias, clamp_direct, clamp_indirect, normal_bias, view_bias, facing_bias, validity_threshold, dilation_threshold, dilation_radius - and use_data_display and data_display_size.

TUNING A VOLUME PROBE, from one workflow: Surfel Resolution (surfel_density) default 20 was far too low (40, 60, 80 and 100 were tried, with diminishing returns near 100); Surface Offset (surface_bias) raised from 0 removes banding, and too high clips through to the other side; Search Distance (its capture distance) kept small, or a point jumps outside the wall and samples world light; normal_bias lowered and view_bias raised removes bleed under objects; use_data_display shows the points. Keep the outermost row of points just inside the walls.

KEPT OUT: the grid resolution - resolution_x / y / z from 4.2, grid_resolution_x / y / z on 3.6 - is refused, as bl_create_light_probe leaves it out by a standing decision (its names differ by build); whether this call should take it is an open decision. type and name are refused too: another type is another probe.
bl_set_light_shadow:
The engine-specific shadow settings that live on a Blender LIGHT - the general half (hide_render, per-ray visibility, holdout, shadow catcher) is bl_set_object_visibility, because those live on the OBJECT. THIS AREA MOVES MORE THAN ANY OTHER, read off bl_rna on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1: light.cycles.cast_shadow exists on 3.6 ONLY and was removed at 4.2; CONTACT SHADOWS exist on 3.6 and 4.2 and EEVEE Next dropped them at 4.4; shadow_buffer_samples/_size are 3.6 only; and jitter, filter radius and max resolution arrived at 4.2. ANYTHING THIS BUILD LACKS IS REFUSED, naming which builds have it - accepting a key and writing it only where it exists is how a caller asks for shadows off, gets shadows on, and is told nothing. Values are read back per key because several are silently CLAMPED rather than refused, and `clamped` reports where the stored value differs from the request. Settings the ACTIVE ENGINE will not read (cycles.* under EEVEE, contact shadows under Cycles) are still written - a scene is often set up under one renderer and rendered with another - but reported in inertUnderThisEngine so the difference is visible.

Parameters (all default None: left as the light has it; at least one setting must be given). object (str, required; also accepted as light or name) is a LIGHT object. On the light, every build: enabled (bool) is use_shadow, the master shadow toggle; soft_size (float) is shadow_soft_size, the radius that softens the shadow edge (POINT and SPOT; on AREA and SUN it changes nothing, as measuredNoEffect says); buffer_clip_start (float) is shadow_buffer_clip_start, the shadow map's near clip (read only by 3.6's EEVEE). 3.6 and 4.2 only: color ([r, g, b], finite) is shadow_color. 4.2 and later: filter_radius (float) is shadow_filter_radius, jitter_overblur (float) is shadow_jitter_overblur (it acts only with jitter on) and max_resolution (int) is shadow_maximum_resolution - EEVEE settings. 3.6 and 4.2 only: contact_shadow (bool) is use_contact_shadow, with contact_distance, contact_bias and contact_thickness (float) - EEVEE contact shadows. On light.cycles: cycles_cast_shadow (bool, 3.6 only) is cast_shadow; every build: cycles_max_bounces (int) is max_bounces, cycles_mis (bool) is use_multiple_importance_sampling, is_portal (bool) makes an area light a light portal and is_caustics_light (bool) marks the light for shadow caustics.

OUT: ok, light, engine, applied (each key read back off the light), clamped ({key: {requested, stored}} where Blender stored something else, or null), inertUnderThisEngine (cycles keys under a non-Cycles engine, contact keys under Cycles, or null), note, measuredNoEffect ({key: why} for keys measured to change no pixel for this light type and engine, or null), measuredNoEffectNote, blenderVersion.

Refused with nothing changed: an unknown key; an object that does not exist or is not a LIGHT; no setting given; a color that is not a list of at least three; any key this build lacks (the refusal names the property and the builds that have it). A value that fails to parse - a bad boolean word, a fractional int, a non-finite number or color - is refused while the keys are being written, so the keys before it in the order above may already have been applied.
bl_add_particles:
Add a Blender particle system: EMITTER throws particles over time (steam, sparks) and HAIR instances geometry across a surface without moving (rubble, grass). Type-specific settings are refused on the wrong type. render_type OBJECT without instance_object renders NOTHING and Blender reports no error, so the two are validated together. AN EMITTER DEFAULTS TO render_type HALO, WHICH ALSO RENDERS NOTHING in EEVEE, Cycles and Workbench - pass instance_object or instance_collection to see the particles; the response's renderNote says whenever a system will draw nothing. HAIR takes NONE, PATH, OBJECT or COLLECTION and defaults to PATH. ON A HAIR SYSTEM normal_factor IS THE STRAND LENGTH TOO: hair_length = 4 x normal_factor, one stored value, so normal_factor 0 means no hair - send one of the two; a pair that disagrees is refused.

HAIR AND SCATTER SETTINGS (2026-10-04), on bl_add_particles and bl_set_particles alike, each read back in the system's row:
- children {type NONE | SIMPLE | INTERPOLATED (the build's own list), viewport, render, clump, clumpShape, length, radius, roughness {uniform, endpoint, random}}. viewport is child_nbr on 3.6 and child_percent from 4.x, resolved per build; INTERPOLATED children follow the guides (20 hairs at viewport 10 gave 200 child particles on every build). child_count and children together are refused - child_count is SIMPLE children at one count.
- material: the render material, a slot number (1 is the first) or the name of a material in one of the object's slots - a hair shader in a second slot.
- collection {pickRandom, useCount} for a COLLECTION render. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: 20 hairs on a 3-object collection gave 7, 7 and 6 per object with Pick Random off (it cycles by particle index) and 8, 7 and 5 with it on.
- rotation {advanced, randomFactor, phase, phaseRandom}. Any rotation value turns rotations on, and on a HAIR system Advanced too (use_advanced_hair: a new system has it OFF on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1 alike - 3.6's RNA default reads True, but the system a modifier makes reads False, measured); an explicit advanced false beside rotation values on HAIR is refused.
- groups {density, velocity, length, clump, kink, roughness1, roughness2, roughnessEnd, size, tangent, rotation, field, twist}: each a vertex group name or {group, invert}, "" to clear. They live on the particle SYSTEM, not its settings, on all three builds; a name the object lacks is refused with its groups. A density group painted at 0.5 thins an area (1.0 is full density).
Every value is checked against the build's RNA before the first write; bl_set_particles reports the previous values in before.

DENSITY BY VERTEX GROUP (2026-10-05): vertex_group_density names a vertex group of the emitter whose weights scale where particles grow - fur on one part of a body. The group lives on the particle SYSTEM, where no other writer reaches; it is checked before anything is created and read back as vertexGroupDensity (bl_list_particles too). Blender grows the density between weighted and unweighted vertices, so a group spreads a little past its own vertices - pick the inner vertices for a sharp edge. An empty string clears it.

VELOCITY ALONG THE EMITTER'S AXES, HAIR DYNAMICS AND STRAND SHAPE (2026-10-05): object_align_factor [x, y, z] (-200 to 200) is velocity along the emitter object's own axes - rain falling straight down is normal_factor 0 and [0, 0, -1] - and object_factor carries the emitter's own motion into the particles. hair_dynamics (HAIR only) {use, quality, pinStiffness, mass, bendingStiffness, collision {distanceMin, collection}, cacheRange [start, end]} writes the system's own cloth (psys.cloth, which exists only with dynamics on - so the other keys need use true or dynamics already on); bl_bake_physics {object, modifier: the system's name} bakes it. strand_shape {shape (-1 to 1), rootRadius, tipRadius, radiusScale, closeTip} sets how a strand renders. Every row now carries objectAlignFactor, objectFactor, strandShape and hairDynamics read back, and an EMITTER's liveParticles - the alive count and bounds at the current frame, off the evaluated system. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: object_align_factor [0, 0, -5] put 20 particles released at frame 1 between z -2.5 and -1.0 at frame 10, the control at 0; a hair system's dynamics baked 12 frames.

AGE IN EEVEE (2026-10-08): EEVEE does not give particle instances Particle Info's Age or Lifetime - an age-driven colour renders its first stop on every spark (Cycles colours each by age). For sparks or embers that cool in EEVEE, keep the age in a geometry-nodes simulation instead: bl_add_group_node zone {kind SIMULATION}, inside it Named Attribute 'age' + 1 into Store Named Attribute, new points joined each frame; Instance on Points after the zone; in the material an Attribute node with attribute_type INSTANCER and attribute_name 'age' drives the colour. Measured in EEVEE on 3.6.23 to 5.2.1 (test_blender_instancer_age): twelve instances, each brighter than the next by its own age.
bl_set_particles:
Change a Blender particle system that ALREADY EXISTS. bl_add_particles STACKS - three calls give three systems on one object, all emitting - which is right for particles, where dust and sparks on one mesh is ordinary, and it meant the only way to change a count was to add a fourth system beside the one you meant to edit. GROOMING THE GUIDES (2026-10-05): edit {tool COMB | PUFF | CUT | LENGTH | SMOOTH, center [x,y,z] (world), radius, strength (0-1; LENGTH -1 to 1), direction [x,y,z] (COMB's stroke, required there), falloff SMOOTH | LINEAR | CONSTANT, symmetry 'X'} runs one brush pass over a HAIR system's guides, alone in its call. Each key's weight is the falloff of its distance from the center times the strength; the root never moves. COMB moves the keys along the stroke and keeps every segment's length (so a combed tip also drops); PUFF turns each segment toward the surface normal at the root; CUT scales a guide from its root by 1 - the tip's weight, LENGTH by 1 + it; SMOOTH pulls each inner key toward its neighbours' middle. symmetry 'X' runs the same pass mirrored across the object's X (the stroke mirrored too). Reply: guides, keysPerGuide, guidesMoved, longestDisplacement, tips (up to 8 moved guides' tip before and after, read off the evaluated hair) and readBackMatches.
THE ROUTE, measured first on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: writing a hair key's co or co_local does nothing (the original's co reads 0,0,0 and the evaluated hair does not move, in or out of particle edit mode), and particle.brush_edit's poll fails without a 3D view; one particle-edit toggle gives the original system its guides, and HairKey.co_object_set moves a key for good (a tip set 0.3 along X read back 0.3 along X; is_edited true; it survived another toggle). That is what this does. Measured on all three: a COMB at radius 0.6 moved 16 of 60 guides, a CUT at 0.5 everywhere moved each tip 0.25 on 0.5 guides, a LENGTH at 1 doubled them. Once edited, writing the count or the hair length regenerates the guides and drops the edit.

vertex_group_density (2026-10-05) changes the vertex group that scales a system's density, as bl_add_particles sets it; an empty string clears it, and a group the object lacks is refused with nothing changed. object_align_factor, object_factor, hair_dynamics and strand_shape as on bl_add_particles (2026-10-05).
bl_set_physics_world:
The SCENE-level Blender simulation settings. bl_physics_info has always reported substeps and solverIterations and nothing could write either, so the addon could add rigid bodies, bake them, and report exactly how the solver was configured while being unable to change any of it. Those two are what you raise when bodies jitter or tunnel through a floor, and scene gravity drives every rigid body in the file. A GRAVITY VECTOR IS INERT WHILE use_gravity IS OFF - Blender stores it either way, so setting it alone changes three numbers and not the simulation, and passing gravity turns the toggle on unless you say otherwise. CHANGING A SOLVER SETTING DOES NOT RE-SIMULATE: an existing bake stays on disk and stays marked valid, so every frame you look at was computed with the OLD settings - cacheIsBaked and cacheIsOutdated are reported, and a bake made stale by the change is named. The rigid-body-world keys are REFUSED when the scene has no world rather than conjuring one, because a scene-wide simulation is not a side effect a settings call should have; add a rigid body first.

PARAMETERS (all default unchanged; at least one must be passed). solver_iterations (whole number): the rigid body world's constraint solver iterations per substep; Blender clamps it. time_scale (float): the simulation speed multiplier, 0 freezes it. split_impulse (bool): use_split_impulse, which reduces bounce on stacked bodies. enabled (bool): the whole rigid body world on or off. cache_start, cache_end (whole numbers): the rigid body world's point cache frame range. cache_step (whole number): written to the cache's frame_step, which on a rigid body world reads back 1 whatever is sent (measured), so it lands in clamped with a cacheStepNote. Every key except gravity and use_gravity needs a rigid body world.

OUT: ok, scene, hasRigidBodyWorld, applied {gravity, useGravity, and with a world substeps, solverIterations, timeScale, splitImpulse, enabled} read back, clamped {key: {requested, stored}} or null, gravityWasEnabledAutomatically, cacheIsBaked, cacheIsOutdated, cacheFrameRange [start, end], cacheFrameStep, cacheStepNote, note (the gravity toggle turned on, or a solver change over a baked cache that is now stale - re-run bl_bake_physics with clear:true, then bake again).

REFUSED with "NOTHING was changed": no setting passed; a world-only key on a scene with no rigid body world (one is not created - add a rigid body first); a gravity that is not three finite numbers; a value of the wrong kind (a fraction for a whole number, a word that is not a boolean). Every value is parsed before the first write.
bl_mesh_stats:
Vertex/edge/face/triangle counts and a world bounding box for a Blender mesh, plus the EVALUATED counts after modifiers - a Subsurf mesh has a base count and a rendered count differing by an order of magnitude, and both are reported rather than one chosen for you. THE BOX IS COMPUTED FROM VERTICES, NEVER FROM obj.bound_box, which is CACHED AND STALE: measured on all four builds, move a vertex to z=50 and bound_box still reports the old extent - mesh.update() does not refresh it, only view_layer.update() does. A box read off bound_box after any edit is quietly wrong, which is the worst kind of wrong for a number people position things against. Also guards the case where evaluated_get silently returns the UNevaluated object, which happens when the object is not in the active view layer's depsgraph. An object that draws instances - Geometry Nodes instances, particles, instancing - answers with instancesNote: instances are not part of any evaluated mesh, so this does not see them (measured on 3.6-5.2). ATTRIBUTES: `attributes` lists the base mesh's named attributes and evaluated.attributes the evaluated mesh's, with evaluated.attributesAddedByModifiers naming what the stack added - an Ocean's foam layer, a Store Named Attribute's output - which is what a material's Attribute node reads BY NAME. A CURVE, TEXT or SURFACE object is measured by its evaluated mesh (base is null - splines are not vertices), so what a bevel, an extrude, a resolution or a node group builds on a curve is readable. attribute_stats - a LIST of names, ['foam', ...], or true for every named attribute - reads what those attributes HOLD - min, max and mean per component (colours linear, as a shader reads them), off the evaluated mesh when there is one (attributeStatsFrom says which): a name that exists can still hold nothing useful, as an Ocean's foam under a JONSWAP spectrum does (0.093-0.105 everywhere, so a ColorRamp starting at 0.35 renders black). An unknown name is refused naming the attributes that exist. colorAttributes lists the colour attributes, and activeColorAttribute and renderColorAttribute say which one is active and which one renders - bl_set_vertex_color's make_active and make_render, which can differ. With frame=N it measures at that frame and puts the scene frame back; a cloth, soft body or rigid body cache that is unbaked, outdated or ends before N is refused rather than read. A mesh with shape keys beyond its basis is evaluated like a modifier stack - the keys deform with no modifier, and the evaluated box is where the keyed mesh is. With instances=true it lists each instance the object draws, its source and world transform.

THE OTHER COMPONENTS OF THE EVALUATED GEOMETRY (2026-10-04). components: true answers counts per component - mesh (vertices, edges, faces), pointCloud (points), curves (curves, points), instances (count), volume and greasePencil present or not - and the named attributes of each, read by Object.evaluated_geometry from Blender 5.0 (measured on 5.2.1). attribute_values {component MESH | POINTCLOUD | CURVES | INSTANCES (default MESH), domain, name, limit (default 100, at most 10000), start (default 0: the first value to return, to page past limit)} returns one attribute's values off that component, with its domain, data type, count, start and truncated (values follow the page); an index stored on the INSTANCE domain reads back 0-6 off 7 instances (the instances' attributes live on the point domain of Blender's instances point cloud, reported as INSTANCE). A missing attribute is refused with the names the component has, a wrong domain with the one it is on. On 3.6 and 4.4 there is no evaluated_geometry: components answers the evaluated mesh and drawnInstances - every instance the depsgraph draws, which counts a point cloud and curves too (7 instances beside one curve and one point cloud read 9, measured on 3.6.23 and 4.4.0) - with componentsNote naming the build, and attribute_values beyond MESH is refused naming 5.0.

A FRAME CHANGE STEPS EVERY LIVE SIMULATION (2026-10-05): moving the scene's frame evaluates each unbaked cloth, soft body, emitter or dynamic-hair particle system, dynamic-paint canvas and rigid body world in the view layer, and a fluid domain whose cache type is REPLAY - on an object hidden with the eye or from the render too (only hide_viewport or the modifier's show_viewport off takes it out). A leftover cloth on a render-hidden object stepped against a body's collision during a pose check and asked for 58.7 GB. So a call that would move the frame past such a cache's first frame is REFUSED before anything changes, naming each simulation and the colliders it would step against; bake them, take them out of the depsgraph, or pass allow_simulation=true, and the reply's simulationsStepped and colliders say what stepped. A Geometry Nodes simulation zone is listed (geometryNodesSimulations) and not refused: Blender exposes no baked flag for it.

instances: true or {start, limit (default 1000, at most 10,000), matrix}. Every evaluated instance the object draws - Geometry Nodes instances, particles, a collection instance's Empty (which answers its instances only) - as rows {i, source (an index into sources), location (meters), rotation (XYZ Euler radians), scale, matrix when asked}, world space, and sources [{kind OBJECT | GEOMETRY, source (the object), type, data, count}]. A Geometry Nodes instance draws a temporary object whose data keeps only its source mesh's NAME (measured on 5.2.1), so an Object Info source is found by that name; kind GEOMETRY is geometry the tree made itself. On 3.6-4.4 a Geometry Nodes point cloud or curves output is drawn as an instance too and is listed with its type. A start past the end is refused.
bl_list_group_nodes:
Every node and link in a Blender node group, plus whether the Group Output is actually reachable. That last line is the point: an unlinked Group Output is NOT an error, and it does NOT pass the geometry through - the modifier evaluates to EMPTY and the object disappears from the viewport and every export (measured on 3.6, 4.2, 4.4 and 5.0). The TERMINAL depends on the tree type - a Composite node for the compositor, a Material/World Output for a shader tree, a Group Output for a geometry group - so the answer is right for each rather than reporting a correctly wired compositor as inert. The `group` argument also addresses trees that are OWNED by something rather than living in bpy.data.node_groups: 'scene:compositor', 'scene:world', 'material:<name>' and 'world:<name>'. That is how a MATERIAL's shader graph is authored - bl_describe_material could read one in full while bl_set_material_properties could write only the Principled BSDF's own sockets, so the addon could describe a graph in detail and not add a node to it.

WHETHER A LINK CARRIES A FIELD (2026-10-04): every link row has fromShape and toShape, each end's own display_shape as Blender reports it - CIRCLE a single value, DIAMOND a field or a value, DIAMOND_DOT a field holding one value; 5.x adds LINE (geometry), VOLUME_GRID and LIST (the build's own list; read on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1). An Index output linked into Store Named Attribute's Value is DIAMOND at both ends on all three; a geometry link is CIRCLE before 5.0 and LINE on 5.2.
bl_list_images:
Every Blender image datablock in the file, by name, with its source, pixel size, channel count, filepath, packed flag, user count and fake-user flag - the second collection found created, consumed and not listable, by re-running the question that produced bl_list_node_groups. Images are made by bl_create_texture and bl_bake_texture and loaded for HDRIs and renders; bl_create_texture and bl_set_material_texture both take an image NAME; clear_scene purges them and bl_file_info counts them. Nothing listed them: the only two places in the whole addon that enumerated image names were inside REFUSALS, capped at twenty-five, so a caller discovered images by deliberately asking for one that does not exist. Neither asymmetry audit catches this shape, and both are right to pass - images have a creator and are reached by a caller-supplied key, so what is missing is a third thing they do not ask about. sizePx and users are reported because a 4096 image is a different proposition from a 64 one when choosing what to plug into a material, and an image with no users and no fake user is one the next save deletes. Pass source to filter by Blender's own image source enum (FILE, GENERATED, VIEWER); omit it for all of them.

Parameters: limit (int, default None = every row) caps the rows returned after sorting by name and after name_excludes; it must be a whole, non-negative number. name_excludes (list, default None) drops images whose name CONTAINS any of the given strings, case-insensitively (a single string is accepted too; empty strings are ignored). count is the number that matched before the cap. source is compared exactly (case-sensitive) to the image's source; a value Blender does not use is not refused, it matches nothing.

OUT: images [{name, source, sizePx [w, h], channels, filepath, packed, users, fakeUser, tiles [{number, size}] on a TILED (UDIM) image}], count (matched), filteredBy (the source or null), totalInFile. With limit: returned and truncated, plus truncationNote when rows were dropped. sizePx reads [0, 0] for an image whose size cannot be read.

Refusals (a read; nothing is changed): a limit that is not a whole number or is negative; name_excludes holding a non-string; name, image, filter or path (each refused with a pointer to what to use instead); any other unknown key.
bl_group_nodes:
Wrap existing Blender nodes in a labelled frame (mode FRAME), or move them into a new node group (mode GROUP) whose sockets are the links that crossed the boundary (each copy compared with its node before the originals go; refused and undone if one differs).

HOW (2026-10-04). mode FRAME makes a Frame node (name, label) and puts each node in it through the same rule as bl_add_group_node's `parent` - a node's location then reads relative to the frame. mode GROUP does what Blender's Make Group does, natively, because node.group_make needs a node editor a headless Blender does not have: each node is made again inside a new node group of the tree's kind (name), with its own settings, colour ramp, curves and input values copied, and every copy is COMPARED with its node - settings, ramp and unlinked input values - before anything is removed; a copy that reads back differently is refused naming the node and the part, and the call takes back the group it made. The links between the moved nodes are rebuilt inside; each outside source feeding them becomes one group input and each inside source used outside one group output (socket types from the build's interface, refused for a type it cannot expose), and the group node (label) is wired where the nodes were, at their centre. Reply: nodeGroup, groupNode, moved (each node and the name of its copy), interface [{name, inOut, identifier, from}], linksInside, linksIn, linksOut. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: a noise, a two-stop ramp and a Math MULTIPLY moved into a group kept Scale 7, MULTIPLY with 0.5 and the stops, the material's Base Color and Roughness fed by the group node; a Transform between a geometry tree's Group Input and Output became a group with one input and one output and the object's evaluated box did not move.
REFUSED: a tree's input and output nodes and frames; a zone's input or output and a node holding item-list entries (a capture, bake, menu or index-switch item) - their item lists and pairing are not copied, so group them in Blender or leave them out. The organizing is all this does: the evaluated result is the same before and after.
bl_set_node_property:
Change a Blender node that ALREADY EXISTS - its PROPERTIES (enums, toggles, vector fields: a Math node's operation, a Noise Texture's dimensions) and its INPUT SOCKETS (a Noise Texture's Scale, a Bump's Strength and Distance, a Mix Shader's Factor). Both were write-once until they came here: properties until 2026-09-07, input sockets until 2026-09-20, when a plaster variant could not re-tune its PeelBump for want of this call. ADDRESSED LIKE EVERY OTHER NODE OP: `group` takes a node group by name, or 'scene:compositor', 'scene:world', 'material:<name>', 'world:<name>'. `inputs` is {socket: value} keyed by the socket's name, its identifier (Value_001 - a Math node's three inputs are all called Value) or its index, converted exactly as bl_add_group_node's `inputs` are: finite numbers only, a vector or colour needs ALL its components ([r,g,b] into a colour keeps its alpha), a datablock socket takes a NAME. It is applied AFTER `properties`, because a data_type or operation decides which of several same-named sockets is live, and a LINKED input is refused - Blender reads the link and never the value (remove the link with bl_link_group_nodes remove=true first). inputsApplied is read BACK off each socket. ALL OR NOTHING: every property and input is snapshotted first and put back if any key refuses, so a refusal's 'The node was NOT changed.' is true - it was not until 2026-09-20. Unknown or read-only property names are refused BY NAME with that node type's settable list attached, enums validate against their own items, and values are read back rather than echoed. A property that holds a DATABLOCK - a Texture Coordinate's object, an Image node's image - takes the datablock's NAME; null clears it. A group node's node_tree stays with bl_add_group_node's node_group, which checks the kind of tree. ITEMS: items={collection, add [{name, type, format}], rename {old: new}, remove [names]} edits a node's item collection - a simulation or repeat zone's state items, capture, bake, menu and index-switch items, a File Output node's slots (with a per-slot image format) - each type from the build's own list, and base_path sets a File Output's folder on any build.

HIDE UNUSED SOCKETS (2026-10-04): hide_unused_sockets true hides every enabled socket of the node that has no link - Blender's own Toggle Hidden Node Sockets, done natively - and false shows every socket again; socketsHidden lists what is hidden afterwards ("in.<identifier>" / "out.<identifier>"). Layout only: a hidden socket keeps its value. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1: a Principled BSDF fed on Base Color and Roughness hid every other socket and kept those two. Duplicating a Group Input node and hiding its unused sockets lets a few vectors feed one region instead of one input linked across the whole tree. CURVE (2026-10-06): curve={component, points [[x, y], ...], handles} - or a list of them - shapes an RGB Curves (component C, R, G or B; C is the combined curve), Vector Curves (X, Y, Z) or Float Curve (component left out) node: two or more points inside the node's clip range, handles AUTO | AUTO_CLAMPED | VECTOR, one for all or one per point. The reply's curve is read back off the node and curveEvaluated samples each written curve at eleven x through Blender's own evaluation; bl_list_group_nodes values reads curveMapping on any curve node. Refused with the node unchanged: an unknown component, one point, a point outside the clip range, two points at one x, a node with no curve mapping. Case: a pale material given an S curve - [[0, 0], [0.25, 0.15], [0.75, 0.85], [1, 1]] on C - ahead of a Hue/Saturation node.

SETTLED 2026-10-11 (one live pass on Blender 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, each call read back): the Principled BSDF's Thin Wall is an input socket on 5.2 only (inputs {"Thin Wall": true}); earlier builds refuse it naming the sockets they have. A Sound socket (5.2's Sample Sound Frequencies) takes a bpy.data sound by name (bl_add_sound loads one) and reads it back. Bundle and closure item collections are edited with items {collection, add [{name, type}]}: a Combine Bundle's items, a Closure Output's input_items and output_items.
bl_add_collision:
Give a Blender object a Collision modifier so cloth, softbody and particles collide with it. RIGID BODIES DO NOT USE THIS - they collide through the rigid body world, so a floor for a falling crate needs bl_add_rigid_body type=PASSIVE instead. Giving the floor a Collision modifier and expecting a bounce is a common silent mistake.

A RIGID BODY THAT MUST PUSH CLOTH (rule d, measured 2026-10-05 on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.2.1). Cloth collides only with objects carrying a Collision modifier, and the coupling is one-way: a 0.4 m ACTIVE ball dropped 1.5 m onto a pinned 3 m cloth sheet fell straight through it to z -27.6 by frame 60 in every variant - nothing in the cloth ever holds a rigid body up. With bl_add_rigid_body alone the sheet did not react at all (its lowest point at frame 40 read -0.17, the same as with no ball). Give the rigid body this Collision modifier as well, and set its collision shape to SPHERE: only then did the sheet react to the ball passing (-0.07 at frame 40); with CONVEX_HULL or MESH plus the Collision modifier the sheet read exactly as with no ball. A rigid body that must rest ON cloth is not reachable this way - use a soft body or a cloth (pressure) object for the falling thing. The Collision modifier's place in a soft cube's stack (above or below its Cloth) changed nothing in one measurement: a 1.5 m pressure cube dropped on a collision floor read the same lowest point (0.5953, 0.3696, 0.0644 at frames 20, 40, 60) both ways on all three builds; read the rest height back (bl_mesh_stats at a frame) rather than relying on an order.

THE CLOTH'S OBJECT-COLLISION DISTANCE (rule e). ClothCollisionSettings.distance_min defaults to 0.015 on every build (the self-collision distance too; 0.001 is a tuned value, not the default). bl_list_modifiers(rna true) reads it on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1, and bl_set_modifier writes it ({"collision_settings": {"distance_min": 0.1}}). It is keyable: bl_set_keyframe on 'modifiers["Cloth"].collision_settings.distance_min' (and the self-collision distance beside it) at 0.1 on frame 30 and 0.015 on frame 60 made two curves on all five builds, and bl_evaluate_at_frame read 0.1, 0.0575 and 0.015 at frames 30, 45 and 60. The cloth simulates with the keyed value: a sheet falling onto a collision ball read its lowest point -0.85 / -1.17 / -1.31 at frames 30 / 45 / 60 with the key against -0.96 / -1.30 / -1.41 without it - a larger distance early keeps the cloth off the collider and lets the impact respond faster. Bake again after keying (bl_bake_physics rebake).
bl_mesh_distance:
How far one Blender mesh stands from another - a garment from its body, a cuff from its sleeve: each vertex's signed gap to the nearest point of target (negative inside), as stats overall and in bins {zStep, sectors, center} by height and angle round an axis, with radius (cross-section) and edge-length stats per bin.

WHY: the garment passes measured the gap from a cloth to its body by height and angle (a hood stood 5-7 cm off at the neck base at rest), and edge lengths and cross-sections by region, in raw Python each time. HOW: each vertex of object (evaluated - modifiers, keys and pose applied - unless evaluated=false) is measured to the nearest point of target's surface through a BVH, signed by the target's face normal there; a vertex farther than max_distance (default 1 m) is left out and counted as far. inside counts the negative gaps. BINS: zStep metres from the object's lowest vertex, sectors equal angles counter-clockwise from +X round a vertical axis through center [x, y] (default the target's bounding-box centre); each bin row has vertices, inside, gap, radius (distance from the axis) and edgeLength (edges whose midpoint falls in it). Stats are count, min, median, the percentiles asked (default [5, 95], linear between ranks) and max. region (box | sphere | vertexGroup with minWeight) limits the object's vertices. Measured 2026-10-05 on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2 against a 256-sided cylinder: a ring at 0.55 m reads 0.05 exactly, one at 0.6 m 0.1. LAYERS: the sign comes from the nearest face, so against a target with a lining measure one layer at a time. Refused: object = target, a target with no faces, a region that holds no vertex, every vertex far, bad bins or percentiles.
bl_deformation_stretch:
How much a skinned Blender mesh's edges stretch over animation frames, by region: posed over rest edge length per frame as p05/p50/p95/max and the share above threshold, per region {name: box | sphere | vertexGroup} in rest space, with the worst edges and their weights.

WHY: a garment's inner-sleeve vertices 100% on the upper arm beside torso vertices 100% on the spine tore 30-95x with the arm up, and only posed-over-rest edge length per region told that hard weight seam from cloth that merely moves (the body's own armpit skin measured the same way gave the target: p95 3.4x). HOW: each frame the scene goes there, the mesh is read as it evaluates (armature and every other modifier, the object's transform applied) and each edge's length is divided by its rest length - the base mesh in world scale. An edge is in a region when its rest midpoint is inside (both ends in the group for a vertexGroup); with no regions there is one, 'all'. Per region and frame: edges, min, the percentiles (default 5, 50, 95), max and shareAbove (threshold default 1.5); maxRatio and maxP95 over the frames. A sliver edge inflates max, so read p95 beside it. worst (default 10) lists the most stretched edges: frame, ratio, rest length, rest midpoint and each end's top three weights. action plays that action on the mesh's armature for the call and puts the old one back; the scene frame is put back. allow_simulation as on every tool that moves the frame. Measured 2026-10-05 on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a strip weighted 1.0 on one bone and 1.0 on the next, the second bone moved 1 m along the strip, reads 11.0 on the two seam edges and 1.0 elsewhere. Refused: a modifier that changes the topology (no edge would match its rest), 0 or more than 500 frames, a region with no edge, an unknown action.
bl_build_rib:
Grow a band off a Blender mesh's open boundary loop along a bone or axis: a RIB (cuff, hem band) to a radius or to rays at under meshes plus ease, or a FRILL in tiers with a fullness reached by folds.

WHY (2026-10-04): cuffs and a hem band were built in raw Python as rings from a cut edge along a bone (or straight down) to a radius taken from rays to the body plus ease; frills were not built at all. loop picks the rim ({near: [x,y,z]} world, {vertex}, {edge} or {index}; optional when the mesh has one open loop). The band runs along bone {armature, bone} (the posed bone's line, rings centred on it), or axis [x,y,z] through the loop's centroid, or by default the loop's own normal turned away from the faces it bounds; each rim vertex keeps its angle and height, ring k sits length x k / rings further on (rings default 4). World units; the new faces wind like the surface they continue. RIB: each vertex's radius goes from the rim's own toward radius, or toward a ray from the line out through the vertex to the nearest under mesh (evaluated) plus ease (default 0.005), over blend (default length) with a smoothstep; with neither the band keeps the rim's radius; a missed ray keeps it and is counted (rayMisses). slot (a material) goes on the last slot_length (default all) - on a mesh with no slot an empty slot 0 is added first. FRILL: tiers (default 1) of length each, tier k+1 grown off tier k's hem, the hem's radius the start's x scale (default 1.5); fullness (hem length / start length) is reached by waves folds (default 8, at least 4 rim vertices each) whose amplitude is solved for; separate_objects puts each tier in its own object (<object>_Frill<k>, its top ring a copy - join_objects and merge_vertices join them). Reply: rings with radius stats, or tiers with measured fullness and amplitude; rimNear, a point on the new hem for bl_fold_boundary_under loop_near; new face and vertex counts. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a sleeve cuff under an arm of radius 0.04 ends at 0.045 with ease 0.005; a two-tier frill at fullness 2 reads back hems 2 and 4 times the start. Refused before any write: no or an ambiguous loop, a rim vertex on the line, length or rings out of range, radius with under, an unreachable fullness or one under the scale's, too few rim vertices for the folds, the other variant's keys. bl_gather_loop is the gather variant.
bl_gather_loop:
Gather a Blender mesh's open boundary loop like elastic: a shrink weight group falling off from the rim, the cloth's shrink set to strength, and optionally the rim pulled in now and smoothed.
