WHY (2026-10-04): a waist or ankle pulled in like elastic was pinned or shrunk vertex weights plus smoothing, written by hand. loop as bl_build_rib's. group (default Gather) is written over: 1 on the rim, falling linearly to 0 at reach (default 0.05 m) measured along the mesh's edges. set_cloth points the object's Cloth modifier's shrink group at it with shrink_min 0 and shrink_max strength: Blender scales a spring's rest length by 1 - shrink_min - (shrink_max - shrink_min) x weight, so a weight-1 rim rests at 1 - strength of its length - measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2, a tube's rim at strength 0.3 settled at 0.7 of its length in 40 frames, its top ring unchanged. apply pulls each weighted vertex toward the loop's axis by strength x weight now (a round rim comes out at exactly 1 - strength), then smooth_iterations (default 2) passes move the falloff vertices, not the rim, toward their neighbours' mean by half their weight. Reply: rim vertices, the group's vertex count and weight stats, the rim's length before and after (apply), the cloth settings read back. Refused: strength outside 0-1 (exclusive), reach not above 0, smooth_iterations without apply, set_cloth with no Cloth modifier, apply on a mesh with shape keys.
bl_trim_to_outline:
Trim a Blender sheet to a smooth outline round an axis or bone - radii {front, side, back} or [[angleDeg, r], ...] - cutting along the curve, its new edge snapped onto it and relaxed on the original surface.

WHY (2026-10-04): a hood's skirt was trimmed in raw Python to a radius R(theta) round the neck bone, its new edge snapped onto the curve and relaxed; bl_bisect_plane cuts only along a plane. The axis is bone {armature, bone} (the posed bone's line) or center [x,y,z] with axis (default +Z), world units. The angle is measured round the axis from front (default -Y, laid square to the axis); radii {front, side, back} puts side at 90 degrees both ways, and [[angleDeg, radius], ...] (3 or more keys) names its own; a smooth periodic curve runs through the keys. A point's distance from the axis line is compared with R at its angle, at any height: keep INSIDE (default) keeps what lies within, OUTSIDE what lies beyond (a hole). Each crossing edge is split where it crosses, the faces across are split between the points (a quad cut across a corner keeps a five-sided remainder), the faces beyond are deleted; relax (default 10) passes move each new rim vertex halfway to its rim neighbours, back onto the original surface and out to the curve, and 30 snap passes follow. Reply: facesRemoved, rimVertices, curveError (largest |distance - R|), surfaceDistance (largest distance from the original surface), boundaryLoopsBefore/After, the keys used. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a grid trimmed to front 0.3, side 0.4, back 0.45 stands 0.3, 0.4 and 0.45 out; a sphere's two caps keep every vertex on the untouched sphere within 1e-5. Refused: nothing within or nothing beyond the outline, front along the axis, a radius at or under 0 or keys that dip under 0 between them, bone with center or axis, shape keys.
bl_add_inner_layer:
Make a Blender garment two-sided or lined: flipped, inset copies of chosen faces (part_near, near_openings, or faces), kept loose, joined at the rims into one closed shell, or a new object; evenly spaced lines in a band.

WHY (2026-10-04, 2026-10-06): a garment seen without its body (an asset viewer) lets the background through a sleeve, hem or collar - the far wall faces away and is culled; and a firm hood or collar is a panel set cloned inward and joined at the rims into one closed shell, the closed volume cloth pressure needs. part_near [x,y,z] (world) takes the loose part nearest the point; near_openings (world units) takes every face whose centre is that close to a rim vertex of the openings (every open boundary loop, or openings [{near}|{vertex}|{edge}|{index}, ...]); faces takes ALL, {vertexGroup, minWeight}, {slot: name or index} or {indices: [...]}. Any together; a face is copied once. The copies are moved offset (default 0.002) along side INSIDE (against the normal, default) or OUTSIDE, wound the other way unless flip_normals is false, put in vertex group group (default InnerLayer, weight 1) and in slot (a material; on a mesh with no slot an empty slot 0 is added first). join NONE keeps them loose in the mesh; RIM adds a quad from every rim edge of the chosen faces to its copy - one closed, consistently wound shell (needs INSIDE and flipped; a rim edge that also bounds an unchosen face is counted in rimEdgesShared); OBJECT makes them a new object name (default <object>Lining). internal_lines n cuts n evenly spaced lines into the copies between a band's two edges (a tube's two rims, or a four-cornered strip's long sides), in lines_group (default <group>Lines) - a stretch tape. uv_offset [u, v] moves the copies' UVs ([1, 0]: one tile over); otherwise they share the outside's UVs, so delete the group's faces on a bake copy. One layer per group: a group that already holds vertices is refused. Reply: facesByPart, facesByOpenings, facesByFaces, facesAdded, verticesAdded, rimFaces, layerObject, gap {min, max}, facesOpposed, internalLines {count, vertices, lengths}. Measured on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a 10 x 10 grid lined at 2 mm with join RIM is 240 faces with no boundary, non-manifold or flipped edge; four lines round a 32-sided band are rings of 32. Refused: no selector, nothing chosen, offset outside 0-0.1, a group in use, a bad side, join or faces, RIM outside or unflipped, lines on faces that are not a band, a taken name, an unknown material, shape keys.
bl_blend_weights:
Blend a source mesh's skin weights into a Blender garment under a soft mask - {box | sphere | band {zFrom, zTo}} with a falloff, or a vertex group's weights - then smooth inside the mask, cap the influences and normalize. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.

WHY: bl_transfer_weights' destination mask is in or out, so a region given the body's weights jumped from the garment's to the body's at its edge. The fix that worked, by hand: the body's weights blended in with a falloff (a neck band by height, spheres at the armpits), smoothed only where the mask is above 0, capped and normalized. HOW: at each garment vertex the source's weights are interpolated over the nearest face of the source's evaluated surface (world space; a source modifier that changes its topology is refused). The mask is worth 1 inside a shape and falls linearly to 0 over falloff metres outside it (several shapes: the largest); a vertexGroup mask is that group's weight. Each blended group becomes (1 - m) x garment + m x source; smooth passes (default 0) move a masked vertex toward its neighbours' mean by smooth_factor (default 0.5) times m; max_influences keeps the largest groups; normalize (default true) makes a masked vertex's blended groups sum to 1. The groups blended are the garment's armature's deform bones when it has an Armature modifier, else every group of either mesh but a mask's own - name them with groups to leave a pin group out. Groups the source has and the garment lacks are made (groupsCreated). Reply: verticesMasked, verticesFullyMasked, weightChange stats, cappedVertices, maxInfluencesAfter. dry_run writes nothing. Measured 2026-10-05 on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2: a strip on group A under a box mask with 0.2 m falloff over a source on B reads A 0.75 / B 0.25 0.15 m outside the box and A 0.25 / B 0.75 0.05 m outside. Refused: no mask, no vertex under it, source = object, a source with no faces, a bad shape, smooth over 200.
bl_add_strip:
Add a strip to Blender's sequencer: MOVIE (with its sound), IMAGE, SCENE, META, or an effect - COLOR, TEXT, ADJUSTMENT, a transition (CROSS, WIPE...) or a filter over inputs. An occupied channel is refused. Call mif_help("bl_add_strip") first.

type is MOVIE, IMAGE, SCENE, META or one of the build's own new_effect types (COLOR, TEXT, ADJUSTMENT, CROSS, GAMMA_CROSS, WIPE, ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, ALPHA_OVER, ALPHA_UNDER, COLORMIX, GLOW, GAUSSIAN_BLUR, SPEED, MULTICAM; TRANSFORM and OVER_DROP up to 4.4; COMPOSITOR on 5.2) - an unknown type is refused naming the build's list. A sound strip is bl_add_sound's. scene picks whose sequencer (default: on 5.0+ the workspace's sequencer scene when one is set, else the window's scene). channel 1-128 defaults to the lowest free over the strip's frames; a channel another strip occupies there is refused, never shuffled. frame defaults to the current frame. length (frames) is required for COLOR, TEXT, ADJUSTMENT, MULTICAM and COMPOSITOR. An effect with inputs [names] (two for a transition, one for GLOW, GAUSSIAN_BLUR, SPEED) spans its inputs' overlap - Blender ignores any length given, so frame and length are refused with inputs. MOVIE: file; with_sound (default true) adds its sound strip on the next free channel above, same start, cut to the picture's length (a one-second 24-frame movie in a 25 fps scene has 25 frames of sound); the reply's fpsNote says when the movie's rate differs from the scene's. IMAGE: file, or file plus files [names in its folder] for one strip per sequence. SCENE: source_scene, scene_input CAMERA|SEQUENCER, scene_camera. TEXT: text, font_size, color [r,g,b,a], location [x,y] in 0-1, align_x LEFT|CENTER|RIGHT (align_x up to 4.2, alignment_x from 4.4 - mapped). COLOR: color [r,g,b]. META: strips [names] gathered by Blender's meta_make (an effect fed by a gathered strip goes with it; the reply names it). settings {property: value} writes any other writable RNA property of the made strip (a WIPE's angle in radians, blur_width, transition_type; a blur's size_x / size_y); a setting Blender refuses removes the strip again. Reply: the strip row (name, type, channel, frameStart, frameEnd, duration, contentStart, blend, opacity, inputs, source with its frames and fps, modifiers) and the name Blender gave.
bl_edit_strip:
Edit a Blender sequencer strip: move, trim, slip, split, delete; blend, opacity, crop, transform; mute, lock, fades; RNA settings; its modifier stack (add, set, move, remove). Call mif_help("bl_edit_strip") first.

Everything is checked before the first write. frame moves the whole strip so it starts there; channel moves it to a channel - either refused when another strip occupies the place. trim_start / trim_end are the new first and last frame shown (timeline frames, after any move) and cannot go past what a movie, image, scene or sound holds; slip moves the content under fixed handles. split cuts at a frame (split_method SOFT or HARD) and the reply's right is the new right-hand strip; a split of a strip that feeds an effect is refused, because splitting an effect's input and then moving its other input crashes Blender. An effect with inputs is moved and trimmed through its inputs. delete removes the strip (refused while an effect uses it). blend_type, opacity (0-1), saturation, multiply, mute, lock, volume (sound, scene and meta strips); crop {minX, maxX, minY, maxY} in pixels; transform {offsetX, offsetY, scaleX, scaleY, rotation (degrees), origin [x, y], filter}. fade_in / fade_out (frames) key opacity - volume on a sound strip - 0 to 1 over the head and 1 to 0 over the tail on the scene's action, as Blender's Fade In and Out does; the reply lists the keys. swap_inputs swaps a transition's two inputs. settings writes any other writable RNA property. modifiers [{name, type?, remove?, enabled?, settings?, index?, curve?}]: type adds one (the build's list: COLOR_BALANCE, CURVES, HUE_CORRECT, BRIGHT_CONTRAST, MASK, WHITE_BALANCE, TONEMAP, SOUND_EQUALIZER, and COMPOSITOR from 5.0), settings writes its properties (bright, contrast...), enabled false mutes it, index moves it in the stack, remove deletes it, curve [[x, y], ...] in 0-1 replaces a CURVES modifier's combined curve (an S-curve: [[0,0],[0.25,0.15],[0.75,0.85],[1,1]]). A locked strip is refused unless lock false comes with the edit. Reply: the strip row after the edit, and the stack.

DUPLICATE, CONNECT, PROXIES (2026-10-08): duplicate {name?, channel?, frame?} copies the strip through Blender's sequencer.duplicate (which leaves the copy on top of the original) and places it at frame (default the same) on channel (default the lowest free one); it is its own edit, and a meta or an effect is refused (it would copy what it holds or feeds on). connect [strip, ...] joins the strip to others so they move together and disconnect true frees it - only where Strip.connections reads the result back: 5.2.1 has it, while 5.0.1 and 4.4.0 have the operators with no read, so they are refused, as is 4.2. proxy {sizes [25|50|75|100], quality 1-100, overwrite, build (default true)} turns a MOVIE or IMAGE strip's proxies on and runs Blender's rebuild_proxy; the reply (and bl_list_strips' proxy) gives the sizes, the folder (<source dir>/BL_proxy/<file> unless a custom directory is set) and the files in it. bl_list_strips rows carry connected [names] and a COMPOSITOR modifier's nodeGroup.
bl_list_strips:
List every strip in a Blender scene's sequencer - range, channel, source, inputs, modifiers - with named channels and, on 5.0+, the workspace's sequencer scene. Read-only.

Strips inside metas are listed too, each with meta naming its parent. Each row has name, type, channel, frameStart, frameEnd (inclusive), duration, contentStart, mute, lock, blendType, opacity, inputs (effects), source (a movie's file, frames and fps; an image sequence's folder and files; a scene strip's scene, input and camera), text and fontSize (TEXT), color (COLOR) and modifiers [{name, type, enabled}] in stack order. stripsRange is the first and last frame over all strips - what bl_set_frame_range fit_to_strips uses. channels lists the channels that are named, muted or locked. On 4.x sequencerSceneNote says the Sequencer shows the window's scene; on 5.0+ sequencerScene and sceneTimeSync are the workspace's. limit defaults to 200.
bl_set_sequencer:
Name, mute and lock Blender sequencer channels ({"3": {name, mute, lock}}); on 5.0+ set the workspace's sequencer scene and Sync Scene Time.

channels takes {"<channel number>": {name?, mute?, lock?}} on the scene's sequencer (scene, default as bl_add_strip). sequencer_scene (5.0 and later) is WorkSpace.sequencer_scene - the scene the Sequencer shows and edits, which need not be the window's scene; bl_add_strip, bl_edit_strip and bl_list_strips then default to it. scene_time_sync is WorkSpace.use_scene_time_sync (the scene's frame follows the sequencer's). Below 5.0 both are refused by name - the Sequencer always shows the window's scene there (bl_set_current_scene). Reply: the channels that are named, muted or locked, and the workspace's state.
bl_set_shading:
Smooth or flat shading, the auto-smooth angle, and weighted normals - none of which the addon addressed at all, so setting flat shading per polygon was a raw Python loop. Hard-surface game assets need it constantly: it is the difference between a bevelled edge reading as a crease and reading as a smear. AUTO-SMOOTH MOVED IN 4.1 AND THE OLD PROPERTY IS GONE - mesh.use_auto_smooth and auto_smooth_angle were REMOVED and replaced by a Smooth by Angle geometry-nodes modifier, so writing the old property on a 4.1+ build raises, and swallowing that would report success having changed nothing on exactly the builds most people run. Both routes are implemented and the response says which was taken, which matters because the 4.1+ one is a MODIFIER: it shows in the modifier list, applies on export, and can be removed. weighted_normals adds the modifier that fixes a bevelled corner shading wrong no matter what the smooth flags say.

Parameters: object (str, required; also accepted as name) is a MESH object in Object mode, not linked from a library. indices (list of int, default None: every face) limits smooth to those face indices; each must be a whole number in range, and indices needs smooth. weighted_normals_mode (str, default None: left as the modifier has it) sets the Weighted Normal modifier's mode, matched case-insensitively against the modifier's own enum (read from the build; CORNER_ANGLE, FACE_AREA and FACE_AREA_WITH_ANGLE on current builds). keep_sharp (bool, default None) sets the modifier's keep_sharp (preserve edges marked sharp). Both need weighted_normals=true; with weighted_normals=true and keep_sharp left out, keep_sharp is written as true, also on a Weighted Normal modifier that was already on the object. weighted_normals=true reuses an existing Weighted Normal modifier or adds MifWeightedNormal; false removes the existing one. auto_smooth_angle is in degrees, 0-180. On 4.1 and later, when shade_auto_smooth does not leave a Smooth by Angle modifier, the sharp edges are marked directly with set_sharp_from_angle and autoSmoothNote says so. Every Weighted Normal modifier is moved below the last Smooth by Angle modifier.

OUT: ok, object, faceCount, facesChanged, smoothFaces, flatFaces, autoSmoothAngle, autoSmoothVia, sharpEdges (on the set_sharp_from_angle route, else null), autoSmoothNote, weightedNormals ({modifier, mode, keepSharp}, or {removed} with a note when there was none to remove, or null), weightedNormalsMoved, weightedNormalsOrderNote, note (when facesChanged is 0), plus meshSharedWith, alsoChangedCount and sharedNote when the mesh is shared with other objects.

Refused with nothing changed: an unknown key; an object that does not exist, is not a MESH, is linked from a library or is not in Object mode; keep_sharp or weighted_normals_mode without weighted_normals=true; nothing to do; an angle outside 0-180; indices that is not a list, not whole numbers or out of range; indices without smooth. A weighted_normals_mode this build lacks or a bad keep_sharp is refused after the modifier step began: a modifier this call added is removed again, an existing one is left as it was. A build with neither auto-smooth route refuses after any face flags were applied, and says so.
bl_list_asset_libraries:
List the asset libraries in Blender's preferences - name, folder, import method, relative path, .blend count - with the build's import methods and whether the preferences are saved. Read-only.

Each row: name, path, pathExists, importMethod, relativePath, blendFiles (the .blend files under the folder, counted up to 2000), and on 5.2 enabled and remote (remoteUrl) - remote libraries are listed, never created. Also importMethods (what this build accepts now), userprefPath, userprefExists, prefsDirty, autoSaveOnQuit (Blender writes dirty preferences when it quits if Auto-Save Preferences is on) and on 5.2 useOnlineEssentials.
bl_set_asset_library:
Register a folder as a Blender asset library (action ADD), change one (EDIT: path, import_method, relative_path, new_name, enabled on 5.2) or REMOVE it; save=true also writes the preferences.

name is unique: ADD of a name in use is refused (Blender would add 'Name.001' in silence); EDIT and REMOVE of an unknown name are refused naming the libraries there are. path must be an existing folder. import_method is LINK, APPEND or APPEND_REUSE before 5.0; from 5.0 LINK, APPEND or PACK (the linked data packed into the file) - APPEND_REUSE is offered there only while the experimental No Data-Block Packing is on (measured: the setter refuses it otherwise), and a method the build lacks is refused naming the list. enabled needs 5.2. The preferences are user configuration, so they are written to userpref.blend only with save=true (Blender's Save Preferences); the reply says saved, and autoSaveOnQuit warns that Blender writes dirty preferences at quit anyway when that preference is on. Every refusal comes before any write. Reply: library (the row, as bl_list_asset_libraries), before (EDIT/REMOVE), every library, saved, saveNote.
bl_list_libraries:
List the .blend libraries this Blender file links - path, missing or not, what each links - and every library override with its state (system or editable) and the edits it stores. Read-only.

libraries: name, filepath, absPath, isMissing, fileExists, parent, linked {COLLECTION|OBJECT|MESH|MATERIAL|...: [names]}, linkedCount, overrideCount, needsResync. overrides: name, kind, state SYSTEM_OVERRIDE (made by Blender to hold the hierarchy) or EDITABLE_OVERRIDE, reference, library, hierarchyRoot, overridden (the RNA paths the override stores). library limits both to one library; limit caps the override rows (500).
bl_set_library:
Relocate a linked Blender library to the .blend it now lives at (filepath), or reload it from disk (reload=true), without reopening this file; reports the overrides a reload brought in.

library is the name bl_list_libraries gives. A relocation is always reloaded; a missing filepath, this file itself, or a reload of a library whose file is missing (Blender's reload raises) is refused before anything changes. Measured on 4.2-5.2: reloading a source that gained an object in an overridden collection resyncs the override on its own, so the new object arrives as an override - listed in added. Reply: before and after (the library row), overrideCountBefore/After, added.
bl_library_override:
Make a library override of a linked Blender collection or object (MAKE), mark members EDITABLE or SYSTEM, RESYNC, RESET, CLEAR it back to linked data, or MAKE_LOCAL. Call mif_help("bl_library_override") first.

MAKE (default) takes a LINKED collection or object (override_hierarchy_create) and, as the outliner does, removes a scene empty instancing it and unlinks the linked copy from the scene's collections. editable names the members to make editable (default the target) and scope picks SELECTED (those), CONTENT (what they hold: a collection's objects and collections, an object's children) or SELECTED_AND_CONTENT; the rest stay system overrides. fully_editable makes every override editable. data lists objects whose data block (a mesh, for its shape keys) is overridden too. EDITABLE and SYSTEM change members of an existing override the same way (data too). RESYNC and RESYNC_ENFORCE resync the whole hierarchy (4.2+). RESET drops the stored edits, CLEAR turns the overrides back into linked data, MAKE_LOCAL makes them local (4.2+); hierarchy=false limits those three to the target. kind (COLLECTION or OBJECT) settles a name both use. Every refusal comes before any write. Reply: hierarchy rows (name, kind, state, reference, overridden), and changed / editable / dataOverrides / removedInstancers / unlinkedFrom, or before, added, removed and reset.
bl_load_clip:
Load a movie, or an image sequence from its first frame, as a Blender movie clip for tracking; reports size, frames, source, fps against the scene's and the color space.

name renames it; colorspace is the build's OCIO name ("ACEScg" on 4.2-5.2), checked before loading; active (default true) makes it the scene's active clip, which the Camera Solver and Follow Track constraints read; set_scene_range sets the scene's frame range to the clip's. A clip whose fps differs from the scene's gets an fpsNote - set the scene's rate before tracking. Refused, nothing added: a missing file, an unknown color space, a file Blender reads with no frames.
bl_list_clip:
Read a Blender movie clip's tracking: each tracking object's tracks (frame span, bundle, error) and solve (average and per-frame error), and the lens, tracker and stabilization settings. Read-only.

clip defaults to the scene's active clip. Each object: name, isCamera, keyframes, reconstruction {isValid, averageError, perFrameError [[frame, px]]}, trackCount, reachStart, reachEnd, reachBoth, tracks [{name, first, last, markers, hasBundle, averageError, bundle, lock}] (limit rows, 500). camera, settings and stabilization are every RNA property by its own name, as bl_set_clip writes them.

SOLVED PATH (2026-10-08): each object's reconstruction carries path [[frame, x, y, z], ...], the solved camera (or object) per frame, before any orient_clip.

stabilizationResidual (2026-10-11): with 2D stabilization on, how much the stabilized tracks still move - maxPixels and its frame, and each location and rotation track's own - computed from the markers with the stabilizer's own model (the weight_stab-weighted mean shift of the location tracks, the mean turn and scale of the rotation tracks about it, each times its influence) and measured against the compositor's Stabilize node on 3.6-5.2; null when stabilization is off. use_autoscale's whole-frame zoom is not in it.
bl_list_collections:
The Blender collection tree with the four different things 'hidden' can mean, kept apart: hideViewport and hideRender are GLOBAL, while exclude and hideInViewLayer (the eye icon, the one people actually click) are PER VIEW LAYER and live on a LayerCollection rather than the collection. A null in a per-layer field means the collection is not in that view layer at all, which is why excluding an orphan does nothing. Also reports orphanCollections and objectsInNoCollection - both invisible everywhere while every field still reads correctly.

Parameters: view_layer (str, default None: the active view layer) names the view layer of the current scene that the per-layer states (exclude, hideInViewLayer, indirectOnly, holdout) are read from; with_objects (bool, default None, read as false) adds each collection's sorted object names; limit (int, default None: every row) caps the collections returned, and the reply then says returned and truncated (with a truncationNote when rows were dropped); name_excludes (str or list of str, default None) drops collections whose name contains any of the terms, case-insensitively, before the limit is applied.

OUT: ok, viewLayer, sceneRoot (the scene collection's name), count (the rows that matched after name_excludes, whatever the limit), collections [{name, inScene, objectCount, childCollections, colorTag, hideViewport, hideRender, exclude, hideInViewLayer, indirectOnly, holdout, objects (only with with_objects)}] sorted by name, orphanCollections, objectsInNoCollection, note, plus returned/truncated/truncationNote when limit was given. orphanCollections is worked out from every collection, before name_excludes and limit are applied. A null per-layer field means the collection is not in that view layer.

Refused: an unknown key; a view_layer the current scene does not have (the refusal lists its view layers); name_excludes holding something other than strings; a limit that is not a whole number or is negative. It only reads.
bl_set_clip:
Set a Blender movie clip's lens (camera), tracker defaults (settings), 2D stabilization and per-track settings by their RNA names; all checked before any write. Call mif_help("bl_set_clip") first.

camera: sensor_width, focal_length, units, pixel_aspect, principal_point, distortion_model POLYNOMIAL / DIVISION / NUKE / BROWN with k1-k3, division_k1/2, nuke_k1/2 (nuke_p1/2 on 5.2), brown_k1-k4, brown_p1/2. settings: default_pattern_size, default_search_size, default_motion_model 'Loc' / 'LocRot' / 'LocScale' / 'LocRotScale' / 'Affine' / 'Perspective' (mixed case - Blender's identifiers; LOC is refused naming them), default_pattern_match KEYFRAME / PREV_FRAME, use_default_normalization, use_default_brute, default_correlation_min, default_margin, default_frames_limit, default_weight, the channel flags. stabilization: use_2d_stabilization, anchor_frame, use_autoscale, scale_max, target_*, influence_*, filter_type. tracks: {track name: {motion_model, pattern_match, correlation_min, margin, frames_limit, weight, weight_stab, lock, color, offset, ...}}. copy_to_scene_camera copies focal length and sensor width onto the scene camera. A key or enum value the build lacks is refused before any write; a value Blender refuses mid-call puts back every earlier write. Reply: each group read back.

PROXIES AND STABILIZATION LISTS (2026-10-08): proxy {sizes [25|50|75|100], undistorted [sizes], quality 1-100, build (default true)} turns the clip's proxies on and builds them; the build is a job, waited for until every size has its files (120 s at most), and the reply lists them from <source dir>/BL_proxy/<file>. In a background Blender that job is never retired and Blender then cancels every later tracking operator on the clip in that session (jobNote) - track before building proxies. stabilization_tracks {location: [names], rotation: [names]} replaces the 2D stabilization's track lists (location one or more, rotation two or more; [] clears), read back.

stabilizationResidual (2026-10-11): with 2D stabilization on, how much the stabilized tracks still move - maxPixels and its frame, and each location and rotation track's own - computed from the markers with the stabilizer's own model (the weight_stab-weighted mean shift of the location tracks, the mean turn and scale of the rotation tracks about it, each times its influence) and measured against the compositor's Stabilize node on 3.6-5.2; null when stabilization is off. use_autoscale's whole-frame zoom is not in it. set_clip answers it after a stabilization, stabilization_tracks or tracks write.
bl_track_clip:
Place markers, detect features at chosen frames and track them both ways through a Blender movie clip; reports each track's frame span and how many reach each end. Call mif_help("bl_track_clip") first.

Steps run in order. markers [{track, frame, co: [x, y] in 0-1}]: a new track name makes a track, an existing one gets a marker; with a new object name they make that tracking object (an object track). detect {frames (default the first), threshold, minDistance, margin, placement FRAME / INSIDE_GPENCIL / OUTSIDE_GPENCIL} runs Blender's feature detection at each frame on the camera's tracks - a later frame finds the features found earlier again, as Blender does. track {direction FORWARDS / BACKWARDS / BOTH (default), tracks (default every unlocked one)} runs each track from its last marker forwards and its first backwards. Reply: madeObject, madeTracks, detectedAt {frame: count}, tracks [{name, first, last, markers}], trackCount, reachStart, reachEnd, reachBoth. Runs headless in a borrowed Clip Editor.

FRAMES AND JOBS (2026-10-08): each detection and tracking step sets the borrowed Clip Editor's own frame as well as the scene's (a background Blender never copies one to the other), and a tracking operator Blender CANCELS is refused rather than answered ok - in a background Blender every one is cancelled after a proxy build, whose job is never retired.
bl_solve_clip:
Solve a Blender movie clip's camera or object motion, then delete the worst tracks and re-solve in rounds to a target error; reports the error per round and per frame. Call mif_help("bl_solve_clip") first.

keyframes [a, b] sets the tracking object's keyframe_a and keyframe_b; "AUTO" is Blender's keyframe selection. tripod uses the tripod solver; refine lists FOCAL_LENGTH, PRINCIPAL_POINT, RADIAL_DISTORTION, TANGENTIAL_DISTORTION. clean {frames, error} deletes tracks shorter than frames or above error (px) after the first solve and solves again. rounds {dropFraction 0.1, targetError, minTracks 8, maxRounds 5} deletes the worst fraction by reprojection error and re-solves until the target, the floor of tracks or the cap. Fewer than 8 tracked tracks is refused. Reply: rounds [{averageError, tracks, deleted}], reconstruction {averageError, perFrameError}, targetReached, every track's error. Measured on a synthetic 30-frame sequence: about 3 px with every detected track, about 1 px after the rounds.

KEYFRAMES CHECKED FIRST (2026-10-08): keyframes [a, b] with fewer than 8 tracks holding a marker on both are refused before anything is written (the solver's own rule; it used to raise after the settings were set), and a solver error is a refusal. The reply's reconstruction carries path [[frame, x, y, z], ...], the solved camera per frame in the reconstruction's space - what a solve is checked against when the real path is known.
bl_orient_clip:
Orient a solved Blender movie clip: floor or wall from three tracks, origin at a track, an axis through one, and a real distance between two; moves the scene camera.

floor or wall: three track names (Blender's Set Floor / Set Wall). origin: one or more (use_median for their median). x_axis or y_axis: one track. scale {tracks: [a, b], distance in meters}: the camera is scaled (Blender's Set Scale), or a tracking object's solution (Set Solution Scale). Every track must be solved; three plane tracks on one point or line, or two scale tracks at one point (one feature detected twice), are refused before anything moves. Reply: applied, the camera's location, rotation and scale, planeResidual (how far the plane's tracks sit off it, 0 when oriented) and scaleMeasured (the scale tracks' distance after).
bl_edit_clip_tracks:
Edit a Blender movie clip's tracks: CLEAR_PATH, REFINE, LOCK, UNLOCK, JOIN, AVERAGE, COPY_SETTINGS, FILTER_SPIKES, PLANE (a plane track from 4), TO_MESH, TO_EMPTIES or DELETE; read back.

WHY (2026-10-08): after track_clip and solve_clip every clean-up step was the Clip Editor's, and the plane track, the bundles as a mesh and the empties that follow tracks were raw Python. Each runs Blender's own operator in a borrowed Clip Editor at frame (its clip user's frame set too - a background Blender never copies it from the scene). action CLEAR_PATH {frame, clear_mode UPTO | REMAINED | ALL}: markers before / after frame; REFINE {frame, backwards}; LOCK / UNLOCK; JOIN (two or more into one); AVERAGE {keep_original}; COPY_SETTINGS {source}: the source track's tracker settings (motion model, match, channels, correlation, margin, weights, colour) onto tracks, read back; FILTER_SPIKES {threshold px a frame, default 5}: deletes tracks whose speed jumps by more than threshold between frames (not Blender's filter_tracks, which first deletes every track shorter than 10 frames); PLANE {name, frame, image, opacity, auto_keying}: a plane track from exactly 4 tracks with markers at frame, its corners read back; TO_MESH {name}: a vertex per solved track; TO_EMPTIES: an empty per track on Follow Track; DELETE. Reply: tracks before / after, madeTracks, madeObjects, the action's read-back and the track summary. Measured on Blender 3.6 to 5.2. Refused, nothing changed: an unknown action, a key of another action, an unknown track, PLANE without exactly 4 tracks with markers at frame, TO_MESH on an unsolved track; after a proxy build in a background Blender the tracker is cancelled, and that is refused by name.
bl_build_tracking_scene:
Build the compositing scene for a solved Blender camera track: camera solver, foreground/background layers, shadow-catcher ground, light, cube, compositor; skip parts; the clip behind the camera.

WHY (2026-10-08): Blender's clip.setup_tracking_scene and clip.set_viewport_background operators poll for a Clip Editor holding a solved clip, so they were unreachable; they run in a borrowed Clip Editor, with the camera's tracking object made active (the poll reads the ACTIVE object's reconstruction - with an object track active it failed). skip [light, ground, cube, backgroundLayer] removes those parts after Blender's build; background (default true) puts the clip behind the camera. Reply: objects, collections, viewLayers, removed, cameraConstraints, cameraBackground, compositorNodes, groundShadowCatcher. Measured on Blender 3.6 to 5.2. Refused: a clip whose camera is not solved, an unknown part, a scene with no camera.
bl_create_grease_pencil:
Create a Blender Grease Pencil object with a first layer and a stroke material, on this build's API generation (legacy GPENCIL on 3.6/4.2, GREASEPENCIL on 4.3+), named in the reply.

WHY (2026-10-08): nothing in the add-on wrote Grease Pencil; an empty Grease Pencil object was declined earlier as a container nothing could fill, and bl_draw_grease_pencil_strokes now fills it. The data comes from this build's own collection - bpy.data.grease_pencils (legacy on 3.6 and 4.2; v3 from 5.0) or grease_pencils_v3 (4.3-4.5) - and the reply's generation says which, because a stroke's width is pixels on GPENCIL and a point radius in metres on GREASEPENCIL. layer (default Lines); material (default '<name> Stroke', made as a black stroke with no fill when no material has that name; color sets it); location; collection (an existing one, default the scene's). Reply: object, generation, layers (with frames), materials, materialMade. Measured on 3.6.23, 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1.
bl_create_image:
Make a blank Blender image datablock - a canvas filled with one colour (alpha, float, UV/colour grid, colour space), kept by a fake user, optionally wired into a material input. bl_save_image writes it to disk.

PARAMETERS. name (string, required): the datablock name; Blender suffixes it when taken (nameWasSuffixed). width, height (whole numbers, required): pixels, 1 to the build's images.new limit capped at 16384. color ([r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], default unset, which leaves Blender's black): the fill of a BLANK image; a missing alpha is 1; values must be inside 0-1 unless float_buffer is on, and an alpha below 1 needs alpha true. float_buffer (bool, default false; sent as float): a 32-bit float buffer, what a 16-bit PNG or an EXR needs. generated_type (string, default BLANK): BLANK, UV_GRID or COLOR_GRID, checked against the build's enum; a grid takes no color. colorspace (string, default unset, which keeps Blender's sRGB): a colour space name from the build, Non-Color for a data map. fake_user (bool, default true): keeps an image nothing uses from being deleted by the next save.

OUT: image, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, size [w, h], float, alpha, generatedType, color [r, g, b, a], colorSpace, fakeUser, users, source, wired (bl_set_material_texture's reply when material and input were passed, else null), note. The image is in memory only until bl_save_image writes it.

REFUSED with "NOTHING was created": a size outside the range; a malformed or out-of-range color, or alpha below 1 with alpha off; an unknown generated_type, or a color with a grid; material without input or input without material; no such material. A colour space Blender rejects (the refusal lists the available ones) or a wiring failure removes the image just made.
bl_create_lattice:
Create a Blender LATTICE object - the thing a LATTICE modifier deforms with. Found by asking what the addon can consume and cannot produce, the sixth time that question has paid: bl_add_modifier learned to point a LATTICE modifier at an object and bpy.data.lattices appeared nowhere else, so the modifier could be aimed and there was nothing to aim it at. TWO THINGS THAT MAKE A CORRECT-LOOKING LATTICE DO NOTHING, both reported rather than left to be discovered. A default lattice is 2x2x2, and eight corner points describe an AFFINE transform and nothing else - it can scale, shear and translate but cannot bend, however far its points are moved; canDeformNonLinearly says which you have. And a lattice only influences geometry INSIDE its own volume, so one created at the origin will not touch a mesh standing elsewhere while the modifier reports itself perfectly configured. Interpolation is validated against this build's own enum. FIT TO OBJECTS (2026-10-05) - Blender's Lattice Deform Selected in one call: fit_to [object names] places and scales the lattice over the objects' joint WORLD bounding box (margin world units added on every side, default 0; the lattice's rest grid is -0.5..0.5, so the box's size is its scale) and puts a LATTICE modifier aimed at it on each object - read the bounds, create, then one bl_add_modifier per object were three steps. Measured: two 2 m cubes at [0, 0, 0] and [4, 0, 1] with margin 0.1 give a lattice at [2, 0, 0.5] scaled [6.2, 2.2, 3.2]. fittedTo in the reply names the objects, the box and the modifier added to each. Refused before anything is made: fit_to with location, rotation or scale; an object that does not exist; one a Lattice modifier cannot deform (MESH, CURVE, SURFACE, FONT, LATTICE only - a light is refused); a negative margin; a box with no thickness on an axis and margin 0.

Parameters: name (str, default None: the op uses "Lattice"; Blender may suffix it on a clash, and nameWasSuffixed says so); resolution ([u, v, w] ints, default None: 2, 2, 2) sets the points on each axis; points_u / points_v / points_w (int, default None) set one axis each and win over that axis of resolution; every axis must be a whole number from 1 to 64. interpolation (str, default None: Blender's own) is matched case-insensitively against this build's Lattice interpolation enum (read from the build; KEY_LINEAR, KEY_CARDINAL, KEY_CATMULL_ROM and KEY_BSPLINE on current builds) and written to all three axes. use_outside (bool, default None: left as Blender sets it) writes the lattice's use_outside flag (Blender's Outside option, which displays and uses only the outer points). collection (str, default None: the scene collection) is an existing collection to link the lattice into. location and rotation (radians) are [x, y, z] or {x, y, z}.

The resolution is written after the object exists, so every resolution rests at -0.5..0.5 on each axis (restBounds reports it).

OUT: ok, name, type (LATTICE), collection, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, location, rotation, restBounds {min, max}, resolution (as stored), resolutionRequested, pointCount, interpolation, useOutside, fittedTo (null without fit_to, else {objects, margin, boundsMin, boundsMax, modifiersAdded, modifierNames}), canDeformNonLinearly, note.

Refused with nothing created: an unknown key; resolution that is not a list of at least three; an axis outside 1..64 or not a whole number; a malformed or non-finite location, rotation or scale; an interpolation this build lacks (the refusal lists the valid ones) or one that is not a string; a bad use_outside word; a collection that does not exist; margin without fit_to; and the fit_to cases in the description.
bl_draw_grease_pencil_strokes:
Draw strokes on a Blender Grease Pencil layer at a frame: points, radius (4.3+) or lineWidth (legacy), strength, material, cyclic; world or local space, or laid on a mesh surface at an offset. Each stroke also takes caps {start, end}, fill {color, opacity}, curveType (4.3+) and hideStroke (5.2+).

WHY (2026-10-08): drawing a 2D shot, outlines on a model or strokes on a surface was raw Python, written three ways for the three API generations. strokes [{points [[x,y,z], ...], radius | radii (GREASEPENCIL point radius, metres), lineWidth (GPENCIL stroke width, pixels), strength | strengths (0-1: point opacity / strength), material (a Grease Pencil material, added to the object), cyclic}]; the other generation's width key is refused naming the right one. layer (made when missing), frame (default the current; a keyframe made when missing), space WORLD (default) or LOCAL, replace clears that frame first. surface {target mesh, offset (default 0.01 m)} moves each point to the nearest point of the target's surface and lifts it along the normal - strokes on a model that do not flicker into it; the reply gives the largest error from that offset. Reply: generation, each stroke's point count, first and last points in world space, material index, width, and the layer's frames with stroke and point counts. Measured on 3.6.23-5.2.1: world points read back exactly with the object moved; points laid on a 2 m cube's top at 0.01 m within 1e-5. Refused, nothing drawn: a non-Grease-Pencil object, a malformed point, strengths or radii not one per point, a material without Grease Pencil data, more than 100,000 points.
bl_set_grease_pencil_effects:
List, add, remove or set a Blender Grease Pencil object's visual effects - Blur, Colorize, Flip, Glow, Pixelate, Rim, Shadow, Swirl, Wave - with every setting read back by RNA name.

WHY (2026-10-11): a Glow on a 2D shot's line work, a Shadow or a Rim were raw Python - obj.shader_effects, the same nine FX_* types on Blender 3.6 to 5.2 in both Grease Pencil generations. action LIST (default) | ADD (type FX_GLOW or GLOW; effect names it, default the type's title) | REMOVE | SET (effect); settings {property: value} for ADD and SET, written by the effect's own RNA types (glow_color, size, threshold, mode, opacity, ...) and read back, all or nothing - a refused setting on ADD removes the new effect. Reply: every effect in stack order with all its settings. Refused: an unknown action or type, an effect the object lacks, an ADD of a name it has, type outside ADD, settings outside ADD and SET, name/type in settings, a property the effect does not have, a non-Grease-Pencil object.
bl_set_grease_pencil_frames:
List and edit the keyframes on a Blender Grease Pencil layer: insert blank ones, delete, move, duplicate, scale their timing, interpolate in-betweens, or set their keyframe type - on either API generation.

WHY (2026-10-11): a 2D shot's timing - holds, a boil's three drawings each held three frames, in-betweens - was raw Python, and the frame API differs by generation (legacy 3.6 / 4.2 frames renumber by writing frame_number; 4.3+ frames are moved with frames.move, their number read-only). layer defaults to the first. action LIST (default) | INSERT frames (blank keyframes; keyframe_type, default KEYFRAME) | DELETE frames | MOVE frames with to (one frame) or offset (any number) | DUPLICATE frames [one] to | SCALE_TIMING frames (default all) factor about pivot (default the first; rounded to whole frames) | INTERPOLATE frames [a, b] step (default 1; keyframe_type default BREAKDOWN) | SET_TYPE frames keyframe_type (KEYFRAME, BREAKDOWN, MOVING_HOLD, EXTREME, JITTER). INTERPOLATE is a native point-by-point blend (position, radius or pressure, opacity or strength; material and cyclic from the first keyframe), because Blender's interpolate operators need an edit-mode 3D view; it needs the same stroke and point counts on both keyframes, no keyframe between them, and neither a breakdown, and replies each in-between's first point in world space. Every check runs before the first write. Reply: the layer's frames after, each with keyframe type and stroke and point counts. Refused: an unknown action, a key the action does not take, a frame the layer lacks, an INSERT or DUPLICATE onto a keyframe, a MOVE or SCALE_TIMING onto a keyframe that stays or putting two frames on one number, offset 0, a factor not above 0, an INTERPOLATE across a keyframe, from a breakdown, between mismatched strokes, or with no frame between at that step.

LIST with detail: true (1.3) adds strokes: per keyframe (frames, default all) every stroke's material, cyclic and points - position (space LOCAL default | WORLD), radius and opacity (4.3+) or pressure and strength (3.6, 4.2), vertex color - capped at limit points (default 5000; truncated says when). The read half of bl_draw_grease_pencil_strokes.
bl_set_grease_pencil_layers:
List, add, remove, rename a Blender Grease Pencil object's layers or set one's properties by RNA name (opacity, blend_mode, use_lights, hide, lock, tint); frames and stroke counts read back. MOVE with direction UP, DOWN, TOP or BOTTOM changes the drawing order. DATA writes the Grease Pencil data's onion skin and auto-lock settings by RNA name. GROUP and UNGROUP put a layer in a layer group (4.3+); MASK and UNMASK add or remove a masking layer (not on 4.3-5.0).

WHY (2026-10-08): a 2D shot's layers (roughs, line, colour, with lights off or a lower opacity) were set in raw Python. action LIST (default) | ADD | REMOVE | RENAME (new_name) | SET; settings {property: value} for SET and ADD, written by the layer's own RNA types and read back (an enum checked against its items) - the legacy layer (3.6, 4.2) and the v3 one (4.3+) have different property sets, both reachable. Reply: every layer with opacity, hide, lock, blend mode, use lights and its frames' stroke and point counts. Refused: an unknown action, a layer the object lacks, an ADD of a name it has, name/info/frames in settings, a property the layer does not have.
bl_set_grease_pencil_material:
Make or edit a Blender Grease Pencil material: stroke {show, color, style, mode}, fill {show, color, style}, any other setting by RNA name; optionally add it to a Grease Pencil object.

WHY (2026-10-08): a solid line material and a fill-only colour material are the first two things a drawing needs; materials.create_gpencil_data was raw Python. create (default true) makes the material, or gives an existing one Grease Pencil data. stroke {show, color [r,g,b(,a)], style SOLID | TEXTURE, mode LINE | DOTS | BOX}, fill {show, color, style SOLID | GRADIENT | TEXTURE}, settings {property: value} for anything else on mat.grease_pencil (5.2's placement_* and random_* included) - each written by its RNA type and read back. object adds it to that Grease Pencil object's materials. Reply: the settings read back (show_stroke, show_fill, colors, mode, styles), the object's materials.
bl_pose_coverage:
Where a Blender body shows through a garment per frame: a ray from each body vertex along its posed normal must meet the garment (inside vs hole). compare_to, an earlier garment version, leaves only what the change broke.

WHY: a weight change showed skin through the back of a shoulder only in a run's back-swing, and the nearest-face sign test (bl_mesh_distance) reads a body as OUTSIDE a garment with an inner layer, because the nearest face is often the inner one - so the test is the ray. HOW: at each frame (the scene frame is put back; allow_simulation as for every frame-moving op) every body vertex in region (box | sphere | vertexGroup, tested in REST space) casts along its posed normal against the garment as it evaluates; a hit within reach (default 0.25 m) covers it. Uncovered vertices are 'inside' (the ray back into the body meets the garment - it is under the skin) or 'holes' (no garment near either way). Reply per frame: uncovered, share, inside, holes, uncoveredVertices (first limit, default 200); uncoveredAnyFrame and worstFrame. With compare_to, per frame shared, newlyUncovered (this garment only - what the change broke) and fixed (compare_to only). Refused, nothing read and the frame unmoved: no frames, compare_to naming the garment or body, a region holding no body vertex, a body whose modifiers change its vertex count. Fix what it finds with bl_push_out_for_poses.
bl_push_out_for_poses:
Push a Blender garment's rest vertices out along their normals where the body shows through in any frame given, enough for the worst pose plus margin, faded over spread; re-measured until no frame fails. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.

HOW: each frame is cast as bl_pose_coverage casts. A body vertex fails when the garment is under its skin (need = depth + margin) or covers it closer than margin (default 0.005 m; need = margin - gap); a hole is counted, not pushed. A need aims 10% (at least 0.5 mm) past margin so the passes converge. The face the ray met moves its vertices by the full need, every garment vertex within spread (default 0.05 m) of the hit point by need x (1 - (d/spread)^2)^2; the largest need over frames counts. Rest vertices move along their rest normals, capped at max_push (default 0.1 m); then it measures again, up to passes (default 4). Reply: before and after per frame (uncovered, inside, holes, closerThanMargin), verticesMoved, push stats, capped, passes, frameRestored. dry_run reports the first pass and writes nothing. Refused, nothing changed: margin below 0, spread 0, no frames, a garment whose modifiers change its vertex count, a garment with shape keys (moving the basis would shift every key).
bl_recipe_fit_outfit:
Fit a bought garment onto a body in one call, check it in test poses, and refuse - naming the pose and the place - where skin shows through or a strap leaves the body.

It composes the tools that exist, on a COPY (output, default '<garment>_fit'); the garment itself is never written. (1) shape: method DEFORM (the default with source_body, the body the garment was made on) carries the copy from source_body's skin onto body's through a Surface Deform binding (bl_transfer_shape_keys), so its ease and folds come along - bodies of different topology are first matched by wrapping source_body onto body (bl_wrap_to_target, landmarks passed through); align RIGID or UNIFORM first fits source_body onto body (bl_fit_mesh) and carries the garment. method WRAP (no source_body) wraps the copy itself onto body at ease - a skin-tight piece. (2) clearance: bl_push_out_of, garment side, to clearance (0.004 m) smoothed smooth (8) rings. (3) weights: bl_transfer_weights from body, bl_normalize_weights to 4 influences, an Armature modifier on body's armature (or armature), parented as the body is. (4) poses: the presets armsRaised, stride and crouch (default), turned by role off the bone names (upperarm / upper_arm / arm, lowerarm / forearm, thigh / upleg, calf / shin / leg, foot, pelvis / hips, spine; the side from the head's x; the character facing -y), or {name, bones: {bone: {rotate: [{axis, degrees}], location}}} in the armature's space, keyed on a scratch action at frames 9001 on and removed afterwards - or {name, frame} you keyed (not mixed with the others). keep_poses keeps that action as 'MifFitPoses_<output>' (unassigned, fake user) to look at with bl_assign_action. (5) push: bl_push_out_for_poses at rest and then across the poses (margin 0.004, spread 0.05, max_push 0.05, passes 4), against the body vertices the copy covers at rest (a ray along the normal leaves it through its inside within cover_distance 0.15, or has come 3 cm or less through it) with the garment point nearest them more than edge_band (0.05 m) from its openings. (6) check: bl_pose_coverage at rest and in each pose. Skin in a fold (its ray meets the body again within 6 cm) and patches of fewer than min_patch (3) connected vertices are left out and counted; more than tolerance (0) vertices left REFUSES. straps {vertexGroup, maxGap 0.02}: a strap vertex resting within maxGap of the body after the fit and farther off it in a pose REFUSES. The refusal names each pose, the bones nearest the places with a count and a point, and deletes the copy unless keep_on_refusal; its payload carries perPose, straps and steps. (7) hide_covered: the body vertices covered in every pose, one ring in from the edge, go in a vertex group 'MifHide_<output>' and a Mask modifier 'MifHide <output>' hides them - turned off while a later fit measures.

Reply: steps (each with what it did), gapToSkin before (the garment on source_body) and after (the copy on body), testedBodyVertices, perPose (uncoveredBeforePush, uncovered, inside, holes, inFolds, isolated, patches), straps (maxGap per pose), hidden. Refused before anything is made: a body with no armature or no bone-named groups, a garment with shape keys, an output name that exists, a pose bone with constraints (a Rigify DEF bone follows its controls - key the controls and pass frames), presets on a rig whose bones are not named for them, DEFORM without source_body, ease with DEFORM, WRAP without ease. A body, source_body or armature hidden in the viewport is shown while it runs and put back; one in a hidden collection is refused. Garments are judged in the poses they will be seen in; a pass here is a measurement, not a verdict on the look.
bl_garment_reshape:
Pull a masked region of a Blender garment toward the nearest skin of a body, or squeeze it toward an axis against the body, keeping keep x the gap above target; a clearance floor, smoothing and a fold count. With dry_run=True it previews each change with its value before and returns a preview_id; preview_id alone commits it, refused if anything changed since.

WHY: a worn-up hood stood 3-5 cm off the head; the fix kept 10% of the stand-off above a target so the folds survived, faded it with height and smoothed the moves - in raw Python. Below the jaw the nearest skin is the shoulder, so the same pull dropped the collar onto it; that band needed a horizontal squeeze toward the neck axis. HOW: mode pull (default) - each masked vertex's gap is its distance to the nearest body point (within reach, default 0.25 m) and it moves toward it; mode squeeze - the gap is along a ray from the vertex toward axis {point, direction (default [0,0,1])}, at right angles to it, and it moves along that ray. New gap = target + keep x (gap - target) (target default 0.005 m, keep default 0.1), times the mask value: one shape or a list of {box | sphere | band {zFrom, zTo}, falloff} or {vertexGroup}, as bl_blend_weights takes it. smooth passes move each move halfway to the mean of its neighbours' moves. CLEARANCE FLOOR: no vertex ends closer to the skin than target, nor closer than it began - such a move is cut back (clamped). A vertex inside the body or within target does not move. The garment's REST mesh moves against the body as it evaluates now. Reply: verticesMasked, moved, move stats, insideBefore / insideAfter, noBody, alreadyWithinTarget, clamped, flipped and flippedFaces (a fold), gapBefore / gapAfter. Check folds later with bl_mesh_quality flipped_against (a copy kept before), and a lining behind its shell with bl_pose_coverage (body = the lining). dry_run writes nothing. Refused, nothing changed: an unknown mode, squeeze without axis or pull with one, keep outside 0-1, target below 0, a mask holding no vertex, object = body, a garment with shape keys.
bl_snap_to_surface:
Snap a Blender mesh's vertices onto another mesh's surface: NEAREST, PROJECT_NORMAL or PROJECT_AXIS, an offset along the surface normal, outside_only to push out only. Reports the vertices that found no surface.

target is the mesh snapped onto, evaluated (its modifiers and pose applied). vertices [indices], vertex_group (weight above 0), or neither for every vertex. mode NEAREST (default: the closest surface point - wraps round a limb), PROJECT_NORMAL (a ray along each vertex normal, both ways, the nearer hit) or PROJECT_AXIS with axis X, Y or Z (world, both ways). offset (world, default 0) lifts the point along the surface normal at the hit. outside_only moves only the vertices below that lifted surface - a push out, never a pull in. max_distance (world): a farther surface counts as none. A vertex on a clipping Mirror modifier's plane stays on it. Reply: moved, alreadyOutside, missed (indices that found no surface, left where they were - push them out by hand), maxMove. Refused with nothing moved when every vertex misses, or on a mesh with shape keys.
bl_add_quads_on_surface:
Draw quads onto a Blender body: rows grown from boundary edges (from_edges, distance, steps) or quads by world corners, each vertex snapped (FACE, FACE_NEAREST), faces turned out, mirror adds a clipping Mirror.

The garment-shell and retopology tool: target is the body (evaluated). from_edges [boundary edge indices - bl_select_edges boundaryOnly gives them] grows steps rows (default 1) of distance (world) each, along direction [x,y,z] (world) or by default out of the faces in their own plane. quads [[[x,y,z] x 4], ...] adds quads by world corner; corners within weld_distance (world, default 0.0001) of each other or of an existing vertex become one vertex. snap FACE (default: a ray along the strip's own normal, both ways - projects like a view, so a ring round an arm collapses to one side), FACE_NEAREST (the closest surface point - wraps) or NONE; offset (world) lifts along the surface normal. Every new face is turned to face away from the target. mirror X, Y or Z adds or reuses a clipping Mirror modifier whose mirror object is the target and puts new vertices that cross or touch its plane on it. Reply: newVertices, newFaces, snapped, missed (left where drawn), clipped, counts before and after. Refused with nothing changed: an interior edge, both or neither of from_edges and quads, a quad with no area or one already a face, two corners welded into one.
bl_subdivide_multires:
Run a Blender Multires modifier's Subdivide (CATMULL_CLARK, SIMPLE, LINEAR), UNSUBDIVIDE or REBUILD, and set its sculpt, viewport and render levels. Total levels before and after, base and top-level vertex counts.

modifier defaults to the object's first Multires (bl_add_modifier type MULTIRES makes one). A subdivide mode adds levels (default 1); UNSUBDIVIDE rebuilds one lower level per pass, levels passes (default 1) or fewer when Blender reports the lowest (lowestReached) - a dense sculpt becomes a light base that still shows every detail at the top level; REBUILD rebuilds every lower level at once. mode may be left out to set levels only. sculpt_levels, viewport_levels and render_levels (0 to the total after) are written after the run; after UNSUBDIVIDE or REBUILD a value above the new total is clamped and reported. Runs Blender's own operators (measured headless on 4.2-5.2). Refused with nothing changed: no Multires, levels with REBUILD, a level out of range, past 2,000,000 top-level vertices, UNSUBDIVIDE on a base that is no regular subdivision or with shape keys.
bl_remesh_mesh:
Remesh a closed Blender mesh in place: mode QUADRIFLOW to a face count, ratio or edge length (symmetry welded), or VOXEL with fix poles, preserve volume and the keep flags. Faces, quads and poles before and after.

QUADRIFLOW takes one of target_faces, target_ratio or target_edge_length - the last two are turned into a face count here, as Blender's panel does (its operator reads the count only; a call that passed a ratio got the 4,000-face default). symmetry [x, y, z] (the mesh's own axes) keeps it symmetric, and the open seam QuadriFlow leaves between the halves is welded (seamWelded). preserve_sharp, preserve_boundary, preserve_attributes, smooth_normals, seed. QuadriFlow is refused on Blender 4.4: it aborted 4.4.0 (std::bad_alloc). VOXEL: voxel_size (object space; default the mesh's own), adaptivity 0-1, fix_poles, preserve_volume, and preserve_attributes or preserve_vertex_colors / preserve_face_sets / preserve_mask - one flag on Blender 4.1+, so they must agree there; the settings are read back off the mesh, where Blender's panel finds them next. Refused with nothing changed: non-manifold edges (open holes - the count is named; close them with bl_fill_mesh_loop first), shape keys, a Multires, a voxel size that would make over 200 million cells.
bl_set_face_sets:
Make, extend or clear a Blender mesh's sculpt face sets - FROM_SEAMS, FROM_MATERIAL, FROM_LOOSE_PARTS, FROM_VISIBLE, FROM_FACES, FROM_BOX - or RELAX the borders between them. Set ids and face counts.

Face sets split a mesh into regions without separating it; bl_sculpt_stroke masks by them (mask {faceSets: [ids]}). They are Blender's own .sculpt_face_set INT face attribute, written directly, so this works headless. FROM_SEAMS: each region bounded by UV seams is a set (bl_mark_seams marks them) - one set per garment panel. FROM_MATERIAL: set = material slot + 1. FROM_LOOSE_PARTS: one set per connected part. These three replace every set. FROM_VISIBLE (the faces not hidden), FROM_FACES (faces [indices]) and FROM_BOX (box {min, max} world, the faces whose centre is inside) go into set_id - a new set one above the highest by default, or an existing id to EXTEND it; a mesh with no sets starts at set 1. CLEAR removes the attribute. RELAX is the Relax Face Sets filter: each vertex on a border between sets moves toward its border neighbours, iterations (default 5) x strength (default 0.5); open-boundary vertices stay. Reply: setCount and every set's id and face count, before and after. Refused with nothing changed: no seams for FROM_SEAMS, an empty box, RELAX with one set or shape keys, CLEAR with no sets.
bl_resize_image:
Resize a Blender image read from a file to an exact width and height and re-encode it (filepath, format PNG, TARGA, OPEN_EXR, JPEG); pack packs the file. Replies sizes before and after, and the written file read back.

WHY (2026-10-06): a painted colour map had to be re-exported at 4K and its normal at 8K; Image.scale appeared only in preview thumbnails and bake_texture only makes an image at a size. The image must be READ FROM A FILE with no unsaved edits (a generated canvas or one with edits in memory is refused - bl_save_image writes it first), so a failed write is undone by reading the file again. A packed image is refused (the packed copy would stay at the old size) and so is a tiled one (scale reaches its first tile). Without filepath the resize lives in memory only and the note says so; with it the datablock is written through bl_save_image's route and points at the new file. An EXR of an 8-bit image is refused. colorspace is set before the resize.
bl_create_udim_image:
Load tile files {1001: file, 1002: file} as one tiled (UDIM) Blender image, optionally wired to a material input; filepath with <UDIM> copies them into one pattern. Replies each tile's size.

WHY (2026-10-06): a face texture on tile 1001 and a body texture on 1002 had to load as one image over two UV tiles, and nothing made a tiled image. Each tile keeps its file's own size. Without filepath the files must already be named by one pattern (body.1001.png, body.1002.png in one folder); with a filepath holding <UDIM> each file is COPIED to its tile's name there - same extension, since bl_resize_image is what re-encodes. Refused before anything is copied or loaded: a missing file, a tile outside 1001-2000, names that fit no pattern, a pattern without <UDIM>, a mismatched extension, and a folder holding OTHER tiles of the pattern (Blender loads every tile it finds). bl_list_images rows of a tiled image carry their tiles. A UV map reaches tile 1002 at u 1-2.
bl_create_view_layer:
Add a Blender view layer - a second pass over the same scene with its own collection visibility and its own outputs. copy_from carries the enabled passes across, because Blender's new layers start from defaults, which is rarely what somebody splitting a shot into layers wants.

name (str, required) is the new layer's name; a name the scene already has is refused rather than suffixed. use (bool, default None) sets whether the new layer renders; omitted, Blender's default for a new layer stands. copy_from copies every use_pass_* flag the source layer has; a pass that cannot be written under the current engine is skipped silently, so check enabledPasses in the reply. Only passes are copied - not collection visibility, samples, AOVs, light groups or a material override. The layer is added to the current scene.

OUT: ok, scene, copiedFrom (or null), then the layer row: name, renders, isActive, enabledPasses (names without the use_pass_ prefix), passCount, samples, cryptomatteDepth, materialOverride, aovs [{name, type}], lightgroups.

Refused: an unknown key; name missing; a view layer by that name already in the scene (NOTHING was created); a copy_from layer the scene does not have, listing the layers present; a use that is not a boolean (NOTHING was created). All are raised before the layer is made.
bl_create_volume:
Create a Blender VOLUME object - the container for OpenVDB grids, filled by geometry nodes or loaded from a .vdb file. The third object type on the same measured argument as bl_create_curves and bl_create_point_cloud, and checked for THIS type rather than assumed from the other two: with a volume-outputting group (Mesh Grid into Mesh to Volume) an empty volume evaluates to a grid on 3.6.23, 4.4.0 and 5.0.1 alike. OPENVDB: filepath loads a .vdb (sequence=true or {frameStart, frameOffset, mode}: every numbered file beside it), and the reply lists its grids - name, data type, channels, voxel size - and the world box; a file Blender cannot read is refused and the object removed. A VOLUME WITH GRIDS AND NO VOLUME SHADER RENDERS NOTHING, which is how this most often looks broken - a fresh volume object has no material at all (reported as materialSlots, a number rather than a warning to be believed) and Blender's default material is a SURFACE shader, which a volume does not use. No material is created for you: choosing somebody's shader is not this op's job. bl_object_info reports the stored and evaluated grid counts separately, which is how you tell an empty volume from a generated one.

PARAMETERS. name (string, default "Volume"): the object and data name; Blender suffixes it on a collision (nameWasSuffixed). location ([x, y, z] or {x, y, z}, default origin) and rotation (Euler XYZ in radians, same forms, default zero): written to the object. scale (same forms, default [1, 1, 1]): written to the object, not echoed in the reply. collection (string, default the scene's root collection): an existing collection to link into. filepath (string): an OpenVDB .vdb file to load into the volume. sequence (true, or {frameStart (the scene frame the sequence starts on, default 1), frameOffset (added to the file number, default 0), mode (CLIP, EXTEND, REPEAT or PING_PONG, this build's list)}): the file is one of a numbered sequence (name_0001.vdb ...) and every number beside it is found; missingNumbers names a gap. Every vector needs finite numbers, and a dict must name at least one of x, y, z.

OUT: ok, name, type (VOLUME), collection, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, location, rotation, dataName, pointCount (0 for a node-driven volume, null for a file), isEmpty (true unless a file was loaded), note, and with filepath: filepath, grids [{name, dataType, channels, voxelSize}], gridCount, activeGrid, bboxWorld and sequence {frames, first, last, frameStart, frameOffset, sequenceMode}, materialSlots (0 on a fresh volume), renderNote (a volume needs a volume shader to render).

REFUSED with nothing created: a malformed or non-finite location, rotation or scale; a collection that does not exist (lists the ones present); a build with no bpy.data.volumes. A filepath that is missing or not .vdb, sequence without filepath or with an unknown key, and a file Blender cannot read grids from (the object is removed again). resolution (set by the generating node or the file) and density (a grid attribute), plus points, count, radius, nodeGroup and material, are refused with a note on where each is set instead.
bl_create_nurbs_surface: Create a Blender SURFACE object - a NURBS surface with real control points (a PATCH, CYLINDER, SPHERE or TORUS), its grid, orders and resolutions read back with the faces it evaluates to. See mif_help. Made with Blender's own Add > Surface primitives (surface.primitive_nurbs_surface_*_add, enter_editmode off, aligned to the world), because a Spline's point_count_u / point_count_v are read-only and a U x V grid cannot be built point by point through the data API - and a SURFACE curve datablock with no spline would be an empty container that renders nothing. kind PATCH (default, a 4 x 4 grid), CYLINDER, SPHERE or TORUS; radius (default 1); location / rotation / scale / collection. controlPoints [[x, y, z] or [x, y, z, weight], ...] moves every control point in the object's space, U fastest - exactly the primitive's count (controlPointCount in the reply), and a different count is refused with the object removed. order_u / order_v (2-6; Blender clamps to the point count), resolution_u / resolution_v (1-1024), endpoint_u / endpoint_v and cyclic_u / cyclic_v set every spline. The reply carries each spline's pointCountU x pointCountV, orders, resolutions and flags, the control points (up to 256), and evaluated {faces, vertices} - what the surface turns into, so 'it has geometry' is measured (isEmpty). Refused in edit mode (an add operator there joins the edited object).
bl_create_metaball: Create a Blender META object - a metaball with its elements (ball, capsule, plane, ellipsoid, cube; radius, stiffness, negative), never an empty one; the family it joins and the faces it evaluates to read back. See mif_help. elements [{type (this build's MetaElement types; default BALL), co [x, y, z] (object space, default the origin), radius (above 0, default 2 - Blender's Add > Metaball), stiffness (0-10, default 2), size [x, y, z] (CAPSULE, PLANE, ELLIPSOID, CUBE; not a BALL), rotation (quaternion [w, x, y, z] or Euler radians [x, y, z]), negative (subtracts)}], 1 to 1000; omitted, one BALL as Add > Metaball makes. resolution and render_resolution (0.005-10000) are the polygonization sizes, threshold (0-5) the influence the surface is drawn at, update_method this build's Metaball.update_method; location, rotation, scale and collection (linked there instead of the scene's root collection; an unknown name is refused before anything is made) place the object. A METABALL'S NAME IS ITS FAMILY: metaballs named Name, Name.001, Name.002 are polygonized together by the lowest-numbered one (the basis), and the others draw nothing of their own - so a create that Blender suffixes joins an existing surface. The reply names the family, its members and its basis (isBasis, familyNote), reads every element back, and gives evaluated {faces, vertices} of the basis's mesh (isEmpty).
bl_create_world:
Create a Blender World datablock. The addon could NAME a world - bl_world_info and bl_set_world both take one - and nothing could make one, which two independent audits reported on the same day from opposite ends. A World that is not the SCENE's contributes no light at all: it is a datablock sitting in the file, and the response says isSceneWorld plus a note rather than leaving a caller to wonder why the render did not change. Pass use_as_scene_world to make it the active one. A name that already exists is refused rather than silently reused, so `created` never lies; edit an existing world with bl_set_world instead.

Parameters: color ([r, g, b], default None: left as the new world's own) is the background color, written to the Color input of the world's Background node; only the first three channels are read, each must be finite, and alpha is stored as 1.0. strength (float, default None: left as created) is written to the Background node's Strength input (the emission multiplier; 1.0 is bright enough to wash out a dark interior). The world is created with use_nodes on and a Background node wired to its output, which is the same node bl_set_world edits. name is also accepted as world; use_as_scene_world defaults to false.

OUT: world (the name Blender gave it), requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, useNodes (true), isSceneWorld, sceneWorldNote (null when it is the scene's world), color [r, g, b] and strength read back off the Background node.

Refused with nothing created: an unknown key; a missing or non-string name; a name a world already has (edit it with bl_set_world); a color that is not a list of at least three or holds a non-finite or non-numeric channel; a strength that is not a finite number; a use_as_scene_world that is not a boolean.
bl_paint_texture:
Paint a Blender image in layers, bottom first: fills (color, palette name, image) through masks of faces, a vertex group, a UV box, brush strokes or an image; MIX, MULTIPLY, ADD, ERASE_ALPHA; symmetry. Replies coverage per layer.

WHY (2026-10-06): nothing painted an image - dynamic paint is a physics wetmap and bake_texture only bakes - and a skin edit is a layer stack: a fill over the whole mesh, a black mask revealed by painting white along a pattern, a fill for one body part, pen lines, symmetry, a layer limited to one UV tile, the variation maps rebuilt by swapping the base underneath. Blender's own brush (paint.image_paint) polls False without a window, so the layers are composited with numpy straight into the pixels on every build. The canvas is image, or material + input (the image an Image Texture feeds into that Principled input). Each layer: fill {color [r, g, b(, a)] | palette name} or {image} (same size), mask {faces [i] | 'all'} or {vertexGroup} (the weight is the strength; both need object_name and read uv_map, default active) or {uvBox [u0, v0, u1, v1]} or {strokes [{points [[u, v], ...], radiusPx 4, strength 1, falloff SMOOTH|LINEAR|CONSTANT}]} or {image} (luminance); no mask paints everything; opacity 0-1; blend MIX|MULTIPLY|ADD|ERASE_ALPHA (ERASE_ALPHA takes no fill); tiles [1001] keeps a mesh mask to faces whose UVs sit in those tiles. base starts from another image's pixels. symmetry X|Y|Z adds the mirrored faces (object space) and mirrors strokes and boxes across the UV tile. Every layer is checked before a pixel is written. A tiled image is refused (Python reaches its first tile only). Painted in memory - bl_save_image writes it; alphaNotSaved warns when an earlier opaque save left the buffer RGB.
bl_project_image_decal:
Project a Blender image from a plane (origin, direction, size, rotation) onto the faces it hits - a logo on a garment: a UV layer and a mask written, back faces wiped, the image mixed over Base Color. Replies faces covered.

WHY (2026-10-06): a logo sprayed onto a garment - placed, scaled and rotated to the target, projected onto the faces it hits with a face limit, the back faces wiped, mixed over the current material - had no call; bl_uv_unwrap BOX writes one layer for the whole mesh. origin is the decal plane's centre (world), direction where it projects; the plane's right axis is direction x world Z (world Y when projecting along Z) and up completes it, both replied (rightAxis, upAxis); rotation turns them about direction, right-handed, in degrees; size [w, h] is the extent in world units. A face is covered when its centre is in front of the plane (within max_depth if given), its projected bounds overlap the decal and it faces the plane (wipe_back_faces false also takes faces turned away - backFacesWiped counts them otherwise). faces limits to those indices; limit keeps the N nearest (skippedByLimit). uv_map (default Decal; an existing one is overwritten, uvMapReplaced) holds plane coordinates, 0-1 inside the decal, on covered faces and -1 elsewhere; mask_attribute (default DecalMask) is a face-corner float, 1 on covered faces. wire (default true) adds an Image Texture (CLIP) through that UV map and a Mix before Base Color with factor image alpha x mask, in material or in every material on the covered faces; a re-run reuses those nodes. Every refusal fires before anything is written.
bl_spray_text_art:
Text in a font -> a spray-paint colour texture and a reveal map (outline, fill and highlight passes trailing a nozzle, a time per pixel) for a decal, and the first reveal at which the paint covers min_readable_area on a decal of decal_size. nozzle {path, radius} paints each pixel when a given nozzle path first passes within the spray radius of it.

WHY (2026-10-07): text art for a decal was made by hand in a one-off script, and a reveal's timing was read from the first frame any paint showed (11 cm2) while nothing read until about 60 cm2 on a dark wall at 4 m. text (font: a .ttf/.otf path, default Blender's built-in) is fitted into size [w, h] px (default 1024 x 512). Layers: fill = the glyphs; outline = the fill grown by outline_width px; highlight = the fill's upper-left edge, highlight_width px; overspray speckles the band overspray_spread px past the outline (that share halved, by seed). colors {fill, outline, highlight} are sRGB 0-1 as picked; the colour image is 8-bit RGBA, alpha the paint softened by softness px. The reveal map is float data written as a 16-bit PNG: R outline, G fill, B highlight, A the first paint, 1.0 where none - each pass over its window in passes {outline: [0, 0.4], fill: [0.4, 0.85], highlight: [0.85, 1]} as a nozzle sweeping its layer's box in columns stroke_width px wide, left to right, up then down; a material shows a pass where its time is at or under its Reveal parameter. nozzlePath gives {layer, t, u, v} points for keying a moving nozzle. readable: firstReveal is the N-th earliest first paint, N = ceil(min_readable_area / pixel area); reveal_keys [[frame, value], ...] put it on a frame.
