Measured on Blender 3.6 to 5.2 - a float image's PNG is un-premultiplied by Image.save whatever its alpha mode, so the reveal PNG is written by the op itself. Refused, nothing made or written: empty text, size outside 16-4096, a pass window not 0 <= from <= to <= 1, a negative width, a path not .png, a missing font file, min_readable_area without decal_size.

DRIPS (2026-10-07): drips {count, length, width, seed} runs paint down from the fill's lower edge (count starts by seed, each length x 0.5-1 px, width px wide, in the fill colour) and run_path writes a 16-bit PNG whose R is each drip pixel's progress, 0 leaving the paint to under 1 at the tip, 1.0 where none; a material shows a drip where that is at or under its RunDown. Reply drips {made, lengthMax, clipped, coverage, starts}. Refused: count outside 1-200, length outside 1-4096, width outside 1-64, run_path without drips.

GRADIENT, SHADOW, DRIP COLOUR (2026-10-08): colors.fill may be a gradient {top, bottom, mottle, mottleSize} - top to bottom over the fill's own rows, each pixel times (1 + mottle x a smooth unit-variance noise about mottleSize px across, by seed; mottle 0-0.5, default 0; mottleSize default 1.2% of the height). shadow {color, offset [right, down] px, opacity (default 1)} paints the outline moved by offset behind it at that opacity, revealed with the outline pass (each shadow pixel in reveal R at the time of the outline pixel it falls from); the default margin grows to hold it, and reply shadow.clipped counts what fell outside. drips.color sets the drips' colour, otherwise the fill's (its top colour for a gradient). Refused: a gradient without top and bottom or mottle outside 0-0.5, a shadow without color or offset or opacity outside (0, 1].

NOZZLE PATH (2026-10-08): the column sweep led or lagged a hand by up to half a metre; nozzle replaces it so the paint appears where the nozzle points, stroke by stroke - each pixel's time is the FIRST moment the nozzle passed within the spray radius of it. nozzle {path, radius | radiusPx, space, decal, offset, coneAngle, timeRange, passes, unreached}: path is 2-4096 points with rising times in any unit (0-1, seconds, frames); space 'uv' (default) [t, u, v] in the image's 0-1 (v up), 'decal' [t, x, y] in decal units from its centre (x right, y up; needs decal_size), 'world' [t, x, y, z] or {t, location, quat} (needs decal_size and decal {origin, normal, up (default world Z), axes 'unreal' | 'blender'} or {origin, right, up} - the decal's centre and axes, normal out of the wall; right is the viewer's right: normal x up in Unreal's left-handed axes, up x normal in Blender's). radius is in decal units (needs decal_size), radiusPx in pixels; coneAngle (world, full angle, degrees) grows the radius by the nozzle's distance off the wall x tan(angle / 2). timeRange [start, end] (default the path's first and last time) maps a time to the reveal value 0-1 (painted times clipped to 0.9998, under the decal material's 0.9999 cut). passes {outline, fill, highlight: [from, to]} in the path's time gives a pass its own stretch; a pass not named shares the whole path. unreached 'leave' (default) leaves a pixel the nozzle never reaches unpainted (1.0 in the reveal map; the colour map keeps it) or 'nearest' paints it at the time of the nozzle's closest pass. Reply nozzle {coverage (% of the letters' fill pixels the path reaches), layers {pixels, reached, unreached, filledNearest, coverage, segment, front}, unreachedPixels, unreachedSample [[x, y] px], front {maxDistance, p95Distance, maxLead, maxLag, maxBeyondRadius} in decal units (pixels without decal_size) - where each pixel's paint appears against where the nozzle is at that moment, lead ahead of its motion and lag behind - decalFrame}; nozzlePath echoes the path {layer 'path', t (reveal), time, u, v}. HAND RECIPE: read_component_pose(actor_path, sockets=['hand_r_socket'], sequence, frame) per frame gives sockets[0].world {location, quat}; pass each as {t: seconds, location, quat} with offset [x, y, z] = the nozzle tip in the socket's own axes (along the can), space 'world', and the decal's frame (mif_spray_decal fills it in). Refused with nozzle: passes, stroke_width, nozzle_samples (the sweep's), radius without decal_size, falling times, world points without decal, an offset on points without quat. Measured on Blender 3.6, 4.2, 4.4, 5.0 and 5.2.
bl_fracture_mesh: Fracture closed Blender meshes into Voronoi cells, one object per cell, in a collection. source RANDOM|VERTS|PARTICLES|POINTS; source_limit per object; recursion; rigid_body {type, collisionShape...}. Replies cell counts, smallest cell, volumes. WHY: Blender's Cell Fracture is an optional extension from 4.2 and is missing from many installs; this is native bmesh, so it works on every build. Each object's EVALUATED mesh (modifiers applied) is cut in world space by the bisector plane between every pair of seed points and each cut is capped - the cells tile the object exactly (their volumes sum to its volume, reported as sourceVolume and cellsVolume). The mesh must be closed (an open surface is refused). source: RANDOM (default) uniform points inside, VERTS the object's own vertices, PARTICLES its own particles, POINTS points [[x,y,z]...] in world space. source_limit 2-5000 (default 100) caps the seeds, an int or {objectName: n} for a per-object count. noise 0-1 jitters the seeds by a fraction of the object's size; seed makes the draw repeatable. cell_scale [x,y,z] stretches the cells along an axis. margin leaves a gap between neighbours. recursion 0-8 levels: each re-fractures recursion_chance (0.25) of the cells, largest first, with recursion_source_limit (8) seeds, stopping at recursion_clamp (250 cells, 0 = no clamp). material_index is the slot the cut faces take; every cell carries the source's slots. collection (default '<object>_cells') is made under the scene when missing. hide_original hides the source in the viewport and the render. rigid_body is bl_add_rigid_body's settings in its camelCase keys ({type: ACTIVE, collisionShape: CONVEX_HULL, density: 2400}) applied to every cell; if it is refused the cells are removed again. Reply per object: cellCount, smallestCell and largestCell {name, volume}, nonManifoldCells, cells [{name, volume, faces, manifold, location}], and created (every cell's name). Then: bl_list_objects near picks cells by distance, bl_copy_animation keys them from one template, bl_bake_physics runs the drop.
bl_copy_animation: Copy a Blender object's action onto targets: copy true (default) gives each its own action to edit alone, false shares it. keys keeps curves whose data path starts with one; frame_offset shifts the copied keys. WHY: bl_assign_action shares ONE action, so an edit to one object's keys moved every object using it; a template animation (a fractured cell's Dynamic flag keyed on at the impact frame, a clip reused on a second rig) could not be copied and then changed alone. copy true names each copy '<action>_<target>' and reports it in created; on Blender 4.4+ each target is bound to the copy's slot for the source, so it plays. keys (copy true only) is a list of data paths or their starts, e.g. ['rigid_body.enabled'] or ['location']; keys matching none of the source's curves are refused. frame_offset (copy true only) moves every copied key and its handles. copy false is Blender's Link Animation Data: the targets play the source's action itself. Each target row reports its action, slot, curve and key counts, and the previous action with whether it survives a save.
bl_paint_weights: Paint a Blender vertex group along a stroke of world points: radius, falloff, strength, mode MIX|ADD|SUBTRACT|REPLACE|LIGHTEN|DARKEN, accumulate, front faces only, a mask, auto normalize. No viewport. Replies vertices touched and weight range. WHY: bl_set_vertex_weights writes listed weights and axis gradients but has no brush; Blender's weight paint operator needs a 3D view, so the brush is done on the mesh data, the same on every build. path is world points, one point is a dab; spacing (a fraction of radius) resamples the path into dabs. Each dab reaches the vertices within radius (falloff_shape SPHERE) or, PROJECTED with view_direction, within radius of the line through the dab along the view - painting through the mesh. f = falloff (SMOOTH, SPHERE, ROOT, SHARP, LINEAR, CONSTANT over distance/radius) x strength. mode: MIX moves toward weight by f, ADD adds weight x f, SUBTRACT takes it away, REPLACE sets weight over the whole footprint, LIGHTEN and DARKEN only raise or only lower. accumulate false (default) lets one stroke change a vertex by its strongest dab only, as Blender's brush without Accumulate; true applies dab after dab (two dabs at 0.5 strength MIX to 1 give 0.75). front_faces_only paints a vertex only when its normal faces the viewer: view_direction (where the view looks, e.g. [0,0,-1] from above) or each dab's area normal. mask {faces: [i]} | {vertices: [i]} | {linked: vertex i} limits the brush to those vertices or to one connected piece. auto_normalize scales the other groups on each painted vertex so it sums to 1 - the deform bones' groups when an Armature modifier binds the mesh (the painted group must then be a bone), else every other group. The group is created when missing unless create_group is false. A stroke that changes no weight is refused with nothing written. Reply: dabs, verticesTouched, weightRange, meanBefore/meanAfter, groupCreated.
bl_add_procedural_texture:
Build a PROCEDURAL pattern into a Blender material and wire it where it is read - type noise, voronoi, wave, gradient, magic, brick, checker, musgrave, whiteNoise or gabor - no texture files. It makes concrete that reads as concrete, worn steel, grain and rust. The write half this addon did not have: bl_create_material sets base colour, metallic and roughness, bl_set_material_texture loads an IMAGE off disk, and everything between was out of reach. type: noise | voronoi | wave | gradient | magic | brick | checker | musgrave | whiteNoise | gabor. MUSGRAVE IS VERSION-GATED and refused by name with the running version where it is absent - it is in 3.6's shader menu and none of 4.2's, 4.4's or 5.0's, having been folded into the Noise texture, and the refusal reads the replacement's real properties off its own RNA rather than quoting a changelog. `input` takes a Principled input by ANY version's spelling - baseColor or 'Base Color', emissive or 'Emission Color' or 'Emission' - because Blender renamed those sockets at 4.0 and a graph should not have to branch on bpy.app.version; `to_node`+`to_socket` targets any node instead, which is how two patterns get combined through a Mix or Math node. THREE TRAPS ARE HANDLED RATHER THAN LEFT TO THE CALLER. A Mapping node is only created when there is something to map and is NEVER left with its Vector unconnected, because an unconnected Mapping Vector is a CONSTANT ZERO and paints the whole surface one flat colour - that is not 'use the default coordinates', which is what an unconnected texture node does, and the two facts sit one node apart. Rotation is DEGREES here and radians on the socket. And a pattern driving a scalar input takes the texture's scalar output (Fac, or Distance on a Voronoi, which has no Fac at all) while one driving a colour takes Color, because Blender converts silently either way and the wrong choice renders plausibly. input:'normal' goes through a BUMP node, not a Normal Map node - the opposite of what bl_set_material_texture does with an image, and deliberately: a procedural pattern is a HEIGHT field, and a Normal Map node would read it as tangent-space RGB and light the surface wrongly while every field still read as correct. Pass relief:'normalMap' for a pattern that genuinely is tangent-space RGB. `color_ramp` inserts a ramp between the pattern and the destination, which is what turns grey mush into a material. EVERY NODE THIS MAKES IS REMOVED AGAIN IF ANY PART OF IT REFUSES, the link is MEASURED off the destination socket afterwards rather than assumed from the call, and a link it replaces is put back if Blender rejects the new one. The response carries a full readback of the texture node so the values can be checked in the same round trip. A bump with no distance gets 1.0 on every build (Blender 5.0 lowered the node default to 0.001, which renders almost no relief); reliefStrength and reliefDistance are read back, and distanceNote says when it filled one in. A uvMap naming a UV layer the material's meshes lack is accepted and answered with uvMapNote: a UV Map node naming a missing layer renders a fixed fallback, not the active layer (measured on 3.6-5.2). scale and offset take a number (X and Y), [u, v] or [x, y, z] - in Object or Generated space pass all three, or the pattern stretches along Z on any face that does not face Z (the reply's scaleNote says so).

RULES - PROCEDURAL MATERIALS, where the recipes disagree (2026-10-06). The axis of a gradient: Separate XYZ on the coordinates (one node and a link) rather than a Mapping node rotated 90 degrees on Y, which left a black plane to fix. Dirt on metal: darken the colour (a Hue/Saturation/Value node and ramp stops) when the dirt changes colour only - one shader, cheaper; mix a darker shader through a Mix Shader with the ramp as factor when it must change roughness or metalness too. A tinted mask: keep the ramp black and white when the mask is reused as a factor, colour its dark stop when it is used only as colour. One scale slider for several textures: multiply each texture's own base scale by the value when their scales differ, feed one value into a shared Mapping node when they scale together. Coordinates: Object for nearly every procedural pattern and UV for images; Generated follows the object's bounds and stretches when the mesh is scaled or deformed, Object follows its transform, and a pattern that must move with a deforming mesh needs UV. BUMP DISTANCE: the Bump node's own default is 1.0 on 4.2 and 4.4 and 0.001 from 5.0 (test_blender_workflow_rules R104), so a recipe states its distance; this call writes 1.0 when none is given on every build and says so in distanceNote. A noise scale is per object and per coordinate (about 1000 on one face, 100 on another at strength 0.08): choose it from one viewport capture, never copy it. Mix RGB and Mix Color are one node on current builds and Specular is Specular IOR Level: a recipe takes the alias, never a build's spelling.
bl_bake_light_probe:
Bake EEVEE's light probe cache - a volume probe's bounce light - for one probe (4.2+) or all; the right operator per build. Replies points, bake time, the cache state where readable and meshes outside the volume.

WHY (2026-10-06): bl_create_light_probe places a probe and bl_set_light_probe writes its settings, and nothing baked it, so a volume probe changed no pixel. Measured on a ceiling only bounce light reaches (64 px, mean luminance): 3.6.23 0.0016 -> 0.333, 4.2.17 0.0016 -> 0.142, 5.2.1 0.0003 -> 0.149. The operator differs by lighting generation: 3.6 bakes one light cache for the whole scene (scene.light_cache_bake; type VOLUME bakes the grids and the cubemaps, SPHERE the cubemaps alone), so object is refused there - pass all; from 4.2 object.lightprobe_cache_bake bakes VOLUME probes only (object = ACTIVE, all = every visible one; the selection is put back) and SPHERE is refused, since sphere probes update live. PLANE is refused on every build. points is the sample count (the grid resolution stays out of every writer by the standing decision). From 4.2 a surface OUTSIDE a volume gets nothing from it - a probe scaled just inside a room baked real data and left the ceiling unchanged - so outsideVolumes names the visible meshes not wholly inside a baked volume (3.6 extends the edge samples). cacheInfoBefore/After is 3.6's gi_cache_info; from 4.2 Blender exposes no baked state, so they are null. warnings: no visible light (the bake sees only the world and emissive surfaces), an engine other than EEVEE. Every refusal fires before the bake.
bl_preview_garment:
Render a garment alone as an asset viewer lights it: EEVEE, an HDRI world, backface culling, base color x ORM AO and ORM blue to metallic; per view. Nothing in the file changes. Replies files, coverage, luminance.

WHY (2026-10-06): judging a texture change on a thumbnail with no sky light shipped a wrong hood lift; the check that worked was EEVEE, an HDRI world, backface culling, the garment alone and the ORM wired as the engine reads it. Cycles is not a substitute - it ignores backface culling, so a garment's inside shows through. The garment is copied AS IT EVALUATES NOW (modifiers, shape keys, pose, a cloth's current state; no simulation is stepped) into a temporary scene with a camera and the world only; everything made is removed afterwards and leftBehind counts what was not. textures {baseColor, normal, orm} are image names in the file or files: Base Color = baseColor x orm.R (AO), orm.G -> Roughness, orm.B -> Metallic, normal through a Normal Map, on the active UV map. A file is loaded Non-Color (normal, orm); an image already in the file keeps its color space - setting it on a generated or painted image reloads it and loses the pixels - and one not Non-Color is warned about. Without textures the object's own materials are rendered, copied with culling on. hdri: city, courtyard, forest, interior, night, studio (default), sunrise, sunset (Blender's bundled worlds) or an image file; hdri_strength. views: FRONT (0, from -Y), RIGHT (90), BACK (180), LEFT (270) or azimuths in degrees, default [FRONT, BACK]; elevation default 10. resolution 64-2048 (512), samples 1-256 (16). Files <prefix>_<view>.png in output_dir; each view replies coverage (the alpha share with film_transparent, default true) and the covered pixels' mean luminance; viewTransform is the scene default the render used.
bl_coplanar_overlaps:
Find faces that z-fight before a mesh goes to Unreal: overlapping triangles in one plane (within 0.15 cm), facing one way, ranked by the overlap's own area; buried, sealed and identical ones are dropped (drop [] keeps them). See mif_help.

WHY. A model built by stacking boxes leaves same-plane, same-facing overlapping faces, and they flicker in the engine (z-fighting): two faces in one plane draw the same depth, so which one wins changes pixel by pixel and frame by frame. From use: 256 of one level's 352 rule-built meshes had some.

HOW. Every triangle of the objects, in world space, is grouped by facing (within 1 degree) and by plane (within plane_tolerance_cm, default 0.15: 1 mm apart still fights at a distance, 2 mm does not). Two triangles of one group whose shapes overlap are clipped one by the other, and the OVERLAP POLYGON'S OWN AREA is reported (areaCm2), not the triangles' - a 1 cm strip along a big triangle reads as the strip. Overlaps under min_area_cm2 (default 0.1) are not counted.

WHAT IS DROPPED, each measured from just above the overlap: buried - two of three rays (along the normal, and tilted) first hit a face from its back, so the overlap is inside a solid; sealed - every one of 24 rays fanned over the hemisphere hits within seal_distance_cm (default 40), a hollow nobody enters; identical - both triangles wear the same material and the same UV there (or, in one object with no UV layer, the same material), so both draw the same pixels. drop names which apply (default all three); drop [] reports every overlap. dropped counts each kind with its area.

THE ANSWER. overlaps: up to limit (default 50, at most 1000) rows, largest first - objects, faces (polygon indices), materials, areaCm2, pointBU and normal; overlapsTotal, visibleAreaCm2, perObject, clean. Rays meet the checked objects and any occluders named (a floor under a wall, say). A list of objects is checked as one scene, which also finds overlaps between them - a door wall with its door leaf. An object with no faces is refused: an empty check is not a clean one.

FIXING ONE. Move one face 2 mm or more off the other, butt the parts instead of running one through the other, or remove the covered face. bl_build_kit_piece follows these rules and checks clean on every kind it builds.
bl_channel_pack_image:
Pack channels of several Blender images or constants into one data texture (ORM, RMA, a mask map) - channels {R, G, B, A} each a number or {image, channel, invert} - or SPLIT one into grayscale maps. Non-Color, resampled to one size, read back per channel. See mif_help.

PACK (default): channels {R, G, B, A} - each a number 0-1 (a constant: occlusion 1, metallic 0) or {image, channel R|G|B|A|LUMINANCE (default the same letter; LUMINANCE for a one-channel image), invert}. R, G and B are required; A only when given (the image then has alpha). The result is a NEW Non-Color image (a packed map is data; an sRGB pack would bend every value) named name (default T_Packed), sized width x height (default the largest source; every other source resampled bilinearly - resampled lists them). Values are read as each image stores them (Image.pixels); outside EXR they are clipped to 0-1 (clippedTo01). filepath writes it through bl_save_image's route and points the image at the file; format PNG | TARGA | OPEN_EXR | any still format (default from the extension); color_depth 8 (default) or 16 for PNG, 16 or 32 for EXR. Without filepath the image lives in memory, kept by its fake user.

SPLIT: image (the packed map) and outputs {R: path, G: path, ...} - one grayscale Non-Color image per channel, named after its file.

Reply: per channel the source and the min / max / mean written, and readBack - each written file loaded again and measured. Unreal's ORM convention is R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic; the Unreal twin of this tool is pack_texture_channels.
bl_remap_datablock:
Replace every use of one Blender datablock with another (materials, meshes, images, node groups, actions...), or mode DEDUPE: merge `.001` copies whose content matches their base, keeping and naming the ones that differ. Users moved per remap. See mif_help.

kind: MATERIAL | MESH | IMAGE | NODE_GROUP | ACTION | WORLD | OBJECT | COLLECTION | CAMERA | LIGHT | ARMATURE | CURVE | TEXTURE | SCENE | ... (bpy.data kinds). mode REMAP (default): source (a name or a list) and target - ID.user_remap moves every user of each source to the target. mode DEDUPE: every `Name.001`-style copy whose CONTENT matches its base `Name` is remapped onto it (materials and node groups: node types, settings, unlinked values and links, compared by type and order so a copy's renamed nodes still match; images: pixels; meshes: vertices, loops and material slots; actions: keys; worlds: color and tree); a copy that differs is listed in kept with the reason and never merged. names limits DEDUPE to those bases. remove: true deletes each replaced datablock once nothing uses it (default false: kept with no users, so purge_orphans or the next save removes it). dry_run reports the plan only. Linked (library) datablocks are refused - localize them first.

Why: an FBX or glTF import, or appending one asset twice, leaves M_Metal, M_Metal.001, M_Metal.002 - each its own material slot and its own Unreal material on the way out. Reply per remap: sourceUsers, targetUsersBefore / After.
bl_batch_rename:
Rename many Blender datablocks of one kind (objects, meshes, materials, images, actions, collections, bones...) by find/replace or regex, prefix, suffix, strip and case; a rename onto a name in use is refused with the pair. See mif_help.

kind: OBJECT | MESH | MATERIAL | IMAGE | ACTION | COLLECTION | NODE_GROUP | CAMERA | LIGHT | ARMATURE | CURVE | TEXTURE | WORLD | SCENE | ... or BONE with armature (the armature object; vertex groups, constraint subtargets and F-curve paths follow, as Blender's own rename does). names limits it to those; match is a regular expression a name must contain. Steps, in order: find -> replace (plain text, or a regular expression with regex: true; \1 groups), remove_prefix / remove_suffix (when present), case (UPPER | LOWER | TITLE | NONE), then prefix / suffix (skip_if_prefixed, default true, leaves a name that already starts with the prefix - so SM_ conventions can be re-applied safely). Unchanged names are skipped; linked datablocks are never renamed.

REFUSED before anything is renamed: a new name already held by a datablock not being renamed, two names becoming one, an empty name, a name longer than Blender's limit (63 bytes below 5.0, 255 from 5.0) - Blender would silently append .001 to one of each pair. A chain (A -> B while B -> C) lands, through unique parking names. dry_run lists the plan; limit bounds the rows listed (the rename covers all).
bl_manage_external_data:
A .blend's external files: REPORT every path (exists, packed, relative), PACK_ALL, UNPACK, MAKE_RELATIVE, MAKE_ABSOLUTE, FIND_MISSING in a folder - counts before and after, missing files named. See mif_help.

action REPORT (default): every image, sound, font, movie clip, cache file, library and volume path with exists, packed, relative and users; before/after counts (files, packed, missing, absolute, relative); kinds and missing_only filter the rows, limit bounds them. PACK_ALL packs every present file into the .blend, one by one, and lists the missing ones in notPacked (Blender's own Pack Resources stops at the first missing file and packs nothing after it - measured on 5.0.1). UNPACK with method USE_LOCAL | WRITE_LOCAL (default; //textures/ beside the .blend) | USE_ORIGINAL | WRITE_ORIGINAL. MAKE_RELATIVE and MAKE_ABSOLUTE rewrite paths; FIND_MISSING searches directory (and below) by file name and repoints what it finds. MAKE_RELATIVE and the local UNPACK methods need a saved .blend (a relative path is relative to it). changed lists each file whose path or packed state moved; a warning names files still missing. Why: a .blend handed to another machine or a render farm opens with pink textures, and nothing said so before.
bl_object_relations:
Blender's Object > Relations: MAKE_SINGLE_USER (data, materials, actions), MAKE_INSTANCES_REAL (collection, particle or node instances to objects), LINK_DATA (a source's data, materials, modifiers or collections onto targets). See mif_help.

action MAKE_SINGLE_USER: objects, what [DATA (default), MATERIALS, ACTIONS] - each shared datablock copied for that object (users before and after). MAKE_INSTANCES_REAL: objects that instance a collection, particles or Geometry Nodes instances become real objects (Blender's Make Instances Real; keep_hierarchy default true, parent default false); the new objects are listed, an object that instances nothing is refused. LINK_DATA: source and targets, what [DATA (default; same object type), MATERIALS, MODIFIERS (copied with their settings), COLLECTIONS]. Make Local is bl_library_override LOCALIZE. Why: a linked duplicate edited by mistake changes every copy; a collection instance must be real before an export that should contain its meshes.
bl_objects_overlap:
Do two Blender objects actually intersect - asked of the GEOMETRY rather than of their bounding boxes, which is what this was being approximated with. An AABB test says two objects overlap when they do not: measured on 3.6, 4.4 and 5.0, a 2m cube rotated 45 degrees about Z and a 1m cube at (1.45,1.45,0) have world AABBs that DO intersect and geometry that never touches. Both answers are returned, so aabbWouldHaveLied shows you the disagreement. FIVE VERDICTS, because 'do they overlap' is several questions: DISJOINT, TOUCHING (surfaces meet, no shared volume), INTERSECTING, A_INSIDE_B and B_INSIDE_A. CONTAINMENT IS THE CASE A SURFACE TEST CANNOT SEE - overlap() reports face-to-face intersection only, so a cube entirely inside another returns ZERO pairs and len(overlap()) alone calls it DISJOINT, the exact opposite of the truth. Trees are built in WORLD space from a transformed bmesh, never BVHTree.FromObject, which silently ignores matrix_world - two cubes FIVE UNITS APART report 2 overlap pairs through it - and which segfaults Blender 3.6 outright on a non-mesh object. facePairs is a yes/no signal and NOT a contact count: two identical coincident cubes return 2 pairs, not 36. An object that draws instances - Geometry Nodes instances, particles, instancing - answers with instancesNote: instances are not part of any evaluated mesh, so this does not see them (measured on 3.6-5.2).

Parameters: b (str, required) is the second object; a and b must both be MESH objects and must differ. tolerance (float, default None, which the op reads as 1e-5, world units) is how far behind the other object's nearest face a sample point must be to count as inside; it cannot be negative. max_samples (int, default None, read as 2000) caps the containment sample points per object; the samples are the world-space vertices and face centroids, and above the cap they are taken by an even stride across the whole list (reported as strideA / strideB), never the first N. It must be at least 1. The op also accepts objects [a, b] as one key, which the MCP tool does not send. evaluated defaults to true.

OUT: ok, a, b, overlapping (verdict is not DISJOINT), verdict (DISJOINT | TOUCHING | INTERSECTING | A_INSIDE_B | B_INSIDE_A), space "WORLD", geometry ("evaluated" or "base"), facePairs, facePairsNote, samplesInsideOther {aInB, bInA}, samplesTested {a, b, strideA, strideB}, aabbSaysOverlap, instancesNote (null when none or evaluated false), aabbWouldHaveLied, note (when the AABBs intersect: whether the geometry agrees; else null).

Refusals (a read; nothing is changed): the same name for both; objects not a two-name list; no object by a name (lists up to 25 present); either object not a MESH; either object's BASE mesh has no faces (checked on the base mesh even when evaluated is true); a negative tolerance; max_samples under 1; any unknown key.
bl_list_library_assets:
Browse a Blender asset library (a library name, a folder or one .blend) without opening its files: assets with kind, catalog, tags, description, author, preview; filtered and paged; the catalog tree. Bring one in with bl_append_from_file. See mif_help.

Give one of library (a name in Preferences > File Paths > Asset Libraries), folder (searched with its subfolders) or file (one .blend). Each .blend's assets are linked into this session long enough to read their metadata and the links are removed again - the open file is not changed (measured: the counts of libraries and materials are the same before and after); the open file itself is skipped. Rows: name, kind (OBJECT | MATERIAL | COLLECTION | NODE_GROUP | ACTION | WORLD | BRUSH | SCENE), file, relativeFile, catalogId, catalog (its path from blender_assets.cats.txt at the root), tags, description, author, hasPreview. Filters: kinds, catalog (that catalog and below), tag (case-insensitive), name (contains). limit (default 200) and offset page; total and truncated say how many matched. catalogs: true (default) adds the catalog tree. Unreadable files are listed with why. Bring an asset in with bl_append_from_file (link or append).
bl_set_collection_exporter:
Blender 4.2+ collection exporters kept in the .blend: LIST, ADD (FBX, GLTF, USD, OBJ, ALEMBIC, PLY, STL with a path and settings), EDIT, REMOVE, EXPORT one collection's or all - file, size and a newer mtime per exporter. See mif_help.

Blender 4.2 and later (refused by name on 3.6, pointing at bl_export_scene). action LIST (default; a collection, or every collection's exporters): index, handler, filepath, absolutePath, fileExists, bytes, mtime. ADD: collection, format FBX | GLTF | USD | OBJ | ALEMBIC | PLY | STL, filepath ('//' relative to the .blend), settings - the exporter's own properties by identifier (global_scale, use_selection, apply_modifiers ...; an unknown key is refused with the list it takes). EDIT: index (default 0), filepath, settings. REMOVE: index. EXPORT: the collection's exporters (index for one) or all: true for every collection's; each row says exported true only when the file exists and is newer than before the call, else why. The settings stay in the .blend, so the next session or a teammate exports the same collections the same way.
bl_set_collection_visibility:
The four meanings of 'hide this Blender collection', taken by their real names because writing the wrong one is a silent no-op that reads back as success on the property that WAS written. hide_viewport/hide_render are global; exclude, hide_in_view_layer (the eye), indirect_only and holdout are per view layer and are refused outright if the collection is not in that view layer, since there is no LayerCollection to write to. EXCLUDE IS NOT HIDING: it removes the collection from the depsgraph entirely, so constraints, drivers and modifiers depending on those objects change behaviour too. Every requested write is verified individually afterwards. indirect_only is a CYCLES feature - under EEVEE it changes nothing (measured 0.0/255 on every supported build), so the response reports inertUnderThisEngine when it is written outside Cycles.

view_layer (str, default None: the active view layer) is the view layer that exclude, hide_in_view_layer, indirect_only and holdout are written to; a name the scene does not have is refused listing the ones present. It does not affect hide_viewport or hide_render, which are on the collection itself. At least one of the six flags must be passed. The collection is found by name (collection, alias name).

OUT: ok, collection, viewLayer, perViewLayerWrites and globalWrites (the keys written), objectCount, excludedFromEvaluation, note (set when the collection is excluded), engine, inertUnderThisEngine (['indirectOnly'] when it was set true outside Cycles, else null), engineNote, then all six read back: hideViewport, hideRender, exclude, hideInViewLayer, indirectOnly, holdout (the per-layer four null when the collection is not in that view layer).

Refused before anything is written: an unknown key; no such collection; no such view layer; a hide_viewport or hide_render that is not a boolean; no flag passed; a per-layer flag for a collection not linked into that view layer. After writing, every requested flag is read back and a mismatch is refused naming wanted and read values - that refusal comes after the writes and does not say nothing changed.
bl_set_color_management:
View transform, look, exposure and gamma - the settings that silently change every pixel of every render and saved image, and the usual answer to 'why does this look washed out'. EVERY ENUM IS VALIDATED AGAINST THE OCIO CONFIG ACTUALLY LOADED, read from the instance rather than bpy.types, because unlike light or camera type these sets are populated at runtime: a studio config renames all of them, and the stock default moved from Filmic to AgX in 4.0. A hard-coded list would refuse the only values that work. The LOOK IS NAMESPACED BY THE VIEW TRANSFORM ("AgX - Punchy"), so the transform is applied first and the look is validated against what the NEW transform offers - and because Blender silently resets look when the transform changes, every requested write is read back from the scene rather than echoed.

PARAMETERS. view_transform (string, default unchanged): a view transform the loaded OCIO config offers; display_device is written first, then view_transform, then look. display_device (string, default unchanged): the display, from the config. sequencer_colorspace (string, default unchanged): the sequencer's colour space, checked against the build's list of colour space names. use_curve_mapping (bool, default unchanged): the view's curve mapping toggle. working_space (string, default unchanged; Blender 5.0+): the scene-linear working space, set through wm.set_working_color_space, whose own enum decides what is accepted; written last and only when it differs from the current one. convert_colors (bool, default true when working_space is passed): convert the file's colours into the new working space, or leave the numbers as they are; only with working_space. At least one setting must be passed.

OUT: ok, scene, before {viewTransform, look, exposure, gamma, displayDevice}, availableViewTransforms, availableLooks, availableDisplayDevices (each null when the build's RNA list is a placeholder that does not hold the current value), availableListsNote, note, and the settings read back: viewTransform, look, exposure, gamma, displayDevice, sequencerColorspace, useCurveMapping, workingSpace.

REFUSED with "NOTHING was changed": no setting passed; convert_colors without working_space; working_space before 5.0; a sequencer_colorspace not in the list; a display device, view transform or look the config does not offer (the settings already written are put back first); a working_space the operator refuses (put back). A requested name that reads back different afterwards, such as a look the new transform resets, puts back what this call wrote and is refused.
bl_set_color_ramp:
Set the STOPS of a Blender ColorRamp node - the one thing the generic node writer cannot do. bl_add_group_node writes node properties by their RNA name and REFUSES pointers, correctly, because a datablock named as a string is stored and ignored; a colour ramp is a pointer to a ColorRamp holding a COLLECTION of elements, so it falls outside that writer twice over. The result was that a ramp could be added to a material and never given a stop - two black-to-white defaults and no way to change them, which makes the node an expensive no-op. A ramp is how a procedural pattern becomes a material: noise on its own is grey mush, noise through three stops is concrete, rust or moss. Address the tree with `material` (a material name) or `tree` (any tree address - a node group, 'material:<name>', 'scene:world', 'scene:compositor'); they are separate parameters rather than two spellings of one because a material NAME and a tree ADDRESS are different things. stops is [{position: 0..1, color: [r,g,b] or [r,g,b,a]}]. A POSITION OUTSIDE 0..1 IS REFUSED RATHER THAN CLAMPED, because Blender clamps silently and the ramp then reads back agreeing with itself and disagreeing with the request. Every stop is validated before the first is written, since the write clears the ramp down to one element before rebuilding it. Blender keeps elements SORTED BY POSITION, so stops sent out of order come back reordered and the response says when that happened - the ramp is correct and the indices are Blender's.

Parameters (each default None: left as the ramp has it; every value is matched case-insensitively against this ramp's own RNA enum, read from the build): interpolation (str) is how color blends between stops - EASE, CARDINAL, LINEAR, B_SPLINE or CONSTANT per the op's own list; color_mode (str) is the color space the blend runs in - RGB, HSV or HSL; hue_interpolation (str) is the way round the hue circle an HSV or HSL blend goes - NEAR, FAR, CW or CCW. hue_interpolation is written whatever color_mode is, and only an HSV or HSL blend reads it. At least one of stops, interpolation, color_mode or hue_interpolation must be given. tree is also accepted as group. A stop takes position (or pos) and color (or colour); a three-number color gets alpha 1.0; at most 32 stops. All three enums are resolved and every stop validated before the first write, and the stops are written last.

OUT: ok, tree, node, nodeType, colorRamp and before (each {interpolation, colorMode, hueInterpolation, stops [{position, color}], stopCount}, read off the ramp), stopCountBefore, stopsReordered, plus orderNote when Blender re-sorted the stops, mutedNote when the node is muted and unlinkedNote when none of its outputs is connected.

Refused with nothing changed: an unknown key; both material and tree, or neither; a material that does not exist; a tree address that does not resolve; a node the tree lacks (the refusal lists its nodes) or one with no color ramp (the refusal lists the ramp nodes); nothing to set; an enum value this build lacks (the refusal lists the valid ones); stops that is empty or not a list, over 32 stops, a stop that is not an object, has an unknown key, no position, a position outside 0..1, no color, or a color that is not 3 or 4 finite numbers.
bl_set_compositing:
Turn the Blender scene compositor on, and the SECOND switch that also has to be on. TWO INDEPENDENT FLAGS decide whether compositing happens: scene.use_nodes (a tree exists and is edited) and scene.render.use_compositing (the render PIPELINE runs it). With the first on and the second off, the whole tree reads perfectly, the compositor backdrop updates, and the rendered file is completely unprocessed - nothing reports it. Both are set and both read back. Wires a default Render Layers -> Composite pair when the tree is empty, because an empty compositor writes nothing at all. Afterwards, address the tree from bl_add_group_node / bl_link_group_nodes / bl_list_group_nodes by passing tree:'scene:compositor'. The same resolver reaches 'scene:world', 'material:<name>' and 'world:<name>'. enabled:false turns the pipeline switch off on every build. From Blender 5.0, scene.use_nodes stays on whatever is written (measured on 5.0.1 and 5.2.1), so there the reply carries useNodesFixed:true and a useNodesNote instead of a refusal - render.use_compositing is the switch the render reads.

Parameters: use_sequencer (bool, default None = left as it is) writes scene.render.use_sequencer - the Sequencer runs after the compositor and its strips override the composited image, so turn it off when a strip exists and the composite should reach the file. with_default_nodes (bool, default None, read as true) wires Render Layers -> Composite (Render Layers -> Group Output, with an Image output declared on its interface, on 5.0 and later) when enabling and the tree has no nodes; false leaves an empty tree empty. On 5.0+ enabling with no compositor node group creates one named "Compositing" and assigns it. use_compositing defaults to follow enabled, and enabled defaults to true. Everything applies to the current scene.

OUT: ok, scene, before {useNodes, useCompositing, useSequencer}, nodesAdded [names], treeName, compositorApi (which scene property holds the tree on this build), addressAs ("scene:compositor"), note, useNodesFixed (true or null), useNodesNote (or null), and the after state as top-level useNodes, useCompositing, useSequencer.

Refusals: a malformed use_compositing, use_sequencer or with_default_nodes ("NOTHING was changed."), or a malformed enabled - all before any write; any unknown key. Two can fire AFTER writes: a default Render Layers link that Blender marks invalid (the two nodes WERE added; the message says to wire them with bl_link_group_nodes), and scene.use_nodes reading back different from enabled (render.use_compositing WAS written, and the message says what it holds). On 5.0+ disabling is not refused when only use_nodes stayed on: that is reported as useNodesFixed.
bl_set_constraint:
Write the TYPE-SPECIFIC settings of an existing Blender constraint - the half nothing could reach. bl_add_constraint sets target, subtarget and influence, which every constraint shares; everything that makes a constraint do its particular job was unreachable. Measured on 4.4: 28 constraint types carry 253 type-specific writable properties between them and NOT ONE type has zero, so no constraint could ever be fully configured. What that cost concretely: a LIMIT_ROTATION or LIMIT_LOCATION is INERT until its limits are set, so the addon could add a limit constraint that limits nothing - present in the stack, reported by bl_list_constraints, doing precisely nothing; a TRACK_TO tracked along Blender's default axis, wrong for most cameras and turrets; an IK took the default chain length. GENERIC, NOT CURATED, deliberately the opposite choice from bl_add_modifier: properties are read off bl_rna at call time, so this accepts exactly what the running Blender accepts and refuses the rest BY NAME with the settable list in the refusal - there is no list here to go stale. Enums are validated against their own items, object pointers resolve by name (pass null to clear one, which is how a pole target is removed), and every key is checked BEFORE the first write so a bad key cannot leave a half-configured constraint. target/subtarget/influence are refused here on purpose: two ways to set one value is a parallel system. Values are read BACK off the constraint rather than echoed from the request.

bone (str, default None) names the pose bone whose stack holds the constraint; the object must then be an ARMATURE with pose data. Omitted, the object's own stack is used. settings keys are the constraint's bl_rna identifiers. ENUM values are upper-cased and checked against the property's items; POINTER values are object names resolved with the usual object lookup (null clears); BOOLEAN takes true/false or 0/1 only; INT and FLOAT must be finite, and an array property takes a list; STRING must be text. Any other property type (a collection such as an Armature constraint's targets) is refused. Besides target, subtarget and influence, name, mute, enabled, show_expanded, active, is_valid, error_location, error_rotation and is_override_data are also refused as shared settings.

OUT: object, holder ('object' or "bone '<name>'"), constraint, type, applied {key: value read back off the constraint; pointers as names, vectors as lists}, appliedCount, isValid, settableHere (every writable type-specific identifier), note.

Refused before anything is written: an unknown key; no such object; bone given on a non-armature, an armature with no pose, or a bone it lacks; no constraint by that name (lists those present); settings missing, empty or not an object; any key not writable or shared; a bad enum, boolean, number or string; a pointer to an object that does not exist. Every key is checked before the first write.
bl_set_keying_set:
A Blender scene keying set: LIST, CREATE, ADD_PATHS / REMOVE_PATHS ({object, dataPath, index, group}), KEY every path at a frame, DELETE. See mif_help.

action LIST (default): the scene's keying sets with their paths and which is active. CREATE: name, paths (optional), active (default true). ADD_PATHS / REMOVE_PATHS: paths [{object, dataPath, index (omitted or -1: the whole array), group}] - dataPath on the object, e.g. 'location' or 'pose.bones["hand.L"].rotation_quaternion'; a path that does not resolve is refused. KEY: inserts a key on every path at frame (default the current frame) and lists the channels keyed. DELETE: removes it.
bl_set_custom_normals:
Write a Blender mesh's custom split normals from a PROXY mesh, a SPHERE center, one DIRECTION, FROM_FACES, SMOOTH, or CLEAR them - masked by a vertex group, mixed; the angle each corner moved read back. Foliage and proxy normals for Unreal. See mif_help.

source PROXY: proxy names a mesh; each vertex takes the proxy's smooth (vertex-interpolated) normal at the nearest surface point - a hemisphere over a canopy, a smooth proxy round a hard-surface part. SPHERE: away from center (world; default the object's bounding-box center). DIRECTION: one world vector. FROM_FACES: each corner its face's normal. SMOOTH: each corner its vertex's averaged normal. CLEAR: remove custom normals. vertex_group masks by weight (0.5 moves half way); mix 0-1 (default 1). On 3.6 custom normals show only with Auto Smooth on, so it is turned on and autoSmoothSet says so (4.1+ have no such switch). Reply: corners, cornersChanged, angleMovedDeg {min, mean, max}, readBackErrorDeg (normals on one smooth fan are shared, so a written normal can differ there - a warning says how much). FBX carries custom normals; Unreal reads them with Normal Import Method Import Normals.
bl_transfer_mesh_data:
Copy UVs, colors, custom normals, edge and face flags, face sets or named attributes from one Blender mesh onto others - the destination layers made first, so nothing transfers silently into a missing layer. Per target what changed. See mif_help.

data: UV (every source UV layer, matched by name) | COLOR (corner and point color attributes) | CUSTOM_NORMAL | SEAM | SHARP_EDGE | CREASE | BEVEL_WEIGHT_EDGE | SMOOTH | FACE_SETS | ATTRIBUTE (with attributes: names); default [UV]. mapping NEAREST_FACE (default; interpolated on the nearest face) | POLYINTERP (projected along the normal) | NEAREST | TOPOLOGY (same counts, by index - refused otherwise). vertex_group limits where data lands on each target; mix 0-1. Route: a Data Transfer modifier per target with object.datalayout_transfer run FIRST - the modifier alone writes nothing into a layer the target lacks and still answers ok, the silent no-op of the hand route - then applied as the first modifier. FACE_SETS and ATTRIBUTE are copied natively by the nearest element in world space (a target attribute of another domain or type is refused). Reply per target: layersCreated, changed (per UV / color layer, the corners whose value moved), flags before/after, attributes, maxDistanceToSource (how far the mapping reached). Weights have their own tool, bl_transfer_weights.
bl_transfer_shape_keys:
Carry shape keys from a Blender mesh onto one of DIFFERENT topology through Surface Deform, key by key - names, sliders and relative keys kept, each key's displacement measured on both. See mif_help.

The target is bound to the source with a Surface Deform modifier while the source shows its Basis; then each key in turn (keys, default all but the Basis) is set to 1 and applied to the target as a new shape key (modifier_apply_as_shapekey, keep_modifier) named after it, with its slider range; a relative key that was transferred too is re-pointed. The modifier is removed and the source's key values and pin are put back. falloff 2-16 (default 4), strength (default 1). A target key of the same name is refused unless replace: true. Per key: sourceMaxDisplacement, targetMaxDisplacement, and a warning when the target moves under 1% of the source (the moved region is far from the target surface). Why: bl_add_shape_key fromObject (Join as Shapes) needs the same vertex count; a facial set or fitting morph made on a template must reach a custom head or a garment.
bl_set_mesh_attribute:
CREATE, WRITE, RENAME, CONVERT or READ a generic Blender mesh attribute (FLOAT, INT, vectors, colors, FLOAT2, QUATERNION 4.2+) on POINT, EDGE, FACE or CORNER - by value, per element, by index or from a vertex group. See mif_help.

action CREATE: name, domain POINT | EDGE | FACE | CORNER (default POINT), data_type FLOAT (default) | INT | BOOLEAN | INT8 | FLOAT_VECTOR | FLOAT2 | FLOAT_COLOR | BYTE_COLOR | INT32_2D | QUATERNION (4.2+; refused by name below, with the build's list) and optionally the values. WRITE: value (one for every element), values (one per element, or per index with indices), or from_vertex_group (a FLOAT POINT attribute takes the group's weights, 0 where unweighted). RENAME: new_name (Blender's own and dot-prefixed names refused). CONVERT: a new domain and/or data_type (geometry.attribute_convert). READ: the attribute's domain, type, element count, a sample (sample, default 8) and min/max for scalars. A values list of the wrong length, an index out of range, or a value of the wrong shape is refused before anything is written. FLOAT2 attributes on corners are what export as extra UV channels; geometry nodes read any of them by name. mesh_stats attributeValues reads them too.
bl_add_hook:
Hook a Blender mesh's, curve's or lattice's points to an object, a bone or a new empty at their centroid, with the inverse matrix reset so nothing moves when it is added - read back. See mif_help.

object: a mesh, curve or lattice in object mode. Points: vertices (indices; a curve's points counted spline by spline, a Bezier point bringing its two handles) or vertex_group (a mesh's group, weight above 0). Hook target: hook_object, or armature + bone, or neither - an Empty is made at the points' centroid (empty_name, empty_size) in the object's collections. The HOOK modifier gets the points (vertex_indices_set), strength, falloff (NONE | CURVE | SMOOTH | SPHERE | ROOT | INVERSE_SQUARE | SHARP | LINEAR | CONSTANT) and falloff_radius, then its inverse matrix is RESET from the hook's transform at bind time (Blender's hook_reset: inverse(object^-1 * hook)) and its center set to the centroid, and it is placed after any leading hooks, before every other modifier. Reply: positionsMovedMax - the hooked points' evaluated world positions before and after the hook was added (0 when the reset worked); a warning when they moved. Why: bl_add_modifier HOOK never set the inverse, so the first hook to an object away from the origin threw the vertices across the scene. Measured: HookModifier.vertex_indices_set exists on 3.6 as on 4.2-5.2.
bl_spin_mesh:
Spin chosen edges, faces or vertices of an existing Blender mesh about an axis - a lip, a flange, a radial copy (dupli) - in place; new faces and the welded seam reported. See mif_help.

One of edges, faces or vertices (indices of the existing mesh). axis (default [0, 0, 1]) and center (default origin) in space WORLD (default) or LOCAL; angle in degrees (default 360), steps (default 12, 1-1024). dupli: copies at each step instead of a swept surface. merge_seam (default true) welds the last ring to the first at 360 degrees; flip_normals flips the new faces. bmesh.ops.spin, written back to the mesh. Reply: newVertices / newEdges / newFaces, boundaryEdgesOnNewFaces (a swept edge's two rims are boundaries), seamWelded at 360 degrees, axisLocal and centerLocal. bl_build_lathe revolves a profile into a NEW object and the SCREW modifier spins a whole object; this spins part of one in place.
bl_set_action:
Protect a Blender action from being destroyed by the next save, or rename it. THE ADDON ALREADY TOLD YOU THIS WAS COMING AND COULD NOT HELP: bl_list_actions reports survivesSave for every action, and bl_assign_action reports previousSurvivesSave for the action it just displaced - which is exactly the moment one drops to zero users. An action with no users and no fake user is DELETED the next time the file is saved, silently, BY THE SAVE SUCCEEDING; it is the same purge bl_save_file reports as purgedOrphans, seen from the side that can prevent it. use_fake_user was writable only by bl_create_action, at birth, so an action that arrived with an imported mesh or was displaced by an assignment could not be protected at all. A fake user is a deliberate reference meaning "keep this even though nothing points at it". Renaming reports the name you actually got, because Blender suffixes a clash rather than refusing and anything looking the action up by the name it asked for would then miss.

frame_range [start, end] sets the action's MANUAL frame range (use_frame_range turns it on or off; cyclic marks it a loop of that range). The FBX all-actions export, bl_export_actions and glTF take each clip's length from it, so a walk cycle with a stray key at frame 300 exports 300 frames long unless its range is set. bl_list_actions reads useFrameRange, manualFrameRange and cyclic back.
bl_export_actions:
Export each action of a Blender armature to its OWN FBX (deform bones, the action's frame range, named A_{rig}_{action}) - the clips half of a character hand-off; an action keying bones the rig lacks is refused. Per file frames, fps, bones. See mif_help.

armature: the armature object. actions (default every action whose curves key one of its bones) - an action keying a bone the armature lacks is refused, naming the bones (retarget or rename first); an action keying no bone is refused. folder: where the files go; pattern names each file ({rig}, {action}; default A_{rig}_{action}; two actions on one name are refused). Each file: Blender's FBX exporter with bl_export_mesh's axes and scale (Z up, -Y forward, centimeters - the skinned send's frame, so the clip lands on the skeleton that send made), the armature alone (include_mesh adds its skinned meshes), deform bones only (deform_only, default true), leaf bones off, one take: the action assigned and the scene's range set to the action's frame range - its MANUAL range when set (bl_set_action frame_range), else its keys' - with every frame kept (simplify, default 0). The armature's action, slot, NLA switch and the scene's range and frame are put back. Reply per file: frames, fps, seconds, bonesKeyed, manualFrameRange, bytes, overwrote. mif_send_to_unreal animations {armature, skeleton} sends them onto an Unreal Skeleton.
bl_export_material_textures:
Save every image a Blender material's Principled inputs read, with engine names (T_{material}_BC / _N / _ORM / _E), color spaces, the normal map's green flipped for DIRECTX and roughness + metallic packed as ORM; constants and node chains not carried are listed. See mif_help.

objects (the materials on them) or materials. For each material's Principled BSDF, every input read straight from an image is written to folder as a PNG (format TARGA for .tga) named by pattern (default T_{material}_{suffix}): BC (Base Color, with the Alpha input's image as alpha when it reads one; sRGB), N (a tangent-space Normal Map node's image; green flipped for normal_convention DIRECTX, Unreal's, the default - OPENGL keeps it), ORM (pack_orm, default true: R occlusion 1, G roughness, B metallic - each from its image's channel, through a Separate Color node too, or the input's constant), or R and M separately with pack_orm false, and E (Emission Color). Linear maps are written Non-Color. Inputs set to a value are returned in constants (baseColor, roughness, metallic, opacity) for the Unreal material; anything else - a ramp, a math node, a procedural texture, a Normal Map strength other than 1, a bump - is listed in notCarried with why (bl_bake_texture / bl_bake_texture_set bake those). mif_send_to_unreal textures {objects} imports them and makes a material per Blender material.
bl_export_camera:
Export an animated Blender camera to FBX in Unreal's axes with its lens animation; focal length, focus distance and f-stop sampled into the reply (FBX has no f-stop channel). The Unreal half reads the file onto a camera binding. See mif_help.

camera: a camera object; file: the .fbx. frame_range [start, end] (default the scene's). Blender's FBX exporter with bl_export_mesh's axes (Z up, -Y forward, centimeters), the camera alone, every frame keyed: its transform, focal length and focus distance animate in the file; the key times are frame / fps (Blender's own FBX import needs anim_offset 0 to land them on the same frames - measured). FBX has no f-stop channel, so lensFrames samples (samples, default 5) each frame's focalLength, sensorWidth, focusDistance, fStop, location and forward for the Unreal side to key. The file's focus distance imports into Unreal 1000 times too far and its scale as 100: mif_send_to_unreal's camera form puts both right. Reply: frames, fps, transformAnimated, lensAnimated, lensFrames, bytes. The Unreal half (import_sequence_fbx onto a camera binding) belongs to the Sequencer tools.
bl_export_groom:
Export Blender hair - Curves objects (4.2+) or a mesh's hair particles - as an Alembic Unreal's groom importer reads, each object one group, in centimeters; what the exporter drops is listed. See mif_help.

objects: Curves objects (Blender 4.2+ hair; each object becomes one groom group) or meshes with hair particle systems; file: the .abc. frame_range (default the current frame: a static groom); scale (default 100: centimeters, as every send here). Written with Blender's Alembic exporter (Y up). MEASURED on 4.2.17, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.1: the exporter keeps a Curves object's positions and its radius as width, and drops every other curve attribute (groom_group_id, groom_root_uv, groom_guide, groom_width all lost) - so groups are carried as separate objects, guides are not carried (Unreal generates them), root UVs come from the importer; carried and notCarried say so. A scripted Unreal import needs the conversion named, rotation X 90 and scale Y -1, or the hair lies on its side (mif_send_to_unreal names it). Written through a temporary POLY curve, the scene untouched: Curves as they evaluate, particle hair as polylines from the particle system, children included, on every build. groups carries each group's curves, points and box in cm. Refused with nothing written, as each crashes the editor in Unreal's groom builder: a group flat along an axis, a curve of one point, a zero-length segment. A frame range of more than one frame writes Curves objects as they stand, and is refused for particle hair. A mesh with no hair is refused.
bl_export_scene:
Write glTF/GLB, OBJ, USD/USDA/USDC/USDZ, Alembic, STL or PLY - everything except the FBX bl_export_mesh owns. Measured: bl_import_mesh took .fbx/.gltf/.glb and bl_export_mesh wrote .fbx and NOTHING else, so glTF could come IN and not go OUT and USD was absent in both directions. The format comes from the EXTENSION. Blender moved its OBJ, STL and PLY exporters to wm.*_export at DIFFERENT versions (OBJ and PLY by 3.6, STL at 4.2) and EACH EXPORTER SPELLS ITS 'only the selection' OPTION DIFFERENTLY - four different keyword names across the six operators - so each format carries a list of candidate operators and its own keyword rather than a guess. Carrying one operator's spelling to another either raises or is silently ignored. A missing exporter (they are add-ons and can be disabled) is reported as a sentence naming the format, not an AttributeError. A frame range on a format that carries no time is REFUSED rather than ignored, because 'I exported an animation' and 'I exported frame 1' look identical afterwards. And ok:true is not a file: the mtime is taken before the call, so a leftover from an earlier run cannot pass as this export. Nor is it everything that was there: each format leaves some object types out - glTF writes lights and cameras only when asked, and OBJ, STL and PLY hold mesh geometry only - so the answer's notCarried names every object in scope the file does not carry, with the parameter that would include it where there is one. Lights and cameras stay out of a glTF by default, as in Blender's own exporter, because in a hand-off file they clutter an Unreal import; include_lights puts point, spot and sun lights in and include_cameras cameras. Both are glTF options, refused on every other format, which decides for itself (USD writes both, Alembic writes cameras). An existing file is REPLACED by default and the answer says so: overwrote, and when true replacedBytes and replacedModified (UTC), measured off the old file before the write; overwrite=False refuses the path by name. Grease Pencil strokes go out as .svg or .pdf (svgStrokes counts an SVG's strokes in the file), refused on Blender 4.3-4.5; a 5.x PDF the exporter does not write is refused after the call.

BVH (1.3): a .bvh writes one armature (object) over frame_start..frame_end (default the scene's); bvh {rotateMode, scale, rootTransformOnly}. The written file's joints and frames are read back (fileInfo); a joint count other than the armature's bones is a warning.
bl_render_still:
Render the current frame to a file. BLOCKS Blender's main thread for the whole render, so start small - a heavy frame exceeds the addon's job timeout and reads as a hung bridge. render() returns FINISHED whether or not a file appeared, so the file is stat'd afterwards and wroteFile/fileBytes are measurements rather than the operator's opinion. PASS return_image=True TO SEE THE RENDER: it comes back as an image block, scaled to preview_max_px on its longest edge (default 1024, at most 1568) and to preview_max_bytes of PNG (default 512 KB), smaller rather than refused; imageBlocks describes it and filePath stays the full file. With _image 'data' it comes back the old way, as `image`, a base64 PNG in the text at preview_max_px (default 128), omitted if its PNG exceeds preview_max_bytes (default 30000); imageOmittedReason then directs the caller to reduce preview_max_px or inspect file_path. renderedWidth/renderedHeight always describe the full artifact. A frame that would step a live simulation is refused unless allow_simulation. COMPUTE BACKEND (2026-10-05): compute_backend NONE (the CPU), OPTIX, CUDA, HIP, METAL or ONEAPI chooses Cycles' device for this in-process still - the choice that bl_render_animation's gpu option makes in its own process. It writes compute_device_type, a USER PREFERENCE and not a scene setting: it stays for every later Cycles render in this Blender session (and is kept if the preferences are saved), and the reply's computeBackend says so with preferenceWas / preferenceNow, the devices ticked and the scene's device. A backend that lists no device here is REFUSED with the backends that do, the preference put back and nothing rendered - measured headless on 5.2.2 with no GPU: compute_device_type takes CUDA though CUDA lists nothing, and Cycles then renders on the CPU in silence. Refused too on a scene that does not render with Cycles. Measured: NONE on the CPU on 4.2.23, 4.4.0, 5.0.1 and 5.2.2; a GPU backend's success path was not run (no GPU on that host).

region [x0, y0, x1, y1] (0-1 of the frame, origin bottom left - Blender's render border) or region_px [x0, y0, x1, y1] (output pixels, origin top left) renders that box alone; crop (default true) writes only the box, false the full frame with the rest empty. The scene's own border is put back after; region in the reply names the box in pixels.
bl_render_animation:
Render a frame RANGE out of process and return immediately with a jobId to poll - the only shape that works, because every addon op runs on Blender's main thread under a 150s job timeout, so an in-process animation render freezes the bridge and the MCP gives up while the render carries on. It renders the SAVED .blend, not this session, so it refuses on an unsaved or dirty file rather than silently rendering the wrong scene; there is deliberately no output override, because -o would desynchronise the frame paths from the ones progress is measured against. Every expected frame path is stat'd BEFORE the render so a leftover file from an earlier run cannot be counted as progress. Poll with bl_render_status. gpu=true switches Cycles to the GPU with the OptiX denoiser for this job only, by injecting a script that runs after the file loads and before the first frame. Its warnings name every simulation that will not animate in that render (bl_render_info outOfProcessSimulations): bake_physics, then save, then render. gpu:true tries OPTIX, CUDA, HIP, METAL, ONEAPI in turn and keeps the first that lists a device; gpu_backend (with gpu:true) uses only that one - pass CUDA where OptiX lists the card but its kernel fails to load and no frame renders. On the GPU the job also turns on persistent data and, off OptiX, the denoiser on the GPU where the build has it - measured 18.5 s to 4.1 s for 12 frames on an RTX 4080 SUPER with CUDA, frames unchanged; the job log names what was applied. One heavy job at a time machine-wide (MIF_MAX_CHILD_JOBS, default 1): refused while another holds the slot; memory_limit_gb ends the render's process tree past that (default half of RAM, 0 none).

region / region_px / crop (1.3) set the render border in the child process only (a --python script before the frames): the session's scene is not touched. The reply's region names the box in pixels.
bl_create_scene:
Create a new, EMPTY Blender scene and return the name it actually got. Every op that takes a scene - bl_render_animation among them - takes it BY NAME, and until this existed nothing in the addon could make one, so a second render configuration (different resolution, frame range or output path) meant editing the only scene there was. The new scene does NOT copy the current one unless copy_from / type ask (NEW, EMPTY, LINK_COPY, FULL_COPY), and is NOT activated - the scene you were in stays current, so building one does not move you out of your work; switch with bl_set_current_scene when you want it. Blender appends .001 on a name collision rather than failing, so use the returned `name`, not the string you sent - `renamed` tells you when they differ.

copy_from (a scene, default the current one) and type (1.3): NEW (empty, default settings) | EMPTY (the source's settings, no objects) | LINK_COPY (its collections and objects shared) | FULL_COPY (independent copies of objects and data) - Blender's New Scene menu, run in this Blender's window with the window's scene put back. Reply: objectCount, collectionCount, made (datablocks the copy made, by kind), objectsShared.
bl_create_text:
Create a Blender text object - titles, labels, mograph, anything with words in the render. An empty body is refused because such an object renders nothing while existing perfectly. align/align_y are validated against the enum this Blender offers. Says so when extrude is 0, since flat text is right for a 2D title and wrong for anything meant to catch a light. A TYPEFACE, NEW 2026-09-07: `font` takes a PATH to a .ttf or .otf. Left out, the text is in Blender's built-in face - which is what every text object this addon made before then was stuck in, because nothing could set one. There is no font library to name into, so it is a path; the same file passed twice reuses one datablock rather than stacking copies. The response says which face the text is actually in and whether it is the built-in.

Parameters: size (float, default None: Blender's own) is the font size, written to the text curve's size; bevel_depth (float, default None) is the curve's bevel depth, which rounds the letters' edges; both must be finite. location ([x, y, z] or {x, y, z}, default None: the origin) and rotation (radians, same shapes, default None: none) place the object; collection (str, default None: the scene collection) is an existing collection to link it into. name defaults to "Text" in the op, and Blender may suffix it on a clash (nameWasSuffixed).

font is resolved, and the file loaded with reuse of an already-loaded copy, before the text curve is made; a path must exist and end in .ttf, .otf, .ttc, .pfb, .woff or .woff2.

OUT: ok, name, type (FONT), collection, requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, location, rotation, font, fontIsBuiltIn, fontPath, fontNote (only on the built-in face), body, size, extrude, align, alignY, note (the flat-text note when extrude is 0, else null). bevel_depth is written and not read back here; bl_set_text reports it.

Refused with no object created: an unknown key; a missing, non-string or empty body; an align or align_y this build lacks (the refusal lists the valid ones); a font path that does not exist, has another extension or that Blender will not load; a non-finite or non-numeric size, extrude or bevel_depth; a malformed location or rotation; a collection that does not exist (make one with bl_create_collection). A font file loaded before a later refusal stays loaded.
bl_create_texture:
Create a legacy Blender TEXTURE datablock - what a DISPLACE modifier reads. Same producer/consumer gap as bl_create_lattice and found in the same pass: bl_add_modifier can point DISPLACE at a texture and bpy.data.textures appeared nowhere else in the addon. THESE ARE NOT SHADER NODES. bpy.data.textures is Blender's older texture system and is what the MODIFIER STACK reads - a DISPLACE modifier cannot take a ShaderNodeTexNoise. Both systems exist, they are not interchangeable, and that is the confusion this is most likely to be met with. The type is validated against this build's own enum (BLEND, CLOUDS, DISTORTED_NOISE, IMAGE, MAGIC, MARBLE, MUSGRAVE, NOISE, STUCCI, VORONOI, WOOD - identical on 3.6, 4.2, 4.4 and 5.0, read off the enum rather than assumed), and `image` is refused for any type but IMAGE rather than accepted and ignored. `file` loads an image from disk as the datablock (type IMAGE implied, colorspace default Non-Color, because a height map is data).

Parameters: name (str, default None, which the op reads as "Texture") is the requested datablock name; Blender suffixes .001 on a collision and the reply says so. intensity (float, default None = left at the new texture's value) and contrast (float, default None = likewise) are the texture's brightness and contrast multipliers, written as given to tex.intensity and tex.contrast; they are parsed before the texture is made, so a non-finite value creates nothing. type defaults to CLOUDS, or IMAGE when file is given, and is matched case-insensitively against the build's enum.

OUT: ok, texture (actual name), requestedName, nameWasSuffixed, type, image (name or null), imageFile (absolute path, with file), imageSize [w, h] (with file), colorSpace (with file), loadedFromDisk, colorSpaceNote (when file named an image already loaded: its existing datablock is used and its colour space changed everywhere), intensity, contrast, users, note.

Refusals ("NOTHING was created." in each): a type this build does not offer (the message lists them); image and file together; colorspace without file; image or file on a non-IMAGE type; no image datablock by that name (lists up to 25); a non-finite intensity or contrast; a file that will not load; a colorspace this build does not have (lists them; an image loaded by this call is removed again); any unknown key.
bl_retarget_action:
Move a Blender action from one armature onto another with other bone names and rest pose - bone map (AUTO by name, or explicit), rest-pose difference compensated, root translation scaled, baked to a new action; per-bone error in degrees. See mif_help.

source and target: armatures in object mode. action: the source's (default its assigned one). map: {targetBone: sourceBone}, or "AUTO" (default) - names matched after dropping prefixes (mixamorig:, DEF-, ORG-, MCH-, Bip01) and separators, sides (.L, _l, Left) kept apart, common synonyms (pelvis = hips, upperarm = arm, upleg = thigh, shin = calf, clavicle = shoulder); unmappedTarget and unmappedSource list the rest. REST-POSE COMPENSATION: each mapped bone takes the source bone's WORLD rotation change from its own rest and applies it to the target bone's rest, so an A-pose clip plays on a T-pose rig; unmapped target bones keep their rest. root_bone (default the mapped bone highest in the target's hierarchy) also takes the source root's translation from rest, times root_scale (default target / source root rest height). Baked frame by frame (frame_range, default the action's) into new_action (default <action>_<target>) in each bone's own rotation mode, with no constraint or operator; assign (default true) leaves it on the target. Reply: bones [{target, source, maxErrorDeg}] - the world rotation the target shows against what was asked, at sample_frames (default 8) frames - and maxErrorDeg; a warning past 1 degree (a constraint, driver or non-inherited rotation on the target). Measured on 3.6-5.2: an A-pose (45 degrees) source onto a T-pose target with other names, within 0.5 degrees.
bl_extract_root_motion:
Move a Blender clip's hips travel (and yaw) onto a root bone - made when the rig has none - or remove it (IN_PLACE); the feet's world positions are compared before and after. The pair of Unreal's extract_root_motion. See mif_help.

armature (object mode) and action (default its assigned one; edited in place). hips: the bone carrying the travel (default a bone named hips / pelvis). mode ROOT_MOTION (default): per frame the hips' horizontal travel (axes XY, or XYZ) from the first frame - and with yaw its turn about Z - is keyed on root (default "root"), and the hips keyed so they stay where they were in the world; a missing root is made at the origin (create_root, default true) with every top bone parented to it (no weights change). IN_PLACE: the travel is taken out of the hips (no root needed). feet (default foot / ankle / toe bones) are compared in world space before and after: maxMoved 0 for ROOT_MOTION (only where the motion is carried changed), the travel for IN_PLACE. The pair of Unreal's extract_root_motion - this fixes the clip at its source, and a rig without a root bone.
bl_set_freestyle:
Blender Freestyle line rendering: on or off, line thickness, line sets by edge type and collection with color, thickness and alpha, and Freestyle edge marks on meshes - read back. Cycles and EEVEE draw it. See mif_help.

enabled turns scene.render.use_freestyle and the view layer's use_freestyle on or off. line_thickness (thickness_mode ABSOLUTE pixels, default, or RELATIVE to 480 px), crease_angle (degrees). line_sets [{name, edgeTypes [SILHOUETTE | BORDER | CREASE | RIDGE_VALLEY | SUGGESTIVE_CONTOUR | MATERIAL_BOUNDARY | CONTOUR | EXTERNAL_CONTOUR | EDGE_MARK], collection, color [r,g,b], thickness, alpha, visibility VISIBLE | HIDDEN | RANGE}] - a set of that name is edited, else made (with a line style of its name); remove_line_sets [names]. edge_marks {object, edges [indices] | sharp: true | seams: true, clear} (or a list) marks edges for EDGE_MARK. Read back: every line set's edge types, collection, color, thickness, alpha. Freestyle draws in Cycles and EEVEE renders, not Workbench (engineNote says so). Measured present on 3.6-5.2; a 64 px Cycles render of a cube against a white world gained its silhouette line.
bl_set_sun_position:
Aim a Blender Sun light (and a sky texture's sun) from latitude, longitude, date, local time and UTC offset - azimuth, elevation, sunrise and sunset back; key_frame keys it for a time-lapse. Pairs with Unreal's set_sun_time. See mif_help.

latitude (north +) and longitude (east +) in degrees, date YYYY-MM-DD (default today), time HH:MM local (default 12:00), utc_offset hours (dst adds one). The solar position is NOAA's (Meeus) without refraction, computed natively - the bundled Sun Position add-on left Blender at 4.2. The Sun light (object, made as "Sun" when missing) is turned so it shines away from the sun; distance also moves it toward the sun. north_offset turns the scene's north from +Y (counterclockwise from above). sky: a world Sky Texture node (true: the first) follows - sun_direction for PREETHAM / HOSEK_WILKIE, sun_elevation and sun_rotation for NISHITA and the scattering skies. key_frame keys the rotation (and the sky's sun) for a time-lapse built call by call. Reply: azimuth (from north, clockwise) and elevation, towardSun in scene axes, sunrise and sunset (local), and a note when the sun is below the horizon. Measured: Greenwich on 2026-06-21 12:00 UTC - elevation 61.9, sunrise 03:43, sunset 20:21.
bl_set_text:
Change an existing Blender text object - the half that did not exist, so text was WRITE-ONCE. bl_create_text could set a body, a size and an alignment and nothing could change any of them afterwards, while bl_object_info REPORTS `body` for a FONT object - the string was readable and unwritable. Re-labelling a sign meant deleting the object and rebuilding it, which loses its transform, its material and anything parented to it. EVERY FIELD IS OPTIONAL and only what you name is touched, so it is safe to call with one key. The response carries `before`, `after` and `changed`, and `changedAnything` is false when the values asked for were the ones already there - so a caller can tell a no-op from a write, which a bare ok:true cannot. `font` is a PATH to a .ttf/.otf, as on bl_create_text.

Parameters (each default None = left as it is; only what is named is written): extrude (float) is the text's thickness - writes TextCurve.extrude; 0 is a flat plane, and the reply adds a note whenever extrude ends at 0. bevel_depth (float) rounds the letters' edges - writes bevel_depth. align (str) is the horizontal alignment, written to align_x; align_y (str) the vertical, written to align_y. Both are upper-cased and checked against the build's own TextCurve enum (read from bpy at runtime; a refusal lists the valid values). No range check is applied to extrude or bevel_depth beyond being finite numbers. object must be a FONT object.
