OUT: object, dataName, before and after {body, size, extrude, bevelDepth, align, alignY, font}, changed [the keys that moved], changedAnything, font, fontIsBuiltIn, fontPath, fontNote (Blender's built-in face only), note (extrude is 0).

Refusals ("NOTHING was changed." - every value is parsed before the first write): no object by that name; not a FONT object; an align or align_y this build does not offer; an empty body; a malformed size, extrude or bevel_depth; a font path with no file, an extension outside .ttf, .otf, .ttc, .pfb, .woff, .woff2, or a file Blender will not load; text, content, fontSize, material, location and rotation are refused naming the right key or tool; any other unknown key.
bl_set_uv_layer:
Choose the ACTIVE UV layer on a Blender mesh, rename one, or remove one. THE ACTIVE LAYER IS THE ONE EVERYTHING WRITES TO - every UV operator and every bake - and bl_uv_info reported it while the only way to CHANGE it was bl_uv_unwrap, which sets it as a side effect of unwrapping. So selecting a layer meant re-unwrapping it and destroying the UVs it held. REMOVING A LAYER SHIFTS EVERY LATER LAYER'S INDEX: measured on 3.6.23 and 5.0.1, with UVMap, A, B, C, removing A moves B from 2 to 1 and C from 3 to 2. Unreal's lightmap coordinate is an INDEX, not a name, so removing an earlier layer silently repoints what the engine reads on a mesh it has already imported - the layers that moved are named in indicesShifted. Removing the LAST layer is refused: it leaves the mesh unwrappable, and texturing and lightmap baking both fail until it is unwrapped again. A mesh is limited to 8 UV layers, which is why removing junk ones matters at all.

object (str, required; alias name) is the mesh object, which must be a MESH. active (bool, default None) true makes layer the active UV layer; false is accepted and changes nothing. active and rename may be combined; remove may not be combined with either. rename longer than 63 characters is refused; a clash with another layer's name is suffixed by Blender (nameWasSuffixed).

OUT: ok, object, layers [{name, index}] after the change, layerCount, activeLayer, activeLayerIndex, activeChanged, removed (name or null), renamedTo (or null), nameWasSuffixed, indicesShifted ({name: {was, now}} for every layer whose index moved, or null), note.

Refused before anything is written: an unknown key; no such object, or not a mesh; a mesh with no UV layers; no layer by that name (lists them); a non-boolean active or remove; remove together with active or rename; none of active, rename or remove; removing the only layer; a rename over 63 characters.
bl_set_vertex_color:
Write a Blender colour attribute - what games use for masks, wear and blend weights, and which the addon could not touch at all. Uses color_attributes, which exists on every supported build, rather than the legacy vertex_colors. Defaults to BYTE_COLOR on the CORNER domain: that is what Blender's own legacy call produced and what survives an FBX round trip. THE NAME CAN FAIL SILENTLY - color_attributes.new() with an over-long name TRUNCATES on 3.6 and RETURNS None on 4.2/4.4/5.0, neither raising - so the length is refused up front and the None guarded anyway. The stored colour is READ BACK rather than echoed: BYTE_COLOR quantises to 8 bits per channel, so asking for 0.25 stores 0.250158, and `quantised` says so instead of pretending the request was the result. A value per vertex makes a smooth mask: vertex_values [0-1, ...] (one per vertex in index order) or [[index, value], ...] (only those vertices) or falloff {points: [[x,y,z], ...] world, radius, inner (default 0), type SMOOTH | SPHERE | ROOT | INVERSE_SQUARE | SHARP | LINEAR | CONSTANT} - 1 within inner, 0 at radius - mixes base_color (default black) toward color by each vertex's value, and on CORNER every corner takes its vertex's value, so the mask has no steps at face borders; blend REPLACE (default), OVER (mixed from the stored value) or MAX (the larger per channel), and the reply's values gives count, min, max, mean and aboveZero.

PARAMETERS. object (string, required): a MESH with at least one face. color ([r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], linear, finite; alpha defaults 1): the value written; required when the attribute does not exist yet, and without it an existing attribute is only made active or render. data_type (string, default BYTE_COLOR): BYTE_COLOR or FLOAT_COLOR; an existing attribute must match. faces (list of face indices, default every element): colour only these faces' corners; needs domain CORNER, and is used only with color. make_active (bool, default true): make it the active colour attribute. make_render (bool, default true): make it the one the renderer uses. On a mesh with no colour attributes, the first one created becomes active and render whatever the flags say.

OUT: ok, object, attribute, created, domain, dataType, elements, elementsWritten, requestedColor, storedColor (read back off element 0), quantised, activeColor, renderColor, note (when BYTE_COLOR quantised the value).

REFUSED with nothing created or changed: a name over 63 characters; a domain other than CORNER or POINT; an unknown data_type; faces with a POINT domain, or faces that is not a list; a malformed or non-finite color; a face index out of range or not a whole number; a make_active or make_render that is not a boolean; no attribute of that name and no color; an existing attribute whose domain or data type differs from the request (delete it first); color_attributes.new() returning None. A mesh with no faces is refused too.
bl_render_viewport:
A Blender playblast: Viewport Render in a session with a 3D View, a matching Workbench render headless - a still or a frame range in seconds per frame; the reply names the route. See mif_help.

file_path (a still, PNG) or folder with frame_start / frame_end (frame_####.png per frame). In a session with a window and a 3D View it is Blender's Viewport Render (render.opengl, overlays with overlays: true); headless, where there is no viewport to draw, a Workbench render with solid shading (shading SOLID | WIREFRAME, color_type MATERIAL default | OBJECT | SINGLE | TEXTURE | VERTEX | RANDOM, the studio light) - route says which ran. camera (default the scene's), resolution_x / _y, percentage. The scene's engine, camera, resolution, output and frame are put back. Reply: framesWritten, files, seconds, secondsPerFrame.
bl_bake_vertex_animation:
Bake a deforming Blender mesh (cloth, a fixed-topology fluid, shape keys, nodes) over frames into vertex animation textures - offsets and normals, a row per frame, a column per vertex - and a rest mesh with VAT_UV; a changing vertex count is refused. Pair of Unreal's bake_vertex_animation. See mif_help.

object: a mesh deformed by its modifiers, shape keys or animation, evaluated per frame of frame_range (default the scene's; max_frames, default 1000). Two textures in folder - <name>_Offset and <name>_Normal (name default VAT_<object>) - one row per frame and one column per vertex (16384 vertices at most): format OPEN_EXR (default) writes the raw offset from the first frame as 32-bit float; PNG writes it 16-bit, normalized to bounds (value = (offset - min) / (max - min)) - bounds returns min and max per axis; the normal texture is normal * 0.5 + 0.5. unreal_axes (default true) writes centimeters with Y negated, as every send here. A new rest object <name>_Rest holds the first frame's shape with a UV channel VAT_UV giving each vertex its column (U) and row 0 (V). A changing vertex count is refused naming the frame - remesh to a fixed topology, or send Alembic. Unreal's own bake_vertex_animation bakes skeletal animation only; this is the Blender half for simulations and deformers.

fps (1.3, wave 3): the scene's frame rate (fps / fps_base), which mif_send_to_unreal's build_parent gives the material's VAT_FrameRate.
bl_bake_pivot_painter:
Bake a Blender model's elements (a mesh's loose parts, or a collection's objects) to Pivot Painter 2 data for Unreal's foliage wind functions: pivot + parent index and X axis + extent textures and the element-index UV. See mif_help.

object: a mesh whose loose parts are the elements (a tree from bl_build_tree / bl_build_plant) - the hierarchy is inferred, largest part first: each part's parent is the larger part nearest it, its pivot the point nearest that parent (the root part's: its lowest point), its X axis toward its farthest point. Or collection: its mesh objects, the hierarchy from their parenting, each pivot its origin and X axis its local X. Written to folder: <name>_PivotPos_ParentIndex.exr (always 32-bit float: RGB the pivot in centimeters, Y negated; A the parent's index, parent_index_encoding INT_AS_FLOAT - Pivot Painter 2's integer bits read as a float, the default - or FLOAT) and <name>_XVector_XExtent (RGB the X axis * 0.5 + 0.5, A the extent / 2048 cm; EXR, or PNG 16 with format PNG); each element's texel is set in the UV layer uv_layer (default PivotPainter). A root points at itself. Reply: elements, hierarchyDepth, textureSize, per element its parent and extent.

uvLayerIndex (1.3, wave 3): the layer's index - the UV channel it becomes in Unreal; null when a collection's meshes hold it at different indices. mif_send_to_unreal's build_parent reads it.
bl_hair_to_cards:
Turn Blender hair (Curves or hair particles) into game hair cards: strands clumped by root into N cards, a tapered ribbon per card along its clump, each card in its own atlas cell (V root to tip). See mif_help.

object: a Curves object (Blender 4.2+ hair) or a mesh with hair particle systems (read as drawn, co_hair). Strands are clumped by their roots (k-means, iterations default 8, seeded farthest-point) into cards (default 24, at most one per strand); each card is a ribbon of segments (default 6) along its clump's mean strand, width at the root (default twice the clump's spread, at least 1 mm) tapering to taper x that at the tip (default 0.3), turned to face out from the groom's center. Each card gets an atlas cell (atlas [cols, rows], default the smallest square), U across it and V 0 at the root to 1 at the tip. A new mesh object <object>_Cards. Reply: cards, triangles, atlas, cellSize, strands. A strand-atlas bake is bl_bake_texture onto the cards from the hair.
bl_bake_texture_set:
Bake several maps of one Blender setup (high-to-low or self) in one job, out of process by default - a second Blender bakes a copy of this session - named T_{object}_{suffix}, ORM packed on request; job_id alone polls it. See mif_help. baked_material makes a new material from the baked maps, and assign_baked puts it in every material slot of the object.

object and types (AO, NORMAL, DIFFUSE, ROUGHNESS, METALLIC, EMIT, CURVATURE, ALPHA, MATERIAL_ID, HEIGHT, POSITION, THICKNESS, COMBINED, GLOSSY, SHADOW): each map is a bl_bake_texture call with the shared settings (width, height, samples, margin, uv_layer, source, extrusion, max_ray_distance, cage; green_channel for NORMAL), written to folder as pattern (default T_{object}_{suffix}: BC, N, AO, R, M, E, Curv, A, ID, H, Pos, Thick, C, G, S) - PNG, EXR for HEIGHT and POSITION. pack_orm adds T_{object}_ORM from the AO, ROUGHNESS and METALLIC maps (occlusion 1, roughness 0.5, metallic 0 for one not baked). out_of_process (default true): this session is saved as a copy to a temp .blend and a second Blender bakes it under one of the machine-wide heavy-job slots and a memory ceiling (memory_limit_gb) - the reply is a job_id at once; bake_texture_set {job_id} returns running, mapsDone, each map's file and pixel signature, the ORM, complete. out_of_process false bakes here and returns the maps. Why: a 4K multi-map bake on the main thread passes the bridge's ceiling, reports a timeout and keeps running.

BASE_COLOR (1.4) is the albedo, baked through an emission of the Base Color input: a DIFFUSE bake is the diffuse color pass, base color x (1 - metallic), so a metal's - or a worn paint's bare metal edges - come out black in it; pass one of the two. A baked material reads the layer the bake wrote: uvMap in the reply names it when uv_layer is not the render-active one. baked_material (a new name) also makes a material with the baked maps on its Principled inputs (BASE_COLOR / DIFFUSE to base color, ROUGHNESS, METALLIC, NORMAL in green_channel's convention, EMIT, ALPHA) - what bl_export_material_textures and the send to Unreal carry; assign_baked puts it in every material slot of the object. Out of process the status call that sees the job finish makes it. The start's reply has snapshot {takenBeforeReply, at, callerDeadline, secondsToSpare}: the session copy the job bakes is written before the answer, and a start that reaches Blender after its caller stopped waiting is refused (callerGaveUp) and starts nothing.
bl_recipe_detail_bake:
Bake a Blender game mesh's NORMAL, AO and CURVATURE from a detail mesh in one call - the detail given, or built from the game mesh (subdivide, folds, displace rules, sculpt) - with a cage from the measured gap, seams and stitches drawn into the maps in millimetres, and checks before it answers: ray misses, black texels in UV islands, a tilted or flat normal map. See mif_help. It takes object, detail or build, types, folder, pattern, width, height, samples, margin, uv_layer, green_channel, cage or cage_distance, max_ray_distance, occluders, stitches, checks, keep_cage, out_of_process with memory_limit_gb, and job_id alone to poll.

object is the game mesh (a UV layer required; uv_layer picks one). detail names an existing high poly, OR build makes one from object: a Catmull-Clark subdivide levels deep (default: enough that the 90th-percentile edge is under the narrowest rule width / 1.5, up to 4 and max_faces, default 2,000,000), kept as name (default <object>_detail), hidden from render because it lies on the game mesh, with the game mesh's transform, vertex groups and armature, then folds [{axis [x,y,z] world, period, depth (scene units), irregularity 0.5, sharpness 2, seed, vertexGroup}] - ridges repeating along axis, their phase bent and height varied by Blender's noise, weighted by the vertex group - then rules (bl_displace_by_rule's SEAM, STITCH, WEAVE, KNIT, on the dense mesh) and sculpt (bl_sculpt_stroke calls, object filled in). build with none of the three is refused: a subdivided copy alone bakes a flat map.

The cage is object pushed out along its vertex normals by cage_distance (default the measured outward gap x 1.25 + 1 mm, at least 2 mm; or cage names one with object's topology); max_ray_distance is the reach past the low (default the measured inward gap x 1.25 + 2 mm). The made cage is removed after unless keep_cage. Every other geometry object is hidden from render for the bake except occluders (e.g. the body under a garment, for the AO). The maps go through bl_bake_texture_set (types NORMAL, AO, CURVATURE; folder, pattern T_{object}_{suffix}, width and height 2048, samples 32, margin 8, green_channel OPENGL or DIRECTX).

stitches [{edges BOUNDARY | UV_SEAMS | SHARP, or edgeIndices, seamWidthMm 3, seamDepthMm 0.6, stitchLengthMm 3, stitchSpacingMm 1.5, stitchOffsetMm 4, rows 1 (0 draws the seam alone), rowGapMm 4, threadWidthMm 1, threadHeightMm 0.35, aoStrength 0.6}]: the stitch layer. Along the game mesh's own edges it draws a seam groove and rows of stitches - each a raised thread with a pit where it goes through - as a height in millimetres, turned into a tangent normal and blended (whiteout) into the baked NORMAL, and darkened into the AO (the groove, and the ground at each thread's foot). No dense mesh needed: a 1 mm thread on a 5 cm game edge. Each edge is drawn once per face it borders, inside that face's UV island and on its side, so a UV seam is drawn on both islands, and the dashes run on one arc length per edge chain so they line up across the cut. The reply's stitchLayer gives per rule the edges, chains, length in mm and texels changed per map.

checks {maxMissPercent 1, maxBlackPercent 0.5, maxMeanTiltDeg 8, minDetailPercent 1}, before it answers: rays cast as the bake casts them (from the cage in along the normal) inside every face of the game mesh, the share that miss the detail - refused BEFORE the bake when over; black or unbaked texels inside UV islands per map (the edge texel of each island left out); the normal map's mean tilt, the share leaning past 3 degrees (detailPercent, after the stitch layer), and the share pointing into the surface. A failed check is refused naming the fix; the meshes it made are removed and the maps stay on disk to look at. The reply names each map with its file, coverage, black texels, and for NORMAL meanNormal, meanTiltDeg, detailPercent, strongDetailPercent (past 10 degrees), invertedPercent and angleP95Deg; the build (levels, faces, what each fold and rule moved), the cage (distance, maxRayDistance, the gaps measured) and the rays.

out_of_process true bakes in a second Blender (bl_bake_texture_set's job, memory_limit_gb): the reply is a job_id, and bl_recipe_detail_bake {job_id} polls it - the status call that sees the bake finish draws the stitches and runs the checks. Why: a character that skips the detailed high poly and its bake reads as clean procedural cloth up close - folds, seams, stitching and wear are carried by these maps.
bl_build_body:
A Blender body with clean joins on a skeleton (armature) or a preset (adult, slim, heavy, child): a quad cage lofted from width and depth tables, limbs joined through quad holes, hands and feet, fitted and subdivided.

WHY (spec 1.4, 2026-11-07): the Skin modifier was the only typed route to a connected body, and its hull leaves a hard crease at every branch - shoulders, crotch, palms - that no radius shapes; a test body had to be generated by hand. HOW: a quad CAGE - a torso of 16 columns from the crotch to the crown, limbs of 10, fingers of 4 - lofted from tables of half-width, front depth and back depth per height (torso) and radii front / inner / back / outer along each limb. The armhole is a patch two faces wide and three tall cut from the torso's side and bridged to the arm; the hip is a crotch vertex that splits the torso's bottom ring into two leg loops; the palm ends in four quads, a finger grown from each, a thumb from a face on its side; the feet are rings turning from the shin to the toes, the heel pushed behind and onto the floor. Muscle and bone forms (pectorals, deltoids, trapezius, shoulder blades, glutes, quads, knee caps, calves, biceps, triceps, forearms) are laid along each ring's outward direction; the head is a blank form (skull, jaw, chin, brow, nose) for a face pass. Then the cage is FITTED so its Catmull-Clark limit surface passes through the table points (Halstead's vertex limit stencil, eight damped passes) and subdivided: a subdivision surface has no crease unless one is marked, so every join is smooth by construction. One closed all-quad mesh.

armature: build on its rest pose - landmarks from the upper arm, forearm, hand, thigh, shin, foot and toe bones of each side, the neck and head, found by name (upperarm_l, upper_arm.L, LeftArm, mixamorig:LeftForeArm, DEF-thigh.R) or named in bones {role: bone} (upperarm_l, lowerarm_l, hand_l, thigh_l, calf_l, foot_l, ball_l and _r, neck, head, pelvis); a role found twice or not at all is refused with the bones listed. The frame is read off the skeleton (left shoulder minus right is +X, world Z up), sides are averaged and the difference reported as skeleton.asymmetry. With no armature the preset's own proportions of height (default adult 1.79 m, child 1.20 m) are the skeleton, and create_armature builds it (23 bones, root to toes, UE names). bind skins the body with automatic weights (bl_set_parent ARMATURE_AUTO, fallback NEAREST). torso [{z, width, front, back}] (meters, z above the floor) replaces the preset's torso table; arms / legs [{at, ...}] replace the limb radii at 0 (shoulder or hip) to 2 (wrist or ankle). finger_curl 0-1 (0.25). subdivisions 0-3 (2); game_ready true or {triangleBudget, ...} picks the most subdivision that fits the budget (30,000 for a body unless given) and returns bl_mesh_quality's gameReady verdict. UVs: seams by rule (the back's midline, under each arm, inside each leg, round the shoulders, hips, wrists, ankles and finger bases, along each finger and the sole) unwrapped and packed into one tile. Vertex groups Body_torso, Body_head, Body_arm_l ... per part.

The reply reads back: cage vertices and faces, subdivisions, counts, fit {maxM, meanM} (how far the fitted cage's limit surface misses the tables), closed {boundaryEdges, nonManifoldEdges, ngons, triangles}, girths {chest, waist, hips} cut from the built mesh, landmarks, skeleton {heightFrom, asymmetry, bones}, vertexGroups, createdArmature, bound and gameReady. Refused before anything exists: an unknown preset, a height outside 0.3-3 m, a table row with a width at or below 0, limb tables not covering 0.2-1.8, a skeleton not standing upright, a cage over the gameReady budget, bind with no skeleton.
